author: lystopad
subject: cl/beacon: resolve payload withdrawals in one place (#23280)
body:
Split out of #23105, which grew too large to review in one piece.

### What this does

`produceBeaconBody` chose between three withdrawal sources inline — a
Gloas head whose payload was revealed, a Gloas head whose payload was
not, and everything before Gloas — each with its own hand-written
conversion loop, and then assembled the payload attributes around
whichever it picked.

The choice is now a method that names what it selects between, and the
attributes come from a single version-aware constructor. What is left
inline is the genuinely fork-specific part: the two fields only Gloas
sends. The three conversion loops go through the shared converter from
#23271, which are the call sites @yperbasis pointed out as still
hand-written when reviewing that PR.

### Behaviour change

The refactor itself is behaviour-neutral, but the constructor also fixes
two cases where the old inline construction built a request the chosen
wire version cannot express:

- **the parent beacon block root is omitted below Deneb** — Capella and
Bellatrix dispatch to `forkchoiceUpdatedV2`/`V1`, and
`validatePayloadAttributesPreFCU` rejects a non-nil parent root there
with `InvalidPayloadAttributesErr`;
- **withdrawals are omitted below Capella** — Bellatrix dispatches to
`forkchoiceUpdatedV1`, which has no withdrawals field, and the
expectation is a non-nil empty slice, so one was being sent.

Both only bite on the engine transport, and both made the request fail
rather than be ignored.

### Withdrawal source equivalence

The routing is otherwise unchanged, including the details that are easy
to lose in a refactor:

- a FULL Gloas head reads from the state copy with the parent payload
applied, not from the head state;
- an EMPTY Gloas head reads the expectation the state already cached,
and does not compute a fresh one;
- before Gloas the expectation is computed from the head state;
- the resulting slice keeps its nil-ness in every case.

`TestExpectedWithdrawalsReadsTheRightSourcePerFork` gives the two Gloas
states different withdrawal outcomes, so it fails if the source
selection is removed rather than passing either way.
`TestPayloadAttributesOmitFieldsTheChosenVersionCannotCarry` pins the
two gates across every fork.

Part of a series splitting #23105.

author: lystopad
subject: execution: key builders by payload timestamp and give them a lifecycle (#23272)
body:
Split out of #23105, which grew too large to review in one piece. The
payload-preparation work there depends on this, but every problem below
is reachable on `main` today, so it stands alone.

Depends on #23343 (now merged), which wakes the real txpool condition
wait when a builder's context is cancelled; without it a discarded
builder can remain parked until another block or shutdown broadcasts the
condition.

### Deduplication remembered only the last request

`lastParameters` held a single set of parameters, so any interleaved
request for a different timestamp destroyed the deduplication for the
first one. A repeated request then started a second builder for a
payload already being built, and the first kept running unreachable.

Builders are now kept by the payload timestamp they are for, next to an
immutable copy of the parameters they were created with. The copy
matters: the caller owns the withdrawals slice and the pointer fields it
passed, and could otherwise mutate them and change what a later
comparison sees. The payload id is written to that copy, never back to
the caller's parameters.

### A failed builder was reused forever

`BlockBuilder` latches its error, so once a build failed every later
request that deduplicated onto it got that error back — spending the
slot waiting for a payload that could never arrive. A failed builder is
now treated as absent and dropped when its error surfaces.

Being stopped is deliberately not failure: a stopped builder still holds
the payload it was stopped for, which is exactly what a repeated request
is asking for.

### Eviction did not bound a builder's lifetime

This is the problem in #23101. Setting the interrupt flag is not enough,
because `Builder.Build` ran its database read view and its transaction
provider on the node-lifetime context, and the flag is not read until
whichever of those is blocking returns on its own — up to most of a
slot. An evicted builder therefore left the map while its goroutine and
read view stayed alive.

A builder now answers two different requests:

- **Interrupt** — return the block you have so far. This is how a
payload is collected and how the maximum build time is enforced; both
want the payload.
- **Discard** — the payload is not wanted, release what you hold. This
cancels the context the build runs under, so a read view or a
transaction provider blocked on it returns at once.

Eviction discards. `BlockBuilderFunc` takes a context, `NewBlockBuilder`
derives a per-builder cancellable one, and `Build` uses it for
`BeginTemporalRo`, `NewSharedDomains`, `createBlock` and `execBlock` —
which is how it reaches `ProvideTxns`. `Builder.ctx` is removed rather
than left beside it.

The maximum-build watchdog interrupts first and then gives the build a
grace of half a slot to finish up — the transaction in flight, the
packing tail, payload finalization. A build that has not returned by
then is taken as stuck and discarded. The grace deliberately bounds
finalization too: an earlier acknowledgement-based variant let a build
that wedged after acknowledging — in finalization, say — keep its
resources forever, and a healthy build inside a single heavy transaction
could not acknowledge at all and was discarded together with its
payload.

Two deliberate limits:

- eviction stays asynchronous, so this is not a hard bound on live
builders at any instant. It changes the window from "until the blocking
call gives up on its own" to "as fast as a cancelled call returns", and
a discarded builder reads as gone at once to new callers — deduplication
passes it over and a new `GetAssembledBlock` answers unknown-payload —
while its goroutine winds down. A collector already waiting keeps a
valid payload that completes as discard lands. Making eviction wait
would block `AssembleBlock` while holding the module semaphore.
- the build context carries no deadline of its own; `buildDuration` and
the stop grace are both derived from the chain's slot length. The grace
bounds only finishing up after the stop, not the build itself, so it is
not a fork-specific build budget.

Fixes #23101.

### Cancellation

Both entry points check for a cancelled caller before acting, so an
expired request reports why it stopped instead of looking like
contention, which callers retry; `AssembleBlock` also refuses once the
module's own context is over, so no builder is born after shutdown.
`GetAssembledBlock` asks the builder whether the build itself failed
rather than inspecting the returned error, which a build can populate
with a context error of its own.

Discard may race a caller already waiting in `GetAssembledBlock`.
`BlockBuilder.Stop` owns that race: discard without a payload returns
`ErrDiscarded` immediately, while a valid payload that completes as
discard lands remains available to the waiting collector and later
retries. A completed payload or build error also wins over simultaneous
caller cancellation, so `Stop` reports the latched outcome rather than
the caller's context error. A failure completed before discard also
remains the build's failure instead of being rewritten as
unknown-payload. Execmodule maps only `ErrDiscarded` to unknown-payload
and drops that builder.

Cancellation reaches finalization and the asynchronous seal-result wait
as well. `finishBlock` checks the context before clearing or publishing
the assembled block and before starting the seal, and `Build` stops
waiting for a seal result when the context ends. `Seal` implementations
must not retain the transaction-backed chain reader after `Seal`
returns, so the cancelled build can release its read resources safely.

The in-process Caplin adapter and `ExecModuleTester` turn an unknown
result into `ErrUnknownPayload`. `IsUnknownPayloadError` recognizes both
that sentinel and the remote Engine API `-38001` error. Block production
treats either form as terminal, warns once, and does not keep polling an
id that cannot produce.

### Tests

Deduplication and lifetime are covered directly: builders kept apart by
timestamp, a superseded builder still packing and still retrievable by
an id already handed out, a collected payload handed back to a repeated
request rather than starting a second builder, a failed builder not
reused and dropped once its error surfaces, a caller cancelled *while
`Stop` is waiting* leaving the builder collectable, an evicted builder
blocked in its provider actually completing rather than merely having a
flag set, a discarded builder reading as gone at once — passed over by
deduplication and answered as unknown by `GetAssembledBlock` — the
watchdog discarding a build that never observes its stop while keeping a
healthy one that is merely slow to observe it, a build that wedges after
observing the stop released at the end of its grace, eviction passing
over a failed builder however live its slot, `AssembleBlock` refusing to
register a builder after shutdown, and the caller's parameters never
written to.

The completion boundary is covered in both directions: discard while
`Stop` is waiting returns unknown when no payload survives, while a
valid payload that completes as discard lands remains replayable; a
failure completed first remains visible; and an unfinished discarded
builder reads as gone immediately. Builder coverage also pins replay
idempotency, the discarded fast path, both finalization cancellation
checks, cancellation of the seal-result wait, and preference for a
completed payload or build error over simultaneous caller cancellation.
The tester and both local and remote Caplin paths cover unknown-payload
conversion, terminal polling, and the warning emitted for that terminal
result.

Part of a series splitting #23105.

---------

Co-authored-by: Andrew Ashikhmin <34320705+yperbasis@users.noreply.github.com>

author: lystopad
subject: cl/beacon: report a failing payload poll once, and an unregistered fee recipient at all (#23274)
body:
Split out of #23105, which grew too large to review in one piece.

### A failing window reported once

`pollAssembledPayload` retries at the retry cadence, so a slot whose
payload never arrived reported itself once per attempt and buried
everything else in that slot.

It is now reported when the window is over, once, carrying the slot, how
many attempts failed and the first reason — the first rather than the
last, because a hundred repeats of "connection refused" followed by one
"still syncing" should not be attributed to the latter.

An unknown payload ID is terminal rather than a transient collection
failure: polling stops after the first response and the request reports
one Warning.

Two cases stay out of warning and error logs:

- a window that fails and then succeeds. That is a healthy slot.
- a caller that went away. A validator client timing out or a node
shutting down cancels the request context, which comes back through the
collection call; that is the slot ending, not the execution layer
failing.

A failure that happened *before* the caller left is still reported,
since giving up is often the consequence of it.

### An unregistered fee recipient is worth saying once

Production falls back to the zero address when nothing is registered for
the proposer, which gives that block's fees away, and said nothing about
it.

It now warns once per proposer, claimed in one step so that block
template requests for the same slot arriving together do not each decide
they are the first, and bounded so an unregistered proposer cannot
accumulate. A dev chain rotates through 64 proposers and never registers
any of them, so remembering only the most recent one warned on nearly
every proposal.

The warning names the registration it consulted rather than claiming
none exists anywhere: under Gloas a signed proposer preference can carry
one, which this lookup does not read. That is #23300.

### Production failures have one owner

`produceBlock` owns the actionable record for failures returned by body
production. Body steps return their causes instead of logging locally,
so a failed proposal produces one record carrying the slot and the
underlying reason. An unknown payload is a Warning; other actionable
failures are Errors.

This covers every body failure path, including an empty payload ID from
`ForkChoiceUpdate`: the returned cause keeps the "EL may be syncing"
hint without a separate warning or a generic follow-up error. Concurrent
body steps report through separate error variables, which are read after
all steps finish.

Caller cancellation is classified at the same boundary and remains a
debug event rather than an error. A failure observed before cancellation
is still returned and reported.

Part of a series splitting #23105.

---------

Co-authored-by: yperbasis <andrey.ashikhmin@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Andrew Ashikhmin <34320705+yperbasis@users.noreply.github.com>

author: lystopad
subject: cl/antiquary: back off retirement steps that keep failing (#23252)
body:
Refs #23224.

`antiquateBlobs` and `antiquate` only log their error, and
`retirementLoop` re-enters every 12s, so a failure that is
**deterministic rather than transient** is retried on every tick for the
life of the process. Nothing about the node's state changes between
attempts, so each retry redoes the same work and logs the same line.

Measured on a Gnosis archive node running `release/3.5`: a missing blob
sidecar at slot 29403906 failed the same range **328 times in 65
minutes** at a flat 12s period. Each attempt re-read ~3900 beacon block
bodies and, before #23233, abandoned a `seg.Compressor` and leaked its
pattern workers — which is what actually OOM-killed the node at
`alloc=58.7GB`.

With #23233 merged the leak is gone, but the retry storm itself remains:
the CPU burn, the log spam, and blob pruning blocked indefinitely.

## Change

Each of the two retirement steps gets its own tick-counting backoff. On
consecutive failures the number of skipped ticks doubles — 1, 2, 4, …
capped at 300 ticks, roughly an hour — and a success resets it. A step
that is simply idle is unaffected, since `ready()` only refuses ticks
after a failure.

Counting ticks rather than reading a clock keeps the loop's existing
cadence as the only time source and makes the unit deterministic to
test.

`antiquate` gets the same treatment as `antiquateBlobs`: it shares the
log-and-continue shape, and `dumpBeaconBlocksRange` has its own fatal
paths (`skipped too many blocks in a row`, `expected %d blocks, got %d`)
that can wedge the same way.

The shutdown path is unchanged — a cancelled context is still neither
logged nor counted as a failure.

## What this does not do

It does not repair the underlying gap. A node wedged on a missing
sidecar stays wedged, just quietly and cheaply instead of every 12
seconds. #23224 tracks what a missing sidecar *should* do — backfill it,
record the gap and continue, or fail permanently — which changes what a
blob snapshot means and wants a Caplin owner's call.

## Test

`TestRetirementBackoff*` pins the four behaviours: an unfailed step runs
every tick, consecutive failures double the gap, the gap caps, and
success resets. Written before the implementation; the type did not
exist, so the package did not build.

`cl/antiquary/...` green, including under `-race`. `make lint` clean.
`make erigon` builds.

author: lystopad
subject: cl/phase1: report forkchoice timeouts and missing payload IDs (#23397)
body:
First of two, extracted from #23105. It addresses the third blocking
concern in domiwei's review and a defect in every Engine API forkchoice
path today, not only the one #23105 adds.

## Problem

`ExecutionClientEngine.ForkChoiceUpdate` had two ways to report a failed
payload request as an empty success.

First, a returned deadline error was mapped to `(nil, nil)`:

```go
if err.Error() == errContextExceeded {
    return nil, nil
}
```

Second, Erigon's configured internal FCU timeout does not reach this
client as an error. The execution module returns `ExecutionStatusBusy`,
the Engine API maps that to `SYNCING` with a null payload id, and the
client returned `([]byte{}, nil)` because `SYNCING` is not a
payload-status error.

For an update carrying payload attributes, a missing id means no payload
build started. A caller treating `err == nil` as success skips the retry
it would otherwise make, so a slow or busy execution layer can cost a
proposal. Block production also reported the empty id as "execution
layer may be syncing", hiding an actual returned deadline.

A head-only update is different: without payload attributes, a null
payload id is expected.

Deadline recognition was also a string comparison against one exact gRPC
message. Any rewording, or a transport that phrases it differently,
silently stopped matching.

## Change

`ErrForkChoiceUpdateTimeout` wraps a returned deadline cause. It is
recognised through a wrapped `context.DeadlineExceeded`, the gRPC status
code, or the old message as a last resort for a transport carrying
neither.

`ErrForkChoiceUpdateNoPayloadID` reports an attribute-bearing response
with no payload id. Payload-status validation runs first, so a supplied
validation error keeps priority. Head-only updates keep their existing
empty-id success.

The missing-id result is not called a timeout. Engine API `SYNCING` can
also represent execution contention, a missing segment, or a head that
is too far away. The separate sentinel states what is known and lets
each caller decide whether to retry or fail.

Call sites keep the behaviour they need:

- `stages/forkchoice.go` and `storeBlockAndBlobs` still tolerate
returned timeouts because they do not need a payload id.
- `block_collector` already warns on any error.
- Block production treats a timeout or an attribute-bearing response
without an id as a failure because it cannot build the block without
that id.

## Verification

Regression coverage checks wrapped context deadlines, gRPC deadline
status, the legacy message, unrelated errors, and a `SYNCING` response
with a null payload id.

- `make test-short`
- `make erigon integration`
- `make check-generated`
- affected-package tests
- `make lint`

---------

Co-authored-by: yperbasis <andrey.ashikhmin@gmail.com>

author: lystopad
subject: cl/beacon: prime the execution layer before a slot this node proposes (#23399)
body:
Payload construction currently starts inside the proposal slot. A busy
execution layer consumes time that the block needs for propagation and
attestation. This PR starts the local payload builder one slot early
when the next proposer belongs to a registered validator. Production can
then collect the prepared payload instead of starting the same build
from cold.

## Scope

Preparation runs only with the validator API and the direct in-process
execution client. It starts at Capella and retires at Gloas, where
builders gossip bids instead. Work is limited to the next slot and stops
early when the proposer is not registered.

Fulu proposer lookahead is consulted before copying and advancing the
full beacon state. A Fulu node that is not due to propose therefore
avoids the large copy and epoch-transition allocation. At a pre-Fulu
epoch boundary, proposer lookup still advances a state copy because the
proposer cannot be read from the unadvanced state.

## Design and correctness

Preparation reads the beacon root, proposer and state from one atomic
head view. It derives the fee recipient, withdrawals and payload
attributes for the target slot, then confirms that the selected
consensus head and local execution head still match the intended
parents.

The direct execution client starts the payload builder directly without
changing fork choice. Production keeps its normal forkchoice update.
Both paths use the same payload-attribute helper, so an identical head
and attributes reuse the existing execution-module build and return the
same payload ID.

A prepared record changes the payload collection window only when its
slot and payload ID exactly match the production result and the builder
has been running for the required minimum time. A changed head, changed
inputs, missed preparation or failed attempt therefore falls back to
ordinary production.

## Liveness and cost

The admission gate covers only each short builder-start attempt.
Production holds the other side of the gate while constructing a
validator block and while storing a locally produced block. Production
can wait only for an attempt that has already entered; new preparation
attempts are refused until production finishes. Preparation never holds
the gate while copying state, advancing slots or waiting to retry.

If the local execution module is busy or has not yet adopted the
intended parent, preparation retries every 100 ms until the target slot
begins. Each builder-start attempt is one-shot; preparation does not add
retry or cancellation behavior to canonical or production forkchoice
updates.

Preparation is best effort. Its failures do not fail a proposal, and
production keeps the cold path when no matching prepared payload is
available.

## Follow-up

An operator setting, preparation metrics and real-execution-module reuse
coverage remain tracked in #23419.

---------

Co-authored-by: yperbasis <andrey.ashikhmin@gmail.com>

author: milen
subject: execution: optimise incoming bal encoding/decoding/validation path (#23417)
body:
for https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/issues/14522

noticed that we were doing unnecessary operations for the incoming bal
at new payload and other places:
- we were doing unnecessary bal validations every time we called rlp
Decode - unnecessary, Decode has only 1 responsibility - to decode rlp
bytes in a struct - validation is a separate check that can be done only
once at API entry point
- we were doing 4 bal rlp Decode calls in 1 new payload request - 1 in
engineapi on receiving it, 1 in `stage_exec` as part of `bal.Process`, 1
more in stage_exec as part of `(*parallelExecutor).execImpl`, 1 in the
read aheader
- we were doing 1 avoidable bal rlp Encode in `bal.Process` as part of
`stage_exec`
- we were also missing the opportunity to do static bal validation as
early as possible and return early in new payload instead of proceeding
forward with execution to later on find out an invalid bal

this was improved by:
- decoupling bal validation checks from bal rlp decoding
- moving decoding and validation at the API entry points, doing them
only once - engine_newPayload, Caplin CL payload consumer, EL block
downloader, InsertBlocks
- introducing `BlockAccessListSidecar` to carry the raw input bytes and
the decoded BlockAccessList type attached to the block so that we
eliminate the unnecessary Decode (need in `stage_exec`) and Encode
(needed in `InsertBlocks`)
- we also introduce memoization of the block access list hash
computation on the sidecar so that the work is not repeated. same goes
for validation too (safe since the sidecar is immutable)

results:
| Operation | Before | After | Reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| RLP decode | 4 | 1 | 3 |
| RLP encode | 1 | 0 | 1 |
| BAL validation | 7 | 1 | 6 |
| **Total operations** | **12** | **2** | **10** |

---------

Co-authored-by: Alex Sharov <AskAlexSharov@gmail.com>

author: Alex Sharov
subject: cl, common: reuse snappy stream codecs from a pool (#23423)
body:
Every `snappy.NewReader` / `NewBufferedWriter` allocates ~142 KB of
scratch buffers (2 allocs). `parseResponseData` built one per response
chunk, so a 64-block `BeaconBlocksByRange` response burned ~8.7 MB of
garbage; the sentinel handlers and the fork-graph state dump paid it per
message.

New `common/snappypool` holds a reader and a writer pool, and every call
site in `cl/` takes its codec from there — including the tests, so
copy-paste keeps using it. `PutReader`/`PutWriter` reset to nil first,
otherwise a parked codec pins the caller's stream or buffer.

The `forkGraphDisk.sszSnappyReader`/`sszSnappyWriter` fields go away
with it: the pool replaces the hand-rolled per-struct cache, and a
closed `afero.File` is no longer retained after a read.

Existing `cl/sentinel/...`, `cl/rpc` and
`cl/phase1/forkchoice/fork_graph` suites pass, `-short` and `-race`.

author: awskii
subject: cl, cmd: collapse the caplin hot sidecar stores onto one bucket store (#23451)
body:
`BlobStore` and `dataColumnStorageImpl` are the same object — an afero
store bucketed by `slot / subdivisionSlot` — with path building and
bucket pruning copy-pasted between them. This extracts the shared half
into a `bucketStore`, fixes two bugs the duplication hid, and moves the
retention floor out of the stores and into the caller.

Both `Prune` implementations walked every 10,000-slot bucket from slot 0
on every call, and `cleanupAndPruning` runs once per slot, so that was
`(head-keep)/10_000` `RemoveAll` syscalls every 12 s on mainnet and
every 5 s on gnosis, against directories the first pass already removed.
It is now a readdir over the buckets that exist.

Closes #23413.

## Changes

- `bucketStore` in `cl/persistence/blob_storage/bucket_store.go` owns
path derivation, write, read, exists, remove, stream and prune. It never
locks; the façades take a slot lock at the granularity of the real
operation — the whole `WriteBlobSidecars` batch, files-plus-count-row in
`ReadBlobSidecars` and `RemoveBlobSidecars`, the whole
`GetSavedColumnIndex` and `RemoveColumnSidecars` loops. Single-file
reads and `stream` take nothing, so a slow peer holds no lock.
- `pruneBelow` readdirs the store root and accepts an entry as a bucket
only when it is a directory whose name parses as `uint64` and formats
back byte-identically. The blob index MDBX lives at
`<CaplinBlobs>/chaindata`, a sibling of the numeric buckets, so a looser
filter would delete it; the old integer-built paths could not reach it.
It continues past a failed `RemoveAll` and returns the first error.
- Writes land by rename onto a temp file, so a failed encode no longer
leaves a truncated file that `Stat` then treats as complete forever.
`ssz_snappy.EncodeAndWrite` flushes in a defer and drops that error, so
`write` hands it a writer that records one.
- `RemoveBlobSidecars` tolerates an already-absent file instead of
returning on the first one and leaving the count row behind.
- `Prune()` and `Prune(keepSlotDistance)` become `PruneBelow(slot
uint64)` on `BlobStorage`, `DataColumnStorage` and `PeerDas`;
`slotsKept` leaves both constructors and the distance is computed in
`cleanupAndPruning`, which is now the only place the three hot floors
are decided. `PeerDas.PruneBelow` still advances the peer-advertised
`EarliestAvailableSlot`.
- `RemoveAllColumnSidecars` is deleted — no production callers.

Retention is unchanged for every flag combination on every network.
Blocks still cut against the stage's observed head and hot sidecars
against the wall clock; unifying those is a separate decision.

## Notes

Overwriting a sidecar that another goroutine holds open fails on
Windows, where `os.Rename` is `MoveFileEx` and needs delete access to
the destination. The target is already a complete file for that `(slot,
root, index)`, so `write` keeps it and reports success rather than
surfacing an error that `gossip_manager` would turn into a peer ban.

Follow-ups this makes cheap, each filed separately: the flat bucket
directory (#23426), the column custody bitmap that would replace 128
`Stat` calls per availability check (#23433), the kzg index rows that
leak on prune (#23432), and a now-dead `ethClock` parameter (#23450).

author: lystopad
subject: cl/beacon: report a syncing node as 503, not 500 (#23464)
body:
Fixes #23462.

A node with no head state — starting up, restarting, catching up —
answered **500 Internal Server Error** on endpoints where `beacon-APIs`
declares **503 CurrentlySyncing**. It is transiently unavailable, not
faulty, and 500 reads as a node fault to operators and alerting.

Same node, same cause, two different codes today: `POST
/eth/v1/beacon/pool/attestations` already returns 503 (`pool.go` sets it
explicitly), while the committee subscription endpoints return 500. That
inconsistency is what makes this an oversight rather than a decision.

## Change

Two paths fed the same wrong code.

**The sentinel was discarded.** `AddAttestationSubscription` built a
fresh error, so nothing downstream could classify it:

```go
-    return errors.New("head state not available")
+    return synced_data.ErrNotSynced
```

**The central mapper had no case for it.** `WrapEndpointError` already
special-cases one sentinel, so this sits next to it — one change
covering every endpoint that surfaces `ErrNotSynced` raw
(`getAttesterDuties`, `getCommittees`,
`PostEthV1BeaconPoolSyncCommittees`, `blockRootFromBlockId`,
`PostEthV1ValidatorSyncCommitteeSubscriptions`):

```go
 if errors.Is(err, fork_graph.ErrStateNotFound) {
     return NewEndpointError(http.StatusNotFound, ErrorCantFindBeaconState)
 }
+if errors.Is(err, synced_data.ErrNotSynced) {
+    return NewEndpointError(http.StatusServiceUnavailable, err)
+}
```

Both subscription handlers now route through `WrapEndpointError` instead
of hardcoding 500, and the syncing case no longer logs at `Error` — a
node that is merely catching up should not fill the log with failures.

Also in this PR:

- **`WrapEndpointError` matched `*EndpointError` by value.** `errors.As`
with a value target never matches the pointer `NewEndpointError`
returns, so an explicit code reaching this helper collapsed to 500.
`HandleEndpoint` checks the pointer form first, so **no endpoint hit
this in practice** — it is latent, not live, and it is a trap for the
direct callers this PR adds. Both forms now match.
- **`ApiHandler.committeeSub` held the concrete
`*CommitteeSubscribeMgmt`**, so the already-generated
`MockCommitteeSubscribe` could not be injected. It now takes the
existing `CommitteeSubscribe` interface. No caller changes — the
concrete type satisfies it.
- Removed a commented-out block in `subscription.go` that proposed this
exact 503 check.

## Spec


[`types/http.yaml`](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/blob/master/types/http.yaml)
— `CurrentlySyncing`: *"Beacon node is currently syncing, try again
later."*

Declared on two affected endpoints:
[`beacon_committee_subscriptions.yaml`](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/blob/master/apis/validator/beacon_committee_subscriptions.yaml)
and
[`duties/attester.yaml`](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/blob/master/apis/validator/duties/attester.yaml).

**Worth a reviewer's opinion:** the spec does *not* declare 503 for
`states/{state_id}/committees`, `pool/sync_committees` or
`sync_committee_subscriptions`, which the central mapping also changes.
I went with consistency — the condition is equally reachable there, the
error body shape is unchanged, and only strict response-code validation
would notice. Happy to narrow it to the two spec-declared endpoints if
you would rather stay literal.

## Scope

This is a conformance and observability fix, not a high-availability
one. Lighthouse does not branch on 503 anywhere in its fallback or
publish path — it derives health from `/eth/v1/node/health` and
`/eth/v1/node/syncing`, and both codes arrive as the same
`RequestFailed(ServerMessage(..))`. Client routing behaviour will not
change.

## Test

TDD, and each guard was verified by mutation rather than by reading:

| Mutation | Test that caught it |
| --- | --- |
| 503 mapping → 500 | `TestWrapEndpointErrorStatusCodes`, both
subscription 503 tests |
| sentinel → bare `errors.New` |
`TestAddAttestationSubscriptionReportsNotSyncedWhileSyncing` |
| pointer match removed |
`TestWrapEndpointErrorStatusCodes/explicit_code_is_preserved` |

The handler tests mock the subscription call, so they cannot catch a
regression in `committee_subscription.go` — hence the separate
package-level test for the sentinel. Coverage also pins the cases that
must *not* change: an unrelated failure still returns 500, and a synced
node still returns 200.

`./cl/beacon/... ./cl/validator/...` green (18 packages). `make lintci`
reports `0 issues`.

author: Alex Sharov
subject: cl/persistence, db: pool zstd decoders, lower what zstd encoders hold (#23435)
body:
Eight caplin decode sites built a zstd decoder per call and released it
with `Close`, which is permanent — so nothing was ever reused.
`base_encoding` now owns a `zstdReaderPool` next to its writer pool, and
the six sites in `historical_states_reader.go` plus `uint64_diff.go` and
`rabbit.go` take from it.

`WithLowerEncoderMem(true)` flips the encoder history buffer from two
windows to one window plus a block (`enc_base.go` `ensureHist`), and
`Reset` keeps that buffer for the encoder's life — so it is what a
pooled or long-lived encoder holds, not a per-call cost. Applied to the
`beacon_indicies` pool and the `db/compress` encoder.

Output is byte-identical, which these paths need: `WriteBeaconBlock`'s
bytes are copied verbatim into the caplin `.seg` files, and
`db/compress` feeds `db/seg`.
`TestZstdWriterPoolMatchesReferenceEncoderOptionsOnLargePayload` pins
that at 4MiB — above zstd's 128KiB block size, where window options
start to change output.

`WithEncoderConcurrency` is deliberately not set: in `db/compress` it is
what serves concurrent `EncodeAll` callers.

Behaviour changes:

- The four `freezeblocks` reader sites propagate the `Decoder.Reset`
error they used to drop.
- All three release helpers drop a decoder whose `Reset(nil)` fails
instead of pooling it. `Reset` returns only `ErrDecoderClosed`, and a
closed decoder cannot be revived, so pooling it poisoned the pool for
the life of the process.
- `historical_states_reader` returns each decoder right after the read
rather than at function exit, so a large-frame decoder is not pinned
across the per-slot diff loop that borrows from the same pool.

Not addressed here: pooled decoders retain their frame-history buffer,
so a multi-MB dump decoder can be reused for small diffs; both decoder
pools use the default `GOMAXPROCS` concurrency, which suits large
payloads and not small ones, so the fix is probably a second pool rather
than one setting. `cl/antiquary/beacon_states_collector.go` holds a
long-lived encoder that did not get `WithLowerEncoderMem`.

author: Kewei
subject: cl: fix Gloas checkpoint sync with external execution clients (#22683)
body:
## Summary

Fix the standalone-Caplin Gloas checkpoint-sync path when using an
external execution client.

- Preserve the skipped-slot checkpoint state root across fork-choice
disk persistence.
- Validate Gloas anchor and downloaded payloads through the external EL
even when insertion is unavailable.
- Encode empty Engine API transaction and versioned-hash inputs as
arrays instead of `null`.
- Bound remote-EL and pending-envelope retry work, release the
fork-choice mutex during envelope `NewPayload`, and refresh identity
before committing the result.
- Terminate stale pending-envelope retries below finalized history or
implausibly ahead of the local clock while retaining recent,
DA-unavailable, storage, and EL-retry work.
- Bound selected-head recovery to two requests per uninterrupted head
episode: the initial request plus one retry for a timeout, sparse
response, late response, or failed application.
- Bound payload-attestation validation memory by sharing same-root state
builds, admitting one full-state build at a time, and caching compact
validation contexts.
- Start PeerDAS only after data-column gossip topics are registered.

## Scope

This PR contains the original checkpoint-sync/external-EL/empty-encoding
work plus the minimal lifecycle corrections required by those paths, the
stale pending-envelope terminal rule observed on devnet, the
payload-attestation OOM fix, and the PeerDAS startup-order fix.

The later downloader/resolver/journal/canonical-ingress work remains in
draft #23249. This PR does not add a general request scheduler, a
negative cache for payload-attestation contexts, or a pre-Gloas
`OnBlock` lock-yield refactor.

Pending-envelope expiry uses the Gloas finalized epoch start as its
inclusive lower bound. A next-slot envelope is retained only within
`MAXIMUM_GOSSIP_CLOCK_DISPARITY`; farther-future slots are rejected
before slot-time conversion. Gossip and local-self-build origins use the
same terminal policy, removals are identity-checked against concurrent
replacements, recent DA/storage failures remain retryable, and a nil
index-repair marker is removed only when its durable envelope no longer
exists.

Selected-head recovery separates in-flight ownership from completed
attempts and guards callbacks with a monotonically increasing claim ID.
Every inconclusive or failed outcome can open one additional attempt,
but a stable EMPTY/malicious head can consume at most two root requests
total until the selected head changes.

## Review follow-up at `4259ba8243`

- Zero-blob anchor/stage payloads now pass a non-nil empty
versioned-hash array to external Engine API clients.
- Local context cancellation/deadline errors from envelope gossip are
converted to gossip `IGNORE`, not peer-invalid rejection.
- Pre-Gloas target slots skip missing-envelope recovery before touching
fork choice; the selected block's actual version remains independently
checked.
- Selected-head claims release on every exit, retry
fetched-but-unapplied envelopes, tolerate one sparse/timeout result, and
remain bounded to two attempts per uninterrupted head.
- Missing durable nil repair markers terminate, and DA-unavailable
entries use the same finality boundary as missing-state retries.
- The duplicate outer `NewPayload` latency observation was removed.

The requested global head sample was not adopted: earlier
recovery/application phases can change fork-choice eligibility, so later
consumers intentionally obtain a fresh selected head. The pre-Gloas
early gate removes the needless current-network work without widening
the consistency window.

## TDD and validation

Red-to-green regressions cover:

- zero-blob anchor and chain-tip Engine arguments;
- gossip cancellation/deadline classification;
- stale versus recent DA retries and missing nil repair markers for both
origins;
- selected-head timeout, sparse, late, canceled, invalid, transient-DA,
ABA, and bounded two-attempt behavior;
- pre-Gloas and exact-Gloas recovery activation.

Validation on the pushed source:

- `go test ./cl/phase1/forkchoice ./cl/phase1/network/services
./cl/phase1/stages -count=1`
- focused selected-head and pending-envelope tests under `go test -race`
- `make erigon integration`
- `git diff --check`
- repeated adversarial Standards, Spec, boundary, fix-delta, and
lifecycle reviews converged on generation
`c9a9d3f602e7ffa5f290d0375106c0c1319c9bdf7f0263553ba8fa0b2e021989`

`make lint` reports 0 issues for the changed surface, then the macOS
secondary pass fails on the pre-existing
`db/seg/decompress.go:residencyOnce` field, which is referenced only by
`residency_gate_linux.go`. This PR does not change that unrelated
platform-specific baseline.

author: Sahil Sojitra
subject: cl: enable errcheck for beacon/cltypes/phase1/validator and fix violations (#23476)
body:
Continues the incremental errcheck rollout for #22538 into `cl/beacon`,
`cl/cltypes`, `cl/phase1`, and `cl/validator`: removes their exclusions
and fixes every violation, including `cl/phase1/core/state/raw`, whose
event-hook setters required propagating errors through the
`abstract.BeaconState/BeaconStateBasic` interfaces and regenerated mocks
- a swallowed error there was silently dropping the antiquary's
persistence-failure signals.

Fixes several real bugs along the way, not just lint-satisfying: an
out-of-range committee index in ToAttestation was silently producing a
malformed attestation instead of being rejected; UpgradeToElectra
silently dropped a validator's excess-balance-queueing failure; and a
test mock for ViewHeadState always returned nil regardless of the
wrapped callback's error, masking failures across six tests.

Addresses review feedback with a few follow-up fixes:

- Propagates the newly fallible `abstract.BeaconState` setters through
their production callers in `cl/transition`. `cl/transition` itself is
not being migrated here and stays excluded from errcheck - but this PR's
own interface change meant those callers could keep silently discarding
the exact same persistence-hook errors one call frame higher, which
would have defeated the point of the fix. Every touched call site's
enclosing function already returned `error`, so this was a mechanical
propagation, not a `cl/transition` migration.
- Fixes two partial-mutation bugs the review surfaced in `SetSlot` and
`ResetEpochParticipation`: on antiquary-hook failure the state was left
half-mutated (slot already changed but not marked dirty for the merkle
tree; `previousEpochParticipation` reassigned before the hook ran). Both
now leave the state unchanged when the hook errors.
- `fork_graph.NewForkGraphDisk` no longer panics on a disk write failure
during startup; it now returns the error through the existing
`cmd/caplin/caplin1/run.go` startup error path.
- Fixes a comment typo (`commitee` -> `committee`).

All other cl/* packages remain excluded from errcheck for a follow-up
PR.

---------

Co-authored-by: Alexey Sharov <askalexsharov@gmail.com>

author: Sahil Sojitra
subject: cl: complete errcheck rollout across cl package and fix violations (#23577)
body:
Completes the errcheck rollout for #22538 across the entire `cl/*` tree.
Started as `cl/beacon`, `cl/cltypes`, `cl/phase1`, `cl/validator`; this
PR adds every remaining `cl/*` package: `cl/aggregation`,
`cl/antiquary`, `cl/das`, `cl/merkle_tree`, `cl/p2p`,
`cl/persistence/blob_storage`,
`cl/persistence/state(+historical_states_reader)`, `cl/rpc`,
`cl/sentinel(+communication/ssz_snappy,handlers,httpreqresp,service)`,
`cl/spectest/consensus_tests`, `cl/transition/impl/eth2(+statechange)`,
`cl/utils/bls`. Only non-cl/* packages remain excluded for future PRs.

Notable fixes beyond lint-satisfying:
- SetSlot/ResetEpochParticipation left the state half-mutated on an
antiquary-hook failure (slot changed but leaf not marked dirty;
previousEpochParticipation reassigned before the hook ran) - both now
roll back cleanly on error.
- fork_graph.NewForkGraphDisk panicked on a disk write failure during
startup; now returns the error through the existing startup error path.
- ProcessPendingConsolidations and two wp.Execute() worker-pool results
in epoch processing were silently discarding real errors; now
propagated.
- Added a "Review also caught and fixed" section covering Alex's direct
commits: the `errors.Is`/`bare-io.EOF` distinction on network streams vs
`bytes.Reader`, the `dropPeer`/`closePeer` dedup (9x repeated block),
two error returns that could never fire (`runDownload`, the one-worker
`ParallellForLoop`), and the `AddAttestation` test now only tolerating
`ErrIsSuperset` specifically instead of masking anything.

Everything else is peer/cleanup operations logging on failure instead of
discarding silently, or straightforward test fixes.

author: lystopad
subject: cl: seed the ENR custody group count instead of an empty entry (#23560)
body:
`setupENR` wrote the `cgc` entry as an empty byte slice:

```go
// cl/p2p/p2p.go
node.Set(enr.WithEntry(p.cfg.NetworkConfig.CgcKey, []byte{}))
```

Empty is the canonical encoding of zero, so a node advertised custody of
no groups.
Nothing corrected it: the only path that rewrites the entry is
`SetCustodyGroupCount`, gated on the count rising above `advertisedCgc`,
which
starts at `CustodyRequirement` — so on a node without attached
validators it never
fires. `p2p-interface.md` notes clients MAY reject a peer advertising
below
`CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT`, so the entry was not merely uninformative.

## Change

Seed the entry with the value `advertisedCgc` already starts at, via a
shared
`EncodeCgc` so the seed and the update path cannot drift on format.

Encoding is unchanged — `big.Int.Bytes()`, big endian with no leading
zero bytes,
zero as the empty string, per `fulu/p2p-interface.md`. The increase-only
gate is
unchanged: `fulu/validator.md` requires a node whose custody requirement
falls to
keep advertising the previous (highest) count, which is what it
implements. Both
are now covered by tests and a comment so neither gets "corrected"
later.

Verified on a gnosis archive node: `cgc` decoded to `0x` before and
`0x04` after.

## Scope

Present on `main`, `release/3.6` and `release/3.5`, and on every chain
with fulu
scheduled — none override `CustodyRequirement`. Cherry-picks to follow
once this
lands.

This does not change how a node computes its own custody, subnet
subscriptions or
column requests: those read the in-memory value, not the ENR. It fixes
what other
nodes believe about this one.

Two related gaps found in review, both pre-existing and filed separately
rather
than widened into this PR: the highest count is not persisted across
restarts, and
an archive node advertises `CustodyRequirement` while custodying all 128
groups.

author: Kewei
subject: cl: validate Fulu cell proof widths (#23578)
body:
## Summary

- reject Fulu and later `BlobsBundleV2` responses when any cell proof is
not exactly 48 bytes
- validate all proof widths before fixed-array conversion or blob
cache/body mutation
- preserve the existing pre-Fulu validation order

## Why

The Osaka Engine API defines each `BlobsBundleV2.proofs` element as a
48-byte `KZGProof`. Block production previously checked only proof
cardinality for Fulu and later. A short proof could therefore panic
during `[]byte` to `common.Bytes48` conversion, while an overlong proof
could be silently truncated.

## Tests

- TDD repro: 47-byte proof panicked before the fix; 49-byte proof
escaped validation
- focused 47/48/49-byte and pre-Fulu ordering tests
- `go test ./cl/beacon/handler -count=1`
- focused `go test -race`
- `make lint` (twice, isolated cache)
- `make erigon integration`

This is the first of the follow-up hardening changes found while
reviewing #23299. Broader Engine response and KZG semantic validation
remain separate PRs.

author: lystopad
subject: cl, cmd/utils: derive the column retention window from the chain config (#23610)
body:
Closes #23411.

The spec states PeerDAS column retention in epochs
(`MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS`), so the slot count
depends on `SLOTS_PER_EPOCH`. `cleanupAndPruning` already derives it
from the active chain config when `ColumnKeepSlots` is zero — but the
flag default was `131072`, mainnet's 4096 × 32, so that branch was
unreachable. Gnosis and Chiado, at 16 slots per epoch, retained 131072
slots against a 65536-slot window: twice the columns they need. Wasted
disk, no correctness impact.

Defaults `--caplin.columns-keep-slots` to `0` and lets the existing
fallback compute the window. No pruning logic changes.

Help text and docs no longer name a fixed slot count, so adding a chain
with its own slot timing needs no further edits here.

`0` meaning "use the spec window" rather than "keep nothing" is the
code's existing convention, kept rather than replaced with a new
sentinel — flagging it in case a reviewer would rather see it changed.

### Test

author: Andrew Ashikhmin
subject: cl, execution: update Chiado bootnodes (#23632)
body:
The new boot nodes were provided by Chetna. 

## Summary

- replace the Chiado CL bootstrap list with four new discovery ENRs
- replace the Chiado EL bootnodes with four discovery-only enodes using
UDP port 30303 and no TCP port
- remove configuration-specific Chiado bootstrap-list tests

## Live network test

Started a fresh Chiado node from commit c43e35de63 with an empty
datadir, no downloader, and no cached peers.

- EL maintained 7 peers: 1 eth69 peer and 6 eth71 peers
- Caplin maintained 1 compatible outbound peer and discovered 50
candidates during subnet search
- several CL candidates were rejected for fork mismatch, while the
compatible peer remained connected
- Caplin downloaded history at about 15-18 blocks per second

Chiado has no EL DNS discovery and the CL static-peer list was empty, so
the peer sets were reached through the new bootnodes. The records are
discovery-only, so direct TCP sessions to the bootnodes are not
expected.

TDD was not used because this is a mechanical bootnode configuration
update.

author: Alex Sharov
subject: exec, commitment, cl/beacon: clear pooled objects (which hold bytecode ptr) (#23642)
body:
seems it's root cause of OOM in tests:
https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/23640

not all pointers was cleared before returning objects to `sync.Pool`

Same class, found by sweeping every `sync.Pool` in the repo:

- `BranchEncoder.ClearDeferred` — up to 50k `*DeferredBranchUpdate`
stayed in the backing array, and that encoder lives inside a
`HexPatriciaHashed` that `Release()` pools.
- `Updates.batchSlab` — truncated between hash-sort batches; one `clear`
on the way out of `HashSort`.
- `responseValidators` — reset its pooled `strings.Builder` on checkout
instead of on return, parking a whole validators response in the pool.

The `returnReadList` clearing was commented out in `bd654e06d` (`save`,
2023-10-17); no rationale was recorded.

`journal.Reset` now clears by `len` rather than `[:cap]`, so a
transaction no longer pays the block's high-water mark; `revert` clears
the stretch it truncates, which is what makes that correct.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/network: fix blob history backfill boundary and sparse-peer startup (#23138)
body:
## Summary

- treat `FrozenBlobs()` as the exclusive end of frozen snapshot coverage
and refresh it between scan batches
- start blob history backfill with any positive peer count while
bounding active work, preserving exact process-local retry ownership,
and revoking completion whenever a new hole appears
- accept legal short or reordered Deneb/Fulu column responses, reject
responses outside the actual peer-filtered request before KZG or storage
work, and persist only complete verified recovery results
- make PeerDAS recovery, pruning, req/resp, Sentinel, and embedded
libp2p stream lifetimes cancellation- and progress-safe

## Root cause

Snapshot coverage owns slots strictly below `FrozenBlobs()`, but the
downloader stopped at the watermark itself. The first unfrozen slot
therefore belonged to neither snapshots nor history backfill. The
downloader also required 16 peers before starting, so nodes with a
healthy but smaller peer set never attempted recovery.

Lowering the peer threshold requires explicit progress and ownership
invariants: empty responses must not advance cursors, active work must
remain bounded, retry identities must not be silently coalesced or
evicted, completion must be revoked as soon as a new retry appears, and
cancellation must reach the underlying embedded libp2p stream. Legal
partial responses must accumulate within the request window, while
unrequested or duplicate data must be rejected before expensive
verification or durable writes.

## Scope

This PR includes:

- exclusive and per-batch refreshed `FrozenBlobs()` handling
- any-positive-peer admission, with peer rechecks immediately before
network recovery
- a backfill-only 15-second request window with exponential no-progress
backoff and at most two active request workers, canceled and joined on
every exit
- legal short or reordered Deneb accumulation by `(block_root, index)`,
with proof/KZG verification and complete-block persistence
- no cursor advancement for empty successful range responses; repeated
no-progress responses back off and trigger the configured HTTP fallback
- an initial best-effort scan of the current non-frozen range; later
passes scan the latest two epochs plus process-local retry identities
for blocks whose recovery failed in this process
- exact sparse retry identity retention without synthetic/coalesced
slots, indexed scheduling, at most eight retry slots per pass, global
retry pacing, fair live-versus-delayed selection, and release below
frozen, retention, or prune floors
- compact process-local PeerDAS recovery ownership with metadata
upgrades, queue-overflow handoff to the delayed scheduler, bounded 16
MiB reconstructed-result caching, and retry after transient storage
validation or final-write failures
- monotonic process-local BlobStore and DataColumnStore prune floors
that prevent active recovery from recreating data below a completed
prune while still allowing cleanup removes
- exact validation of each data-column response against the
peer-filtered wire-request snapshot `(slot, block_root, column_index)`
before KZG verification or storage access; over-cardinality, duplicate,
nil, schema-inconsistent, and unrequested responses are rejected as a
whole
- exact validation of each response chunk's raw fork digest against the
sidecar slot epoch, including same-`StateVersion` BlobSchedule/BPO
transitions, before the response reaches PeerDAS, KZG verification, or
storage
- whole-response preflight of Fulu signed-header signatures against
immutable canonical full/blinded block metadata, preventing a
valid-proof column with a poisoned proposer signature from becoming
durable recovery input
- durable completion publication only when retry ownership is empty,
plus immediate true-to-false revocation propagated to Antiquary when a
new retry is added
- count-only admission for already stored blocks, while Deneb/Fulu/Gloas
data recovered by this pass has independent durable read-back, identity,
commitment, and KZG postconditions
- caller-context propagation through Sentinel, prompt reset of an
established pre-response libp2p stream, preservation of explicit caller
deadlines, and a 30-second fallback for no-deadline req/resp calls
- at most two active forward probes, canceled and joined on completion,
timeout, or caller cancellation
- when the HTTP fallback successfully advances forward sync before P2P,
subsequent batches prefer HTTP until a preferred HTTP attempt cannot
commit blocks or make progress
- envelope batch and attempt timeouts that own the active RPC, with
cancellation-aware retry pacing
- cancellation-aware unsynced waiting and safe low-slot arithmetic

### Resource and lifecycle boundary

Exact same-process retry conservation cannot be combined with a fixed
identity-count cap without silently losing a recovery owner. This PR
therefore keeps compact retry metadata in memory in proportion to the
actual delayed recoverable roots/failures, while using indexed
scheduling, constant global retry pacing, prune/retention cleanup,
bounded live queues/workers, and a separate 16 MiB reconstructed-result
cache. PeerDAS delayed roots already have an over-half quorum of durable
column data, so the retained metadata is proportional to durable
recovery input rather than an independent untrusted payload cache.

The retry ledger, recovery generations, and prune admission floors are
intentionally process-local and reset on restart. This PR does **not**
add durable retry persistence, startup reconstruction, or
crash-consistent handoff. Those restart/durable-ownership semantics,
together with permanent-hole policy and universal recovery-state
reconstruction, are tracked in follow-up #23213 and will be implemented
in a separate PR.

## Validation

- full affected package tests for `cl/das`, `cl/rpc`,
`cl/phase1/network`, `cl/antiquary`, `cl/phase1/stages`,
`cl/sentinel/httpreqresp`, `cl/sentinel/service`, and
`cl/persistence/blob_storage`
- focused race tests for request/validation ownership, storage/prune
ordering, exact retry scheduling, completion revocation, peer-filtered
response membership, cancellation, and stream lifetime
- repeated RED-to-GREEN tests for sparse retry identity, PeerDAS
ownership, transient storage/final-write failures, prune races,
empty-response progress, completion revocation, and
unrequested/duplicate/over-cardinality column responses
- `make lint` repeatedly with isolated caches: `0 issues`
- `make erigon integration`
- independent Deep Standards, Spec, state/lifecycle,
boundary/integration, fix-delta, and evidence-truth review passes
against a pinned immutable generation

Fixes #22429

Durable lifecycle follow-up: #23213

author: Sahil Sojitra
subject: common, cl: enable errcheck across common/* and resolve #23577 review follow-ups (#23669)
body:
Continues the errcheck rollout from #22538 by removing the six
`common/*` bootstrap exclusions from `.golangci.yml` and fixing every
violation this surfaces, plus follow-ups from review on #23577.

#### errcheck: `common/*`

Exclusions dropped for:

`common`, `common/crypto`, `common/crypto/blake2b`, `common/iouring`,
`common/log/v3`, `common/mmap`, , `address.go`, `bytesn.go`,
`blake2x.go`, `logger.go` — explicit `_ =` discards on `Write`/`Log` in
`fmt.Formatter` paths, matching the convention the standard library uses
for the same methods.`iouring_linux.go` — explicit discards on
`Munmap`/`Close` in ring teardown, where there is no caller left to
report to. `blake2b_test.go`, `crypto_test.go` — real error checks via
`t.Fatalf`, in the message style each file already uses.

#### `common/mmap`: TestResidencyProbe on a tmpfs TMPDIR

`TestResidencyProbe` failed on any machine whose `/tmp` is tmpfs
(Fedora's default). tmpfs stores files only in RAM, so `FADV_DONTNEED`
cannot evict them and `mincore` always reports the mapping resident —
the "pages should be cold" assertion was unsatisfiable by construction,
independent of `Resident()`, which is a correct `mincore` wrapper.

The test now allocates on a filesystem whose page cache can actually be
dropped, keeping `t.TempDir()` as the fast path and falling back only
when `TMPDIR` is tmpfs. Behaviour is unchanged where `/tmp` is
disk-backed, including CI. No skip was added; the test runs and asserts
everywhere.

#### Review follow-ups from #23577

#23577 is already merged, so these land here rather than as amendments.

All three are resolved:

* https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/23577#discussion_r3861076326
— the consolidation rollback had no coverage: the only exercise of
`ProcessPendingConsolidations` is the `PendingConsolidationTest`
spectest vector, which never makes `state.IncreaseBalance` fail. Added
two unit tests driving that branch through the package's gomock
`BeaconState`: one pinning that the source balance is restored, one
pinning that a failed rollback is reported through the wrapped error.
Both were mutation-checked — removing the rollback fails them on the
missing restore.
* https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/23577#discussion_r3861076329
— removing the two `defer`s in `EncodeAndWrite` made the comment at
`bucket_store.go` false and the `errWriter` shim dead: both flush errors
now reach the caller, so `w.err` was only reachable once
`EncodeAndWrite` had already returned the same error. Dropped the stale
comment, the shim and the now-unused type.
`TestBucketStoreWriteSurfacesAShortWriteFromTheFinalFlush` still passes,
since `bufio.Writer.Flush` raises `io.ErrShortWrite` itself.
* https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/23577#discussion_r3861076338
— `closePeer` had been inserted between `pruneExcessPeers`' doc comment
and its function, so the subnet wording attached to the wrong function.
Moved the doc back onto `pruneExcessPeers`; the wrapper is left
undocumented.

Thanks @awskii for all three.

author: Alex Sharov
subject: build, db, execution, cl, p2p, rpc, txnprovider: enable staticcheck (SA + S1) and fix what it found (#23652)
body:
`staticcheck` runs by default in golangci-lint v2, but a global `text:`
exclusion muted eight SA checks (`SA1019 SA6005 SA5011 SA4009 SA6002
SA9003 SA4006 SA4010`) and six S1 checks. So those never fired, and
three of the classes fixed here could have regressed unnoticed.

Drops the SA and S1 entries from that exclusion and fixes the 32
findings. `checks:` is golangci's default set less `SA1019` — naming
`SA*`/`S1*` directly would have silently dropped nine ST/QF checks that
were already enforced.

## Two real bugs

**`txnprovider/txpool`** — `OnNewBlock`'s deferred block advances
`lastSeenBlock` and broadcasts `lastSeenCond` when `err == nil`, but
five error paths return through a shadowed `err` (`if err := …; err !=
nil`), leaving the outer one nil. The pool advanced its view of chain
progress and woke waiters after failing to apply a block.

**`txnprovider/shutter`** — `readEonAtNewBlockEvent`'s deferred timing
trace tested a `var err error` that no failing path set: two returns
under `currentEon == nil` assign a shadowed `err`, and the
invalid-activation-block return builds its error inline. It logged
success timings for failed calls.

Both fixed with a named result, so every `return` sets what the defer
reads.

## Lint findings

- `db/seg/parallel_compress.go` — `compressWithPatternCandidates` did
`len(patternCode.word)` and then `if patternCode != nil`. `code2pattern`
only ever holds `&Pattern{}`, so the guard is dead code, not a live
crash; removed the guard rather than the deref.
- `rpc/jsonrpc/debug_api_test.go` — `t.Errorf("nil tx")` does not stop
the test, so the next line dereferenced `tx` anyway. Now `t.Fatalf`.
- `cl/beacon/handler/block_production.go` carried `//nolint:staticcheck
until <url>`, which golangci never applied — the reason needs a leading
`//`. It only looked like it worked because SA9003 was globally
excluded.

The rest are dead assignments, an `aaTxn` the only caller already
passes, a `break` that was the last statement of a `switch` case, and
the S1 simplifications (9 redundant nil-checks beside a `len`, 6
redundant `cap` args, 4 decl/assign merges, 1 single-case `select`, 1
struct conversion).

Also 18 `var err error` hoists scoped down to where they're used; three
of them were closures quietly writing an enclosing `err`.

## Check selection

`checks: [all, -ST1000, -ST1003, -ST1016, -ST1020, -ST1021, -ST1022,
-SA1019]` — golangci's own default minus `SA1019`, which waits on 42
deprecations. The noisy ST/QF checks stay muted by name in `exclusions`,
unchanged from before this PR.

Known gap: `exclusions.presets: legacy` (EXC0005) still mutes `SA4011`
repo-wide, so SA coverage is not total. It is clean today, but un-muting
means narrowing the legacy preset — separate change.

One suppression: `superStringsPool.Put` (SA6002). The superstring
crosses a channel, so the pool cannot hand back the same pointer, and
making it `*[]uint16` would put an indirection in the scan-loop append
to save one 24-byte box per 16MB superstring. Suppressed at the site so
SA6002 stays enforced elsewhere.

subject: all: upgrade minimum Go version to 1.26 (#23735)
body:
Raises the Go floor from 1.25 to 1.26 (because `go 1.27.1` released
today)

- `go.mod`: `go 1.25.7` -> `go 1.26.0` (no `go mod tidy` churn).

contributing doc.

alongside. Whole tree plus every test binary compiles under go1.26.8.

sub-analyzers on. Two are applied here, one commit each:
