author: Alex Sharov
subject: cl/network: make the slow-probe rotation test deterministic with synctest (#23857)
body:
## Problem

`TestForwardRequestMoreRotatesSlowP2PProbes` compressed the request
window to 300ms against a 210ms probe timeout. That left 90ms for two
probe rotations plus scheduling, and a loaded windows-2025 runner ended
the window first:

```
--- FAIL: TestForwardRequestMoreRotatesSlowP2PProbes (0.30s)
    beacon_downloader_test.go:367: request window ended before a healthy probe was processed
```

The failing assertion is not about the behaviour under test. Probe
rotation is genuinely time-based — probe timeout fires, attempt is
cancelled, a new one starts — but the request window is scaffolding, and
the test only passed while those two independent deadlines stayed far
enough apart in wall-clock terms.

## Fix

Run the test inside a `testing/synctest` bubble. The bubble's fake clock
only advances when every goroutine in it is durably blocked, so the
rotation and the window are ordered by construction rather than by how
fast the runner is.

That removes the tuning entirely:

- the four timing overrides are gone — the test now exercises the
**shipped** values (30s window, 21s probe timeout, 300ms interval),
which it never did before
- the two `time.After(time.Second)` guards are gone — a stalled bubble
deadlocks with a goroutine dump instead of hanging
- runtime is 0.00s

`NewBeaconRpcP2P` is constructed outside the bubble: it starts
background loops (an expirable-LRU janitor,
`columnDataPeers.refreshPeers`) that outlive any single request, and a
bubble may not end while goroutines are parked. Every deadline this test
exercises is created inside `RequestMore`, so nothing under test leaves
the bubble.

## Verification

- 50 sequential runs, 30 runs at `GOMAXPROCS=1` under 10 busy-spinning
cores, and `-race`: all pass
- still fails for the right reason — replacing the probe
`context.WithTimeout` with `context.WithCancel` (rotation disabled)
fails in 0.00s with the same message

No skip added.

author: Chase Wright
subject: chainspec, clparams: replace EF bootnodes with NodeOps fleet (#23894)
body:
I am on the Ethereum Foundation's Node Infrastructure team (NodeOps). We
run the bootnodes
that ship in this repository as the "EF" entries for mainnet, Sepolia
and Hoodi. We are
replacing that fleet, and we would like the new records in a release
before the Glamsterdam
client releases.

### What changes

- Add five new EF bootnodes per network. Every node serves all three
networks.
- Remove the legacy EF entries. The new set is a replacement, not an
addition.
- Third-party bootnodes and DNS discovery roots are untouched.

### The new fleet

Five bootnodes, each serving mainnet, Sepolia and Hoodi. They are
geographically distributed,
multi-cloud, and dual stack (IPv4 + IPv6). Each node runs discv4 and
discv5 on the EL port and
discv5 on the CL port, and the fleet spreads across several discovery
implementations so one
implementation bug cannot take the whole set down.

### About the records

- The ENRs are generic bootnode records: no `eth2` field, no `tcp`,
sequence number 1. Clients
dial configured bootnodes regardless of fork, and a static list cannot
be re-signed every
  fork, so we do not include fork data on purpose.
- Where an EL list accepts ENRs, we list the ENR. It covers discv4 and
discv5 and carries the
IPv6 endpoint. Enodes appear only where a list needs them, in the
discovery-only form
  `enode://<pubkey>@<ip>:0?discport=<port>` (no RLPx listener).
- The records are derived from the node keys and are byte-identical
across all the client
PRs. The canonical copies are the eth-clients PRs
(`metadata/bootstrap_nodes.yaml` and
  `metadata/enodes.yaml` for mainnet, sepolia and hoodi).

### Verification

- Each node answers discv4 and discv5 pings from the public internet on
the advertised ports.
- The relevant tests in this repository pass with the new lists (details
below).
- The legacy nodes stay online until client releases with the new
records are widely deployed.
  We will announce the shutdown separately.

### Contact

Chase Wright, EF Node Infrastructure. Discord `MysticRyuujin` (ETH R&D
and STEEL servers), or
chase.wright@ethereum.org.

### This repository

**Files:** `execution/chain/spec/bootnodes.go`, `cl/clparams/config.go`.

**Semantics:** `mainnetBootnodes` / `sepoliaBootnodes` /
`hoodiBootnodes` hold the five EL ENRs
per network (same reasoning as go-ethereum). `V5Bootnodes` swaps the
four EF CL ENRs for the
five mainnet EL ENRs. `sepoliaStaticPeers` loses the five EF entries;
the new nodes serve no
RLPx, so they are not static-peer candidates. Caplin's
`Mainnet/Sepolia/HoodiBootstrapNodes`
swap the EF CL ENRs (4 / 5 / 6) for the five new CL ENRs.

**Tests:** `go test ./execution/chain/spec/ ./cl/clparams/`.

author: Alex Sharov
subject: cl/validator/devvalidator: count the envelope post before queueing its body (#23910)
body:
Fixes a flake in
`TestGloasProposalRetriesSameEnvelopeWithoutRepublishingBlock`, which
failed the `-race` consensus shard on an unrelated PR:

```
--- FAIL: TestGloasProposalRetriesSameEnvelopeWithoutRepublishingBlock (0.52s)
    proposal_submission_test.go:143:
        Error: Not equal:
        expected: 2
        actual  : 1
```

## Cause

The envelope handler queued the body and only then incremented the
counter:

```go
envelopeBodies <- body
if envelopePosts.Add(1) == 1 {
```

`envelopeBodies` is buffered at 2, so the send never blocks. The test
drains both bodies and immediately asserts `envelopePosts.Load() == 2`,
but the assertion is ordered on the channel, not on the counter. The
second post can be received before the handler has counted it, which is
the observed 1.

Swapping the two lines makes the receive the test already waits on
happen after the increment.

## Verification

The window is narrow — 300 local `-race` runs of the unpatched test all
passed. Forcing it with a `runtime.Gosched()` between the two statements
reproduces CI exactly, failing on the first runs with the same
`expected: 2, actual: 1`. With the fix applied and that same `Gosched()`
still in place, 30 `-race` runs pass, as does the package.

TDD note: no new test. The existing test is the reproducer; the change
is to the fixture ordering it asserts on.

author: lystopad
subject: cl/phase1/network: read the blob count under the canonical root (#23895)
body:
`collectIncompleteBlocks` hashed the block it had just read to look up
how many sidecars the
blob store holds for it. `ReadBeaconBlockBodyBySlot` returns a block
**without its execution
payload** — the interface documents this — so that hash is a root which
never existed on chain
and the lookup always misses, reporting zero.

Every Deneb+ block carrying commitments was therefore treated as
incomplete no matter what the
store actually held. The backfill re-requested data it already had, and
on an archive node it
walked back toward the Deneb fork spending the 30s per-block column
timeout on sidecars long
past the retention window. Since the blob dump is gated on that pass
completing
(`antiquary.go`: `if !a.blobBackfilled.Load() { continue }`), the blob
frontier could not
advance at all.

This fix reads the root from the canonical index instead, and skips a
slot with no canonical
root rather than probing the store with a zero key.

Related: #23224 is the wedge this produces — `blob storage count
mismatch at slot 29403906`
retried every 12s forever. That is one of the slots repaired while
validating this fix, and the
frontier advanced afterwards. #23752 is a separate reason blob backfill
cannot converge.

## Evidence

Found on a gnosis archive node whose blob frontier had been stuck at
slot 29,400,000 for about
30 days while beacon blocks reached 29,969,999. One 10,000-slot chunk
was repaired and
independently verified: 251 blob-bearing slots present, each confirmed
by reading the sidecars
back and re-checking the count row. This code still classified all 251
as incomplete. The
goroutine stack showed the pass parked in
`peerdas.DownloadColumnsAndRecoverBlobs` on a
`WaitGroup`, chasing columns no peer retains.

## Measured effect

Validated on the same node, after repairing its blob store out-of-band
so the store genuinely
held the data:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| backward pass | 1.2 slots/sec, never completed across three restarts |
**finished in 39 s** |
| blob dump | gated out, never ran | started 2 s later, completed in
15m25s |
| blob frontier | stuck at 29,400,000 for ~30 days | **29,400,000 ->
29,960,000** |

Before the fix the pass spent the 30s per-block column timeout on slots
whose sidecars were
already stored, so it never reached the end and `blobBackfilled` was
never set. The dump is gated
on that flag, which is why the frontier could not move at all.

## How to tell if a node is affected

`frozen_blobs` should track `frozen_blocks` at roughly the same height;
a persistent and growing
divergence is the symptom. Equivalently `[Caplin] Stat blobs-static=...
blocks-static=...` in the
logs. On the node above the two were 29,400,000 and 29,969,999.

## Tests

`TestCollectIncompleteBlocksSkipsSlotsCompleteUnderTheCanonicalRoot`
keeps the indexed root
distinct from the block's own hash, as a stripped read does, and asserts
a slot already complete
in the store is not queued. Mutation-verified: restoring `HashSSZ()`
fails it.

My first version of that test passed under mutation, because the fixture
seeded the canonical
root *as* the block's hash and the two roots were identical — worth
knowing if you review the
fixture. `newBoundaryDownloader` now seeds the index from the blocks its
reader serves, since a
downloader without an index sees every slot as a gap.

Whole package green, `make lint` clean.

## Deliberately not in this PR

Three sites in this file (`retryBlock`, `recoverDenebBlobs`,
`recoverFuluColumns`) hash a
stripped block the same way and feed the result to
`storedBlobSidecarsComplete`, so a
successfully stored slot is re-queued forever. Fixing those needs the
root carried alongside the
block rather than re-derived per call — a per-block read-only
transaction in those loops is the
wrong shape, and it changes signatures several tests call directly.

`BlobsIdentifiersFromBlocks` (`blobs.go:50`) also hashes the block, and
those identifiers go on
the wire, so peers are asked for a root that never existed. Its only
other caller is
`cmd/capcli`, which passes full blocks where the hash is correct, so
that one cannot simply be
changed here.

Both are tracked in #23896. This PR is the one change validated against
a live node.

author: lystopad
subject: cl, cmd/capcli: fail the chain download when blobs are not fully stored (#23868)
body:
Replaces #23623, which targeted code that #23138 has since rewritten.
Same defect, correct
target, fresh base.

## The defect

`VerifyAgainstIdentifiersAndInsertIntoTheBlobStore` stops at the first
identifier a response
does not match and returns a **nil error** with a partial count. Its
only remaining production
caller discarded both counts:

```go
if _, _, err := blob_storage.VerifyAgainstIdentifiersAndInsertIntoTheBlobStore(
    ctx, blobDB, ids, blobs, ...); err != nil {
```

So a block whose blobs stored partially — or not at all — was reported
as downloaded. The chain
endpoint moved on to the parent, leaving a gap nothing later notices.

## Change

- check the stored count against the request and fail with both numbers
plus the response count
- document the contract on the insert itself, since that count is the
only completeness signal
  it gives a caller
- extract `storeRemoteBlobs` so the check is reachable from a test

## Why not #23623

#23623 put the same check in `BlobHistoryDownloader.storeDenebBlobs`.
#23138 replaced that whole
path with `denebRecoveryBatch`, which handles it more thoroughly than a
warning would: `validate`
returns errors for unrequested, duplicate and empty responses instead of
breaking silently,
`store` writes a group only when complete, and `recoverDenebBlobs`
re-checks each block with
`storedBlobSidecarsComplete` and calls `addRetrySlot` on a shortfall.
The backfill no longer
calls the insert at all, so that half of #23623 is obsolete — and its
test targeted a function
that no longer exists.

What #23138 did not change is the insert's contract or the capcli
caller, which is what this
picks up.

## Tests

`TestStoreRemoteBlobsRejectsAnIncompleteInsert` drives a sidecar whose
header hashes to a
different root, so the insert breaks on the first identifier, stores
nothing and returns nil.
`TestStoreRemoteBlobsRejectsAnEmptyResponse` covers the empty-response
path to the same end.

Mutation-verified rather than assumed: disabling the count comparison
fails both.

`cmd/capcli`, `cl/persistence/blob_storage` and `cl/phase1/network`
pass; `make lint` clean.

author: lystopad
subject: cl/persistence/blob_storage: validate the stored inclusion proof shape (#23934)
body:
Found while addressing @domiwei's review on #23923; the same defect is
on `main`, reached through the Gloas gate that #23868 added.

Skipping the inclusion-proof check from Gloas on also skipped any check
that the proof vector has the length the reader expects.
`WriteBlobSidecars` encodes a short vector happily, but
`ReadBlobSidecars` always constructs a fixed-length proof schema and
rejects the shorter encoding. A response carrying an explicit
`"kzg_commitment_inclusion_proof": []` therefore **replaces a previously
readable sidecar with a file nothing can decode, and reports no error**.
The count row still says the blobs are there.

Measured on this branch before the fix:
`VerifyAgainstIdentifiersAndInsertIntoTheBlobStore` returns `err=nil,
inserted=1`, and the following `ReadBlobSidecars` returns `found=false`
where it returned the sidecar a moment earlier. The beacon transaction
that records the count is separate, so nothing rolls the replacement
back.

The gate appears at two sites and both needed it:

- `VerifyAgainstIdentifiersAndInsertIntoTheBlobStore` — the insert path.
- `VerifyBlobSidecars` — the shared verifier. `cl/das/peer_das.go`
passes a version that can be Gloas and writes once verification
succeeds, so fixing only the first would have left the same path open.

Whether the proof's *contents* are meaningful is fork-dependent; whether
the sidecar is encodable in the shape the reader expects is not. The
length is now checked for every version, before anything is written.

Pinned by
`TestVerifyAgainstIdentifiersRejectsAShortProofWithoutLosingStoredData`,
which asserts both the rejection and that the existing sidecar stays
readable, and by an added case in
`TestVerifyBlobSidecarsGloasDoesNotRequireInclusionProof`. Removing
either check fails its test.

`make lint` clean; `cl/persistence/blob_storage`, `cl/das`,
`cl/phase1/network` and `cmd/capcli` pass.

author: lystopad
subject: cl/phase1/network: require file availability before skipping an archive slot (#23930)
body:
Forward-port of a fix made on `release/3.6` while backporting #23895
(see #23922). `release/3.6` was
the only branch carrying it, which @awskii spotted — `git log --all -S
storedSidecarsAvailable` found
one commit, on that branch alone.

Pruning drops sidecar files but leaves their `BlockRootToKzgCommitments`
rows. A datadir pruned as
non-archive and later reopened with `--caplin.blobs-archive` therefore
carries counts that no file
backs. `collectIncompleteBlocks` finds the stale count, matches it
against the block's commitments
and skips the slot, so the pass can report completion and move
`nextBackfillTargetSlot` past work an
archive node still owes.

This only became reachable with #23895: the earlier payload-stripped
hash missed every count and
queued those slots by accident. Fixing the root removed that accident.

## The check

On an archive node, a count-equal slot is only skipped once **every**
sidecar index up to the
commitment count is backed by a file; the first miss re-queues the
block. Two deliberate choices:

- **a stat, not a read-back** — no KZG work is added;
`TestBlobHistoryDownloaderDoesNotDeepVerifyCountEqualStorage` still
passes with `verifyCalls == 0`.
- **gated on `archiveBlobs`** — a non-archive node prunes on purpose and
must not re-queue what it
  deliberately dropped.

An earlier revision probed index 0 only, reasoning that pruning removes
whole bucket directories so
absence is all-or-nothing. That holds for pruning but not for a rewrite
that publishes index 0 and
then fails, which leaves the count row whole with only part of the data
on disk. @domiwei caught
that on #23922; the loop is the fix.

## Tests

`release/3.6` pins the non-archive direction with
`TestBlobHistoryDownloaderDoesNotRetryIntentionallyPrunedFiles`; this
branch has no such test, so the
gate would have been unpinned here. All three directions are pinned:

- `TestCollectIncompleteBlocksQueuesArchiveSlotsWhoseFilesWerePruned` —
archive node, stale row,
  pruned file, block stays queued
-
`TestCollectIncompleteBlocksQueuesArchiveSlotsMissingALaterSidecarFile`
— two sidecars written,
index 1's file removed, leaving `count=2, index0=true, index1=false`;
the block stays queued
- `TestCollectIncompleteBlocksLeavesPrunedNonArchiveSlotsAlone` — same
state, non-archive, left alone

Mutation-verified in all three directions: dropping the availability
check fails the first, reverting
the loop to probe index 0 only fails the second, and dropping the
`archiveBlobs` gate fails the
third.

`TestCollectIncompleteBlocksSkipsSlotsCompleteUnderTheCanonicalRoot`
pins the probe to the canonical
root and slot rather than `gomock.Any()`, so regressing it to the
block's own hash or a wrong slot
fails the test — verified by changing the production call to `slot+1`.

The mock declaration is one helper called at the seven tests that can
actually reach the check — it
runs only when `archiveBlobs` is set, the count matches and the block
carries commitments, so
hand-built downloaders and tests whose count lookup errors never get
there.

`make lint` clean, `cl/phase1/network` green.

`release/3.5` carries the same fix in #23932.

author: lystopad
subject: cl/persistence/blob_storage: validate sidecar structure before dereferencing it (#23938)
body:
Follow-up to #23934, which is already merged. Found by @awskii reviewing
the same change on #23923 — the fix I added there introduced a panic
where the code it replaced returned an error.

The shape check calls `sidecar.CommitmentInclusionProof.Length()` on a
`solid.HashVectorSSZ` interface field without checking for nil. A JSON
`null` leaves that field nil:

- `BlobSidecar.UnmarshalJSON` pre-fills `tmp.CommitmentInclusionProof`
with `NewHashVector(17)`.
- For `null`, encoding/json does not descend into that pointer and calls
`SetZero()` on the interface instead.
- So `"kzg_commitment_inclusion_proof": null` yields a nil proof, while
`[]` yields a zero-length one.

Measured both, rather than reasoning about encoding/json's behaviour:
`null` → `nil == true`, `[]` → `nil == false`.

**This is a regression #23934 introduced.** Previously the unconditional
`VerifyCommitmentInclusionProof` handled it — it guards
`commitmentInclusionProof == nil` and returns false
(cl/cltypes/blob_sidecar.go:154) — so the caller got a clean "could not
verify blob's inclusion proof". Now it panics.

Reachable through `capcli chain --blobs` →
`retrieveBlobsFromRemoteEndpoint` (JSON decode) → `storeRemoteBlobs`,
which checks only the nil sidecar, index and commitment. A response
repeating the block's real header, index and commitment passes the root
and index matches, then panics. It happens on every fork, because the
length check runs before the version gate.

Severity is a tooling crash, not a node halt: the only production caller
of the insert path is capcli, and the input is a malformed response from
an endpoint the operator chose. The `VerifyBlobSidecars` copy has the
same unguarded call; its callers do not take sidecars from JSON, so it
is not reachable with nil today — guarded anyway, since the two sites
should not disagree.

Both sites now check nil first, matching `blob_sidecar.go:154`. Pinned
by a nil-proof case next to the existing `NewHashVector(0)` one;
removing the guards panics the test.

`make lint` clean; `cl/persistence/blob_storage`, `cl/das` and
`cmd/capcli` pass.

## Second guard: the nested header (`d42a9381c5`)

Raised by Copilot on #23923, and the same defect I filed as #23907 on
2026-09-10.

`VerifyAgainstIdentifiersAndInsertIntoTheBlobStore` dereferences the
nested header twice before
validating anything — once to seed `lastProcessed` ahead of the loop,
once to hash inside it — so a
response that decodes with `signed_block_header` or its `header` absent
panics. `VerifyBlobSidecars`
has guarded exactly this all along; the insert path never did.

The pre-loop read is the one that bites first, so a check placed inside
the loop would not help. The
guard therefore runs over the whole slice before the first dereference,
reusing the existing
"blob response contains incomplete sidecar" wording.

Unlike the nil-proof guard above, this one is **not** a regression from
#23934 — it predates that
change and is present on `main`, `release/3.6` and `release/3.5` alike.
It is fixed here because the
surrounding validation is already being corrected, and leaving one field
guarded and the next not is
how the next reader gets caught.

Pinned by `TestVerifyAgainstIdentifiersRejectsAnIncompleteHeader`,
covering both a nil
`SignedBlockHeader` and a non-nil header struct with a nil `Header`.

Closes #23907.

---------

Co-authored-by: Alex Sharov <AskAlexSharov@gmail.com>

author: Alex Sharov
subject: cl/phase1/network, execution/execmodule: stop two tests racing the Windows clock (#23944)
body:
Fixes both failures in `tests / tests-mac-linux (windows-2025, serial)`,
seen on
https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/actions/runs/34673097118/job/103499473721.
Neither is caused by the PR that surfaced them, and both are specific to
Windows: every other arm of that matrix passed, including `ubuntu-24.04,
serial`, which runs the same commitment path.

## `TestForwardRequestMoreEmptyP2PDoesNotInvalidateHTTPFallback`

```
beacon_downloader_test.go:625: Not equal: expected: 1, actual: 0
    valid HTTP fallback was discarded after an empty P2P response
```

The test sequences itself on two channels. The HTTP handler signals
`fallbackStarted` and then blocks until the test calls `release()`. In
between, the test asserts on the cursor. It also capped
`forwardBeaconRequestTimeout` at 100ms, which is a second clock running
against that handshake. When the runner is loaded enough that more than
100ms passes before `release()`, the request context expires, the
fallback blocks are discarded and the process function is never called.

Reproduced exactly by sleeping 150ms before `release()` on an otherwise
unmodified tree: same line, same message, same expected and actual.

The test already bounds itself with its own one-second guards on
`fallbackStarted` and on `RequestMore` returning, so it does not need
the cap. Dropping the override lets the production default apply and the
handshake decide the sequence.

Verified by keeping the 150ms sleep in place, which now passes, then
removing it and running the `TestForwardRequestMore` family 20 times.

## `TestSlowBlockMetricsAreEmittedForValidatedBlocks`

```
block_metrics_test.go:185: Should be true
    state_hash_ms was zero in every record — commitment timing is not reaching the emitter
```

The assertion needed a measured commitment duration to be positive.
Commitment over a test-sized block takes about 0.1ms, so the result
depends on the clock resolution of the runner, and on `windows-2025,
serial` it reads zero. The check races the clock.

It is replaced by two tests that do not read the clock:

- `TestComputeCommitmentReportsItsDuration` in
`execution/commitment/commitmentdb`: `ComputeCommitment` calls
`AddCommitmentTime` exactly once. It counts calls, not durations.
- `TestRecordBlockMetricsTakesCommitmentTimeFromSharedDomains` in
`execution/execmodule`: with 5ms of commitment time in `SharedDomains`
and a 12ms exec stage, the record gets `StateHash` 5ms and `Execution`
7ms, and the commitment time is drained.

For the second test, `recordBlockMetrics` now takes the exec stage
duration as a parameter instead of reading it from the executor. No
behavior change.

Each new test fails when its wiring is removed: deleting the
`AddCommitmentTime(took)` call fails the first, dropping `StateHash`
from the `Record` literal fails the second.

All other checks in `TestSlowBlockMetricsAreEmittedForValidatedBlocks`
are unchanged.

Not covered without the clock: moving the discarding
`TakeCommitmentTime()` in `validateAndStorePayload` after
`ValidateBlock`.

## Notes

`make lint` reports one gofmt issue in
`db/snapshotsync/snapshots_test.go`. It exists on `main`, and this PR
does not touch the file.

TDD: for the beacon test the reproduction came first and the fix was
verified against it. The execmodule test drove the `recordBlockMetrics`
signature change (red on compile, then green). The commitmentdb test
covers existing behavior, so it was checked by mutation instead.

author: Andrew Ashikhmin
subject: cl/services: harden shared pending-job queue (#23644)
body:
Hardens Caplin's shared pending-job queue for execution-payload
envelopes and payload attestations.

- Enforces capacity with CAS reservations, including in-flight enqueues,
and releases reservations after key-construction errors or panics.
- Uses coalesced wakeups, cancellation checks, and identity-checked
removal. Expiry and post-removal callbacks run after deletion and may
enqueue a replacement.
- Validates queue options, reports admission errors, and counts failed
capacity reservations per queue. Attestation hash errors are returned
instead of ignored.

Service capacities, expiry windows, retry cadence, signed-message
identity, and envelope byte accounting are preserved. Failed gossip
admission returns `IGNORE` without claiming the message was queued. The
queue loop can be stopped and joined for deterministic test cleanup.

Execution-payload bids and REST handlers are unchanged. Beacon blocks
and data-column sidecars are outside this PR; #23646 and #23645 cover
them.

Validation covers queue admission, deduplication, expiry, wakeups,
cancellation, and service integration, including race tests. TDD is
skipped for pure refactors and test-only coverage of existing behavior.

---------

Co-authored-by: Alex Sharov <AskAlexSharov@gmail.com>

author: Kewei
subject: cl: harden Gloas envelope persistence and ingestion (#23152)
body:
## Summary

- replace Gloas envelope files through a temporary file and atomic
rename so failed or concurrent replacements cannot expose partial data
- record and validate the supported envelope fork version in the file,
P2P, and gossip representations; require the standard envelope version
and blob-data HTTP headers
- reuse the fork graph SSZ buffer while detaching transaction bytes that
alias decoder input
- keep `HasEnvelope` on its cache-only hot path; only successful writes
and validated reads promote the cache
- serialize envelope reads, writes, and pruning so stale writers cannot
restore pruned envelopes
- retain structurally invalid files for diagnosis while marking them
unusable in memory; transient I/O failures remain retryable
- validate Gloas envelopes across gossip, RPC, HTTP, checkpoint, block
production, and persistence boundaries before promotion or publication
- bind forward, backward, and recovered P2P envelopes to the canonical
block and signed bid before satisfying roots, suppressing fallback, or
advancing progress
- allow bid and payload fee recipients to differ while retaining payload
integrity through the recomputed block hash
- keep progressive deposits semantically unbounded behind a resource
guard while enforcing the four protocol-limited execution-request lists
- strictly decode parent execution requests and execution payload bids
carried by block gossip
- reject invalid self-build envelopes before gossip while preserving
queued and post-persistence index-repair outcomes
- keep local persistence and index-repair failures separate from gossip
validation outcomes, and start blob backfill independently of envelope
recovery completion
- enforce persisted envelope/block-root identity, reject decompressed
RPC chunks above the 15 MiB transport bound before decoding, and
validate matching nested versions, collection bounds, and complete
nested representations
- bound JSON list and transaction materialization before allocation,
require list decoders to be explicitly configured, reject trailing JSON
values, and retain validated P2P response prefixes on a malformed suffix
- bound prune lock hold time per root and remove envelope files after
invalidating their in-memory lineage
- retain bounded best-effort post-persistence index repair without
allowing stale retries to overwrite newer indices or gating primary
envelope persistence
- keep skipped-FULL recovery bounded while releasing stage readiness,
and retry chain-tip blocks whose parent envelope is only temporarily
unavailable
- preserve blob-backfill completeness transitions for late or replaced
subscribers without invoking callbacks under the downloader lock or
losing concurrent updates
- validate blob-inclusive REST envelopes for config, persistence size,
and canonical block commitments before KZG expansion or column writes;
keep the contents SSZ size contract exact
- construct locally produced Gloas data-column sidecars with progressive
cell/proof lists so their roots match decoded sidecars
- use the first slot of the finalized epoch for the Gloas gossip cutoff,
matching the specification's finalized-epoch boundary

## Production scope

Caplin creates the fork-choice filesystem under
`dirs.Tmp/caplin-forkchoice` and clears it before constructing the fork
graph on every process start. This PR therefore provides intra-process
atomicity, ownership safety, and prune ordering; it intentionally does
not claim crash durability or startup recovery. Directory fsync,
quarantine files, startup scavenging, and
committed-with-durability-warning handling are outside the real
lifecycle and are not included.

Beacon-state persistence remains unchanged. It has a different file
format and lifecycle and should be hardened separately rather than
expanding this envelope-focused change.

The bounded in-memory envelope-index repair tracker is best-effort. When
it is saturated, primary envelope persistence remains non-gating and
auxiliary index recovery falls back to the existing pending/redelivery
path. A durable overflow journal or startup reconciliation mechanism
remains outside this PR.

## Root cause

Envelope writes truncated the final file in place, so a failed
replacement could destroy the previously readable envelope and a
concurrent reader could observe partial data. Reads decoded transaction
slices from the fork graph reusable SSZ buffer, allowing a later read or
write to mutate an envelope already returned to a caller. Pruning also
removed envelope files without coordinating with writers, allowing a
concurrent rename to restore a pruned file.

Envelope validation was also inconsistent across ingress paths.
Canonical SSZ, configured resource bounds, progressive request
semantics, JSON allocation limits, partial P2P progress, canonical block
and bid commitments, and self-build publication errors were not
uniformly enforced before decoded envelopes or parent execution requests
reached hashing, caching, forkchoice, or gossip.

## Validation

- all `cl/...` short-test packages passed; packages affected by local
linker disk exhaustion were rerun with `-p=2`
- affected CL packages: `cl/cltypes`, `cl/cltypes/solid`,
`cl/beacon/handler`, `cl/phase1/network/services`, `cl/phase1/network`,
`cl/phase1/stages`, `cl/phase1/core/checkpoint_sync`,
`cl/phase1/forkchoice`, `cl/phase1/forkchoice/fork_graph`, and `cl/rpc`
- focused `go test -race` for network services, RPC/network partial
responses, fork-choice index repair, JSON decoding, blob-recovery
lifecycle, and fork-graph envelope persistence
- two clean `make lint` scans on the final scoped head
- `make erigon integration`

The behavior changes were driven Red to Green through public handler,
network-service, RPC, forkchoice, stage, and fork-graph methods.
Regressions cover destructive replacement failures, shared-buffer
mutation, prune/write resurrection, unrelated I/O during multi-root
pruning, cache misses waiting on state I/O, transient open/read failures
preserving trusted availability, structural corruption evicting warm
cache, supported-version loss, nested-version mismatch, null list
members before hashing, protocol-versus-decoder bounds, progressive
deposits beyond the legacy Electra limit, alternate collection
representations before persistence, root/file identity mismatch,
oversized allocation and HTTP/P2P responses, malformed nested offsets,
bounded JSON decoding, trailing JSON values, mixed-validity P2P response
prefixes, invalid self-build publication, queued `ErrIgnore` behavior,
post-persistence index repair, bounded blob-recovery retries,
parent-envelope redelivery, blob-content prevalidation, and
failed-removal cache exposure.

author: Alex Sharov
subject: cl: stop two more tests racing the Windows clock (#24000)
body:
problem: two tests race the clock on `windows-2025, serial`: a
test-sized block runs faster than the clock resolution, and 39 slow
builder calls can overrun a 500ms wall-clock bound.

`block_metrics_test.go:163: "0" is not positive`,
`builder_preferences_test.go:224: "511.9391ms" is not less than "500ms"`

Solution: check block metrics against the exec stage timing instead of
requiring positive durations; prove builder concurrency with an
in-flight barrier instead of a deadline.

author: awskii
subject: cl/transition: restore parallel rewards and inactivity epoch loops (#23966)
body:
#13007 set every epoch-processing `ParallellForLoop` to one worker. The
inactivity and rewards loops write only their own validator's score or
balance, and dirty-leaf marking is atomic, so they go back to
`runtime.NumCPU()` workers. On an epoch's first block `ProcessEpoch`
runs twice: on the gossip-validation copy, and again inside `OnBlock`.

| p50 ms | without | with |
|---|---|---|
| inactivity scores | 6.09 | 0.92 |
| rewards and penalties | 38.19 | 30.45 |
| registry updates (unchanged) | 33.11 | 33.30 |
| `ProcessEpoch` total | 153.98 | 143.02 |
| `OnBlock`, epoch-first slot | 280.92 | 265.63 |

Mainnet archive node on an AMD EPYC 4344P (16 threads), same flags,
2026-09-14. Epoch gauges sampled every 10 s: 18 samples without, 78
with. `OnBlock` from the debug log over 37 and 75 epoch-first blocks;
other slots, which skip epoch processing, moved 88.27 → 92.11 ms over
the same windows.

## Changes
- `ProcessInactivityScores`, `processRewardsAndPenaltiesPostAltair`:
`ParallellForLoop(1, …)` → `ParallellForLoop(runtime.NumCPU(), …)`.
- `runEpochTransitionConsensusTest` hashes the state before the pass, as
a node does, so `-race` covers the rewards loop's concurrent dirty-leaf
marking.

Left out: registry updates (exit churn is order-dependent), slashings
(7.19 → 6.43 ms in a benchmark, for 14× the CPU), and the
`MarkLeafAsDirty` reader lock, which takes 73% of the parallel rewards
loop's CPU.

author: awskii
subject: build, cl/spectest: compile and test with GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2 (#24017)
body:
A median `engine_newPayloadV5` request in the benchmark window below is
1.19 MB, almost all of it block access list hex, and the RPC server
spends 8.2 ms on it before `Handling new payload`, mostly in
`encoding/json` validating and decoding that string. Built with
`GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2`, `encoding/json` runs on the `encoding/json/v2`
implementation with no code changes. Go 1.27 makes this the default:
"Marshaling and unmarshaling behavior is preserved, but the exact text
of error messages may differ."

## Changes
- `Makefile`: `export GOEXPERIMENT ?= jsonv2`, so every `make` target,
including `make docker`, builds and tests with it. Setting
`GOEXPERIMENT` in the environment overrides it.
- `cl/spectest/Makefile`: the same line. It runs `go test` itself,
without reading the root Makefile, for the Caplin spec-test workflow.

## Notes
benchmarkoor replay of the 100 jochemnet blocks from 24410421 on an AMD
EPYC 4344P (erigon on 8 CPUs). `25ac06305d90` built with and without the
flag, three interleaved runs per arm after a warm-up:

| | request sent → `Handling new payload`, p50 | `newPayload` p50,
blocks under 200 ms | execution p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `25ac06305d90` | 8.16–8.26 ms | 11.86–12.00 ms | 3.39–3.52 ms |
| `GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2` | 3.02–3.34 ms | 7.02–7.11 ms | 3.49–3.55 ms |

Blocks over 200 ms stay within run-to-run spread. `go build` outside
`make` keeps the old implementation, as do the sonar, test-bench and
test-fuzz workflows, which call `go test` directly.

author: Alex Sharov
subject: execution/engineapi: switch `baseFeePerGas` and `blockValue` to `hexutil.U256` (#24016)
body:
problem: the Engine API types carry `baseFeePerGas` and `blockValue` as
`*hexutil.Big`, so newPayload and getPayload convert `uint256` ->
`big.Int` -> `uint256` for every payload.

Solution: carry them as `*hexutil.U256`. The JSON is byte-identical and
`hexutil.U256` accepts and rejects the same inputs as `hexutil.Big`;
only the Go type name in decode error messages changes.
`TransitionConfiguration` had no users and is removed.

n1, getPayload response with 16 transactions, 6 runs: decode 35 -> 33
allocs, encode 40 -> 36 allocs; time within noise.

author: Kewei
subject: db/integrity: validate frozen blob sidecar snapshots (#23927)
body:
## Summary

- add `CaplinBlobSidecars` as an explicit slow check under `erigon
snapshots integrity`
- validate required frozen blob coverage and the word/index geometry of
visible blob and paired beacon segments
- validate canonical block identity, stored body-root linkage, sidecar
count/order/identity, direct block-commitment equality, commitment
inclusion proofs, and KZG proofs
- use the Caplin indexing DB for canonical beacon roots and return a
non-zero error for missing or invalid data even when `--failFast=false`

Run it with:

```console
erigon snapshots integrity --datadir <path> --check=CaplinBlobSidecars
```

## Scope

This is the at-rest frozen snapshot verifier from #23911. It
intentionally does not implement peer repair, atomic segment
replacement, or the publication/seeding gate yet, so it does not close
#23911.

#23918 fixes the separate `capcli blob-archive-store-check` preflight
for the mutable blob archive store. The two checks are complementary:
that command checks archive-store counts before freezing, while this PR
checks the resulting `.seg/.idx` snapshots semantically. Peer recovery
remains dependent on the canonical-root work tracked by #23896.

## Review feedback addressed

- pass the Caplin indexing DB and already-resolved beacon config to the
checker; close the associated resources in dependency order
- remove the unreachable silent-skip and duplicate config lookup
- validate segment word count plus index presence, key count, base data
ID, and ordinal offsets before slot traversal
- compare every sidecar commitment directly with the beacon block
commitment, including Gloas
- make the non-canonical sidecar test reach the intended sidecar-root
branch
- cover extra sidecars at empty slots and invalid commitment inclusion
proofs
- verify stored pre-Gloas blinded and Gloas full body roots before using
their commitment lists

## Validation

- `go test ./cl/persistence/format/snapshot_format
./db/snapshotsync/freezeblocks ./db/integrity ./cmd/utils/app -count=1`
- `make lint` (two clean runs)
- `make erigon integration`
- `git diff --check`

Focused tests cover complete and missing sidecars, wrong
count/index/root/header signature, invalid KZG and inclusion proofs,
extra sidecars at empty slots, malformed records, missing indexes and
ranges, segment cardinality, canonical block availability, non-empty
Deneb payloads, Fulu sidecars, and Gloas commitment/body-root
mismatches.

author: Kewei
subject: cl: harden execution payload envelope admission (#24039)
body:
## Summary

- reject envelope builder mismatches before admission or persisted reads
at REST and gossip ingress, including header-only checkpoint anchors
using the anchor state bid identity
- bound same-identity admission waiters and use nonblocking admission
attempts for queued retries, with identity-scoped pacing for unavailable
persisted lookups
- preserve the prior ability to redeliver after degraded persistence
while emitting the validated envelope, and revalidate pending indices
before acceptance
- move copied-state and signature gossip validation off the exclusive
forkchoice lock and bound concurrent validation
- preserve REST duplicate response policy and recover admission after
stale or incomplete persisted markers

## Scope

This is the ingress/admission slice only. It does not change
execution-request limits, HTTP duplicate policy, or index-repair event
metadata.

## Validation

- bug fixes driven by focused failing tests, including P2P-to-REST,
pending-worker stale-marker handoff, and header-only anchor admission
- `make lint` repeated to clean results
- `make erigon integration`
- `go test ./cl/beacon/handler ./cl/phase1/forkchoice
./cl/phase1/network/services -count=1`
- focused stress and race tests for admission, pending retry,
finalization, lock cleanup, duplicate policy, and stale persisted
recovery

author: lystopad
subject: cl: request blobs under the canonical root, and put the block signature on ColumnSyncableSignedBlock (#24053)
body:
Fixes #23896.

`ReadBeaconBlockBodyBySlot` decodes blocks **without their execution
payload** — its doc says so, and
both branches end at the same decoder, the database path (`slot >
BlocksAvailable()`) as well as the
segment path. Hashing the result yields a root that never existed on
chain, and peers index data
columns and blob sidecars by the real root, so every by-root request the
blob backfill made matched
nothing and ran to its timeout.

The effect is that **`BlobHistoryDownloader` never recovered anything**.
Blobs were present only where
live gossip had already caught them; a slot that missed live recovery
stayed empty forever and the
archive dump wedged behind it.

## 1. Carry the canonical root

`collectIncompleteBlocks` already reads the canonical root from the
index for its store lookup and
then discards it. It now carries it as `incompleteBlock{block, root}`.

- **Fulu** — the block is wrapped in a `rootedColumnBlock` overriding
`BlockHashSSZ()`.
- **Deneb** — `blobsIdentifiersFromRootedBlocks` builds by-root
identifiers from the supplied roots.
The exported `BlobsIdentifiersFromBlocks` is unchanged: its one
production caller,
`cmd/capcli/blob_store.go`, works on a remotely fetched block that still
has its payload, so its
  self-hash *is* the real root.

Three further sites derived the root by hashing and needed threading
too, or the fix would have been
half-applied: `newDenebRecoveryBatch` keyed its group map on the
self-hash (so identifiers could never
have matched), and `retryBlock`/`readRetryBlock` re-hashed on the retry
path.

## 2. Put the block signature on `ColumnSyncableSignedBlock`

Found in review by @awskii and Copilot. This is why the PR touches
`cl/das` and `cl/cltypes`.

`newBlobRecoveryMetadata` read the proposer signature with a **type
switch on the two concrete block
types**. A wrapper matches neither, so `hasSignature` stayed false — and
both comparisons guarding on
it were written `metadata.hasSignature && …`, so both short-circuited to
accept:

- `peer_das.go:1566`, which rejects **and bans** a peer whose
column-sidecar header signature does not
  match the block
- `peer_das.go:342`, in `validateStoredBlobRecoveryMetadata`

A peer could then answer a Fulu backfill request with an authentic
header, valid cells and proofs and
an arbitrary signature: accepted, persisted, and copied verbatim into
the reconstructed sidecars.
Nothing downstream covers it — `resolveColumnSidecarSlotAndRoot` binds
the header to the requested
root by `HashSSZ` only, and `VerifyBlobSidecars` is called with a nil
header-verification func.

It mattered **because** part 1 works: before it, that path asked for a
root no peer had, so the check
protected nothing in practice.

`BlockSignature()` is on the interface now — both implementers already
had the field — and the type
switch is gone, so a wrapper cannot drop the check.

## 3. Remove `hasSignature`

With the type switch gone the field was set true at the only
construction site, making both readers
always-true conjuncts and the two assertions on it checks against a
constant. Removing it leaves the
signature comparison unconditional, which is what moving the accessor
onto the interface guarantees.

## Also from review

- `blobsIdentifiersFromRootedBlocks` is unexported — `incompleteBlock`
is unexported, so nothing
  outside the package could construct the argument.
- The displaced doc comment is back above `BlobsIdentifiersFromBlocks`;
the rooted variant has its own.
- A retry slot with no canonical row is logged rather than skipped
silently. It is reachable only from
the segment path, is never trimmed (`trimRetryRanges` drops only frozen
slots), and would otherwise
  hold the backfill incomplete forever with no output naming the cause.

## Measured on a live gnosis archive node

**Before**, 12 hours at `caplin_peer_count` 127:

| | |
|---|---|
| backfill recovery attempts | 843 |
| failed with `context deadline exceeded` | **842** |
| unique slots affected | 202, retried up to 6× each |
| live gossip recoveries (`blobsRecover`) | 131 |
| overlap between the two sets | **0** |

Disjoint: a slot was either caught live or never recovered at all.

**After**, same node and datadir:

```
DownloadColumnsAndRecoverBlobs elapsed=1.247s   slots=[30104691]
[blobsRecover] recovering done slot=30104691 numberOfBlobs=1 elapsedTime=100ms
```

`elapsed` went from a flat 30.000 s to **~0.97 s**, and `[blobsRecover]
recovering done` accompanied a
backfill target for the first time. The 30 s was never work; it was
waiting for peers to answer a
request for a root that does not exist.

Twenty minutes later every sampled slot from the failing set was served
and the frontier had unwedged:

```
frozen_blobs  30,060,000 -> 30,080,000
frozen_blocks               30,089,999
gap                              9,999   (the structural resting value)
```

That run used the `release/3.6` backport of part 1, before parts 2 and 3
existed.

## Tests

- `TestRecoverFuluColumnsRequestsTheCanonicalRoot`,
`TestBlobsIdentifiersUseTheSuppliedRoot` — the
request carries the canonical root, using a fixture where it differs
from the block's own hash.
- `TestNewDenebRecoveryBatchGroupsOnTheCanonicalRoot` — response
grouping is keyed on it. Added
because every migrated fixture makes the two roots equal, so the old map
would still have passed.
- `TestRootedColumnBlockPreservesTheSignature` — the wrapper exposes the
wrapped block's signature.
- `TestNewBlobRecoveryMetadataCarriesTheSignature` — sets a **non-zero**
signature and checks it
survives both a plain block and a wrapper. The existing fixtures sign
with zero, so an equality
  against them would have been vacuous.
- `TestReadRetryBlockReturnsTheCanonicalRoot` — the retry path
re-resolves the root for a slot pulled
off the retry ledger. Nothing covered it, so reverting that lookup to
the self-hash would have kept
  every other distinct-root test green.

All mutation-verified: reverting each path fails its test, including
restoring the concrete type
switch, which fails on the wrapper case specifically.

`./cl/...` passes; `make lint` clean.

## Related

- #23927 validates frozen blob segments at rest; this fixes the recovery
that keeps them complete.
- #24037 covers `capcli dump-blobs-snapshots` writing hollow segments —
a separate defect.
- Backports to `release/3.6` and `release/3.5` to follow.

author: awskii
subject: execution, rpc: decode block access list addresses without interning (#24024)
body:
`AccountChanges.DecodeRLP` interns every address with `unique.Make` on
the request goroutine, before `Handling new payload`. Most of that time
goes to new handles: `weak.Make` and `runtime.AddCleanup` insert span
specials, walking the span's list. `AccountChanges.Address` is now a
`common.Address`, and the code that needs a handle interns it once per
account.

## Changes
- `execution/types`: `AccountChanges.Address` is `common.Address`.
- `VersionMap.WriteChanges`, `bal.ToWriteSet`,
`calcState.LoadFromBALUpTo` and the BAL state warmup intern the address;
the BAL builder stores `addr.Value()`.
- Tests build `AccountChanges` with `common.Address`.

## Notes
benchmarkoor replay of the 100 jochemnet blocks from 24410421 on an AMD
EPYC 4344P (erigon on 8 CPUs): `25ac06305d90`, whose touched files match
`main`, with and without this change, both built with
`GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2` (#24017), three interleaved runs per arm after a
warm-up. 41 blocks take over 200 ms:

| request sent → `Handling new payload` | sum, 41 blocks | p50, 41
blocks | p50, other blocks |
|---|---|---|---|
| `25ac06305d90` | 716–757 ms | 13.7–15.4 ms | 2.92–3.00 ms |
| this change | 431–471 ms | 7.4–9.3 ms | 2.90–3.01 ms |

The interning moves rather than disappears: one profiled run shows
`unique.Make[[20]byte]` at 0.82 s against 0.53 s on `25ac06305d90`, now
in the warmup workers (0.38 s) and `verifyAuthorities` (0.30 s). Total
`newPayload` time over the 41 blocks is not separated from run-to-run
drift. No new test: behavior is unchanged and the existing BAL tests
cover it.

author: Andrew Ashikhmin
subject: cl: harden local payload preparation and Gloas fallbacks (#23436)
body:
Follow-up to #23399. ## Why Starting the local execution builder in the slot before a known proposer duty reduces cold-start work. Production can reuse that work only for an identical build request and payload ID; preparation must also yield to production, publication, and adoption. ## Behavior - From Capella onward, nodes with the validator API and direct execution client use `StartPayloadBuild`, never a speculative fork-choice update (FCU). - Before Gloas, preparation builds on the selected execution head; a Gloas target with a pre-Gloas head uses the pre-fork parent. - Steady-state Gloas preparation covers genuine EMPTY paths whose parent is already the execution head. It waits for PTC only for a current-slot head; FULL and FULL-to-EMPTY paths stand down. - Production resolves its proposal's parent, sends the normal FCU, and inherits warmup only for an exact payload-ID match. - Gloas production verifies the beacon parent before execution work, including the fork-transition slot. A root mismatch or failed head lookup rejects the proposal. Only unresolved payload status or an unreadable FULL envelope on a verified head uses the EMPTY-parent fallback; read failures carry their cause. - The registered-builder bid endpoint checks the beacon root and execution parent from one coherent head snapshot, then rechecks the root, payload status, and live PTC-derived parent path after envelope resolution and before caching. It shares production's parent-resolution rules, including the EMPTY fallback. Head changes return HTTP 404 whether detected before building or during revalidation. - A missing MEV-Boost client or a relay bid that fails validation keeps the local payload. Relay checks include the expected withdrawals root and fork-correct blob limits, with schedules applied from Fulu. - Proposer-preference retries receive HTTP 200 only when the stored message and signature both match. Conflicts return indexed HTTP 400 errors without replacing the accepted preference. ## End-to-end flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Slot N: proposer duty for N+1"] --> B["Wait for slot N selected head
or bounded stale-head fallback"] B --> C{"Fork and parent path"} C -- "Pre-Gloas" --> D["Derive production-equivalent inputs"] C -- "Gloas target with pre-Gloas head" --> E["Use pre-fork parent
and transition withdrawals"] C -- "Current-slot Gloas head" --> F["Wait for PTC deadline
and re-read head"] C -- "Older Gloas head" --> G{"Resolved Gloas path"} F --> G G -- "Genuine EMPTY" --> D G -- "FULL or FULL-to-EMPTY" --> H["Stand down"] G -- "Pending, root mismatch,
or lookup failure" --> I["Retry later"] E --> D D --> J["StartPayloadBuild without FCU"] J --> K["Record payload ID, head,
and earliest successful start"] K --> L["Production resolves proposal parent"] H -. "proposal time" .-> L I -. "proposal time: re-resolve" .-> L L -- "Gloas root mismatch
or head lookup failure" --> X["Reject proposal"] L -- "resolved parent or EMPTY fallback" --> P["Send normal FCU"] P --> M{"Same payload ID?"} M -- "yes" --> N["Advance first collection by
inherited warmup, capped"] M -- "no" --> O["Use normal collection timing"] ``` The scheduler waits for the current slot's selected head through its attestation deadline. It may then use an older head unless local block work or an active `OnBlock` call blocks the fallback. A rejected block does not suppress it for the rest of the slot. ## Input and state guarantees - Preparation and production share parent resolution. A Gloas proposal with a pre-Gloas parent uses the advanced state's withdrawal sweep. Gloas-at-genesis follows the EMPTY path and uses cached withdrawals. FULL production applies the parent's execution requests before deriving withdrawals. - Shared attributes cover timestamp, `prevRandao`, fee recipient, withdrawals, parent beacon root, slot, and target gas limit. Payload-ID mismatches log both heads. - Preparation and normal v3/v4 self-build production use the validator registration's fee recipient. The registered-builder bid endpoint uses the proposer preference's recipient; different recipients are different build requests. - Head root, proposer, and state come from one view; the root is rechecked before and after builder startup. - Head-event publication reads the root, slot, and payload status from one coherent snapshot, avoiding inconsistent data or dropped events caused by separate reads. - Gloas head calculations use one slot snapshot for filtering, weights, and payload tiebreakers. Pre-fork calculations recheck the fork after checkpoint I/O to avoid overwriting a newer Gloas head, and pre-Gloas results carry PENDING status. - Scratch state reuses large buffers, resets to the source fork version on copy, and is released after a settled outcome or target-slot change. - Fulu lookahead rejects unregistered proposers before copying; pre-Fulu epoch-boundary checks advance state when needed. - A 500 ms lead floor is checked before and after state work; block work is checked before copying and builder startup. - Settled outcomes are keyed by target slot, head, registration generation, Gloas path, proposer index, and effective target gas limit (including whether it is set). Unrelated preference changes do not trigger re-preparation. - Pending or root-mismatched Gloas status is not primeable. Concurrent Gloas head readers recheck the cache under the store lock to avoid duplicate tree walks. Current-slot PTC votes leave the cache intact; slot transitions and accepted late PTC votes invalidate it. ## Coordination ```mermaid flowchart TB V["Validated production"] --> R["Shared block-work gate"] P["Active publication, storage, and adoption"] --> R E["Local envelope execution"] --> R D["Preparation tick"] --> C{"Gate idle?"} C -- "no" --> Z["Skip this tick"] C -- "yes" --> W["Derive state and attributes"] W --> X{"Exclusive TryLock"} X -- "busy" --> Z X -- "acquired" --> Q{"Produced-slot marker pending?"} Q -- "yes: release gate" --> Z Q -- "no" --> S["StartPayloadBuild"] R -. "blocks early probe" .-> C R -. "excludes builder startup" .-> X M["Bounded produced-slot markers"] -. "signing and queued-storage gap" .-> D M -. "recheck under lock" .-> Q I["Active OnBlock"] -. "suppresses stale fallback" .-> D ``` Shared block-work holders may overlap. Preparation derives state outside the gate, then uses exclusive `TryLock` and rechecks produced-slot markers before builder startup. This closes the production-to-signing race. Preparation never queues ahead of handler work; handler work may wait for a short builder-start call already in progress. Per-slot markers cover a bounded signing margin, not arbitrary signer or queue delays. A waiting publication call clears its marker only after successful integration. Non-waiting publication and failed attempts retain it, subject to expiry or selection of a head for that slot. Queued storage holds no gate; it takes the shared side when it runs. Separate envelope publication does not manage the marker. Network imports remain outside the gate; active `OnBlock` only advises the stale-head fallback. ## Collection timing Production advances collection only for an exact prepared payload-ID match: ```text collection advance = min(inherited warmup, maximum prepared advance) first collection = normal first collection - collection advance ``` The first poll is clamped to now. The cap leaves the builder running into the proposal slot; earlier successful collection trades some transaction recency for earlier readiness. | Fork timing | Normal first poll | Earliest prepared first poll | Maximum advance | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Pre-Gloas | 2.9 s | 0.9 s | 2.0 s | | Gloas EMPTY | 2.15 s | 0.65 s | 1.5 s | These values assume a 12-second slot. Shorter warmup advances collection proportionally; a missing or mismatched prepared build keeps the normal window. ## Suggested review order 1. `cl/beacon/handler/payload_preparation.go`: scheduling, supported paths, memoization, and coordination. 2. `cl/beacon/handler/block_production.go`: parent resolution, liveness fallback, collection timing, and publication markers. 3. `cl/phase1/forkchoice` and `cl/phase1/core/state/raw/copy.go`: head-status freshness, active imports, and version-safe state reuse. 4. `cl/pool/epbs_pool.go` and `cl/phase1/execution_client/execution_client_direct.go`: preference storage and direct builder startup. ## Verification Handler, state, and fork-choice unit tests, targeted race tests, `make lint`, and `make erigon integration` pass. Regression coverage includes head verification at the Gloas transition, head-lookup failure propagation, bid-endpoint head-change responses, relay withdrawals roots and fork-specific blob limits, queued-storage marker retention, missing Gloas payload data, and prepared Gloas EMPTY collection. Behavior-preserving cleanups and comment edits use existing tests rather than new red–green cycles. ## Remaining work - #23551: steady-state Gloas FULL priming needs a canonical execution-head update; envelope validation with `NewPayload` does not move the head. - #23419: broader execution coordination and observability, intra-slot builder reuse, repeated Gloas-envelope decoding, stable-failure memoization, an independent disable setting, and the hybrid engine client's payload-ID byte order. - Preparation policy for very short slots or expensive epoch transitions remains separate design work.

author: Kewei
subject: cl: align blob pruning with configured serve range (#24044)
body:
Fixes #23752.

## Summary
- derive blob pruning and non-archive backfill floors from the
configured wall-clock epoch window
- clamp the mandatory blob range to Deneb and use the PeerDAS window for
Fulu-era recovery
- repair count-only holes left by prior pruning without retrying Fulu
slots after their data-column window expires
- preserve archive/no-pruning behavior and exact-floor writes

- mainnet retention increases from 128,600 to 131,072 slots (about 17.9
to 18.2 days at 12-second slots)
- Gnosis and Chiado retention increases from 128,600 to 262,144 slots
(about 7.4 to 15.2 days at 5-second slots)

The Gnosis/Chiado change nearly doubles the retained blob horizon;
actual disk growth depends on blob usage and storage characteristics.

## Validation
- go test ./cl/clparams ./cl/phase1/network ./cl/phase1/stages -count=1
- focused race tests for pruning, restart recovery, wall-clock
boundaries, and Fulu retry aging
- fast and full golangci-lint: 0 issues

- make erigon integration
- adversarial Standards/Spec, Boundary, Lifecycle, and evidence-truth

author: lystopad
subject: cl/beacon/synced_data: swap head state under lock instead of copying under it (#24165)
body:
Fixes #24164.

## Problem

`OnHeadStateWithBlockRoot`/`OnHeadState` copied the entire incoming
`CachingBeaconState` while holding `s.mu`/`s.accessLock` for writing.
`ViewHeadState`, `ViewPreviousHeadState`, and the single-field accessors
(`ValidatorPublicKeyByIndex`, `ValidatorIndexByPublicKey`,
`CommitteeCount`, `HistoricalRootElementAtIndex`,
`HistoricalSummaryElementAtIndex`) all take the matching read lock, so
every one of them was blocked for however long that copy took.

This is the state-backed remainder of #23154 that #23155 explicitly
scoped out: #23155 publishes the selected head identity (root/slot)
before the state copy runs, so identity-only reads no longer wait on it,
but state-backed reads still do. Any duty computation needing actual
state content - not just a root - goes through `ViewHeadState` and is
still exposed.

Reproduced on a mainnet validator node running a release/3.7 dev build:
sync-committee efficiency dropped to 94.60% (199/3686 missed) in a 24h
window while attestation efficiency stayed at 99.59%, matching #23154's
own description of this failure mode (attestation data is produced
before the head-state update; sync-committee messages need the state
after it). Full field evidence is in #24164.

## Change

Both `OnHeadState` and `OnHeadStateWithBlockRoot` now acquire a new
`writeLock sync.Mutex`, independent of `mu`/`accessLock`, before doing
any work - `OnHeadState`'s `BlockRoot()` resolution included, not just
the copy - then call a shared `publishHeadStateLocked` (documented as
requiring the lock already held), which:

1. Copies the incoming state under `writeLock`.
2. Takes `mu`/`accessLock` only to swap the copy in as the new head
state and demote the current head state to previous (`previousHeadState
= headState; headState = copied` - a pointer reassignment, no data copy)
- an O(1) critical section regardless of state size.

`writeLock` matters because it isn't just about latency: without it, a
writer that started earlier but is slower to resolve its root or copy
its state could be overtaken and then overwritten by a writer that
started later but finishes faster - a silent regression to a stale head,
not just a slow reader. This applies equally to `OnHeadState` (root not
yet known, one caller - `cmd/capcli`, called sequentially today, but
still part of the exported `SyncedData` contract) and
`OnHeadStateWithBlockRoot` (root given, used by every concurrent caller:
forkchoice, forward sync, block production). `UnsetHeadState` also takes
`writeLock` (before `mu`), so it can't land in the middle of an
in-flight publish and then get resurrected by it.

Net effect: lock hold time for readers is now O(1); writers stay fully
serialized in arrival order, same guarantee the old single-mutex design
gave for free. `previousHeadState` is now the actual prior `headState`
object (aliased, not copied into a reused buffer) - same observable
content, one fewer full-state copy per update. No behavior change to any
exported signature.

## Testing

Per this repo's TDD convention, each fix has a test that reproduces it
against the commit before the fix and passes after:

- `TestViewHeadStateDoesNotWaitForHeadStateCopy` - a `ViewHeadState`
reader is not blocked for the incoming state's copy duration (only the
swap). Uses `copyHookForTest`, a package-level hook bound to the copy
itself via a small `copyState` helper (not just called before it - so
the hook's pause point can't be separated from the copy by a future
reorder), to pause a writer at an exact point and prove a concurrent
read completes while it's genuinely paused there.
- `TestOnHeadStateWithBlockRootSerializesConcurrentWriters` - a writer
cannot be overtaken and overwritten by a writer that starts later.
Deterministic: holds `writeLock` directly to represent a writer already
inside its critical section.
- `TestOnHeadStateSerializesAgainstOnHeadStateWithBlockRoot` -
`OnHeadState`'s root resolution is covered by the same serialization as
`OnHeadStateWithBlockRoot`'s copy, not just the copy step. Drives both
writers through the real public API with a calibrated head start
(documented in the test).
- `TestUnsetHeadStateSerializesWithPublish` - `UnsetHeadState` cannot be
resurrected by a publish that was already in flight when it was called.
Same hold-`writeLock` technique.

Plus:
- `TestOnHeadStateWithBlockRootColdStart` - first update populates head
state, no previous state yet.
- `TestOnHeadStateWithBlockRootDemotesPriorHeadToPrevious` -
`ViewPreviousHeadState` observes the state that was head right before
the latest update, proving the alias-based swap is behaviorally
equivalent to the old copy-based one.
- `TestOnHeadStateWithBlockRootConcurrentReadWrite` - races real writers
against real readers through the public API. Passes under `-race`.

Full existing suite (`cl/beacon/synced_data`, `cl/beacon/handler`,
`cl/phase1/stages`) passes unchanged, including the
generation-consistency and TOCTTOU-regression tests added for #23155.
All new tests pass under `-race`, repeated.

## Trade-offs

- `OnHeadState`/`OnHeadStateWithBlockRoot` now always allocate a fresh
state copy (`newState.Copy()`), rather than reusing a preallocated
buffer via `CopyInto` on the steady-state path. This trades a modest
increase in per-block allocation for removing the reader-blocking lock
hold - the copy's own cost is unchanged either way, only whether readers
wait for it. Flagging in case reviewers want a buffer-pooling follow-up
instead; I kept this PR to the minimal change that fixes the blocking
behavior.
- Not backporting in this PR. release/3.6 already carries #23155's
prerequisite (backported as #23172, included in v3.6.1) so this fix
would cherry-pick cleanly there. release/3.5 never received
#23155/#23172, so it still has the original (larger) #23154 bug, not
just this remainder - a release/3.5 backport would need that fix first.
Happy to open both as follow-ups if maintainers want them.
- #24197 tracks two remaining test-hardening items from review
(real-path writer-ordering coverage, `accessLock` accessor coverage) -
explicitly scoped as non-blocking follow-ups, not production bugs.

author: Thomas Sprayberry
subject: cl: expire ttl cache entries on read instead of sweeping (#24022)
body:
Closes #23848

## Summary

- `cl/phase1/core/state/lru.CacheWithTTL` wrapped an `expirable.LRU`
built with a ttl, whose cleanup goroutine cannot be stopped (`Close` is
commented out in golang-lru v2.0.7 and there is no newer release), so
every cache built per request, per peer or per test leaked a goroutine
for the life of the process.
- The cache is now a `simplelru.LRU` under the wrapper's own mutex with
no background work at all: `Add` stamps a deadline on the entry under
the lock and reclaims up to two expired entries from the least recently
used end, and `Get` treats an entry past its deadline as a miss and
drops it. There is no sweep goroutine, no separate expiry order and no
`Close`, so there is nothing to wire and nothing left to leak.
- `p2pManager.bannedPeers` was declared, assigned and never read; it is
deleted rather than converted. The sentinel peers pool keeps its own,
separate ban cache.
- The beacon rpc client's peer refresh loop ran on
`context.Background()` and never exited; it now ends with the client's
ctx, and `TestNewBeaconRpcP2PStopsPeerGoroutinesWhenContextEnds` pins
that with `goleak`.

## What lazy expiry changes

Reads are unchanged: a value past its deadline is never returned. What
differs is residency. Nothing removes an expired entry on a timer any
more. An entry that is never read again reaches the least recently used
end in deadline order, where an `Add` reclaims it, up to two per `Add`
and stopping at the first live entry, so a cache that is written to
holds roughly a ttl's worth of entries, as it does on `main`. An entry a
`Get` promoted is reclaimed once everything less recently used than it
has gone, which under continued writes is within two ttls of its `Add`.
A cache that stops being written to keeps what it holds, up to its size
cap, until the next `Add`. `Len` counts residents, expired or not. Its
one reader is `Pool.LenBannedPeers`, which feeds the disconnected figure
of `Sentinel.GetPeersCount` (`cl/sentinel/sentinel.go:250`); that figure
can now include bans past their 30 minutes until a `BanStatus` lookup, a
later ban or the 100,000 cap drops them. It is a report, not a decision.
Eviction order is by recency as before, and an expired entry can hold a
slot that a live one would otherwise take, so hit rates can differ from
the swept version at the cap. No other caller reads `Len`, and the
wrapper has no `Contains` or `Keys`. `Get` does not extend an entry's
deadline; only `Add` does.

## Decisions, against `main`

- **`simplelru.LRU`, not `expirable.LRU`.** On `main` the expirable
cache brings its own goroutine, its own lock and 100 expiry buckets, and
the goroutine cannot be stopped. The wrapper already serialises every
call under one mutex, so the base only needs to be an LRU with nothing
to stop. It rejects `size <= 0`, which `New` already refuses and no
caller passes; `NewWithTTL` panics on it rather than growing an error
return every call site would have to thread.
- **No sweep goroutine; `Add` reclaims the expired tail.** Expiry on
read alone would let a cache fill to its size cap, and for three caches
the ttl is the practical memory bound because their values are large and
their keys are never read again: `shuffledIndiciesCacheReader` (64
entries of 8 bytes per active validator), `bid_validation_states` (4
full beacon state copies) and `aggregation_in_committee`. Dropping up to
two expired entries from the least recently used end on every `Add` is
O(1), needs no extra structure and nothing to stop, and keeps a
written-to cache near a ttl's worth of entries; two per `Add` stays
ahead of the one entry an `Add` inserts, so a backlog drains. Dropping
the goroutine also removes the ownership question for caches with no
natural owner: the historical states reader's `shuffledIndiciesCache`
(#24148) no longer starts anything when the antiquary rebuilds the
reader after a failed initialisation, so that leak goes with this change
too.
- **The deadline is stamped under the lock.** Time spent waiting for the
mutex is not charged to the entry's ttl, so a long wait cannot store a
value that is already expired.

## Tests

`cl/phase1/core/state/lru`: 21 tests. A test back-dates an entry's
deadline under the lock instead of sleeping past a short ttl; the one
test that waits on the clock holds the cache lock for 100 ms to show the
deadline is taken under it, and a slow scheduler can only make it pass.
Covered: a live hit; an expired entry stays resident until read, then a
`Get` returns the zero value, misses and drops it; the deadline boundary
(live at the deadline, expired one nanosecond after); the deadline is
stamped at `Add`, under the lock; `Add` on an existing key renews its
deadline and replaces its value, before and after expiry; `Get` does not
extend the deadline; size eviction is by recency and reports the
eviction; the cap bounds a cache of live entries; an `Add` reclaims two
expired entries from the least recently used end and stops at the first
live one; writes drain an expired backlog; steady write traffic holds
residency to the ttl, not the cap; an entry a `Get` promoted is
reclaimed once it reaches that end; reclamation moves neither counter;
`Remove`; a ttl of zero or less never expires and reclaims nothing; a
non-positive size panics; hit and miss counters move exactly once per
`Get`; concurrent `Add`, `Get`, `Remove` and `Len` on overlapping keys
with a 1 ms ttl under `-race`.

Run: `go vet` on every touched package; `go test -race -count=1
./cl/phase1/core/state/lru/ ./cl/rpc/`; `go test ./cl/p2p/
./cl/sentinel/ ./cl/sentinel/peers/ ./cl/sentinel/handlers/
./cl/phase1/network/services/ ./cl/aggregation/
./cl/validator/attestation_producer/`.

The `WaitGroup.Go` lint fix is a mechanical test refactor, so it uses
the existing tests without a new TDD cycle. Cache tests pass normally
and with `-race`; `make lint` and `make erigon integration` also pass.

AI assistance: the fix and tests were drafted with AI tooling in my
workflow and verified by running them as described. I am responsible for
the change and will handle review feedback.

---------

author: lystopad
subject: docs: record the blob snapshot invariants agents keep getting wrong (#24145)
body:
Four additions to the agent guidance, each from a mistake made during a
mainnet blob sidecar repair. All references verified against `main`.

**`db/agents.md`**

- Blob segments are `<range>-blobsidecars.seg` but their index is
`<range>-blocksidecars.idx` (`snaptype/type.go:155`). A glob on one name
silently misses the other — this caused three separate incidents in one
day: stale indexes after a delete, orphaned indexes after a version
bump, and a cleanup that skipped a whole decade of files.
- Blob snapshots rest up to one `CaplinMergeLimit` behind beacon
snapshots by design (`antiquary.go:499` refuses to dump a partial
range), so a resting gap of 9,999 is healthy.

**`cl/agents.md`**

- Blob retirement is gated on `blobBackfilled` (`antiquary.go:240`), so
a gap the backfill cannot fill stops **all** blob retirement, including
provably complete ranges far below it. Observed live: 48 chunks of
verified data parked behind ~2,000 slots. The gate returns silently,
with no log or metric. `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS` is how
long peers *must* serve rather than a ceiling, so a gap past it is not
guaranteed retrievable rather than certainly unfillable.
- In archive mode the backfill applies no retention floor
(`blob_downloader.go:343`); only the non-archive path clamps
`targetSlot` and `retryFloor`. Each batch is bounded by
`requestBlobBatchExpiration` (15s, `blobs.go:35`) and returns early on a
complete response, but the enclosing loop does not terminate for slots
that stay unavailable.
- `frozen_blobs` is published only from the forkchoice stage
(`phase1/stages/forkchoice.go:64`) and the gauge starts at zero, so zero
cannot establish whether blob snapshots exist. The shipped dashboards
already guard it with `> 0`.

**`AGENTS.md`** — a TDD note on changing bounds and constants.

A deliberate tolerance and an off-by-one are indistinguishable at the
call site. The `(beaconTo - 1)` in the blob coverage check was nearly
"fixed" to require the blob and beacon frontiers to match, which would
have made the integrity check reject every healthy node and block
snapshot publishing outright. The accompanying red test passed because
it encoded the same wrong assumption as the change. A reviewer caught
the premise, not the arithmetic.

Docs only, no code change.

_Updated after review: the retention, retry-bound and metric claims were
over-absolute and have been qualified — see the review threads. One of
them was not merely theoretical: a mainnet archive node recovered a
46-day-old gap from peers while I was asserting that could not happen._

author: Andrew Ashikhmin
subject: cl: remove test workarounds for the ttl cache's old goroutine (#24204)
body:
Follow-up to #24022, which is merged.

Closes #24148. The fix for it is in #24022, which removed the goroutine
that issue tracks but closed only #23848.

## Changes

- **Revert #23847.** It shared one `peers.Pool` across the `cl/sentinel`
tests because every pool started two ttl-cache cleanup goroutines that
could not be stopped. Since #24022 the cache starts no goroutine, so the
shared fixture, its two comments and `TestFixtureReusesOnePeerPool` have
no reason left, and the comments would be false. Measured on this
branch: 100 pools add no goroutines.
- **`TestCacheWithTTLWriteTrafficBoundsResidencyByTheTTL`: a step of one
minute instead of one second.** The live keys sat half a second from
their deadline, so a stall of that length between the last writes and
the assertion dropped one of them and failed the length check. Every
deadline is now thirty seconds from the clock on either side.

## Tests

Test-only changes with no new behaviour, so no TDD cycle: the first is a
removal and the second is a constant.

`go test -race -count=3 -shuffle=on ./cl/sentinel/`, `go test -race
-count=5 ./cl/phase1/core/state/lru/`, `make lint` and `make erigon
integration` pass.
