author: Sahil Sojitra
subject: cl/phase1/forkchoice: don't hold the fork-choice lock across blocking EL calls in OnBlock (#23691)
body:
Closes #23529.

### The problem

`OnBlock` takes `f.mu` at the top and holds it for the whole function,
with `engine.NewPayload` sitting inside that critical section. That is a
round trip to the EL, tens to hundreds of milliseconds, and while it is
in flight `OnTick`, `OnAttestation`, `GetHead` and every read-lock user
are stuck behind the same mutex. One slow EL response stalls attestation
processing and head computation for the whole node.

Not a data race — the old code was correct, just serialised on EL
latency. The Gloas path already yields the lock through
`newPayloadWhileYieldingForkChoiceLock`; the pre-Gloas path never picked
it up.

### The fix

`NewPayload` now goes through
`newPayloadForBlockWhileYieldingForkChoiceLock`, which releases `f.mu`
for the call and takes it back before touching any store state.
Admission is unchanged: `payloadValidationAdmission` still serialises
every EL validation across fork choice and the sync stages.

### What gets rechecked after the lock comes back

Anything checked on entry can go stale during the window, so the whole
entry check is re-run rather than picking off individual conditions:
`validateBlockAdmissionLocked(block, rejectEquivocation, newPayload)`.
That covers finality moving past the block or onto another branch, and
an equivocating header inserted while we waited. `invalidateCachedHead`
runs right after the relock, since a `GetHead` during the window would
refill the cache from pre-block state.

The same check also runs inside the helper once the admission token is
won, so a block that went stale while queued does not spend a slot on
the shared gate. It needs `f.mu`, and the caller already owns the global
token, so it uses `TryRLock` and skips when the lock is busy — waiting
there would park the protocol-wide token behind whoever holds the lock.
Skipping is not free: the block still reaches the EL, and the caller
records a status and an optimistic entry before its own re-check rejects
it. It is the cheaper of the two.

Ordering matters in one place. The post-EL re-run sits **after** the
payload-status switch; putting it before means an `INVALIDATED` verdict
or an EL error is neither recorded nor returned.

`getHead` also re-reads the justified checkpoint under `f.mu` and
retries if it moved, matching `getHeadGloas` — this change widens its
sample-before-lock window to span the whole EL call.

### Publishing the verdict

Holding the lock continuously meant a duplicate `OnBlock` could never
issue a second `NewPayload`: the next caller saw the recorded verdict
before reaching the EL. Releasing it breaks that, because the finishing
caller has to reacquire `f.mu` before recording anything and the queue
drains first.

So the helper records the verdict while it still holds the token —
`verifiedExecutionPayload` for VALID, `payloadStatusByRoot` and
`executionPayloadStatus` for INVALID, with invalid checked ahead of
valid. Two constraints on the invalid side:

- **Keyed by the payload, not just the beacon root.** Two beacon blocks
can differ in state root or graffiti and carry the same execution
payload, so a root-only key lets the second one resend it.
- **Nothing is cached unless the payload names its own hash.** The
claimed `BlockHash` is unauthenticated at that point, so the key is
derived with `ComputeBlockHash` and the verdict cached only when derived
equals claimed. Caching a mismatch would blacklist a hash the payload
never owned.

Those two status caches are bounded, so a busy queue can evict the
verdict before the caller relocks and makes it durable.
`inFlightInvalidPayloads` bridges that gap: written behind the same
derived-equals-claimed gate, read by `executionHashMarkedInvalid`, and
cleared once the writer's own durable write has happened. It is
deliberately not refcounted through `executionPayloadRoots`, so the
writer has to clear its own key — the helper returns the hash it
published, which is what lets a caller that merely short-circuited on
the verdict avoid retracting somebody else's entry.

The Gloas path keeps the older behaviour, since its predicate is
envelope persistence, which cannot be published without `f.mu`. That
window pre-dates this PR.

### Tests

22 in `cl/phase1/forkchoice/on_block_lock_scope_test.go`, ordered with
channels — no sleeps anywhere, the timeouts are only failure deadlines.
They cover the lock actually yielding, each rechecked condition, verdict
publishing and both constraints above, the in-flight set's write, clear
and writer-gating, and two concurrency cases.

Every fix is mutation-checked: removing the line it protects makes the
matching test fail.

Two things are covered by reasoning rather than a test, and I would
rather say so than imply otherwise:

- The end-to-end queued-and-went-stale sequence, and the gossip-verdict
mapping for an admission failure caught while queued. Both need a caller
parked on the admission channel at a known moment, which is not
observable from outside without a test-only hook. I wrote both, found
they passed with the fix reverted, and deleted them.
- The `getHead` retry loop. The one-shot rejection of a superseded
checkpoint is pinned; forcing a real retry needs the checkpoint to move
inside a single call. The loop is a copy of `getHeadGloas`, whose retry
is equally untested.

### Scope

`engine.GetBlobs` is also a blocking EL call under `f.mu` in the same
function. An earlier revision of this PR yielded the lock there too;
that was removed because it lifted the only cap on concurrent `GetBlobs`
calls without adding one back. HEAD calls it exactly as main does.
Tracked separately, along with the length-only `elHasBlobs` check.

author: lystopad
subject: cl/antiquary: give a blob backlog the same compression parallelism as EL catch-up (#24316)
body:
Fixes #24310.

`antiquateBlobs` always passed `1` as `compressWorkers`, so a node
behind on blob retirement compressed gigabyte segments single-threaded
for the whole backlog.

Measured on a sepolia archive node clearing a 72-chunk range (10,470,000
→ 11,189,999) after a store repair: **54 min per ~1.45 GB chunk**, about
**2.4 days**, with exactly one `seg/parallel_compress.go` goroutine
throughout.

One worker at the tip is deliberate and stays — retirement covers a
single chunk there and should not compete with execution. EL retirement
draws the same line by sync cycle:

```go
// execution/stagedsync/stage_snapshots.go
if s.CurrentSyncCycle.IsInitialCycle {
	cfg.blockRetire.SetWorkers(estimate.CompressSnapshot.Workers())
} else {
	cfg.blockRetire.SetWorkers(1)
}
```

Caplin had no equivalent, so it stayed at `1` however far behind it was.
The pending range now decides: two chunks or more is a catch-up.

## The shared build limiter

Going parallel means honouring the limiter Caplin has been bypassing.
`segmentsBuildLimiter` is created once in `node/eth/backend.go` and
passed to both `NewBlockRetire` and `caplin1.RunCaplinService`; its size
defaults to 1, "allows 1 kind of snapshots to be built simultaneously".
Caplin's acquisition is commented out, and the commented code would not
have worked — its `defer` re-acquires instead of releasing.

At one worker that omission was cheap. At full width it would not be:
both sides size themselves from the same estimate, which budgets 50% of
RAM per build, so two concurrent builds spend the whole budget.

A dump that cannot take the limiter **falls back to one worker** rather
than skipping. Blob retirement is gated on the whole range landing, so a
skipped dump leaves the gate shut and the node grinding — the failure
mode in #24112. Slower is acceptable; stalled is not.

## Tests

`isBlobBacklog` pins the threshold deterministically, including a
non-advancing range that must not underflow into an enormous backlog.

`blobCompressWorkers` pins the limiter behaviour without a live
antiquary: the tip leaves it free, a backlog holds it and gives it back,
a taken limiter falls back to one worker, and no limiter still goes
parallel. Those assertions hold on a single-core runner, where a
worker-count comparison alone would prove nothing.

Mutation-verified: lowering the threshold to one chunk, always reporting
a backlog, dropping the underflow guard, always going parallel, going
parallel without the limiter, and never releasing it are each caught.

**Known gap:** reverting the call site in `antiquateBlobs` to a
hardcoded `1` still leaves the suite green. Covering that needs
`antiquateBlobs` reachable in a test — a live DB, snapshots and blob
storage — which is a larger change than this warrants. The selection
logic it calls is fully covered; the line wiring it in is not.

**Not addressed here:** `DumpBeaconBlocks` in the same function has the
identical shape, but its segments are far smaller so the effect is much
weaker — worth its own change if measurements justify it.

author: Sahil Sojitra
subject: lint: enable staticcheck's ST1019, ST1016, ST1012, ST1017, ST1005 (#24332)
body:
### Summary

Per #24021 (endorsed there by @taratorio): turns on the five staticcheck
checks we'd left switched off, and fixes everything they find.

- **ST1019** — a package imported twice under two different names in the
same file
- **ST1016** — a type's methods not agreeing on a receiver name
- **ST1012** — an error var not named `errFoo`/`ErrFoo`
- **ST1017** — Yoda conditions
- **ST1005** — error strings that are capitalized or end in punctuation

### Nature of the changes

All mechanical: dropping a redundant import alias, renaming a receiver
consistently across a type's methods, renaming an error var (and every
reference to it), flipping a comparison's operand order, or reformatting
an error string's casing/punctuation. No behavior changes.

`gofumpt` (the other half of #24021) already landed separately in #24182
and #24183.

### One documented exception

`RwTx.AsyncClone` (`db/kv/temporal/kv_temporal.go`) keeps its outlier
receiver name. Its body constructs a value of an embedded type also
named `tx`; renaming the receiver to match the rest of `RwTx`'s methods
would make that construction ambiguous with the receiver itself, so the
rename isn't safe. Excluded narrowly for just this one file in
`.golangci.yml`, with the same reasoning also left as a comment on the
method itself.

### Verification

- Build passes clean
- `go vet` output matches the pre-existing baseline exactly, nothing new
- Full test suite passes
- Lint is clean, run twice per this repo's non-determinism note
- Diffed against `main` to confirm every change is exactly the intended
fix, nothing else

author: lystopad
subject: cl/beacon: publish sync-committee messages in background instead of blocking the request (#24259)
body:
Fixes #24258.

## Problem

`PostEthV1BeaconPoolSyncCommittees` published sync-committee messages to
gossip synchronously, on the HTTP request's own context, before writing
the HTTP response, and swallowed any publish error at `Debug`. The
handler blocks for the full duration of gossip validation/handoff,
coupling HTTP response latency to a single-threaded event loop shared
with the much higher-volume attestation topics, and whatever error
`Publish` returns never surfaced to the caller, an HTTP status, or any
metric.

Cross-referencing a Lighthouse VC log against the beacon API's
`rewards/sync_committee` endpoint confirmed real, on-chain misses on a
mainnet node — see #24258 for the evidence.

**Correction (2026-09-24):** an earlier version of this description and
#24258 claimed the request context being cancelled on handler return
could abort an in-flight publish. That's wrong — the handler cannot
return (and so `net/http` cannot cancel `r.Context()`) while it's still
blocked on the synchronous `Publish` call, and go-libp2p-pubsub
v0.11.0's `Topic.Publish` only consults its `ctx` parameter inside the
optional `WithReadiness` path, which Erigon's no-options call never
takes. Caught by an independent third-party review of this PR; full
detail in the correction section of #24258. The on-chain misses are
real; this PR does not establish their specific original cause, only
that decoupling the publish call removes the HTTP-latency coupling and
makes every failure path observable and, where the failure is known
before the response is written, reported to the caller. A later review
raised a further, specific, unresolved doubt about the original
cross-reference's slot alignment — see the follow-up comment on #24258.
Also unresolved either way in this session.

## Prior art

Both geth (`eth/handler.go`'s `txBroadcastLoop`) and reth
(`TransactionsManager`) decouple RPC-accept from network-broadcast the
same way: the RPC handler only inserts into a local pool and returns; a
single long-lived background worker, subscribed to a pool/feed channel
at node startup, does the actual broadcast, independent of any
individual request's context.

## Fix

`GossipManager` already runs lifetime-scoped background goroutines off
its own internally-owned context - this reuses that instead of
introducing a new context-derivation pattern:

- A bounded `publishQueue` channel plus one dedicated worker goroutine,
started alongside the existing ones. The queue is sized to
`beaconConfig.SyncCommitteeSize` (with a 64 floor) so it can absorb a
full sync-committee burst without dropping.
- `PublishBackground(name string, data []byte, expiry time.Time, logCtx
...any) error` on the `Gossip` interface: enqueues non-blockingly and
returns a stable sentinel error (never nil-but-silently-dropped) when
the message was never admitted - full queue, shutdown in progress, an
unresolvable fork digest, or already past `expiry`. The fork digest is
resolved and captured at enqueue time, not re-resolved when the worker
drains the job, so a message accepted just before a fork activates still
publishes to the topic it was actually validated against.
- `expiry` (slot end plus the protocol's maximum gossip clock disparity,
computed with exact time arithmetic) is checked both at admission and
again immediately before the actual publish - a message that goes stale
while queued behind other work is dropped instead of spending a
compress/peer-lookup/publish cycle on it, without blocking fresh work
behind it. This is a staleness check, not a validity/authentication one
- see Known limitations below.
- `PostEthV1BeaconPoolSyncCommittees` calls `PublishBackground` instead
of the synchronous `Publish(r.Context(), ...)`. A non-nil return - a
*known* failure, not an unknowable later network one - is now surfaced
as HTTP 500 for an otherwise-valid batch, instead of a silent 200.
Validation failures (the existing indexed 400 behavior) take precedence
when a batch has both, without discarding the admission failure:
`PublishBackground` still logs and counts it either way.
- Every drop path is observable and correctly categorized:
`caplin_gossip_publish_queue_rejected_total{topic,reason}` for
admission-time rejections (never queued), separate from
`caplin_gossip_publish_accepted_total{topic}` and
`caplin_gossip_publish_outcome_total{topic,outcome}`
(handoff_ok/publish_error/panic/expired) for work that *was* admitted.
- `PublishBackground` never blocks the caller - not on queue capacity,
not on shutdown: it checks the manager's own lifetime context directly
(a plain, already non-blocking read) and the worker simply returns on
`ctx.Done()` without an explicit drain step. A message admitted right at
shutdown may end up queued with nothing left to process it, which has no
functional effect - it was never going to publish either way, the same
as one correctly rejected at admission. An earlier version of this PR
added an admission gate (atomics, a drain step, dedicated test-only
hooks) purely to keep the accepted/outcome counters exactly equal at
process exit; per review from domiwei and AskAlexSharov, that complexity
wasn't worth what it bought, so it was removed - the counters still hold
the invariant during normal operation, just not necessarily at the exact
moment of shutdown.

Ordering across queued messages doesn't matter here - gossip has no
ordering contract between different validators/subnets.

Scoped to sync-committee messages only, where the on-chain evidence is.
The same synchronous-publish-with-swallowed-error pattern exists at 13
other call sites in `pool.go`, `block_production.go`, and `epbs.go` -
left as a separate follow-up to keep this PR focused. Full histograms
(queue-wait/publish-call duration) and an in-flight gauge were
considered and deliberately left out of this PR's scope - the
accepted/outcome counters above already fix the modeling gap (a rejected
admission being counted the same as an accepted-then-dropped job);
histograms are a real but separate enhancement.

## Known limitations (tracked, not fixed here)

- **#24305**: a seen-key cache hit doesn't re-validate replacement bytes
under the same key, pre-dates this PR (unchanged service code), and
requires Beacon API access to reach; left as its own change since it
touches the shared seen-key cache used elsewhere too. (The other gap
#24305 originally tracked - `ErrIgnore` exempted then published anyway -
is now fixed here: `PostEthV1BeaconPoolSyncCommittees` skips
`PublishBackground` entirely on `ErrIgnore`, verified against the real
service.)
- `handoff_ok` in the new outcome metric means the local pubsub library
accepted the publish call - it is not evidence of remote peer receipt or
sync-aggregate inclusion. Neither this metric nor the two-host delivery
test below establishes that a duty reliably arrives before its useful
deadline; treat the two-host test as a transport smoke test, not a
timing/reliability guarantee.
- The captured fork digest is read from the wall clock at enqueue time,
not derived from the validated message's own epoch; this predates the
queue and is unchanged by it.
- **#24319**: if the single publish worker gets stuck on one call (e.g.
the shared pubsub event loop is congested enough to back up its internal
send buffer), the bounded queue can fill with jobs that expire before
the worker reaches them, and admission then rejects fresh, still-valid
messages with no path to reclaim that wasted capacity. A per-job context
deadline doesn't fix this - go-libp2p-pubsub's local-publish path
doesn't consult the caller's context past the `WithReadiness` option we
don't use. The real fix (evicting expired entries from the queue on
full-queue admission) is a genuine change to the queue's concurrency
model, tracked separately.

## Testing

`cl/phase1/network/gossip/gossip_manager_test.go` and
`cl/beacon/handler/pool_test.go`, each verified by mutation (the
corresponding regression fails reliably when the fix is reverted):

- `PublishBackground` never blocks its caller on queue capacity or
shutdown; drops rather than blocks once the queue is full, sized to hold
a full `SyncCommitteeSize` burst.
- The fork digest used to publish is the one captured at enqueue time,
even if it changes before the worker drains the job.
- Expiry: the exact inclusive boundary (just before/at/just after the
deadline), a job going stale while queued behind other work without
blocking fresh work behind it.
- A panic in one queued publish doesn't take down the worker, and its
recovery log includes the same validator/subnet/slot context the
ordinary failure path already logs.
- A queued message reaches the real gossip `Publish` path end-to-end,
including a two-host test proving some bytes cross a real connection
(see Known limitations - this is a transport smoke test, not a full
protocol/timing test).
- A message is dropped observably once the manager has shut down,
whether triggered via `Close` or the parent context passed into
`NewGossipManager` being cancelled directly (the actual production
path); `PublishBackground` racing concurrently with either never panics
or deadlocks, and the worker always terminates.
- The accepted/outcome counters satisfy the invariant that at quiescence
*during normal operation*, a topic's accepted count equals the sum of
its terminal-outcome counts - compared as deltas against a baseline,
since these are process-global collectors never reset between test runs
(an earlier version of this test compared raw values and flaked under
`-count=2`; fixed and verified up to `-count=5`).
- `PostEthV1BeaconPoolSyncCommittees` calls `PublishBackground`, never
the blocking `Publish`; a full queue returns HTTP 500 for an
otherwise-valid batch; a validation failure takes precedence over an
admission failure when a batch has both.

`go build ./...`, `go test ./cl/beacon/handler/...
./cl/phase1/network/gossip/... -race`, and `make lint` all pass.

author: Kewei
subject: cl: align Gloas consensus and APIs with v1.7.0-beta.2 (#23845)
body:
## Summary

Align Caplin's Gloas consensus behavior and Beacon/Builder APIs with
`consensus-specs` v1.7.0-beta.2, including the missing beta.0
prerequisites required to reach the beta.2 target correctly.

The branch was rebased onto current `main` at
`1ca363730a90ef2419d98f0150e1961d1eb27d84` and reduced from 51 changed
files to 37. Operational hardening that is not required for beta.2 has
moved to two stacked follow-ups.

## Main changes

- initialize anchor PTC votes as uncast and use the parent header slot
for payload settlement, attestation processing, and rewards
- enforce pre-Gloas boundaries for proposer preferences, PTC duties, and
payload attestations
- validate builder version/activity, parent-requested exits, equal
block/parent hashes, gossip timing, and the beta.2 voluntary-exit
wall-clock rule
- keep bounded parent builder-exit summaries so untrusted bid validation
does not perform unbounded disk I/O, with restart/eviction fallback
- serve canonical FULL execution-payload-envelope ranges with bounded
work and explicit unavailable-history behavior
- accept beta.2 invalid transition fixtures without `post.ssz_snappy`
and apply per-case fork config overlays
- pin and pass the official beta.2 mainnet Gloas fixture corpus

## Scope split

- #24279: chain-tip payload-envelope recovery, persisted
replay/revalidation, and checkpoint/P2P plumbing
- #24280: voluntary-exit admission, publication coalescing, eviction
identity, and finalized pruning

Both follow-ups remain stacked on this branch and need rebasing onto
this rewritten head before their next review.

## Latest main rebase

- Base: `1ca363730a90ef2419d98f0150e1961d1eb27d84`
- Head: `86f9315cdbaf3a00d2847352dbe54a0e2b6bd50a`

## Validation

- `go test ./cl/phase1/network/services ./cl/phase1/forkchoice
./cl/sentinel/handlers ./cl/beacon/handler -count=1`
- `go test -tags=spectest ./cl/spectest -run '^Test$/^mainnet$/^gloas$'
-count=1`
- focused race tests for PTC duties and execution-payload-envelope
ByRange handling
- `make lint` (two clean consecutive runs)
- `make erigon integration`
- adversarial review covered fork-direction symmetry, zero/nil/genesis
boundaries, stale or unavailable state, bounded untrusted work, cache
refresh after waits, REST/gossip error-classification boundaries, and
local-self-build ingress

The previous review's actionable failures and concurrency findings are
covered by focused regression tests. GitHub CI passes on head
`86f9315cdbaf3a00d2847352dbe54a0e2b6bd50a`.

## Devnet 11 experiment

The retained experiment used an older head with embedded Caplin and 15
active Lighthouse validator keys. Attestations and payload attestations
were observed, but no proposer duty occurred before the public endpoints
and discovered peers became unavailable. The beta.2 head has not been
redeployed to the stopped devnet.

## Residual risk and deferred work

- the cold envelope disk-read path permits only one active read;
acquisition waiters remain bounded by gossip validation concurrency,
while a permanently wedged storage call can retain the token until the
underlying API becomes cancellable
- full mandatory-range execution-envelope archival remains architectural
follow-up; pruned, inconsistent, or incompletely scanned history returns
`ResourceUnavailable`
- broader coordinated forkchoice ordering work tracked upstream in
`ethereum/consensus-specs#5563`, `ethereum/consensus-specs#5586`, and
`ethereum/consensus-specs#5125` remains outside this delta

author: lystopad
subject: cl/phase1/network/services: authenticate sync-committee seen-key duplicates before acting on them (#24376)
body:
Fixes findings 2 and 3 of #24305.

## Problem

`syncCommitteeMessagesService.ProcessMessage` deduplicates on `(subnet,
slot, validator_index)` - a cache hit returned `nil` unconditionally,
without checking whether the *submitted* `beacon_block_root`/`signature`
matched what was actually verified for that key.

Two consequences, both on the same line:

- **Finding 2 (security):** a second submission with *different*,
never-verified content for an already-seen key was treated the same as a
genuinely re-validated message. On the REST path this reaches
`PublishBackground` (unsigned bytes admitted to the gossip queue); on
the raw gossip path, `ProcessMessage`'s `nil` maps to
`pubsub.ValidationAccept` in `newPubsubValidator`, so the same content
would be forwarded to peers, never having had its signature checked.
- **Finding 3 (efficiency):** even a *legitimate* retry of the exact
same, already-published content hit the same `nil` path, so the REST
handler called `PublishBackground` again and spent another queue slot on
a message that had already gone through admission once.

## Fix

The seen-key cache now stores what it actually verified
(`beacon_block_root`, `signature`), and a cache hit compares the
submission against it:

- **Different content** → `ErrIgnore`, without verifying or acting on it
- matching the spec's own same-slot dedup rule, just correctly applied
to the case that slipped through before.
- **Matching content, not yet published** → `nil`, unchanged - a retry
after a failed `PublishBackground` admission (e.g. a full queue) still
gets a real attempt.
- **Matching content, already published** → `ErrIgnore` - no second
queue slot spent on it.

"Already published" needs the service to learn about publish *outcome*,
not just verification, since verification and publish are two separate
steps (the service verifies; `pool.go` publishes, later, possibly
failing). Added `MarkPublished(subnet, slot, validator_index,
beacon_block_root, signature)` to `SyncCommitteeMessagesService`, called
by the handler only after `PublishBackground` actually succeeds.

## Testing

`cl/phase1/network/services/sync_committee_messages_service_test.go`:
- A replacement with different content is `ErrIgnore` and never reaches
`BlsVerifyMultipleSignatures` (a second, unexpected mock call would fail
the test).
- The original message is unaffected by a rejected replacement in
between.
- A retry of the same content, with no `MarkPublished` call, still
succeeds (`nil`) - the queue-full recovery path is preserved.
- A retry after `MarkPublished` is `ErrIgnore`.

`cl/beacon/handler/pool_test.go`:
- A successful `PublishBackground` triggers `MarkPublished` with the
message's own content.
- A failed `PublishBackground` does not.

Each behavior was checked by mutation (reverting the relevant code line
and confirming the corresponding test fails for the right reason, then
restoring it) before being left in place.

`go build ./...`, `go test ./cl/phase1/network/services/...
./cl/phase1/network/gossip/... ./cl/beacon/handler/... -race`, and `make
lint` all pass.

author: lystopad
subject: cl/beacon, cmd: prepend EL+CL client identification to custom graffiti by default (#24369)
body:
## Summary

Closes #24366.

Caplin's default block-production graffiti already implements the
client-version graffiti standard (`engine_getClientVersionV1`-based
EL+CL code and commit prefix), but only when the block-production
request has no `graffiti` param at all. Any caller-supplied graffiti —
including from an external validator client with its own graffiti (e.g.
Lighthouse VC paired with Erigon EL + Caplin BN) — fully replaced it,
leaving zero attributable client-identification data for
client-diversity dashboards.

- Default behavior now **prefixes** the identification segment to
caller-supplied graffiti as well, truncating the caller's text to
whatever room remains in the fixed 32-byte graffiti field (a
consensus-level SSZ `Bytes32`, not a convention). The segment stays at a
fixed offset (bytes 0-N) regardless of custom-graffiti length. This
matches the actual [flexible
standard](https://hackmd.io/@wmoBhF17RAOH2NZ5bNXJVg/BJX2c9gja)
Lighthouse itself links to — its default case is also
identification-segment-first, with a ~20-byte threshold before
degrading. Lighthouse's and Teku's own implementations instead put the
segment *last* (append, not prefix), which needs a graduated truncation
table on their side; putting it first here means tooling can read it at
a fixed offset without one.
- New flag `--beacon.api.preserve-graffiti` (default `false`) opts out:
caller-supplied graffiti is used verbatim (right-padded, not truncated
or prefixed), for operators who want full control over their graffiti.
It does not exactly reproduce pre-PR byte-for-byte behavior for a
short/underspecified hex `graffiti` value specifically (right-pad vs.
the old left-pad) — right-padding is now the one consistent convention
on both the default and opt-out paths.
- **This is a default-behavior change** — see the `ChangeLog.md` entry.
Operators who already set a custom graffiti will start publishing their
EL+CL client identification by default, and a custom graffiti longer
than 19 bytes (25 before the execution client's version resolves) will
be truncated.
- Startup and diagnostic logging: `LogGraffitiIdentification` logs the
default segment once at beacon-node startup and triggers the execution
client's version lookup; `logGraffitiIdentificationOnce` logs it again,
once, if/when that lookup resolves to something new;
`warnGraffitiTruncatedOnce` warns once the first time a real proposal's
graffiti is actually truncated.

## Changes

- `cl/beacon/handler/block_production.go`:
`identificationSegment()`/`identificationSegmentFor()`,
`combinedGraffiti()` (prefix + truncate via `truncateAtRuneBoundary`),
`graffitiFromHex()` (right-padded hex decoding), `requestGraffiti()`
(dispatches on `PreserveGraffiti`), and the three logging functions
above.
- `cl/beacon/beacon_router_configuration/cfg.go`: new `PreserveGraffiti`
field on `RouterConfiguration`, already threaded into `ApiHandler`.
- `cmd/utils/flags.go`, `node/cli/default_flags.go`,
`cmd/caplin/caplinflags/flags.go`, `cmd/caplin/caplincli/config.go`,
`cmd/caplin/main.go`: CLI flag plumbing for both the main erigon binary
and the standalone `cmd/caplin` binary.
- `cmd/caplin/caplin1/run.go`: calls `LogGraffitiIdentification()` once
at Beacon API startup.
- `docs/site/docs/fundamentals/caplin.md` (+ regenerated
`llms-full.txt`): documents the flag and the default behavior.
- `ChangeLog.md`: breaking-change entry for v3.8.0.
- Test fixtures in `block_production_graffiti_test.go` that mock "the
connected execution client" now use Erigon's own `EG` client code
instead of `GE` (Geth), since these tests exercise Caplin's own
default-graffiti mechanism — `TestGraffitiClientCode`, which tests the
generic code-clamping utility on arbitrary strings, is left with its
`GE`/`GETH` example since that's illustrating the clamp behavior, not
simulating a paired client.

## Test plan

EL-unavailable consensus-only segment, UTF-8 rune-boundary truncation,
non-UTF-8 graffiti, an invalid byte within budget not mistaken for a
split rune), `graffitiFromHex`, `requestGraffiti` (default combine vs.
`PreserveGraffiti` opt-out),
`LogGraffitiIdentification`/`logGraffitiIdentificationOnce` (fires at
most once each), and `warnGraffitiTruncatedOnce` (fires at most once).
- [x] `TestGetEthV3ValidatorBlockKeepsSelfBuildEnvelopeByBlockRoot` now
also asserts on the produced block's actual `Body.Graffiti`, exercising

`combinedGraffiti`), not just those functions directly.

previously never touched the execution client; updated them to seed a

author: Kewei
subject: cl/beacon/handler: fix PTC duties dependent root and fork-epoch duties (#24393)
body:
Fixes #24116.

## Summary

Two fixes to `POST /eth/v1/validator/duties/ptc/{epoch}`, so that a
validator client refetches PTC duties exactly when they change.

### 1. Use the PTC shuffling-dependent root

The endpoint returned the proposer dependent root
(`epoch*SLOTS_PER_EPOCH - 1`), read from a second head-state view. The
[Beacon
API](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/blob/master/apis/validator/duties/ptc.yaml)
defines it as `get_block_root_at_slot(state,
compute_start_slot_at_epoch(epoch - 1) - 1)`, or the genesis block root
on underflow. This is the attester arithmetic, and it must equal
`current_epoch_dependent_root` / `next_epoch_dependent_root` of
`head_v2`.

Effects of the old root:
- at Gloas genesis, the next-epoch request returned 404;
- the root for a fixed next epoch changed on every head update, so
validator clients downloaded the duties again without a reorg.

The handler now uses `computeDependentRootSlot(epoch, S, true)` and
computes the root and the duties in one `viewHeadStateWithIdentity`
callback. A failed root lookup is unreachable for the admitted epochs
and now returns 500 instead of the undeclared 404.

### 2. Do not serve fork-epoch PTC duties from a pre-Gloas head

While the head is still in epoch `F-1` (`F = GLOAS_FORK_EPOCH`), a
request for epoch `F` was answered by `ComputePTC` on the Fulu state.
That prediction is not final. `upgrade_to_gloas` builds the PTC for `F`
with `initialize_ptc_window` after `process_epoch` of `F-1`, and
`compute_balance_weighted_selection` uses the effective balances updated
there. The Beacon API root for epoch `F` is `(F-1)*S-1`, and it stays
the same across the fork. So a validator client that cached the
predicted duties never refetches them, and can act on wrong PTC duties
for the whole first Gloas epoch.

The endpoint now returns 503 for a pre-Gloas head. The existing guards
already limit requests to `GLOAS_FORK_EPOCH <= epoch <=
current_epoch+1`, so this only affects the fork epoch while the head is
before the fork. From the first Gloas head onwards, the duties come from
`ptc_window`. Returning an empty duty list would be worse: the client
would cache it under the same root and miss epoch `F`.

This 503 is a deliberate choice that the Beacon API does not describe.
It matters for the Sepolia Glamsterdam fork (epoch 353024).

Consequences for validator clients:
- during epoch `F-1`, a validator client logs failed PTC duty requests
for epoch `F` (for example `Failed to download PTC duties` in the
Lighthouse VC) and retries on the next slot;
- PTC members of the first Gloas slot learn their duty only after the
first Gloas block is imported, because the head stays pre-Gloas until
then.

Other clients behave in a similar way: Nimbus also returns 503 from a
pre-Gloas head, and the Lighthouse BN returns 500 from a Fulu head
because its `get_ptc` needs `ptc_window`. Prysm returns 200 with an
empty list, which is the caching problem described above.

## Tests

- `TestPostPtcDutiesDependentRootAtGloasGenesis`: head at slot 0, epochs
0 and 1 return the genesis root. On the old code, epoch 1 returned 404.
- `TestPostPtcDutiesDependentRootAtEpochOne`: head in epoch 1 at a slot
> 0 returns the slot-0 root, equal to `head_v2`.
- `TestPostPtcDutiesDependentRootMatchesHeadV2`: current and next epoch
roots equal `head_v2` and the Beacon API formula.
- `TestPostPtcDutiesDependentRootUnchangedWithinEpoch`: head advancement
within an epoch keeps both roots unchanged.
- `TestPostPtcDutiesForkEpochUnavailableBeforeGloasHead`: a populated
pre-Gloas head returns 503 for the fork epoch, where the old code
returned 200 with predicted duties; a Gloas head then returns 200.

All tests were checked to fail against the pre-fix production code, or
against the targeted mutation, for the intended reason.

## Validation

- `go test ./cl/beacon/handler ./cl/beacon/beaconevents -count=1`
- `make lint` (two clean passes)
- `make erigon integration`

author: Kewei
subject: cl/clparams, cl/spectest: set PAYLOAD_DUE_BPS to 5000 and check mainnet config against spec fixtures (#24420)
body:
## Summary

consensus-specs
[#5414](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5414) (released
in v1.7.0-alpha.12) changed `PAYLOAD_DUE_BPS` from 7500 to 5000, which
moves the payload deadline to 50% of the slot. Caplin still uses 7500.

Caplin uses this value in three places:
- the PTC `payload_present` deadline in `GET
/eth/v1/validator/payload_attestation_data`;
- the builder handoff deadline;
- the dev validator's envelope deadline.

With 7500, Caplin reports envelopes first seen between 6 s and 9 s into
the slot as present. Spec-compliant clients report them as absent.
Sepolia activates Gloas at epoch 353024 (2026-10-06 13:53 UTC), so this
also needs a backport to `release/3.7`.

## Why the spec tests did not catch it

The CL fixtures are pinned at v1.7.0-beta.2, which already has the new
value. The spectest harness overlays each fixture's `config.yaml` onto
Erigon's config, so the cases never see Caplin's built-in defaults. No
state-transition case depends on this value.

## Changes

- `cl/clparams/config.go`: `PayloadDueBps` 7500 -> 5000.
- `cl/spectest/mainnet_config_test.go`: a new subtest,
`Test/mainnet_config`.
- It builds the spec mainnet config from the pinned fixtures. Per key it
takes the value most `config.yaml` files agree on, ignores
`*_FORK_EPOCH`, and fails on a tie.
- It compares that config with `MainnetBeaconConfig` and the mainnet
`NetworkConfig`.
- Spec keys without a Caplin config field must be listed explicitly:
`hardcoded` (Caplin's value is compared) or `notCompared`. Any other key
fails, so a new spec key needs an explicit decision.
- It runs inside the existing `Test`, so it has the same
`ERIGON_SKIP_CL_SPECTEST` gate and CI's `-run=/mainnet/` selects it.
- `cl/beacon/handler/epbs_test.go`: the payload attestation deadline
test now uses the default config (6 s boundary). It also has one case
with a non-default `PayloadDueBps`, to check that the endpoint reads the
configured value.

`MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` is excluded from the comparison: Caplin uses 15 MiB,
the spec 10 MiB. This is tracked in #24417.

## Testing

- **TDD:** before the fix, the new subtest failed with `PAYLOAD_DUE_BPS:
Erigon 7500, spec 5000`. The handler test fails with 7500, and also with
5000 hardcoded in `epbs.go`.
- **Mutation checks:** each of these makes the subtest fail:
  - changing a hardcoded constant such as `PayloadAttestationDueBps`;
  - removing a key from `notCompared`;
  - disabling the tie check.
- **Checks run:**
  - `make lint`
  - `make erigon integration`
  - `cd cl/spectest && make mainnet`
- the tests in `cl/clparams`, `cl/beacon/handler`, `cl/validator`,
`cl/phase1/forkchoice` and `cl/spectest`

author: Chase Wright
subject: cl/utils/eth_clock: encode ENR next_fork_epoch as little-endian (#24405)
body:
`ForkId()` writes `next_fork_epoch` in the ENR `eth2` field with
`binary.BigEndian`. The [p2p-interface
spec](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/82b6e507dc31f6f7052e79b16ecfe3778c1b38f6/specs/phase0/p2p-interface.md#eth2-field)
defines the value as an SSZ-encoded `ENRForkID`, and an SSZ `uint64` is
[little-endian](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/802485ec74a6986542bd53bf153189623aab440c/ssz/simple-serialize.md#uintn).

The bug does not show while no fork is scheduled, because
`FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH` (`0xffffffffffffffff`) is the same in both byte
orders.

Decoded from the `eth2` field of a live Caplin v3.7.0 (`bdc78cc4`) node
on Sepolia:

| field | value |
|---|---|
| fork_digest | `0x74d01459` |
| next_fork_version | `0x90000076` (Gloas, correct) |
| next_fork_epoch bytes | `00 00 00 00 00 05 63 00` |
| expected bytes for epoch 353024 | `00 63 05 00 00 00 00 00` |

A spec-compliant decoder reads the advertised epoch as
`27871520252493824`, not `353024`. A crawler of the Sepolia network sees
this on all 25 Caplin v3.7.0 nodes that it found. Prysm, Teku, Lodestar,
and Nimbus nodes in the same crawl encode the epoch in little-endian
order.

Caplin never decodes the `eth2` value of a peer (the only uses of
`Eth2key` are the two `node.Set` calls in `cl/p2p/p2p.go`). Thus this PR
changes only the encoder. The fork digest does not change, so gossip
topics and Status handshakes are not affected.

`TestForkIdNextForkEpochIsLittleEndian` schedules Gloas at epoch
`0x0102030405` on a copy of the Chiado config and checks the exact
bytes. Before the change, it fails with `actual: 00 00 00 01 02 03 04
05`. The existing `TestForkIdNextForkVersionWithoutScheduledFork` now
also decodes in little-endian order. It checks only `FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH`,
so it could not find this bug.

author: Andrew Ashikhmin
subject: cl/services: handle local block errors and back off retries (#23646)
body:
Fix failure handling in the existing beacon-block scheduler:

- Treat local block-index read/write failures as gossip `IGNORE` and
retain blocks for retry, instead of penalizing the sender. Warn once per
queued job for these failures. Canceled block-index reads or initial
block writes still return gossip `IGNORE` and retain the block for
retry, without storage-failure warnings or new backoff. After a
successful import, warn on finalized-index write failures other than
caller cancellation, without rejecting the block.
- Do not queue blocks ignored before signature verification.
- Back off queued `ErrNewPayloadNoStatus` failures from 250 ms to 2 s.
The same backoff covers local block-index read/write failures in
block-only imports, but not storage errors in publication callbacks. The
first queued attempt stays on the normal 50 ms tick. Other dependency
failures retain the fast retry cadence without resetting the accumulated
retry backoff.

Retry backoff is scoped to each store generation. A newer publication
callback resets the retry deadline and delay; ordinary duplicates and
stale schedules preserve them.

Publication waiters, 30-second expiry and `block_gossip` timing remain
unchanged. No shared-queue migration or capacity limit is introduced.

TDD was skipped for behavior-preserving refactors and comment changes;
existing service tests, including race tests, were used for those edits.
The log-only cancellation guard intentionally has no log-capture test;
existing cancellation and finalized-index tests were used instead.

---------

Co-authored-by: Alex Sharov <AskAlexSharov@gmail.com>

author: Andrew Ashikhmin
subject: cl: schedule Sepolia's 200M gas limit at Glamsterdam (#24395)
body:
Schedule Sepolia's default gas-limit target at **200,000,000 from epoch
353024**, implementing
[eth-clients/sepolia#130](https://github.com/eth-clients/sepolia/pull/130).

Caplin now reads and exposes `GAS_LIMIT_SCHEDULE` and selects the active
entry using the proposal epoch. Local payload construction and builder
bid selection use the scheduled target, with matching signed proposer
preferences taking precedence, including values below or above the
schedule. The payload-attributes event at the Gloas boundary also
advertises the scheduled target. The actual block gas limit follows the
existing gradual adjustment rule.

Empty schedules are serialized as `[]` for validator-client
compatibility. Custom config loading normalizes blank or null YAML
schedules to an empty slice.

Tests cover empty and populated schedules, omitted, blank, null, and
empty-array custom YAML values, the pre-Gloas guard, and proposer
precedence. A later-Gloas regression test uses a Gloas base state and
checks that the 200M scheduled target overrides a 60M parent bid. TDD
was used for the API regression; the test split and comment
clarification are refactoring/documentation exceptions.

author: Sahil Sojitra
subject: db: remove unused function parameters and dead code (#24375)
body:
Replaces the earlier blanket `_`-renaming approach for `db/` with actual
parameter removal: this only touches free functions/methods that aren't
bound to any interface or callback type (checked individually via `var _
Interface = ...` assertions, function-value passing, mock embedding,
etc.). Anything still required by an interface or callback signature
keeps its parameter name as-is, since Go only complains about unused
imports/locals, not unused parameters.

Also deletes a few methods that turned out to have zero callers anywhere
in the repo: `Aggregator.OpenList`, `SnapshotRepo.IntegrateMergedFiles`,
and four `MemoryMutation` stubs (`Last`, `Stream`, `StreamAscend`,
`StreamDescend`) that were just `panic("not implemented")`.

Verified with `go build ./...`, `go vet`, and the full test suite for
every touched package.

things found along the way that look like pre-existing issues, left out
of scope here:
- `PruneAncientBlocks`'s `timeout` param is required by the
`dbservices.BlockRetire` interface, but the implementation never
actually uses it, so callers' timeout values are silently dropped.

author: lystopad
subject: cl/beacon/handler: publish blobs from the request on a node that did not produce the block (#24404)
body:
Fixes #23112.

## Problem

`POST /eth/v{1,2}/beacon/blocks` decodes the block together with its
`blobs` and `kzg_proofs`, but the broadcast builds sidecars only from
the node's `blobBundles` cache. That cache holds only bundles the node
produced itself. A validator client that publishes to several beacon
nodes therefore gets 500 `missing blob bundle for commitment …` from
every node except the one that built the block. This affects blocks with
blobs, both before Fulu (blob sidecars) and from Fulu on (data column
sidecars).

## Fix

`postBeaconBlocks` builds the blob bundles for the block with
`requestBlobBundles` and passes them to the broadcast, which uses them
instead of the cache.

- Cheap checks run before any KZG work. The fork the request is labelled
with must match the block's slot. The number of commitments must be
within the limit gossip uses (`MaxBlobsPerBlockByVersion`, and from Fulu
on `GetBlobParameters(epoch)`). The numbers of blobs and proofs must
match the commitments: one proof per blob before Fulu,
`CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB` cell proofs per blob from Fulu on.
- A bundle the node already has is taken from the cache, unless its
proof count does not fit the block's fork. The remaining bundles come
from the request and are KZG-verified. From Fulu on the cells computed
for verification are kept on the bundle, so the column build does not
compute them again.
- Request data is never written to the cache. The block is validated
only later, and a rejected request must not leave data that a later
publish would use.
- A request that fails any of these checks gets 400. A request that has
blobs but no commitment list gets its own message. A request without
blobs, or without a block (for example JSON `"signed_block": null`),
behaves as before.
- Gloas is not affected: its blobs travel in the execution payload
envelope, not in the block request.

`blobBundleCacheSize` now sizes the cache for two full blocks at the
highest blob limit in the schedule (`MaxBlobsPerBlockUpperBound`), with
the previous 48 as a minimum. Above 48 blobs a block would evict its own
bundles before it is published.

Behaviour changes:
- The producing node now returns 400 for a request whose blob or proof
counts do not match the commitments, or whose fork does not match its
slot. Before, it ignored the request's blobs. It still does not verify
the request's copy of a blob it has cached, so a bad proof for such a
blob gets 200 on the producing node and 400 on other nodes. The node
publishes its own, correct copy either way.
- The KZG work runs before block validation. Block validation happens
inside the broadcast, under the payload-preparation gate, and while the
gate is held, speculative payload preparation is skipped. Verifying
there would hold the gate about 200 ms longer. The blob limit bounds the
cost of a request whose block is then rejected.
- Verification cost on a node that did not produce the block, for 21
blobs on a 16-core machine: about 13 ms for Electra and about 220 ms for
Fulu. The Fulu column build then takes about 40 µs, since it reuses the
cells.

## Tests

`cl/beacon/handler/block_production_request_blobs_test.go`, with real
KZG data:

- Through `PostEthV2BeaconBlocks`, on a node with an empty cache:
- Electra, SSZ and JSON: the blob sidecar with the request's blob,
commitment and proof is published. Before the fix this returns 500
`missing blob bundle`.
- Fulu: all 128 data columns are published, and each passes
`VerifyDataColumnSidecarKZGProofs`.
- A block that fails validation gets 400. Nothing is published or
cached.
- A Fulu-slot block labelled `electra` gets 400. Nothing is published or
cached.
- `requestBlobBundles`:
- valid Electra and Fulu bundles are returned, with the Fulu cells kept,
and nothing is cached
- a cached bundle is used even when the request carries a bad proof for
it
- a cached bundle with the wrong proof count for the fork is replaced by
the verified request copy
  - a fork that does not match the slot is rejected
- at the edges: the last Electra slot and the first Fulu slot, both ways
round, and the blob limit right before and at a blob schedule entry
  - blobs without a commitment list get their own error
- too many commitments are rejected before verification, both for the
Electra limit and for a Fulu blob schedule limit
  - a missing proof or blob is rejected
  - one bad proof rejects the whole request
  - a missing block is left to block validation, with no panic
- `collectPublishedPayloadData` reuses cells kept on a bundle, and
`blobBundleCacheSize` follows the blob schedule.

Each behaviour was checked by mutation. Each of the following makes a
test fail:
- removing the fork check, the blob limit, the Fulu schedule limit, the
nil guard, the count check, or verification
- computing the epoch one slot early or late, `>=` for the limit, or
reading the schedule for the previous epoch
- writing request bundles to the cache
- using a cached bundle with the wrong proof count
- ignoring the request bundles in the broadcast
- not keeping or not reusing cells
- one proof per blob on Fulu, a wrong cell index, or verifying only the
first cell
- sizing the cache for one block

`go test -race ./cl/beacon/handler/...`, `go build ./...`, `make lint`
and `make lintci` pass.

The same code is on release/3.7 and release/3.6, so both need backports.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/phase1/stages, cl/phase1/forkchoice: replay persisted Gloas parent payloads (#24274)
body:
## Summary

- recover retained FULL-parent Gloas envelopes during a later chain-tip
batch when the parent payload has no usable EL verdict
- replay the stored payload to the EL with one bounded budget per batch,
split fairly across the parent roots that FULL children in the batch
actually need and that need an EL call, and deduplicate sibling retries
- preserve EMPTY-branch progress when a FULL sibling's parent replay
fails, and never reserve replay budget for EMPTY children
- do not record a `None` status when the replay budget or context runs
out before the EL answers, so a locally available parent is not marked
unavailable
- preserve no-EL, known-status, validation-error, and pruning behavior

## Context

Within a running Caplin process, a stored FULL parent can still have
payload status `None` when a chain-tip batch reaches its child: the
earlier EL call failed or timed out, and the regular pending retry has
not repaired it yet (the entry is still queued behind others, the
per-cycle retry budget ran out, or the entry was dropped at the
pending-queue cap). `validateParentPayloadPath` then rejects the child
with `ErrParentEnvelopePending` in every batch, and chain-tip sync
previously skipped the stored envelope, so nothing replayed it while the
node was behind the tip.

The retained-root payload status itself lives in the fork graph, so this
is not about losing the verdict cache. SYNCING/ACCEPTED map to
`NotValidated` and are accepted optimistically; only a missing verdict
blocks the child.

This PR is intentionally scoped to same-process retries while the parent
graph entry remains retained. It does not provide process-restart
recovery: production startup clears the temporary `caplin-forkchoice`
directory and reconstructs an empty envelope index. Durable restart
recovery and the separate block-collector catch-up changes investigated
on Glamsterdam Devnet 8 remain outside this PR.

The per-batch body of `listenToIncomingBlocksUntilANewBlockIsReceived`
is extracted into `processChainTipBatch` without behavior changes so the
full batch sequence can be tested.

## Fork-choice changes

- `markPayloadStatus` no longer takes the fork graph's `lifecycleMu`
read lock a second time when it invalidates descendants inside an outer
`WithRetainedBlock` call. A nested `RLock` on a `sync.RWMutex` can
deadlock when a writer (pruning) waits between the two acquisitions. For
this, `WithRetainedBlock` now passes the retention check to its
callback: `WithRetainedBlock(root common.Hash, fn func(isRetained
func(common.Hash) bool)) bool`. All implementations and callers are
updated.
- `MarkPayloadStatusAndGasLimitIfRetained` records the payload status
and the gas limit under one retained-root guard. The no-engine apply
path now also records the gas limit when it marks a payload
`NotValidated`, so bid validation on no-EL nodes finds the parent gas
limit.

## Testing

- `go test ./cl/phase1/forkchoice/... ./cl/phase1/stages -count=1`
- `TestStoredParentReplayRootsExcludeEmptyChildren` fails without the
`parentEnvelopeRequired` filter in `storedParentReplayRoots` (EMPTY
child's parent counted) and passes with it
- `TestChainTipBatchReplaysStoredParentPayload` drives
`processChainTipBatch` with a real `ForkChoiceStore`: VALID replay
unblocks the FULL child, a missing verdict keeps it for retry, and the
EMPTY sibling progresses in both orders; it fails when the replay gate
is disabled
- `TestChainTipBatchReplayBudgetSkipsParentsWithUsableVerdict` fails
when a parent with a usable verdict takes a replay budget slot
- `TestOnExecutionPayloadWithoutEngineMarksPayloadOptimistic` fails when
the no-engine apply path does not record the gas limit
- `TestStoredParentPayloadReplayWithoutVerdictKeepsStatus` fails without
the context checks in `ensureStoredParentPayloadAccepted` (EL called
with a spent budget; `None` recorded after the deadline) and passes with
them
- `go test -race ./cl/phase1/stages -run
'TestStoredParent|TestParentEnvelopeRequired|TestEnsureStoredParent|TestChainTipBatch|TestGloasPayloadRetry|TestDrainPendingGloasPayloads'
-count=1`
- `make lint` (clean)
- `go build ./cmd/erigon ./cmd/integration`

The branch has not been separately deployed as a full-node replacement.

author: Andrew Ashikhmin
subject: cl/services: harden deferred Gloas data-column sidecars (#23645)
body:
Use the shared bounded queue for Gloas data-column sidecars awaiting
their block. Keep the existing 4,096-entry limit, 24-second expiry, and
500 ms retry interval.

- Store sidecars directly, keyed by their full SSZ root, so an
unverified candidate cannot suppress a different candidate for the same
block and column through deduplication.
- Check the subnet before queue admission. Bound column/proof lengths
and check block-independent structure before hashing or retaining a
sidecar. Failed admission preserves the missing-block gossip `IGNORE`
verdict.
- Queue only at gossip ingress. Retain the original entry and expiry
when processing reports a missing block. Remove expired or finalized
entries and entries whose processing succeeds or returns a terminal
result. Retries neither re-enqueue nor infer the error from a later
block lookup.
- Keep per-sidecar queue-full diagnostics alongside the shared rejection
counter. Fulu validation is unchanged.

Regression tests cover admission bounds, processing at the blob limit,
content deduplication, subnet checks, changing block availability,
original expiry, capacity, and finalized/expired removal. TDD was used
for the retry and admission fixes; it was skipped for comments,
behavior-preserving cleanup, and restoring Fulu behavior, using existing
tests for those edits.

Closes #24398. Deferred candidate-flooding protection and peer penalties
after deferred validation are tracked separately in #24416.

author: Andrew Ashikhmin
subject: cl/p2p: allocate test listener ports per transport (#24475)
body:
The partial-startup tests reused a port selected for TCP as a UDP port,
and vice versa. If the other protocol could not bind that number, libp2p
failed before Erigon reached the partial-startup check. This caused the
Windows failure in [the merge-queue run for
#23645](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/actions/runs/36835801159/job/110282830672).

Probe the unblocked transport with its own protocol and release the
probe immediately before startup. Both tests keep the occupied listener,
the specific startup-error assertion, the nil-manager assertion, and the
check that the successful listener was closed. This changes only test
setup.

TDD used the existing tests: a temporary fault-injection overlay
reproduced the merge-queue error before the fix, and both tests passed
with the same injected conflicts after the fix.

author: Andrew Ashikhmin
subject: execution, cl: share assembled payload conversions (#24477)
body:
Embedded Caplin and the Engine API kept separate block-to-payload
mappings. #24453 fixed a mismatch between them. Share
`ExecutionPayloadFromBlock` and the CL conversion
`ExecutionPayload.ToEth1Block` through `engine_types`, so both paths use
the same mappings.

Addresses the [follow-up review on
#24453](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/24453#pullrequestreview-5376920986).
The chain reader keeps its existing empty extra-data and withdrawal
containers.

Move the BAL conversion tests next to the shared helper and keep caller
integration tests in place. Add a direct hash round-trip test with
populated fields, including legacy and typed transactions, withdrawals,
and BAL.

`ToEth1Block` now rejects a nil beacon config before constructing the CL
block and uses the configured limits directly. Its regression test was
verified red → green for Phase0 and Gloas. TDD was skipped for the pure
refactor; the hash round-trip test was checked by omitting transactions
and clearing withdrawal amounts.

author: Andrew Ashikhmin
subject: cl, ci: test Caplin block production and blob publication (#24543)
body:
Add a generic embedded Caplin block-production integration test for
Pectra, Fusaka, and Glamsterdam. Submit an ETH transfer and a blob
transaction carrying two real blobs to Erigon's transaction pool. Build
through Caplin's direct execution client, then validate and import the
payload in a second Erigon execution instance. Check transaction
inclusion, blob gas, returned blobs and commitments, the canonical head,
and the recipient's balance.

Publish the built block through a second Caplin handler with an empty
blob cache. Pectra and Fusaka supply blobs in the block request;
Glamsterdam supplies them in a separate execution-payload envelope.
Verify the published blob/data-column sidecars, KZG proofs, inclusion
proofs where applicable, block references, and complete column count.
The handler uses the existing mocked consensus-validation and gossip
services; execution and KZG verification are real.

Wire the existing Caplin-only Glamsterdam transition config into the
main Kurtosis matrix with the CI-built image, in both serial and
parallel commitment modes. The Assertoor test starts at the fork epoch,
requires three fresh Caplin proposals with execution payloads, and
checks execution head progress. CI loads the playbook from the PR
commit, including for fork PRs. Use a separate QUIC port because the
pinned package launcher uses port 4001 for discovery. Blob coverage is
in the Go integration test.

Validation:

- Red for #24404: a temporary Go overlay disables forwarding request
blob bundles to the broadcast, restoring publication from the local
cache only. Pectra and Fusaka fail with HTTP 500 `missing blob bundle`;
Glamsterdam passes.
- Red for #24453: temporary Go overlays independently clear `SlotNumber`
or `BlockAccessList` from the assembled payload. Each makes Glamsterdam
fail during payload import with `cannot derive rlp header: mismatching
hash`; Pectra and Fusaka pass. The conversion now lives in
`engine_types.ExecutionPayloadFromBlock` and
`ExecutionPayload.ToEth1Block` after #24477.
- The updated Go integration test passes for all three forks. `make
lint`, `make erigon integration`, and `actionlint` pass.
- A shell check reproduces the redundant pull before the cache guard and
confirms that the updated step only pulls missing images.
- The gas-limit fixture and fork-wait value are test setup changes; they
use existing checks instead of a separate TDD cycle.
- Both Caplin Kurtosis jobs pass on `5cc6d2b81d`:
[serial](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/actions/runs/37196949891/job/111422421144)
and
[parallel](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/actions/runs/37196949891/job/111422421195).
Both playbooks match slots 8, 9, and 10, including the first Gloas
block.

author: Alex Sharov
subject: execution/engineapi: payload bodies serve stored tx bytes and stream their JSON (#24220)
body:
engine_getPayloadBodiesByRange/ByHash V1 and V2 served each block by
decoding every stored transaction and re-encoding it (43% of CPU at
c64), then encoded the answer through reflection (21.5%); they now read
the stored bytes (unwrapping the RLP string a typed tx may be stored in)
and stream the JSON.

The stored record is checked for its framing only - the envelope, the
field count, and nothing trailing. The fields are not read, so this is
weaker than `DecodeTransaction`: a record framed as a transaction but
holding a non-canonical field is served as it is. `DumpTxs` decodes
every transaction before it writes a segment, so only a database record
written outside the normal write path can be in that state.

author: Andrew Ashikhmin
subject: cl/p2p: bound GossipSub control-message size to prevent IHAVE memory exhaustion (#24616)
body:
## Problem

Caplin raises the GossipSub frame cap to `GossipMaxSizeBellatrix` (15
MiB) for large beacon blocks. On `go-libp2p-pubsub` v0.11.0 that cap is
the only bound applied before a frame is decoded, and
`ControlIHave.Unmarshal` appends one Go `string` per message ID with no
count limit. The `handleIHave` guards run only after the decode. So an
unauthenticated peer (Caplin's listener binds `0.0.0.0:4001` when
embedded) can send one in-cap IHAVE frame carrying millions of
zero-length IDs and force unbounded allocation; a short burst OOM-kills
the process, taking the EL and embedded beacon node down together.

## Fix

Bump `go-libp2p-pubsub` to v0.17.0, which validates the raw
control-message size against a separate 512 KiB default *before*
unmarshalling, allocating nothing. The oversized frame now resets the
stream before any per-ID string exists. The default applies
automatically; control messages are small metadata, so 512 KiB is ample
while the 15 MiB cap still covers blocks and blobs.

**Scope:** this bounds control-message *bytes* to the upstream 512 KiB
default, which removes the reported unbounded, retained OOM. v0.17.0
exposes no per-record ID-*count* knob (`MaxIHaveLength` is a post-decode
handler guard), so a maximum-size control frame still incurs a bounded
(~262k IDs), transient, GC-collected decode — upstream's accepted
posture, not the reported crash.

`go mod tidy` drops `gogo/protobuf` (v0.17.0 moved to
`google.golang.org/protobuf`) and promotes `go-msgio` to direct (used by
the test).

## Test

`TestPubsubRejectsOversizedIHave` sends an IHAVE frame under the 15 MiB
cap but over the 512 KiB budget to a node built from Caplin's own
`pubsubOptions`, and asserts the stream is reset instead of the RPC
being delivered to the pubsub event loop. It fails on v0.11.0 (frame
decoded and delivered) and passes on v0.17.0.

Existing `cl/p2p`, `cl/sentinel`, `cl/phase1/network/gossip` and
`txnprovider/shutter` tests pass; binaries link; lint is clean on the
changed package.

## Backports

Present on maintained release lines (reported against v3.6.1), which
also pin v0.11.0. A backport per `release/*` line is warranted as a
follow-up.

Addresses ethereum-bounty/erigon#39
