`TestVerifyUnverifiedGloasPayloadsDoesNotRecordTimeoutAsVerdict` failed
(a status was recorded) without the timeout guard.
`TestForwardSyncFlushesBlockCollectorAfterInsertion` failed (no flush)
without the flush in `forwardSync`.
`TestVerifyUnverifiedGloasPayloadsChecksDirectExtensionWithEmptyCursor`
failed (no `NewPayload` call for the new head) without the new-head
check.
- Devnet with the restart fault (setup below):
- Fix 1: in one run the restarted node's ForwardSync took two minutes
and its first ChainTipSync timed out; the timeout now went to
ForkChoice, and attestation data moved off the genesis root right away
instead of waiting for a block of the current slot. In embedded mode the
hop straight after ForwardSync failed once (`block ... not found`),
because ForwardSync's blocks reached the EL only when ChainTipSync
flushed them, and the next cycle published the head; ForwardSync now
attempts that flush itself before it returns.
- Fix 2: in a run with both fixes, the first ChainTipSync cycle after
ForwardSync re-verified one stored envelope and the node followed the
head from then on; the network finalized, and at the slot-170 check all
five nodes had the same block roots for slots 160-169. Without fix 2 the
same restart stayed on the EMPTY parent for about 60 slots.
- The devnet runs predate the follow-up commits; the zero-peer
ForwardSync transition, the at-target retry, the ForwardSync flush, the
execution-engine readiness check before the sweep, the timeout guard and
the new-head check are covered by unit tests only.
- `make lint`
- `make erigon integration`
- `go test ./cl/phase1/stages/...`

## Devnet

Devnet used below: a local Kurtosis network with Lighthouse v8.3.0-rc.0
(beacon node and VCs), Teku 26.9.1, Prysm v7.2.0 and two Caplin nodes on
v3.7.1 plus this change (one as a separate `caplin` service, one
embedded in Erigon), 128 validators per participant (Caplin 40%), Fulu
at genesis, Gloas at epoch 2, and spamoor sending transactions and
blobs. Fault runs also skipped the proposals of slots 64 and 65 and
restarted the embedded Erigon at slot 67. Every run used one image with
all the fixes in this series, so the runs show the combined effect, not
one PR in isolation.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/beacon/handler: fix the Gloas attestation data index and pool attestation publishing (#24547)
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes two attestation bugs.

1. **Gloas attestation data index.** In Gloas, `attestation_data.index`
tells fork choice whether the attested block's payload is canonical: 0
for a block of the attestation slot, otherwise 1 when the validator's
fork choice has the block FULL and 0 when EMPTY. Caplin returned 0 for
every Electra-or-later request, so after a missed slot its validators
voted EMPTY for blocks whose payload was present. In a devnet every
attestation the Caplin validators published after the Gloas fork had
index 0. For a block from an earlier slot, `GET
/eth/v1/validator/attestation_data` now sets the index from the payload
status the fork choice head's chain gives that block: the head node
itself, or the head's ancestor at that slot, since attestation data is
cached per slot and can name an ancestor of the current head. Caplin's
fork choice also makes a block FULL when its payload is optimistic (not
yet verified by the EL). The endpoint should return neither index for
such a block: index 0 would vote for the EMPTY node against the node's
own fork choice, and a node that has not verified the payload, including
this one, ignores an index-1 attestation for it. So the endpoint returns
503 for an earlier-slot block that the head's chain has FULL while its
payload is not verified. The Beacon API separately requires a 503
whenever the response `beacon_block_root` is optimistic; this PR does
not add that general check.
2. **Pool attestations the node ignored were still published.** `POST
/eth/v1/beacon/pool/attestations` and `/eth/v2/beacon/pool/attestations`
published an attestation even when the attestation service returned
`ErrIgnore` for it (v2 logged it, v1 treated it as success). The gossip
layer accepts the node's own messages without validating them again, so
peers received attestations this node had ignored. In a devnet a
restarted Caplin served attestation data from a stale head; its own
validation ignored the result (`head epoch 0 too far from attestation
epoch 2`), but it published it, and Lighthouse banned the node less than
half a second later (`AttesterNotInCommittee`). Ignored attestations are
no longer published. Except for `ErrAttestationAlreadySeen`, they return
indexed failures instead of a silent 200, as the Beacon API specifies,
and are logged at Debug. An attestation already seen from the same
validator for the same target epoch returns success without being
published again: that check runs before the signature check and is keyed
only by validator and target epoch, so the signature and later checks do
not run and the submission is not fully validated.

Because ignored attestations other than already-seen ones now fail, the
epoch check must not reject valid ones. When no block arrives for a
whole epoch, the head stays in epoch E while the clock reaches E+2, and
the service admitted at most E+1. It now admits E+2 when fork choice has
seen no block at a later slot than the head: the committees of E+2 use
the RANDAO mix of epoch E, which is final once E has ended if the head
state holds every block of E. A head state whose slot is behind fork
choice's highest seen slot, as when ForwardSync serves the anchor head
after importing later blocks, stays limited to E+1, so the stale-head
case above is still not published. At a fork boundary such an
attestation still fails, because the signing domain comes from the head
state's fork; that already applies to E+1 and is left for a separate
fix.

## Changes

- `cl/beacon/handler/block_production.go`: `gloasAttestationIndex`; 503
for an earlier-slot block that the head's chain has FULL while its
payload is not verified; the index is set once for cached and produced
attestation data.
- `cl/beacon/handler/pool.go`: publish only attestations that pass
validation; already-seen ones succeed without publishing; other ignored
ones are indexed failures logged at Debug.
- `cl/phase1/network/services`: `ErrAttestationAlreadySeen` for the
already-seen case; `validationEpochRange` admits head epoch + 2 when
fork choice has seen no block at a later slot than the head state.

## Testing

- **TDD:** `TestGetEthV1ValidatorAttestationDataGloasPayloadIndex`
covers an earlier-slot FULL head, an earlier-slot FULL ancestor of the
head, and their FULL-but-unverified variants, which return 503 through
the handler's cache-hit and cache-miss paths (with a stub producer). Its
two earlier-slot verified FULL cases fail on main, and its
FULL-but-unverified cases fail when the handler returns 200 with index
0. `TestPoolAttestationsDoNotPublishIgnored` covers the v1 and v2
handlers with mocked service results: an already-seen error returns 200
without publishing, and stale-head and invalid-signature errors return
400 without publishing. Its stale-head cases fail on main, and its
already-seen cases fail if the handler publishes on
`ErrAttestationAlreadySeen`.
`TestAttestation/TestAttestationProcessMessageAllowsSecondEpochWhenNoLaterBlockSeen`
checks that head epoch + 2 is accepted when no later block was seen, and
that head epoch + 3, or head epoch + 2 after a block past the head was
seen, is still ignored; its first check fails without the
`validationEpochRange` change.
`TestAttestation/TestAttestationSeenOnlyAfterSignatureVerification` now
checks `ErrAttestationAlreadySeen`.
- Devnet with the restart fault (setup below): Lighthouse applied no
`attn_single_not_in_committee` penalty to Caplin, compared with 9 in a
run without this change and without the head publication fix. The devnet
runs predate the 503 for unverified payloads, the already-seen change
and the head epoch + 2 validation.
- `make lint`
- `make erigon integration`
- `go test ./cl/beacon/handler/... ./cl/phase1/network/services/...
./cl/phase1/forkchoice/...`

## Devnet

Devnet used in the testing above: a local Kurtosis network with
Lighthouse v8.3.0-rc.0 (beacon node and VCs), Teku 26.9.1, Prysm v7.2.0
and two Caplin nodes on v3.7.1 plus this change (one as a separate
`caplin` service, one embedded in Erigon), 128 validators per
participant (Caplin 40%), Fulu at genesis, Gloas at epoch 2, and spamoor
sending transactions and blobs. Fault runs also skipped the proposals of
slots 64 and 65 and restarted the embedded Erigon at slot 67. Every run
used one image with all the fixes in this series at the time of the run,
so the runs show the combined effect, not one PR in isolation.

author: Kewei
subject: cl: fix publication of self-built Gloas blocks and payloads (#24545)
body:
## Summary

Three problems made Caplin lose its own Gloas blocks or their payloads
around and after the fork. Nine of the eleven commits address them. Five
mainly address the first problem (one of them is a refactor and one only
changes test timing), two the second, and two the third (one only
corrects code comments). The other two commits add an exception to the
envelope-by-root endpoint and then revert it, so that endpoint is
unchanged from main (see "Not changed here").

1. **Synced head lagged fork choice within a slot.** In Gloas the fork
choice head can move to another block without a new block arriving
(attestations move it, or an envelope makes a child built on the FULL
parent reachable). `SleepForSlot` slept to the next slot, so the synced
head state, which block production and the beacon API read, stayed old.
The next proposer failed with `fork choice head changed: proposal parent
X, current head Y`. From Gloas, `SleepForSlot` now polls the cached fork
choice head every 200 ms and runs the ForkChoice stage when it differs
from the synced head; a head that the stage did not publish can wake it
again after a second. A poll that finds the head cache invalidated
recomputes the head under the fork choice lock; on mainnet attestations
invalidate it continuously, so the interval limits this loop to about
five recomputations a second. The head changes it is for (attestations,
the payload deadline, PTC votes) usually come seconds before the next
slot; one in the last 200 ms of a slot is still picked up by the
ForkChoice stage after the slot starts.
2. **Queued envelopes waited a slot for their columns.** An envelope
that arrives before its block's custody columns is queued, and once its
block was imported only chain tip sync retried the queue, once per slot.
Columns often complete seconds after the envelope, so the next proposer
saw the parent EMPTY, built on it, and was reorged by peers that applied
the payload. While `SleepForSlot` polls, it now retries, within the
slot, queued gossip envelopes of blocks from the head's slot or the
previous slot onward, whichever is earlier, whose column data is
available or that commit to no blobs: while a block's columns are
missing it checks their availability at most every 250 ms (about every
400 ms at the 200 ms poll), and it attempts to apply each envelope at
most once a second.
3. **Columns gossiped before the block was stored.** A Gloas data column
sidecar has no signed block header, and Lighthouse, on a column for an
unknown block, requests the block from the peer that sent it. Caplin
gossiped its columns while the block was still being stored and answered
`blocks_by_root` with nothing; Lighthouse scores that as a low-tolerance
error and banned both Caplin nodes around the fork. For a self-built
Gloas block with columns to gossip, the publisher now waits up to one
second for the local store before gossiping them. If the store fails or
is slower, the race remains: the columns are gossiped anyway, because
holding back the columns of an already gossiped block would make it
unavailable.

## Changes

- `cl/phase1/stages/sleep_for_slot.go`, `clstages.go`: head-change wake
and envelope retry in `SleepForSlot`. Before Gloas it still sleeps to
the next slot, but now returns when its context is cancelled.
- `cl/phase1/forkchoice/on_block.go`, `forkchoice.go`:
`RetryDataAvailablePendingExecutionPayloadEnvelopes` with per-envelope
pacing (tests in `on_execution_payload_test.go`).
- `cl/beacon/handler/block_production.go`: wait up to one second for a
self-built Gloas block's local store before gossiping its columns.

## Not changed here

- The poll runs only while `SleepForSlot` waits for the slot after the
highest seen block. If that slot's block is missing, the stage graph
runs ChainTipSync until a block of the current slot or a later slot
arrives, so a head change from attestations during a missed slot reaches
the synced head late, as on main.
- `SleepForSlot` runs `GetHead` and the envelope retry synchronously, so
one in-flight operation can run past the slot boundary. The retry walks
queued envelopes in cache order, not the head's first. The availability
check that runs under the fork choice lock is the same path gossip
envelopes and ChainTipSync retries take on main.
- The wake compares head roots only. If the head's envelope arrives
after the ForkChoice stage run by a wake has sent its forkchoice update,
the update with its payload hash is sent at the next slot, after
ChainTipSync waits for the head's envelope, as on main.
- After the fork choice head moves back to the parent of a self-built
block, or before it moves to the block, `GET
/eth/v1/validator/execution_payload_envelopes/{slot}/{beacon_block_root}`
returns 404 for the block's envelope, as on main. The Lighthouse VC
fetches the envelope only after `POST /eth/v2/beacon/blocks` succeeds,
and Caplin answers that call with 200 only after it has imported the
block (202 if it found the block invalid). In the devnet the head stayed
on the parent after the import, the VC got 404, never published the
envelope, and the block went out without its payload. Serving the
envelope while the head is the parent would also serve it for a block
that fork choice re-orged away from or that Caplin rejected, and the
Beacon API says that after a re-org between block production and
envelope retrieval the VC gets 404.

## Testing

- **Tests:** `sleep_for_slot_test.go` (wake on head change, re-wake
after the interval, queued-envelope retries invoked while polling),
`on_execution_payload_test.go` (retry once columns arrive, retry of a
zero-blob envelope after a failed store, back-off after a failed
attempt, probe pacing) and
`TestBroadcastGloasBlockPublishesColumnsAfterLocalStore`. The wake,
re-wake and retry tests call functions that are new in this PR, so they
do not compile against main; with main's behaviour emulated, the wake,
re-wake, retry-after-columns, probe-pacing and cancellation tests fail,
and the back-off test is a pacing guard. On main the column test fails
because broadcast gossips the columns before it waits for the local
store; here, with a fake store job, it sees no columns before the job
completes and 128 after. Commit e563825bbe4 restores main's
envelope-by-root handler and test unchanged, so it adds no test: the
existing cases of `TestGetValidatorExecutionPayloadEnvelopeByBlockRoot`
cover 404 for a root that is not the head. With the retry code of
e563825bbe4, which checked PeerDAS data availability before it applied
any queued envelope, the zero-blob retry test fails.
- Devnet (setup below), with the fixes up to 57fc712d075 and the restart
fault: the standalone Caplin logged no `fork choice head changed`; the
restarted embedded node logged it for slots 68 and 69, while it was
still catching up after the restart.
- `make lint`
- `make erigon integration`
- `go test ./cl/beacon/handler/... ./cl/phase1/forkchoice/...
./cl/phase1/stages/...`

## Devnet

Devnet used below: a local Kurtosis network with Lighthouse v8.3.0-rc.0
(beacon node and VCs), Teku 26.9.1, Prysm v7.2.0 and two Caplin nodes on
v3.7.1 plus this change (one as a separate `caplin` service, one
embedded in Erigon), 128 validators per participant (Caplin 40%), Fulu
at genesis, Gloas at epoch 2, and spamoor sending transactions and
blobs. Fault runs also skipped the proposals of slots 64 and 65 and
restarted the embedded Erigon at slot 67. Every run used one image with
all the fixes in this series at that time, so the runs show the combined
effect, not one PR in isolation. The runs predate the last five commits
of this PR, from 612c183355b on: they also served a self-built envelope
whenever the head was its parent, which e563825bbe4 reverts.

author: Kewei
subject: cl: fix req/resp concurrency, chain tip request pacing, BlocksByRange range and sidecar finalized slot checks (#24550)
body:
## Summary

Five req/resp and sync fixes, one commit each (plus a test fix). This
combines the drafts #24513, #24514 and #24515 with a new concurrency cap
and chain tip poll pacing.

1. **Concurrent request cap.** The spec says a requester must not have
more than `MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS` (2) open streams with one peer for
one protocol, and lets the responder penalize extra ones. Caplin had no
bound: the column downloader starts a request every 100 ms, so after a
restart the embedded node opened many `data_column_sidecars_by_root`
streams to Lighthouse at once; Lighthouse rejected the third and later
ones (`already 2 active requests with the same protocol`, -5 each) and
banned the node. `requestPeer`, which every outgoing request goes
through except the one Status handshake per connection, now refuses a
third stream with `ErrPeerBusy`. Responders may penalise extra streams
per request type, so the cap counts streams per peer and request type,
and all versions of a request share it (for example
`beacon_blocks_by_range/2,beacon_blocks_by_range/1` and
`beacon_blocks_by_range/2` alone).
2. **Chain tip retry pacing (#24513).** `fetchBlocksFromReqResp` retried
at once after any error except `ErrNoPeers`, flooding rate-limiting
peers until the stage deadline. It now waits 300 ms between retries, as
forward sync does.
3. **BeaconBlocksByRange range (#24514).** The handler scanned 96 slots
and stopped after `count` blocks, so empty slots in `[start_slot,
start_slot+count)` were filled with blocks after the range, `count=0`
returned one block, and a block after the first 96 slots of a 128-slot
request was not found. It now searches `[start_slot,
start_slot+min(count, MAX_REQUEST_BLOCKS_DENEB))`, keeps the 96-block
response limit, and rejects a `start_slot+count` overflow with
`InvalidRequest`. `TestSentinelBlocksByRange` relied on the old behavior
and now requests the whole range.
4. **Fulu sidecar finalized slot (#24515).** `FinalizedSlot()` is the
last slot of the finalized epoch, but the spec ignores sidecars only up
to `compute_start_slot_at_epoch(finalized_checkpoint.epoch)`. Caplin
ignored valid sidecars for up to 31 slots after the checkpoint, for
example every sidecar in the first epoch of a new network.
5. **Chain tip poll pacing.**
`startFetchingBlocksMissedByGossipAfterSomeTime` polls peers with
BeaconBlocksByRange until fork choice has seen the target slot. After a
successful response it selected between the send on `respCh` and a
one-second timer meant as the pause between polls; `respCh` is buffered
(1024 entries), so the send was normally ready at once and the next
request went out as soon as the previous one returned. While
`HighestSeen()` and the current slot do not change, for example at a
slot with no block, every poll is the same request. Prysm v7.2.0 charges
BeaconBlocksByRange against a per-peer bucket by the requested slot
span, not by the blocks returned, and counts each rejected request as a
bad response. In a devnet, at a slot with no block, a Caplin node sent
Prysm 18 identical requests (`start_slot=64, count=7`) within 0.2 s;
Prysm rejected the later ones as rate-limited, the node reached the
bad-response threshold (`got 5, threshold 5`), and Prysm disconnected it
as a bad peer when it reconnected. The loop now sends the response and
then waits `chainTipPollInterval` (1 s). Unlike item 2, which pauses
between retries after a failed request, this pauses after a successful
poll. In a devnet run with this branch and other Caplin fixes (#24512,
#24544-#24548 and two sentinel changes), Prysm logged no rate-limited
request and no bad-peer disconnect.

Known limit of (1): the cap counts Caplin's own open requests and frees
a slot when Caplin cancels one. A slow responder may still be finishing
the cancelled stream, so it can see a third request. In one devnet run
where Lighthouse was slow, Lighthouse still logged 19 `already 2 active
requests` errors for Caplin; another run with the same concurrency cap
had none.

Not changed here:
- The blob sidecar check (`blob_sidecar_service.go`) and the Gloas path
still use `FinalizedSlot()`: the blob topic is deprecated from Fulu, and
the Gloas spec has no such finality condition.
- BeaconBlocksByRange caps `count` at `MAX_REQUEST_BLOCKS_DENEB` instead
of rejecting a larger request. The spec states that limit for
requesters, and Caplin's own chain tip sync can request more than 128
slots; making it stay within the limit is a follow-up.

## Changes

- `cl/sentinel/service/service.go`: per-peer, per-request-type stream
count in `requestPeer`.
- `cl/phase1/stages/chain_tip_sync.go`: retry pause;
`chainTipPollInterval` pause after every successful poll. If `respCh` is
full, the poll loop now waits for the consumer instead of dropping the
response when the timer fires first.
- `cl/sentinel/handlers/blocks.go`: requested range only.
- `cl/phase1/network/services/data_column_sidecar_service.go`: compare
with the finalized checkpoint's start slot (the checkpoint is read once
for both finality checks, with an overflow guard), and look up the
finalized ancestor no lower than the anchor slot.

## Testing

- **TDD:** these failed before their changes:
`TestPeerRequestLimitsConcurrentStreamsPerPeerAndRequestType` (a v2-only
third request is not refused while two v2,v1 requests of the same type
are open), `TestFetchBlocksFromReqRespPacesRetriesAfterRequestErrors`,
`TestStartFetchingBlocksMissedByGossipPacesSuccessfulPolls` (more than 3
polls against a peer that returns no blocks), four of the six
BlocksByRange table cases (out-of-range blocks, `count=0`, a block after
the first 96 slots, overflow), and the sidecar tests for a slot after
the finalized epoch start and the anchor clamp. The other BlocksByRange
cases and the sidecar mismatch test are guards that pass on both
versions. The sidecar boundary test and the updated too-old-slot test
also fail on the old code, but only because they no longer set the
mock's `FinalizedSlot()`.
- `make lint`
- `make erigon integration`
- `go test ./cl/phase1/network/services/... ./cl/phase1/stages/...
./cl/sentinel/...`

author: Kewei
subject: cl/phase1/stages: stop leaking the chain tip fetch goroutine after cancellation (#24765)
body:
## Summary

During ChainTipSync, `startFetchingBlocksMissedByGossipAfterSomeTime`
(`cl/phase1/stages/chain_tip_sync.go`) polls peers with
BeaconBlocksByRange and reports a failed fetch on `errCh`.
`fetchBlocksFromReqResp` retries request errors until the context is
done, so its only error return is `ctx.Err()`. Before this change, the
goroutine then tried to send that error with a bare `errCh <- err`.

`chainTipSync` creates `errCh` unbuffered, and
`listenToIncomingBlocksUntilANewBlockIsReceived` is its only reader. At
the 25-second timeout in `chainTipSync`, the reader can return on
`ctx.Done()` before the goroutine reaches the send. If the target block
arrives first, the reader returns nil and the deferred cancel in
`chainTipSync` ends the context. When the reader had already returned,
the send blocked until the process exited.

So a ChainTipSync cycle whose context ended while a BlocksByRange
request was in flight or in the retry backoff could leak one goroutine.
The bare send is older than #24550; it was reported as a follow-up in
the #24550 review.

The send now selects on `ctx.Done()`, as the `respCh` send already does.
While the context is live, a reader still receives the error; once the
context is done, the goroutine returns.

## Not changed here

- `errCh` is kept. With the current `fetchBlocksFromReqResp` it only
carries `ctx.Err()`, which the reader already sees through `ctx.Done()`,
so it could be removed. Keeping it is the smaller change and keeps the
error path if the fetch later returns a non-context error.

## Changes

- `cl/phase1/stages/chain_tip_sync.go`: select on `ctx.Done()` around
the `errCh` send.
- `cl/phase1/stages/chain_tip_sync_test.go`:
`TestStartFetchingBlocksMissedByGossipReturnsAfterCancelWithoutErrorReader`.

## Testing

- **TDD:**
`TestStartFetchingBlocksMissedByGossipReturnsAfterCancelWithoutErrorReader`
runs the poll loop against a sentinel whose requests always fail, with
an unbuffered `errCh` and no reader. It waits until the sentinel has
received a request, cancels the context, and requires the goroutine to
return within 5 s. With the production file from `main` it fails (`fetch
goroutine did not return after cancellation`, after 5.5 s); with the fix
it passes in 0.5 s, and 20 out of 20 runs pass with `-race`.
- `go test -p 2 -count=1 ./cl/phase1/stages/`
- `make lint`
- `make erigon integration`

author: Kewei
subject: cl/phase1/network/services: accept aggregates of a new epoch before its first block (#24766)
body:
## Summary

Caplin's aggregate service had no wall clock. It bounded the accepted
epoch range with `validationEpochRange(headState, highestSeen,
highestSeen, ...)`, so the range reached the next epoch only once fork
choice's highest seen slot did, which `OnBlock` advances when it imports
a block. When the first slot of epoch E+1 has no block, the head state
stays in E, and every aggregate for E+1 was ignored with `epoch outside
validation range` until `OnBlock` saw a block of E+1:

- From gossip, the service ignores the aggregate at the epoch check, so
it is not forwarded and does not reach the attestation pool or fork
choice.
- From the validator client (`POST
/eth/v1/validator/aggregate_and_proofs`), the node does not add the
validator's aggregate to its pool or fork choice. On `main` the handler
still publishes it and answers 200. With #24629 it is not published and
the request reports a failure.

For the epoch, the gossip spec (`beacon_aggregate_and_proof` as modified
in Deneb, kept in Electra and Gloas) only requires it to be the current
or previous epoch by the wall clock, with a
`MAXIMUM_GOSSIP_CLOCK_DISPARITY` allowance; whether a block of that
epoch has been seen plays no part. #24544 already noted that at the
first slot of a fork, when that slot has no block, the aggregates of
that slot are still ignored by this check.

The service now gets the Ethereum clock and passes its current slot to
`validationEpochRange`, as the attestation service does.
`validationEpochRange` is unchanged, so both paths now apply the same
rule:

- E+1 is admitted once the clock or fork choice's highest seen slot
reaches it. Its committees use the RANDAO mix of E−1, which is final in
a head state of epoch E.
- E+2 is admitted when fork choice has seen no block at a later slot
than the head state (the guard from #24547). Its committees use the
RANDAO mix of E, which is final only if the head state holds every block
of E. The aggregate path needs this guard as much as the attestation
path: an aggregate checked against committees from a non-final mix would
usually fail the aggregator membership check, and gossip rejects such a
message instead of ignoring it. Before this change the aggregate path
never admitted E+2: that needs a current slot in E+2 or later while no
block past the head state has been seen, and the current slot it passed
was the highest seen slot.

## Not changed here

- The spec's future-slot check (the aggregate's slot must not be later
than the current slot, with the `MAXIMUM_GOSSIP_CLOCK_DISPARITY`
allowance) is still missing, so an aggregate for a later slot of an
admitted epoch is not ignored for that reason. It was missing before as
well; with this change it also matters for an epoch whose first block
has not been seen yet.
- The epoch range has no `MAXIMUM_GOSSIP_CLOCK_DISPARITY` allowance: an
aggregate for E+1 that arrives shortly before the clock reaches E+1 is
still ignored. The attestation service behaves the same.
- The lower bound is still the head state's previous epoch, so it can be
older than the wall-clock previous epoch when the head epoch lags.
- #24629 adds the same clock parameter for its fork digest check. A
trial merge of the two branches conflicts only in the two `clock :=`
lines of the test setup helpers; the production files merge cleanly.

## Changes

- `cl/phase1/network/services/aggregate_and_proof_service.go`:
`NewAggregateAndProofService` takes an `eth_clock.EthereumClock`; the
epoch range check passes `ethClock.GetCurrentSlot()` as the current
slot.
- `cmd/caplin/caplin1/run.go`: pass `ethClock` to the aggregate service.
- `cl/phase1/network/services/aggregate_and_proof_service_test.go`: the
setup helpers pass a real clock with genesis at the start of the test,
so its current slot is 0 and the existing tests keep their meaning; one
new test.

## Testing

- **TDD:**
`TestAggregateAndProofAllowsEpochReachedByClockBeforeItsFirstBlock` has
two cases with the head state in epoch E and no block past the head
seen: an aggregate for E+1 and one for E+2, each with the clock at the
aggregate's slot. Both fail with `epoch outside validation range` when
the range check passes the highest seen slot as the current slot, as on
`main`, and pass with the fix. The unchanged
`TestAggregateAndProofRejectsBeyondNextEpochDespiteForkchoiceHavingSeenIt`
covers the head epoch + 2 guard on the aggregate path: it fails if the
`highestSeenSlot <= headState.Slot()` condition is removed from
`validationEpochRange`.
- `go test -p 2 -count=1 ./cl/phase1/network/services/
./cmd/caplin/caplin1/`
- `go test -race -count=3 -run TestAggregateAndProof
./cl/phase1/network/services/`
- `make lint`
- `make erigon integration`

author: Kewei
subject: cl/phase1/forkchoice: reject attester slashings with no slashable validator, handle huge indices (#24771)
body:
## Summary

Two fixes in the fork choice attester slashing check
(`OnAttesterSlashing`), which gossip, the REST pool endpoint and the
block service (for the operations of an imported block) use.

**Huge validator index.** `isUnequivocating` converted the validator
index to `int` before its bounds check. On 64-bit builds, a slashing
whose two attestations share an index from 2^63 to 2^64-8 made the byte
index negative, and the slice access panicked. This happens in the check
whether all intersecting indices were already seen, which runs before
the attestation data, the indices and the signatures are checked, so a
gossip peer or a REST client can trigger it. The gossip validator
recovers the panic and rejects the message. For REST, `net/http`
recovers it and ends the request without an answer instead of answering
400. A block with such a slashing fails the state transition before the
block service imports its operations. `isUnequivocating` now does the
division and the bounds check on `uint64`, so such an index counts as
not seen, and the slashing fails the normal validation (`invalid
validator index`).

**No slashable validator.** When a slashing had an intersecting index
that was not seen before and passed the data, index and signature
checks, but no validator in the intersection was slashable in the state
used for the check (the head state, or the justified state while
syncing), `onProcessAttesterSlashing` did not add it to the pool but
returned nil. So gossip accepted and forwarded the slashing, and the
REST endpoint answered 200 and published it. The `attester_slashing`
gossip rules ignore a slashing whose intersecting indices were all seen
before; Erigon checks this before validating the slashing, as the spec
lists it. After the data, index and signature checks, the rules reject a
slashing in which no validator of the intersection is slashable, and
`process_attester_slashing` asserts the same.
`onProcessAttesterSlashing` now returns `no slashable validators in
intersection`: the gossip validator rejects the message through its
normal error path, which also asks the peer banner to ban the sender,
and REST answers 400 and does not publish it. The error is returned
after the existing loop that marks the intersection indices as
equivocating, so fork choice tracks them as before (the fork choice
`on_attester_slashing` handler marks them without a slashability check).
The block service checks the slashings of an imported block in a
goroutine started after `OnBlock`. If such a slashing is not already in
the pool or fully seen, and the head state used for the check already
includes the block, no intersecting validator is slashable any more, and
the returned error is logged at debug level.

## Not changed here

- The same bitlist is both the gossip "already seen" set and fork
choice's equivocating indices, and the indices are marked before the
slashability check. So a repeat of a slashing rejected for having no
slashable validator is ignored instead of rejected again (the spec marks
indices as seen only after all checks pass), and the REST endpoint,
which treats an ignore as success, answers 200 and publishes the repeat.
Both behave as on the base. Fixing this means keeping the two sets
apart, which is a larger change.
- A gossip copy of a slashing that arrives after a block with the same
slashing updated the head, but before the block service imports the
block's operations and marks the indices, is now rejected and its sender
may be banned (no validator of the intersection is slashable in the head
state), as the spec's reject rule says. The peer ban handling for
rejected gossip is unchanged here.
- `setUnequivocating` converts the index to `int` the same way. It only
receives indices that were already looked up in the state, so it is left
as is.
- The staged sync block import (`processBlock` in
`cl/phase1/stages/clstages.go`) calls only `OnBlock`, so the attester
slashings of those blocks do not mark equivocating indices. The
equivocating indices are also not persisted across restarts.

## Changes

- `cl/phase1/forkchoice/on_attestation.go`: `isUnequivocating` computes
the byte index, the bounds check and the bit on `uint64`.
- `cl/phase1/forkchoice/on_attester_slashing.go`: return an error when
no validator in the intersection is slashable, after the equivocation
marking and before the pool insert.
- `cl/phase1/forkchoice/forkchoice_test.go`:
`TestAttesterSlashingSeenCheckHandlesHugeIndex`,
`TestAttesterSlashingRejectsWhenNoValidatorIsSlashable`,
`TestAttesterSlashingAcceptsWhenAnyValidatorIsSlashable`.

## Testing

- **Red on the base:** `TestAttesterSlashingSeenCheckHandlesHugeIndex`
fails with `index out of range [-1152921504606846976]` and passes with
only the `on_attestation.go` change.
`TestAttesterSlashingRejectsWhenNoValidatorIsSlashable` fails with `An
error is expected but got nil` and passes with only the
`on_attester_slashing.go` change; it also checks that the slashing is
not in the pool and that its indices are marked as equivocating.
`TestAttesterSlashingAcceptsWhenAnyValidatorIsSlashable` passes before
and after: a slashing with one slashable validator is still accepted and
added to the pool.
- `go test -p 2 -count=1 ./cl/phase1/forkchoice/...
./cl/phase1/network/services/ ./cl/phase1/network/gossip/
./cl/beacon/handler/`
- Fork choice spec tests: `go test -count=1 -v -run
'Test/mainnet/.*/fork_choice' ./cl/spectest/` with the v1.7.0-beta.2
fixtures (no failures; 285 `PASS` and 27 `SKIP` lines), including
`discard_equivocations_on_attester_slashing`.
- `make lint`, `make erigon integration`.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/sentinel/handlers: return zero chunks for data column by-root misses (#24772)
body:
## Summary

Caplin's `DataColumnSidecarsByRoot` handler answered a valid post-Fulu
request with `3: ResourceUnavailable` when it found none of the
requested sidecars. That happens in normal operation:

- the block root is not indexed yet because the block is still being
imported, including a block the node itself just proposed and published;
- the block is known but the requested columns are not stored, for
example because they are outside the node's custody.

The Fulu p2p spec says the response "may be less in the case that the
responding peer is missing blocks or sidecars" and "MUST consist of zero
or more `response_chunk`". For this protocol it allows
`ResourceUnavailable` only when a requested root references a block
earlier than `minimum_request_epoch`, and phase0 says that code "is only
valid as a response where specified". Prysm and Lighthouse skip missing
data and close the stream without an error code. If at least one sidecar
was found, Caplin already returned only what it had, without an error
code at the end.

Impact: in a Kurtosis devnet where most nodes had 64 validators instead
of 128, so they custody fewer column groups, Lighthouse v8.3.0-rc.0 (a
supernode) got 76 `ResourceUnavailable` responses from the Caplin node
with embedded Caplin, which custodied 64 column groups. All 76 requests
were sent before that node logged `OnBlock` for the requested block.
Lighthouse counts an error response as a custody download failure, and a
custody request fails with `TooManyFailures` once a column has three
failures. An empty response does not count toward that limit. All 20
`TooManyFailures` and the 3 lookups Lighthouse dropped with
`TooManyAttempts` in that run followed these errors. In the same run,
after each of 3 such errors right after that node restarted, Nimbus
lowered the peer's score and dropped the connection. No missed slot was
caused by these errors.

Fix: when the lookup finds nothing and hits no storage or stream error,
close the stream with zero chunks, as the handler did before #21686 and
as the by-range handler does. The `ResourceUnavailable` answer to
requests received before the Fulu fork is unchanged. Roots of blocks
older than `minimum_request_epoch` are still skipped, so a request with
only such roots now gets zero chunks instead of `ResourceUnavailable`;
the spec allows both. Caplin's own client already handles a zero-chunk
response on this protocol: `httpreqresp` turns the EOF into an empty
success and `cl/das` skips empty results.

## Not changed here

- The handler still looks up the block root in the beacon index before
reading column storage, so sidecars that are already stored for a block
whose index is not written yet are not served. The spec says clients
"MUST respond with at least one sidecar, if they have it" and "SHOULD
include a sidecar in the response as soon as it passes the gossip
validation rules"; Lighthouse also serves columns from its pending
caches. That is a separate change.
- Related handlers that are not part of this fix:
- `beaconBlocksByRootHandler` answers an empty root list with
`ResourceUnavailable`.
- `dataColumnSidecarsByRangeHandler` writes sidecars in the requested
column order and can stop in the middle of a block. The spec requires
`(slot, column_index)` order and all requested sidecars of each included
block.
- The execution payload envelope handlers do not serve envelopes newer
than the latest finalized checkpoint when those fall outside the
`MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS` range, which Gloas requires.

## Changes

- `cl/sentinel/handlers/data_cloumn_sidecar.go`: remove the `count == 0`
branch that wrote `ResourceUnavailable`; the handler now returns
`responseErr`.
- `cl/sentinel/handlers/data_column_sidecar_test.go`:
- `TestDataColumnSidecarsByRootMissingRootReturnsResourceUnavailable`
becomes `TestDataColumnSidecarsByRootMissingRootReturnsEmptySuccess`.
- New `TestDataColumnSidecarsByRootMissingColumnReturnsEmptySuccess`:
the root is indexed and column 0 is stored, column 1 is requested.
- `expectDataColumnSidecarEmptyResponse` now requires `io.EOF` instead
of accepting any read error, and no longer sets a 200 ms read deadline,
so a timeout or reset no longer passes as an empty response.

## Testing

- **TDD:** with only the test changes,
`TestDataColumnSidecarsByRootMissingRootReturnsEmptySuccess` and
`TestDataColumnSidecarsByRootMissingColumnReturnsEmptySuccess` fail
(they read the `0x03` byte); every other test in the file passes,
including the ones using the stricter helper. With the fix, all pass.
- `go test -p 2 -count=1 ./cl/sentinel/... ./cl/das/ ./cl/rpc/`
- `make lint`
- `make erigon integration`

author: Kewei
subject: cl/phase1/network: defer the gloas checkpoint anchor when the checkpoint url cannot serve its child (#24708)
body:
## Summary

With `--caplin.checkpoint-sync-url` set, a fresh checkpoint sync whose
anchor is a Gloas block can fail to finish when the configured endpoint
cannot serve the anchor's canonical child.

Backward sync decides whether the anchor's payload was revealed (FULL or
EMPTY) from the anchor's canonical child, and it fetches that child only
from the checkpoint sync URL, by slot. checkpointz, the default Sepolia
endpoint, serves only checkpoint blocks and answers every other slot
with `500 {"code":500,"message":"block not found"}`. One such status
fails the whole 64-slot range. The error was logged at DEBUG,
`processResponses` returned nil, and `RequestMore` retried the same
range forever, so nothing in the default log showed why the node never
synced.

Without the flag, backward sync gets no URL: `caplin1.RunCaplinService`
sets the network id to the custom network, which has no default
endpoints, before the stages start. The anchor is then persisted without
classifying its payload, so the default configuration does not hit this.

Now, after `maxGloasSuccessorFailures` (3) source failures for the
anchor, the anchor is persisted without classifying its payload in the
call that reaches the limit, and backfill continues to its ancestors:
the path that nodes without a URL already use. Source failures are:

- an HTTP failure that returns no blocks and that the slot-by-slot retry
confirms: the range's slots are fetched again one at a time, and the
first slot that fails counts;
- a sweep that reaches the current slot without finding a child (a
source that answers 404 for every slot except checkpoints looped the
same way);
- a served range whose first block is not a child of the anchor (the
child is no longer served but a later descendant is; this used to count
as disconnected and abort backfill after three attempts).

Until the limit is reached, the anchor is classified when the range
returns a connected prefix that starts with its valid child, also when a
later slot fails, or when the slot-by-slot retry reaches and returns
that child. A failing slot cancels the other in-flight requests of the
range, which can include the child, so a range that fails without
returning blocks is fetched again one slot at a time: 404s are skipped,
and the retry stops at the first block or error, so an error on a slot
before the child still counts as a source failure. The batch path and
the root lookup fallback both defer this way. After a restart the stored
Gloas anchor is read from the database also when a URL is set, on each
attempt until backfill moves past it, and it is then classified or
deferred like an anchor from the peer batch; a failed database read is
logged and falls through to the root lookup fallback. A served chain
that starts at the anchor's child but whose parent links break later
still counts as disconnected, and a child that fails the state
transition from the anchor state is still rejected at once. Successor
fetch failures, the deferral and a failed root lookup are logged at
WARN.

The child is still never taken from P2P: a child that passes the state
transition from the anchor state is valid but not necessarily canonical,
and two valid children can disagree on the anchor's payload status. The
existing tests for that rule are unchanged.

## Not changed here

- Deferred-anchor handoff is unchanged here. ForwardSync performs a
best-effort startup recovery; its overlapping range path may also
recover the anchor when it receives the anchor and its child.
ChainTipSync invokes the same recovery before a direct child that claims
the anchor payload. These paths do not provide a complete per-child
EL-handoff guarantee, and fork choice can treat a header-only anchor as
EMPTY. This remains follow-up work.
- `caplin1.RunCaplinService` forcing the custom network id, which leaves
default-configuration nodes without an HTTP fallback in backfill.

## Changes

- `cl/phase1/network/backward_beacon_downloader.go`: count source
failures per anchor and defer the anchor at the limit
(`resolveGloasLookahead`), use the blocks returned before a failing
slot, fetch the range again one slot at a time when a failure returns no
blocks, process a Gloas anchor read from the database like one from the
peer batch, also on retries, let a failed database read fall through to
the root lookup, and log failures and the deferral at WARN.
- `cl/phase1/network/backward_beacon_downloader_test.go`: thirteen new
tests.

## Testing

- **TDD:** with the production file from `main`, these fail:
`TestBackwardGloasAnchorDefersWhenSuccessorSourceFails`,
`TestBackwardGloasAnchorDefersWhenSuccessorSourceHasNoChild`,
`TestBackwardGloasAnchorDefersWhenDirectChildIsNotServed`,
`TestBackwardGloasRootFallbackAnchorDefersWhenSuccessorSourceFails`,
`TestBackwardGloasPersistedAnchorDefersWhenSourcesFail`,
`TestBackwardGloasPersistedAnchorClassifiedWhenSuccessorSourceServesChild`,
`TestBackwardGloasPersistedAnchorRetriedWithRetainedChild`,
`TestBackwardGloasSuccessorFromPartialHTTPRange`,
`TestBackwardGloasAnchorClassifiedWhenLaterSlotFailureCancelsChild` and
`TestBackwardGloasSuccessorRangeRetryOfOnly404sIsEmpty`. The last two
also fail with the production file of the first commit (00d90dfe572),
which has no slot-by-slot retry: there the cancelled child request
counts as a source failure, and a range whose only failure is a single
500 keeps the search at slot 11. Three pass before and after.
`TestBackwardGloasAnchorClassifiedWhenSuccessorSourceRecovers` checks
that the URL still classifies the anchor when it recovers before the
limit. `TestBackwardGloasAnchorRootFallbackAfterDBReadError` and
`TestBackwardPreGloasPersistedAnchorNotProcessedFromDB` guard the
database read, which now also runs when a URL is set: a read error still
reaches the root lookup, and a pre-Gloas block read from the database is
not processed. They pass on `main` because it skips that read when a URL
is set and uses its result only for a Gloas anchor.
- Sepolia, a fresh node next to a synced one, with
`--caplin.checkpoint-sync-url=https://checkpoint-sync.sepolia.ethpandaops.io/eth/v2/debug/beacon/states/finalized`;
Caplin's data was deleted before each run, the EL data was kept. Both
builds were release/3.7 with other open Caplin PRs; the second one also
had an earlier revision of the first commit, which differs only when the
anchor is already stored in the database or the database read fails. The
second commit (slot-by-slot retry) was not part of either run; against
checkpointz it adds one request per attempt, because the child's slot
answers 500 again.
- Without these changes: checkpoint sync at slot 11310752, then `initial
GLOAS successor fetch failed ... HTTP block fetch slot 11310753: status
500` 23 times at DEBUG in under two minutes, with backfill stuck at the
anchor.
- With the first commit: three successor fetch failures within two
seconds, then the deferral WARN for slot 11310752. Backfill finished and
ForwardSync reached 36 s from the chain tip.
- `go test -p 2 ./cl/phase1/network/ ./cl/phase1/stages/`, `make lint`,
`make erigon integration`.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/phase1/network: verify gossip signatures before forwarding and keep messages on their fork's topic (#24629)
body:
## Summary

Caplin forwarded gossip messages that other clients reject, and those
clients then lowered its score and disconnected it. This fixes two
causes in the gossip validators, and the REST endpoints that published
aggregates and attestations on the wrong fork's topic.

**Includes #24544 (main is merged into this branch).** Before #24544,
four aggregate and attestation signature checks took their domains from
the head state, so valid messages near a fork boundary could fail
signature verification: for example a new-fork attestation before a
new-fork state became head, or a late pre-fork aggregate against a
post-fork head. With this change, the gossip validator would reject such
a message instead of forwarding it and try to queue a ban of its sender.
#24544 computes all four domains from the message's epoch. Main, with
#24544 and #24547, is merged into this branch.

go-libp2p-pubsub counts a rejected message as an invalid delivery
against the peer it came from and against every other peer that
delivered the same message. Prysm v7.2.0 disconnects a peer whose gossip
score is below -100, and it decays the invalid-delivery count to 1% over
50 epochs.

**1. Signatures are verified before a message is accepted.** Since
#17926 moved gossip validation into libp2p topic validators, the result
of a service's `ProcessMessage` decides whether libp2p forwards the
message, and nil becomes `ValidationAccept`. For aggregates,
attestations, voluntary exits and BLS-to-execution changes, the service
queued the BLS check in the batch verifier and returned nil, so the
message was forwarded before its signature was checked.

These four `ProcessMessage` paths now wait for their own message's
result from the batch verifier: nil for a valid signature, otherwise
`ErrInvalidBlsSignature` or the verification error, so an invalid
message is rejected instead of forwarded. Batching is kept: libp2p runs
validators concurrently, so waiting validators share a batch. A batch is
verified at 50 entries or after `batchCheckInterval`, now 50 ms instead
of 500 ms, because at low traffic the interval adds to each hop's
forwarding delay. If the validator's context is cancelled or the
verifier stops before the result arrives, the wait returns `ErrIgnore`.
The REST BLS-to-execution change endpoint uses the same path, so a
change with an invalid signature is now reported as a failure instead of
being published.

The verifier reports a batch's results before it runs callbacks or bans
a peer:
- The message callbacks (pool insertion, fork choice updates, events)
run after the results are reported, on one goroutine per message type,
in order. The runner's queue holds 1024 callbacks, so a slow callback
holds up later results only if the runner falls that far behind.
`ImmediateVerification` still runs the callback before it returns.
- When a batch fails, every entry is rechecked and its result reported
before the verifier queues a ban.
- When `ProcessMessage` returns an error other than an ignore, the
gossip manager rejects the message and tries to queue a ban of its
sender's encoded peer ID (`pid.String()`). It used to queue the raw
`peer.ID` bytes, which the sentinel cannot parse, so these bans failed.
Because a rejection can now lead to a ban, some local faults are ignored
instead: a data column sidecar whose custody column lookup or write
fails, and an execution payload envelope for which fork choice returns
an error that it does not mark as an invalid envelope (outcomes that
already had their own handling keep it). The verifier queues at most one
ban per failed batch, and only for an entry whose result no validator
received: the sync committee message and contribution paths, which stay
asynchronous, and validators that stopped waiting.
- `BanPeer` can block while the sentinel closes the peer, so the gossip
manager and the verifier each queue bans for one background worker, with
room for 256. A ban that does not fit is dropped without retry; a later
invalid message from the peer queues another one.

**2. Aggregates and attestations stay on their fork's topic.** The
gossip validator decoded every message with the wall-clock fork's types,
and the aggregate and attestation services validated it with the fork of
the message's slot; the topic's fork digest was not used. Around a fork
Caplin is subscribed to both topics, so after the fork an aggregate for
the last pre-fork slot published on the post-fork topic was validated as
a pre-fork aggregate, accepted and forwarded. Prysm v7.2.0 rejects such
aggregates (`Verification of aggregate failed`).

The validator now decodes with the fork of the topic's digest
(`StateVersionByForkDigest`, which includes BPO digests); a topic digest
that cannot be parsed or is not known is ignored. Aggregates and
attestations carry the topic digest, and the services ignore one whose
slot's epoch has a different fork digest (`ComputeForkDigest`) than its
topic. This applies in both directions and across BPO boundaries, which
keep the fork version but change the digest. Ignore rather than reject
follows the Altair p2p spec:

> Messages SHOULD NOT be re-broadcast from one fork to the other.

> Peers who propagate messages on the pre-fork topics MUST NOT be scored
negatively.

Because gossip now decodes with the topic's types, a block or data
column sidecar decoded with another fork's types than its slot's can
arrive while both topics are subscribed. Such a message is ignored
before it is cached, queued or stored: its decoded version must equal
the fork version of its slot. The existing `ForkSchemaMatchesSlot` only
separates Gloas from earlier forks, so it would let an Electra-decoded
block at a Fulu slot through.

**3. REST aggregates and attestations are published on their own fork's
digest.** `POST /eth/v1/validator/aggregate_and_proofs` published on the
current fork's topic, also when the service had ignored the aggregate. A
validator client that resumed after a fork submitted aggregates for the
last pre-fork slot, and Caplin published them on the post-fork topic.
The endpoint now validates against and publishes on the fork digest of
the aggregate's own epoch. It does not publish an aggregate the service
ignored and reports it as a failure for that index, and it reports a
failed publication. Two cases succeed, as in Lighthouse. A resubmission
of a signed aggregate that the endpoint already validated is published
again, so a retry after a failed publication reaches gossip. An
aggregate from an aggregator already seen for that epoch, with another
aggregate or with the same aggregate through gossip, succeeds without
being published. The v1 and v2 attestation pool endpoints also publish
on the digest of the attestation's epoch, so an attestation for the last
slot before a fork or BPO boundary, submitted just after it, is not
published on the new topic, where nodes with this change ignore it.

Devnet (Kurtosis; Fulu at genesis, Gloas at epoch 2, 12 s slots;
Lighthouse v8.3.0-rc.0, Teku 26.9.1, Prysm v7.2.0, Nimbus v26.10.0 and
two Caplin nodes; the proposers of slots 64 and 65 were paused for 28 s
across the fork):
- Without this change (two runs): after resuming, a paused node
published aggregates for slot 63, the last Fulu slot, on the Gloas
topic. In one run this was a Caplin node, whose paused validator client
submitted them over REST; in the other it was Nimbus. In each run Prysm
rejected three of these aggregates (`Verification of aggregate failed`),
and within about 1.5 minutes disconnected both Caplin nodes with Goodbye
reason 251 (`client banned this node`). When they reconnected it
disconnected them again with `gossip score below threshold` (scores
between -448 and -861, threshold -100).
- With the first six commits of this change, on release/3.7 with the
other open Caplin fixes (#24512, #24544-#24548, #24550, #24627, #24628),
and the same pause pattern (a Caplin node's validator client and
Nimbus): Prysm rejected six slot-63 aggregates on the Gloas topic, all
from Nimbus, and did not disconnect either Caplin node. At slot 170 all
six CL nodes were at justified/finalized 4/3. That build did not include
the later commits (ban ownership in the verifier, the REST attestation
digest, the bounded ban queues, the encoded peer ID for gossip bans,
publishing an already-seen REST aggregate again, review simplifications,
test calls adapted to main after the rebase, the merge with main, and
the changes for the second review).

Not changed here:
- Sync committee messages and contributions still verify asynchronously,
so they are still accepted before their signatures are checked. Their
services call the verifier while holding the service mutex and the
head-state read lock, so waiting there would serialize their validation.
- The spec rule to ignore an aggregate whose aggregation bits are a
subset of (or equal to) those of an aggregate already seen for the same
data is not implemented:
> [IGNORE] A valid aggregate attestation defined by
`hash_tree_root(aggregate.data)` whose `aggregation_bits` is a
non-strict superset has _not_ already been seen.
- Caplin removes the old fork's topics about 8 slots after a fork,
earlier than the spec's two epochs. After that, publishing a REST
aggregate or attestation for a pre-fork slot fails, and the endpoint
reports it as a failure for that index.
- The REST voluntary exit and BLS-to-execution change endpoints still
publish a message the service ignored and only log a failed publication.
- A BPO change keeps the fork version, so a block or data column sidecar
on the topic of another BPO digest is not caught at admission. It is
decoded and processed correctly; only the topic differs.
- The REST block endpoint publishes a block and its sidecars on the
wall-clock fork digest, not on the digest of the block's epoch. At a
fork boundary where both forks share the block layout, a block published
in another epoch than its slot's goes to a topic where nodes with this
change ignore it.
- Some local faults in other gossip paths, mostly inside fork choice,
still make the gossip manager reject the message and try to queue a ban
of its sender.
- The aggregate service bounds the accepted epoch range by the highest
seen slot, not by the wall clock.
- The 50 ms batch interval was not benchmarked. Prysm v7.2.0 uses 5 ms.
- A REST BLS-to-execution change that reaches signature verification
waits for the batch verifier's result. At low traffic the 50 ms batch
interval can add up to 50 ms for each such change. A separate PR will
switch that path to immediate verification.

## Changes

- `cl/phase1/network/services/batch_signature_verification.go`:
`VerifyAttestation`, `VerifyAggregateProof`, `VerifyVoluntaryExit` and
`VerifyBlsToExecutionChange` replace the `Async*` variants of these four
and wait for the entry's result; results are reported per entry,
callbacks run on a runner goroutine per queue, bans go through a queue;
`batchCheckInterval` is 50 ms; a BLS verification error is logged at
debug level instead of critical.
- `cl/phase1/network/services/aggregate_and_proof_service.go`,
`attestation_service.go`: return the verifier's result;
`TopicForkDigest` on the gossip message and the digest check. The
aggregate service takes the `EthereumClock`
(`cmd/caplin/caplin1/run.go`). For a REST submission identical to a
signed aggregate it already validated, it returns
`ErrAggregatorAlreadySeen` (`constants.go`) wrapped in `ErrIgnore`; the
seen-aggregator cache stores that aggregate's root. For any other
aggregate from an aggregator already seen for that epoch, it returns
`ErrAggregatorAlreadyKnown` wrapped in `ErrIgnore`.
- `cl/phase1/network/services/voluntary_exit_service.go`,
`bls_to_execution_change_service.go`: return the verifier's result.
- `cl/phase1/network/services/block_service.go`,
`data_column_sidecar_service.go`: at admission, the decoded version must
equal the fork version of the slot. The data column sidecar service also
ignores a failed custody column lookup or sidecar write.
- `cl/phase1/network/services/execution_payload_service.go`: a fork
choice error that is not marked `ErrInvalidExecutionPayloadEnvelope` and
has no handling of its own is ignored at the gossip entry; an envelope
waiting in the pending queue is kept and retried after such an error.
- `cl/phase1/network/gossip/gossip_manager.go`: decode with the topic
digest's fork, pass the digest to messages that take it, ban queue with
the sender's encoded peer ID, `PublishToForkDigest` (also in the
`Gossip` interface and its mock).
- `cl/phase1/network/gossip/gossip_subscription.go`: `GetTopic` reads
the pubsub topic under the subscriptions lock, so publishing does not
race `Remove` clearing it when an old fork's topic is removed.
- `cl/beacon/handler/pool.go`: the aggregate and attestation endpoints
use the digest of the message's epoch. The aggregate endpoint reports an
ignored aggregate as a failure, except a resubmission of an aggregate it
already validated, which it publishes again, and an aggregator already
seen for that epoch, which succeeds without publishing. It reports
failed publications.

## Testing

- **TDD:** these failed before their change:
- Verify before accept:
`TestAggregateAndProofGossipDoesNotAcceptBeforeBLSVerification`,
`TestAttestationGossipNotAcceptedBeforeSignatureVerification`,
`TestVoluntaryExitGossipNotAcceptedBeforeSignatureVerification`,
`TestBlsToExecutionChangeGossipNotAcceptedBeforeSignatureVerification`.
- Batch verifier: `TestBatchSignatureVerifierReportsEachEntryResult`,
`TestBatchSignatureVerifierReportsBeforeBlockingCallback`,
`TestBatchSignatureVerifierWaitReturnsIgnoreOnContextCancel`,
`TestBatchSignatureVerifierContinuesWhileCallbackBlocked`,
`TestBatchSignatureVerifierImmediateVerificationRunsCallback`,
`TestBatchSignatureVerifierContinuesAfterBlockingBan`,
`TestBatchSignatureVerifierDoesNotBanWaitedEntry`,
`TestBatchSignatureVerifierBansWhenWaiterCancelsAfterAdmission`,
`TestBatchSignatureVerifierBoundsBlockingBans`.
- Gossip manager: `TestNewPubsubValidator_DecodesWithTopicForkVersion`,
`TestNewPubsubValidator_UnknownForkDigestIgnored`,
`TestNewPubsubValidatorCarriesExactTopicForkDigest`,
`TestNewPubsubValidatorRejectsWhilePeerBanBlocks`,
`TestNewPubsubValidatorContinuesAfterPeerBannerPanic`,
`TestNewPubsubValidatorBansEncodedPeerID`,
`TestTopicSubscriptionsGetTopicReturnsSnapshot`.
- Fork digest:
`TestAggregateAndProofGossipPreForkAggregateOnPostForkTopicNotAccepted`,
`TestAggregateAndProofGossipNewForkAggregateOnOldForkTopicNotAccepted`,
`TestAggregateAndProofGossipRejectsDifferentBPOForkDigest`,
`TestAttestationGossipPreForkAttestationOnPostForkTopicNotAccepted`,
`TestAttestationGossipRejectsDifferentBPOForkDigest`.
- Schema at admission:
`TestBlockServiceProcessMessageIgnoresForkSchemaMismatchBeforeStorage`,
`TestProcessMessage_IgnoresPreGloasSchemaAtGloasSlotBeforeStorage`,
`TestGloasProcessMessage_IgnoresGloasSchemaAtPreGloasSlotBeforeQueueing`;
exact fork version:
`TestBlockServiceProcessMessageIgnoresExactForkVersionMismatchBeforeStorage`,
`TestProcessMessage_IgnoresExactForkVersionMismatchBeforeStorage`.
- Local faults:
`TestProcessMessage_WhenCustodyLookupFails_ReturnsErrIgnore`,
`TestGloasProcessMessage_WhenCustodyLookupFails_ReturnsErrIgnore`,
`TestProcessMessage_WhenStorageFails_ReturnsError` and
`TestGloasProcessMessage_WhenStorageFails_ReturnsError` (now require
`ErrIgnore`),
`TestExecutionPayloadServiceIgnoresLocalProcessingFailure`.
- REST: `TestPoolAggregatesAndProofsDoesNotPublishIgnoredAggregate` (now
expects a failure for the ignored aggregate),
`TestPoolAggregatesAndProofsPublishesOnMessageEpochForkDigest`,
`TestPoolAggregatesAndProofsRetriesAfterPublishFailure`,
`TestPoolV1AttestationsPublishesOnMessageEpochForkDigest`,
`TestPoolV2AttestationsPublishesOnMessageEpochForkDigest`.
- Already-seen aggregate:
`TestAggregateAndProofImmediateRetryReturnsAlreadySeenOnlyForSameAggregate`
(also checks that a different aggregate returns
`ErrAggregatorAlreadyKnown`), and the retry in
`TestPoolAggregatesAndProofsRetriesAfterPublishFailure`.
- These pass before and after their change and guard the other side:
`TestExecutionPayloadServiceRejectsInvalidEnvelopeProcessingFailure` (an
invalid envelope is still rejected),
`TestExecutionPayloadServicePendingRetriesLocalFailure` (existing; the
pending queue still retries a local failure),
`TestPoolAggregatesAndProofsDoesNotPublishKnownAggregate`. No test for
the log level change.
- Block service tests and the data column sidecar suite now use fork
epochs or sidecar versions that match their fixtures, which the exact
version check requires.
- No new tests for the review simplifications. Logging the invalid
signature where the peer to ban is picked and renaming `publishToDigest`
to `PublishToForkDigest` do not change message handling. The deleted
"topic fork digest is missing" branches were unreachable in production:
the gossip validator sets the digest right after decoding, and the REST
handlers set the digest and leave `Receiver` nil.
- The 16 existing Gloas data column sidecar tests now enable Gloas in
their config; they used Gloas sidecars with Gloas disabled, which the
new schema check ignores.
- `make lint`
- `make erigon integration`
- `go test ./cl/phase1/network/... ./cl/beacon/handler/...
./cl/phase1/forkchoice/...`
- `go test -race` on `./cl/phase1/network/services/` (verifier and
service tests) and `./cl/phase1/network/gossip/`

author: lystopad
subject: cl/beacon/handler: size attestation candidates by their new attesters (#24798)
body:
Follow-up to #24566 that addresses its non-blocking review notes.

- `newAttestationCandidate` no longer reserves `len(attestingIndicies)`
entries in its three slices. The loop keeps only attesters with new
flags, and every candidate lives until `selectAttestations` returns. An
aggregate that earlier blocks already included reserved the full
committee size for nothing; with a full pool (10,240 aggregates of ~425
attesters) that was up to ~74 MB. Memory now follows the number of new
attesters.
- Removes the docstring on `newAttestationCandidate`, which repeated the
comment on `attestationCandidate`.
- Removes the redundant `b.ResetTimer()` calls, because `b.Loop()`
resets the timer.

## Test

`TestNewAttestationCandidateReservesNothingWithoutNewFlags`: an
aggregate of 425 attesters that already have all flags set must reserve
no capacity. It fails before the change (capacity 425) and passes after
it. Selection benchmarks are unchanged (~5 ms/op).

The Gloas scoring note on #24566 is pre-existing and separate; it is not
part of this PR.

author: lystopad
subject: cl/phase1/core/state: log fork upgrades at debug level (#24702)
body:
The fork-upgrade log lines fire on every state copy that crosses a fork
epoch, so after a fork a node logs "Upgrade to Gloas complete" many
times per slot at Info. Debug is enough: the upgrade is routine and the
state version is visible elsewhere.

Split out of #24643 at the reviewer's request; no behaviour change
beyond the log level, so no test (trivial change per the TDD
guidelines).

author: Andrew Ashikhmin
subject: cl/transition: verify the payload withdrawals root before applying withdrawals (#24803)
body:
Pre-Gloas `ProcessBlock` built the expected withdrawals from the state
and handed that list to `ProcessWithdrawals`. The spec's
`process_withdrawals` takes the payload's withdrawals, so `ProcessBlock`
now checks that the payload header's withdrawals root equals the root of
the expected list before the list is applied. Going through the header
keeps full and blinded bodies on one path, so relay-built blocks get the
same check.

The check also runs when full validation is disabled, including block
production. This rejects local EL payloads with unexpected withdrawals
before a block is returned for signing.

Tests cover an extra payload withdrawal, a wrong withdrawals root in a
blinded Capella block, and an unexpected withdrawal during local
production. They require the `withdrawals root mismatch` error. Each
regression was confirmed to fail before its fix and pass after it.

Validation:

- `go test ./cl/transition/... ./cl/beacon/handler
./cl/phase1/forkchoice/... ./cl/antiquary/... -count=1`
- 296 mainnet consensus sanity block cases across Capella, Deneb,
Electra and Fulu.
- `make lint`
- `make erigon integration`

Fixes erigontech/security#82.

author: Bruce0X
subject: cl/beacon/handler: answer 206 from node health while syncing (#24719)
body:
`GET /eth/v1/node/health` starts from `http.StatusOK` as the code to
return while the node is syncing, and only uses another code when
`syncing_status` is passed. The Beacon API spec says the endpoint
answers 206 while the node is syncing and describes `syncing_status` as
an override of that 206. Caplin therefore tells load balancers and
monitors that a node still syncing is healthy, unless every caller knows
to add `?syncing_status=206`.

The default is now `http.StatusPartialContent`. The handler also rejects
a `syncing_status` outside 100..599, which is the range the spec allows;
before, a value below 100 reached `WriteHeader`, which panics for those
codes, and a value like 600 was sent as a status no client understands.
The range check runs before the syncing check, so a synced node that
ignored an out-of-range value and answered 200 now answers 400 as well.
The same handler serves the root route `/`, so the 206 applies there
too; both are noted under Breaking Changes in ChangeLog.md.

`TestGetNodeHealthWhileSyncing` covers the default, a custom code, the
bounds 100 and 599, and values below and above the allowed range;
`TestGetNodeHealthWhenSynced` covers the synced path. On main the
default case returns 200 and the out-of-range cases do not return 400.
