author: Kewei
subject: cl/phase1/forkchoice, cl/phase1/network/services: ignore local block import errors and attester slashings that need an unavailable justified state (#24821)
body:
## Summary

A non-ignore error returned by a gossip service's `ProcessMessage` makes
the gossip validator reject the message. Since #24629, when a peer
banner is configured, that rejection also tries to queue a ban of the
sender (an applied ban closes the peer's connection and keeps it banned
for up to 30 minutes). #24629 already ignores local failures in the data
column sidecar and execution payload envelope services. This PR does the
same for two more paths where a local fault can reject a valid message:
block import and attester slashings while syncing.

**Blocks.** After gossip validation, the block service imports the block
with `OnBlock`. An `OnBlock` error that the service did not schedule or
back off was returned as is, so the block was rejected and the validator
tried to queue a ban of its sender. These errors include local ones, for
example:

- the data availability check cannot determine the node's custody
columns or read the index of saved columns (PeerDAS), cannot read the
blob sidecars (Deneb), or cannot write the blob sidecars;
- the parent state cannot be loaded or replayed, including
`ErrMissingSegment`;
- the EL returns an error together with a VALID, SYNCING or ACCEPTED
status;
- a fork choice cache update fails after the state transition.

`OnBlock` marks a permanently invalid block with `ErrBlockInvalid`
(failed state transition, EL `INVALID`, KZG commitments that do not
match the transactions, a block that does not descend from the finalized
checkpoint, an invalid parent payload path). For errors that the
existing scheduling and backoff branches do not handle, the block
service now returns `ErrIgnore` unless the error is `ErrBlockInvalid`.
So after gossip validation a block is rejected only when fork choice
marks it invalid.

Three invalid-block returns in `OnBlock` did not wrap `ErrBlockInvalid`
and would have become ignores. They are now wrapped with
`ErrBlockInvalid`:

- a payload that is already known to be invalid (`block is invalid`);
- a payload whose block hash does not match its contents (`OnBlock:
invalid execution payload hash`);
- a payload that was marked invalid while its EL call was in flight
(`ErrInvalidExecutionPayloadEnvelope` from
`rejectKnownInvalidPayloadStatusLocked`).

With the marker, these errors also end the block's retry job, like other
invalid blocks. So a REST v2 block publication with such a payload
answers 202 (broadcast, failed integration) instead of retrying the
import until the job expires after 30 seconds.

**Attester slashings.** While the node has no head state (`Syncing()`),
`OnAttesterSlashing` checks a slashing against the justified state. A
failure to load that state was returned as is, and a missing state made
`onProcessAttesterSlashing` return `no state accessible`. Both rejected
the slashing, and the validator tried to queue a ban of its sender.

Now a load error is logged and handled like a missing state.
`onProcessAttesterSlashing` first runs the checks that need no state:
that no index list is longer than its capacity, whether every index in
the intersection was already seen, and whether both attestation data are
present and slashable. Without a state, it also checks that both index
lists are sorted sets. Only then does it return
`synced_data.ErrNotSynced`, which the gossip validator ignores. So
without a state, a slashing with non-slashable data or unsorted index
lists is still rejected (unless all its intersecting indices were
already seen, which is an ignore, as with a state), and validation
against an available state is unchanged. `ErrIgnore` is not used here
because the REST attester slashing endpoint publishes a slashing that
returns `ErrIgnore`; with `ErrNotSynced` it keeps answering 400 for
these cases. A slashing whose intersecting indices were all seen before,
including index lists that do not intersect, returns `ErrIgnore` without
a state too, as it does with a state, so the endpoint now answers 200
and publishes it while the justified state is missing, as it does on
`main` when a state is available.

## Not changed here

These candidates were checked and left as they are:

- Execution payload envelopes: fork choice wraps several errors in
`ErrInvalidExecutionPayloadEnvelope` that look local. Commitment
validation hashes an already imported beacon block. The builder
signature check reads the proposer (for a self-build) or the builder,
and the domain, from that block's post-state.
`ProcessExecutionPayloadEnvelope` can fail to hash that state or find
fields missing. These failures can only happen if an invariant is
already broken: the block was hashed when it was imported; a valid Gloas
state (from the fork upgrade, the state transition or SSZ decoding) has
the builder list, the latest bid and the expected withdrawals; the
block's state transition already validated the bid's builder, and
envelope validation checks the envelope's builder index against the
block's bid first; and `GetDomain` does not fail. Fork choice also calls
`blockState.SetPreviousStateRoot(block.Block.StateRoot)` before
`ProcessExecutionPayloadEnvelope`, so its state hashing fallback does
not run. The mismatches these functions report (wrong builder, bad
signature, wrong commitments) are peer faults and stay REJECT.
- Gloas block gossip validation returns a plain `parent block not found`
when fork choice has the parent's header but not its block
(`block_service.go:609`). Fork choice adds a block before its header and
prunes both together; the anchor, which has a header and no block, has
its own case. Only a prune running between the two lookups can reach it,
and pruning drops only blocks more than three epochs before the
finalized checkpoint.
- Payload attestations: the PTC, domain and PTC validator lookups
(`payload_attestation_validation.go:188-222`) read the state of the
attested block at the attestation's slot, which is checked just before.
A missing state is already ignored.
- Execution payload bids: a nil builder list or nil builder entry
(`execution_payload_bid_service.go:777-784`) cannot occur in a valid
Gloas state. An out-of-range, inactive or wrong-version builder is a
REJECT in the spec and stays one.
- If finality advances while `OnBlock` runs and the block stays above
the finalized slot but no longer descends from the finalized checkpoint,
it is still rejected: the gossip rule is "[REJECT] The current finalized
checkpoint is an ancestor of the block", and `OnBlock` returns
`ErrBlockInvalid`. If finality advances past the block, `OnBlock`
returns nil without adding it, as before.
- A block that the new fallback ignores during direct gossip processing
is not newly queued for a retry, the same as before, when it was
rejected. If a scheduled attempt returns a non-`ErrBlockInvalid` error
after adding the header, the job remains non-terminal; any later attempt
skips `OnBlock` because the header is known, so the failed post-header
`OnBlock` work is not run again.
- While syncing, attester slashings are still checked against the
justified state. This matches the fork choice `on_attester_slashing`
handler, but the gossip rule uses the head state, so a slashing of a
validator that the justified state does not know yet is still rejected
(unless all its intersecting indices were already seen). The fork choice
spec tests process slashings in this mode.
- For a gossip slashing from Electra on, while the justified state is
unavailable, each index list length is bounded only by the mainnet
capacity that the SSZ decoder uses (131072). So on the minimal preset,
whose limit is 8192, a slashing with more than 8192 indices that passes
the other checks is ignored instead of rejected.
- Since #24771, `isUnequivocating` no longer panics on 64-bit builds for
a validator index from 2^63 to 2^64-8. While the justified state is
missing, the node cannot tell that such an index is out of range: a
slashing that has it in both index lists and passes the checks that need
no state returns `synced_data.ErrNotSynced`, so gossip ignores it and
the REST endpoint answers 400. With a state it is rejected, as on
`main`.
- Since #24771, a slashing in which at least one intersecting index was
not seen before and that passes the data, index and signature checks is
rejected when no validator of the intersection is slashable. That check
needs the state: while the justified state is missing, such a slashing
that passes the checks that need no state returns
`synced_data.ErrNotSynced`, so gossip ignores it and the REST endpoint
answers 400.
- The attester slashing gossip service decodes with `DecodeSSZ`
(`attester_slashing.go:35`), which accepts some non-canonical encodings,
for example an offset that leaves a gap before a nested index list. Most
gossip services do the same; blocks and the Gloas-only topics use
`DecodeSSZStrict`. With a state, `main` accepts such a slashing if it is
otherwise valid. While the justified state was missing, `main` rejected
such a slashing unless it was already in the operations pool; now, if it
passes the checks that need no state, it returns
`synced_data.ErrNotSynced` and gossip ignores it. Strict decoding for
these topics is a separate change.

## Changes

- `cl/phase1/network/services/block_service.go`: after the existing
scheduling and backoff branches, `ProcessMessage` returns `ErrIgnore`
for every remaining import error except `forkchoice.ErrBlockInvalid`.
The existing branches are unchanged.
- `cl/phase1/forkchoice/on_block.go`: wrap the three invalid-payload
returns with `ErrBlockInvalid`.
- `cl/phase1/forkchoice/on_attester_slashing.go`: while syncing, a
justified state load error is logged and handled like a missing state;
`onProcessAttesterSlashing` checks for a missing state after the checks
that need no state, then checks that both index lists are sorted sets
(their lengths were already checked against their capacities), and then
returns `synced_data.ErrNotSynced`.
- `cl/phase1/network/services/block_service_test.go`:
`TestBlockServiceIgnoresLocalOnBlockFailureOnly`.
- `cl/phase1/forkchoice/fork_choice_test.go`,
`cl/phase1/forkchoice/on_block_lock_scope_test.go`: assert
`ErrBlockInvalid` in `TestOnBlockHashMismatchPreservesVerifiedPayload`
and `TestOnBlockMalformedHashIsNotCachedAgainstTheClaimedHash`; new
`TestOnBlockRejectsPayloadInvalidatedDuringValidation`.
- `cl/phase1/forkchoice/forkchoice_test.go`:
`TestOnAttesterSlashingIgnoresMissingJustifiedStateWhileSyncing` (also
with an Electra-capacity slashing of 2049 indices that targets a
pre-Electra epoch),
`TestOnAttesterSlashingRejectsInvalidSlashingWhileSyncing`
(non-slashable data and unsorted indices, with the justified state
available, missing, or failing to load); the test fork graph can return
a `GetState` error.

## Testing

- **Red on `main`:** with the production files from `main`, these fail:
`TestBlockServiceIgnoresLocalOnBlockFailureOnly/local_failure`, all four
subtests of
`TestOnAttesterSlashingIgnoresMissingJustifiedStateWhileSyncing`
(missing state and load error, each with the single-index and the
2049-index slashing),
`TestOnBlockRejectsPayloadInvalidatedDuringValidation`,
`TestOnBlockMalformedHashIsNotCachedAgainstTheClaimedHash` and
`TestOnBlockHashMismatchPreservesVerifiedPayload` (its `block is
invalid` assertion also fails on its own when only that marker is
reverted). The `missing` and `load_error` cases of
`TestOnAttesterSlashingRejectsInvalidSlashingWhileSyncing`
(non-slashable data, unsorted indices) fail too: before it checks the
slashing, `main` returns `no state accessible` for a missing state, or
the load error. The reverse cases
`TestBlockServiceIgnoresLocalOnBlockFailureOnly/invalid_block` and the
`available` cases of
`TestOnAttesterSlashingRejectsInvalidSlashingWhileSyncing` pass before
and after; `invalid_block` fails if the block service ignores every
import error.
- `go test -p 2 -count=1 ./cl/phase1/network/services/
./cl/phase1/forkchoice/... ./cl/phase1/network/gossip/
./cl/beacon/handler/`
- Fork choice spec tests: `go test -count=1 -v -run
'Test/mainnet/.*/fork_choice' ./cl/spectest/` (v1.7.0-beta.2 fixtures,
285 passed, 27 skipped by the suite), including
`discard_equivocations_on_attester_slashing`.
- `make lint`, `make erigon integration`.

---------

Co-authored-by: lystopad <oleksandr.lystopad@erigon.tech>

author: Kewei
subject: cl/phase1/network, cl/beacon/handler: handle gloas proposer preferences in the epoch before the fork (#24809)
body:
## Summary

The Gloas p2p spec says for `proposer_preferences`: "Nodes SHOULD
subscribe to this topic at least one epoch before the fork activation.
Proposers SHOULD broadcast their preferences in the epoch before the
fork." Phase0 p2p derives a topic's fork digest from the context epoch
of the message. The Gloas spec does not define the context epoch for a
preference, and the two clients I checked differ:

- Prysm subscribes to `proposer_preferences` only on digests from Gloas
on and joins them in the epoch before the fork. It accepts a preference
on the current digest or on the next epoch's digest, and publishes on
the digest of the proposal epoch (`BroadcastForEpoch`).
- Lighthouse also subscribes to `proposer_preferences` only on Gloas-era
digests (`core_topics_to_subscribe`) and joins them one epoch early, but
it publishes every message on the current digest. During the last Fulu
epoch its preferences for the first Gloas epoch therefore go out on the
Fulu digest.

Caplin lost these preferences in three places (G is the Gloas fork
epoch):

- Inbound: the `proposer_preferences` topic was registered with
`withBeginVersion(clparams.GloasVersion)`, which the gossip validator
evaluates with the version of the current epoch. During epoch G-1 this
condition was false for every preference from a peer, on any fork
digest, so the message was ignored before decoding and before
`ProposerPreferencesService` saw it. Gossipsub marks a message ID as
seen before it runs the validator, so later copies of the same message
on that topic did not reach the validator again while the ID stayed in
the seen cache.
- Subscription: the gossip manager joined the next fork digest's topics
only 8 slots before the digest change, so on mainnet-preset networks it
was not on the Gloas `proposer_preferences` topic during the first 24
slots of G-1.
- Outbound: preferences submitted through the beacon API were published
on the current fork digest, which during G-1 is the Fulu digest, a topic
Prysm and Lighthouse do not subscribe to.

Impact at a Gloas activation (of Caplin's built-in configs only Sepolia
schedules Gloas so far; mainnet and Hoodi do not yet): a Caplin node
would miss the peers' preferences for epoch G that were gossiped during
G-1. Unless it got a matching preference another way, its
`execution_payload_bid` validation then ignores a bid for such a
proposer's slot (no matching preferences), so it neither keeps nor
relays the bid. Preferences submitted to Caplin during G-1 did not reach
Prysm and Lighthouse nodes.

Fix:

- `proposer_preferences` has no version condition any more. A preference
on a known fork digest is no longer stopped by the fork version and,
after the existing head-slot and rate-limit conditions, goes on to
`ProposerPreferencesService`, which already ignores proposal epochs
before G. So during G-1 Caplin takes the preferences on the Gloas digest
and the ones Lighthouse publishes on the Fulu digest, and after G the
ones still in flight on the Fulu digest. When the same signed preference
is published on both digests (for example by two beacon nodes that pick
different digests), Caplin stores and relays the first copy it accepts,
on that copy's topic, and its duplicate check (slot and dependent root)
ignores a later one. This follows the Altair gossip transition rules
("Messages on pre and post-fork variants of topics share
application-level caches"; "Messages SHOULD NOT be re-broadcast from one
fork to the other"). Prysm and Lighthouse nodes are not on the Fulu
topic during G-1, so a Fulu copy does not stop them from relaying the
Gloas copy.
- On each fork-check tick and at the end of each service registration,
the gossip manager joins the `proposer_preferences` topic, and only that
topic, for the fork digests of the next epoch and of the epoch one epoch
and two slots ahead. The preferences service accepts preferences for
epoch X+1 from the start of epoch X minus
`MAXIMUM_GOSSIP_CLOCK_DISPARITY` (500 ms); with two slots the topic of
epoch X+1 is joined by the tick in slot 32X-2, so with the unaligned
ticker the margin is one slot minus 500 ms (11.5 s on mainnet) when that
tick falls at the end of the slot. The registration-time call gives a
node started during G-1 the topic before the beacon API starts, and in
the last slots of an epoch the second digest is that of the epoch after
next, so a digest change right after the next one (for example a BPO at
G+1) is joined before G starts. All other topics keep the 8-slot switch
and the delayed unsubscribe of the old digest.
- `subscribeUpcomingTopics` no longer stops at a target topic that
already exists. It subscribes that target with the source topic's expiry
(`SubscribeWithExpiry` never shortens an expiry; an expiry in the past
is ignored), which heals a copy that was added but not subscribed, and
goes on with the next topic. Before, joining that topic again returned
`topic already exists` and stopped the loop, so the regular switch 8
slots before the digest change could leave the topics after it (in map
order) unsubscribed. It also skips a source topic that the delayed
cleanup removed after the topic list was taken, and
`TopicSubscriptions.Get` now returns a copy made under the lock, so
reading the source's expiry does not race with the cleanup's
`Unsubscribe`, whose timer fires in phase with the fork-check ticker.
- `postProposerPreferences` publishes with
`GossipManager.PublishToForkDigest` (from #24629): on the digest of the
proposal epoch while the current epoch is before G, and on the current
digest from G on. During G-1 the Gloas digest is the only
`proposer_preferences` digest Prysm and Lighthouse subscribe to. From G
on, Caplin publishes on the current digest because peers can join the
next digest late (8 slots before the change in earlier Caplin versions).
Each request publishes on one digest, not on both: in the epoch before a
later digest change, Prysm, Lighthouse and Caplin stay subscribed to the
current digest, and a node that accepts both copies ignores the later
one.
- Publish errors are reported as in `pool.go`: a `ComputeForkDigest`
error returns 500, a publish error adds a failure entry for that index
(400), and an identical retry of a stored preference is published again
instead of being acknowledged without a publish, so a retry after a
failed publish gets another publish attempt (publishing a message again
on the same topic is a no-op in libp2p while its ID is in the
delivered-message cache).

## Not changed here

- `execution_payload_bid`, `execution_payload` and
`payload_attestation_message` still ignore messages before the fork. The
spec's pre-fork note covers only `proposer_preferences`, and the Altair
fork transition rules allow ignoring messages on post-fork topics before
the fork. A bid for the first Gloas slot sent during the last Fulu slot
is still ignored. Passing the topic's version to the gossip conditions
would change this, but also the boundary behaviour of the other
version-gated topics, so it is left for a separate change.
- The fork-check goroutine still assumes, as on `main`, that service
registration finishes before its first tick, one slot after the gossip
manager starts, and the registration-time call runs concurrently with
it. A copy made between adding a topic and subscribing it is now
subscribed on the next tick by the existing-target repair. Starting the
loop only after registration is left for a separate change.
- The old fork digest's topics are still removed 16 slots after the
regular switch, about 8 slots after the fork; the Altair transition
rules recommend two epochs.
- The no-service fallback of `postProposerPreferences` (not used by
`run.go`) still acknowledges an identical retry without publishing it.
- Overlap with #24776: both PRs change the `proposer_preferences`
registration line in `cl/phase1/network/registry/register.go` (this PR
removes the version condition, #24776 replaces the rate limiter), so the
second one to merge gets a one-line conflict. The resolution keeps both
changes: `waitReady, proposerPreferencesRateLimiter()`. The registry
test of this PR is in its own file.

## Changes

- `cl/phase1/network/registry/register.go`: no version condition for
`proposer_preferences`.
- `cl/phase1/network/registry/register_gloas_boundary_test.go`: new
test.
- `cl/phase1/network/gossip/gossip_manager.go`: new
`subscribeUpcomingProposerPreferences`, called on every fork-check tick
and after each service registration; name filter, existing-target repair
and removed-source skip in `subscribeUpcomingTopics`.
- `cl/phase1/network/gossip/gossip_subscription.go`: `Get` returns a
copy of the entry.
- `cl/phase1/network/gossip/gossip_manager_test.go`,
`gossip_subscription_test.go`: four new tests.
- `cl/beacon/handler/epbs.go`: publish preferences with
`PublishToForkDigest`, report publish errors, publish identical retries.
- `cl/beacon/handler/epbs_test.go`: one new test; three tests changed.

## Testing

- **TDD:** each test fails with its production change reverted and
passes with it:
- `TestRegisterGossipServicesProcessesGloasPreferencesOneEpochEarly`
(current epoch G-1, current digest Fulu, next epoch's digest Gloas; one
case publishes on the Fulu topic created at registration, one on the
Gloas topic joined at registration, both through the validator because
the test's host is nil): with `register.go` from `main` both cases fail
with `validation ignored`; with the earlier topic-version condition the
Fulu case does; without the join after registration the Gloas case fails
with `topic not found`.
- `TestGossipManagerSubscribesProposerPreferencesOneEpochEarly`: calls
`subscribeUpcomingProposerPreferences` at slot 32G-35 (not joined) and
32G-34 (joined and subscribed; `beacon_block` not joined); with one slot
instead of two, the topic is not joined at 32G-34.
-
`TestRegisterGossipServiceSubscribesProposerPreferencesForNextEpochImmediately`
(registration in the last slot of G-1, with a BPO digest change at G+1):
without the call after registration both topics are missing; joining
only the digest one epoch and two slots ahead misses the G topic, and
publishing on the G digest fails with `topic not found`.
- `TestSubscribeUpcomingTopicsSubscribesExistingTargetAndContinues` (one
target added but not subscribed): without the skip, `topic already
exists`; without the repair, the target stays unsubscribed.
- `TestTopicSubscriptionsGetReturnsSnapshot`: with `Get` returning the
stored entry, a later change of the entry's expiry is visible to the
caller.
- `TestPostProposerPreferencesPublishResultsAndDigest`: a publish error
returns 400 with a failure entry for that index and a
`ComputeForkDigest` error 500 (both 200 before); with the current epoch
at Gloas and a different digest for the next epoch, the preference is
published on the current digest (the proposal epoch's before).
- `TestPostProposerPreferencesAcknowledgesOnlyIdenticalRetries`: with
the service, the identical retry is published again (no publish before).
- `TestPostValidatorProposerPreferencesGloasForkBoundary` (real clock in
G-1) and `TestPostProposerPreferencesWithoutServiceConcurrentRequests`:
with the `Publish` call from `main`, unexpected `Publish` and missing
`PublishToForkDigest`; with `PublishToForkDigest` on the current digest,
the fork boundary test fails on the digest (Fulu instead of Gloas).
- The nil check for a source topic removed after the topic list was
taken has no test: it needs the delayed cleanup to run between the two
lookups.
- A probe on `main` with a remote gossipsub peer and the mocked current
epoch at G-1 showed that a message on a topic registered with
`withBeginVersion(clparams.GloasVersion)` never reaches
`ProcessMessage`; with the current epoch at G it does.
- `go test -p 2 ./cl/phase1/network/registry/
./cl/phase1/network/gossip/... ./cl/beacon/handler/`; `-race` on the
registry and gossip packages; `make lint`, `make erigon integration`.
- Not run on a devnet across a Gloas fork.

author: Kewei
subject: cl: verify proposer slashing signatures over the header and accept one per proposer (#24846)
body:
## Summary

Gossip and REST validation of proposer slashings
(`cl/phase1/network/services/proposer_slashing_service.go`) computed
each header's signing root over the whole `SignedBeaconBlockHeader`
(header and signature) instead of over `signed_header.message`. The
phase0 `process_proposer_slashing`, whose conditions the
`proposer_slashing` gossip topic requires, signs
`signed_header.message`, so every correctly signed proposer slashing
failed with `invalid signature`:

- On gossip the slashing was rejected. Since #24629, a rejection makes
the gossip manager try to queue a ban of the sending peer, so this bug
can cause an honest relaying peer to be banned.
- `POST /eth/v1/beacon/pool/proposer_slashings` answered 400 for a valid
slashing and did not add it to the pool or publish it.
- Valid slashings therefore never reached the operations pool through
gossip or REST, so the node did not include them in the blocks it
proposed.

Block import is not affected: proposer slashings inside a block are
checked by the state transition, not by this service.

The first commit computes the signing root over `signedHeader.Header`,
as the blob and data column sidecar services already do for their signed
headers. The other signature checks in `cl/phase1/network/services`
already sign the object the spec defines; for signed envelopes that is
the inner message or header.

Once valid slashings pass, the service starts to fill its proposer
cache, which makes older paths in `ProcessMessage` reachable. The second
commit fixes them:

- A proposer cache hit returned nil, which the gossip manager maps to
ACCEPT. After one slashing for a proposer was accepted, any later object
whose first header names that proposer skipped every check and was
relayed, also a malformed one. The gossip rule IGNOREs everything after
the first valid proposer slashing for a proposer, so a cache hit now
returns `ErrIgnore`.
- A pool hit also returned nil. The pool key hashes only the two
signatures (`pool.ComputeKeyForProposerSlashing`), so the signatures of
a pooled slashing copied onto other headers were accepted without
validation. The shortcut is removed: such an object is now validated and
rejected, and repeats are caught by the proposer cache.
- The proposer cache was checked at the start and filled at the end, so
two different valid slashings for the same proposer processed
concurrently were both accepted, added to the pool and emitted. The
proposer is now claimed with `LoadOrStore` after both signatures verify,
and the loser gets `ErrIgnore`.
- The proposer cache was an LRU of 100 entries, so once 100 other
proposers had been accepted, a second valid slashing for an evicted
proposer was accepted again. It is now a `sync.Map` that does not evict.
An index is stored only after a slashing signed by that proposer
verifies, at most once per validator index. Lighthouse also keeps
observed proposer indices in a set without a size limit.

After this, every `ErrIgnore` from the service means that the proposer
has already been claimed by a fully validated slashing. `POST
/eth/v1/beacon/pool/proposer_slashings` treated both nil and `ErrIgnore`
as success and published the submitted object. With the first commit
alone, the cache and pool shortcuts returned nil, so the handler could
publish unvalidated objects. On `ErrIgnore` it now answers 200 without
publishing. The Beacon API asks the node to broadcast a slashing that
passes validation. Lighthouse answers 200 without publishing for an
already known proposer, and Caplin's attestation handlers do the same
for an already seen attestation (`ErrAttestationAlreadySeen`).

## Not changed here

- release/3.7 has the same bug. A `[r3.7]` backport will follow once
this merges.
- If `Publish` fails for a slashing submitted over REST, the handler
still answers 200, as before. With the second commit, a resubmission
gets `ErrIgnore` and is not published again. The slashing was added to
the pool before `Publish`, so it stays in the pool unless the usual pool
eviction or finalized-state pruning removes it, and the node can include
it in a block it proposes while it passes the usual block production
checks. Lighthouse also records the proposer before it publishes and
does not publish a resubmission for a known proposer.
- The proposer set lives until restart; Lighthouse additionally clears
its set at fork boundaries.
- The event is still sent inside `ViewHeadState`, under the head state
read lock.
- Related services have similar gaps: concurrent valid voluntary exits
or BLS changes for the same validator both return nil (only one is
stored); sync committee contributions return nil for an already seen
contribution; the REST handlers for voluntary exits, attester slashings,
BLS changes and sync committee contributions still publish on
`ErrIgnore`.

## Changes

- `cl/phase1/network/services/proposer_slashing_service.go`: compute the
signing root over `signedHeader.Header`; replace the proposer LRU with a
`sync.Map`; return `ErrIgnore` when the proposer is already there;
remove the pool shortcut; claim the proposer with `LoadOrStore` after
the signatures verify, and only the winner adds the slashing to the pool
and emits it. The `proposer_slashing` LRU hit and miss metrics go away
with the LRU.
- `cl/phase1/network/services/constants.go`: remove
`proposerSlashingCacheSize`.
- `cl/phase1/network/services/proposer_slashing_service_test.go`: new
tests with real `fork.ComputeSigningRoot` and BLS signatures:
`TestProposerSlashingServiceAcceptsSpecSignedHeaders` (a slashing signed
as the spec does is accepted and pooled),
`TestProposerSlashingServiceIgnoresMalformedAfterAccepted` (a malformed
slashing for an accepted proposer is ignored and not pooled),
`TestProposerSlashingServiceKeepsAcceptedProposerAfterManyOthers` (after
100 other proposers, a second valid slashing for the first proposer is
still ignored) and
`TestProposerSlashingServiceConcurrentValidationAcceptsOne` (two valid
slashings for one proposer are held at signature verification until both
arrive; exactly one is accepted and pooled, the other is ignored). In
`TestProcessMessage`, the mocked test expects `ComputeSigningRoot` to be
called with each header, the seen-proposer case expects `ErrIgnore`, and
the pool case now checks that pooled signatures on invalid headers are
rejected, not ignored.
- `cl/beacon/handler/pool.go`: on `ErrIgnore`, answer 200 without
publishing.
- `cl/beacon/handler/pool_test.go`: new
`TestPoolProposerSlashingDoesNotPublishIgnored`.

## Testing

- **TDD:** with the production file from `main`,
`TestProposerSlashingServiceAcceptsSpecSignedHeaders` fails with
`invalid signature`. With the production files of the first commit (the
services test package then needs a one-line shim, `seenProposers.Store`
to the old `cache.Add`, to compile), these fail and pass with the
second: `TestProcessMessage` (the seen-proposer and pooled-signature
cases return nil),
`TestProposerSlashingServiceIgnoresMalformedAfterAccepted` (nil instead
of `ErrIgnore`),
`TestProposerSlashingServiceKeepsAcceptedProposerAfterManyOthers` (the
evicted proposer is accepted again),
`TestProposerSlashingServiceConcurrentValidationAcceptsOne` (both
accepted, in 20 of 20 runs) and
`TestPoolProposerSlashingDoesNotPublishIgnored` (unexpected `Publish`).
- `go test -race -count=50 -run TestProposerSlashing
./cl/phase1/network/services/`
- `go test ./cl/phase1/network/services/ ./cl/beacon/handler/`
- `make lint`
- `make erigon integration`

author: awskii
subject: cl: recheck the head root in the cached-state fast path and test the head-copy paths (#23962)
body:
#24165 already copies the new head outside the reader locks. This PR
fixes a race in the cached-state fast path and keeps two tests main
lacks.

## Changes
- `useCachedStateIfPossible` matched `HeadRoot()` before taking the
head-state lock, so a publish in between returned the new head's state
for the old root. It now reads root and state together via
`ViewHeadStateWithIdentity` and falls back to the previous head if the
head moved. `TestHeadFastPathRechecksRootAfterHeadMoves` publishes right
after `HeadRoot()`; before the fix the lookup returned slot 2 for the
slot-1 root.
- `TestFailedHeadUpdateKeepsHead`: a failed copy leaves `StateHead()`,
the head and the previous state unchanged.
- `TestPreviousHeadFastPathUsesAuthoritativePriorRoot`: the
previous-head path returns the state for a root that depends on
`previousStateRoot` and misses for the recomputed root.

---------

author: Kewei
subject: cl/phase1/forkchoice: record gloas payload status when el validation is skipped (#24878)
body:
## Summary

After a restart of a node with an embedded EL, the Gloas fork choice
head stayed behind the imported chain and climbed back only one block
per ChainTipSync cycle. The forkchoice update for the stale head made
the EL unwind, and validator duties were served on the stale head. A
node that checkpoint-syncs with an embedded EL takes the same code path.

Payload verification status is kept only in memory. Startup creates a
fresh fork choice store, and ForwardSync replays the downloaded Gloas
envelopes into it. When the attached EL supports insertion (the embedded
EL, through the direct client or the in-process Engine API client),
ForwardSync replays the envelopes with `validatePayload=false`.
`applyEnvelopeCoordinated` persisted these envelopes but recorded a
payload status only when no engine was attached. Gloas fork choice
offers the FULL variant of a block only when its payload status is
`NotValidated` or `Validated`, so `computeHeadGloas` stopped at the
first replayed block whose child builds on its payload.
`verifyUnverifiedGloasPayloads` looks for unverified payloads only at
the selected head and its ancestors, so it never reached the replayed
blocks above the stale head: each cycle validated one more block and the
head moved up by one.

Measured on `main`:

- Local devnet, embedded node restarted at slot 70: ForwardSync finished
after 6 s with the EL at the tip, then the head went back to slot 65 and
the EL unwound to block 63. The head advanced one slot at a time from 65
to 69 and then jumped to the live tip at slot 75, 55 s after startup.
The node's proposal at slot 73 was built on an EMPTY parent and was
missed.
- A node joining the same devnet by checkpoint sync took 373 s to catch
up, with its head about 32 slots behind the tip.
- On Sepolia, catching up after a restart took about 8.5 minutes.

Now `applyEnvelopeCoordinated` also records a status when an engine is
attached but the call skips EL validation: `NotValidated`, or
`Validated` when a validated verdict for the root or the execution
payload hash is already cached (the same rule as in
`applyPayloadValidationResultLocked`). This check is needed because
`markPayloadStatus` keeps a `Validated` status recorded for the same
root and any known `Invalidated` status, but not a `Validated` verdict
that is cached only for the execution payload hash; without it, a
concurrent validating call can lose that verdict.

With `validatePayload=false`, the replay still runs the full envelope
commitment checks, including the locally derived block hash, and
`ProcessExecutionPayloadEnvelope`, including the builder signature. It
does not call `NewPayload`, and, as before, it skips
`validateEnvelopeAgainstBlockAfterCommitments` and the payload arrival
record; ForwardSync also passes `checkBlobData=false`, so data
availability is not checked during the replay. `NotValidated` means that
these checks passed and there is no EL verdict yet; it is the status
that the path without an engine already records.

Replayed payloads are now eligible for FULL head selection right away,
so on a single chain the head reaches the newest replayed block in one
fork choice pass. The sweep then asks the EL to validate the unverified
payloads on the head's ancestry.

Other callers: with an attached EL, the chain-tip parent replay passes
`validatePayload=false` only for envelopes that are already stored, and
those return at the `HasEnvelope` check before the new code. Gossip, the
beacon API, envelope recovery and the pending-envelope retry request EL
validation when an EL is attached. Without an engine, the path still
records `NotValidated`, except that a cached `Validated` verdict is now
kept.

## Not changed here

- Persisting payload status across restarts. With an insertion-capable
EL, replayed payloads start as `NotValidated` and the sweep validates
them again.
- The sweep direction: `verifyUnverifiedGloasPayloads` still looks only
at the selected head and its ancestors.
- ForwardSync records the status before it queues the block and its
envelope in the block collector, which it flushes after the replay; a
flush failure is logged, not returned. This order is unchanged.
- A stale-head guard for block production, for example refusing to
produce while the served head is far behind the highest seen slot.
- `is_syncing` and `is_optimistic` reporting.
- v3.7.1 is affected too; a `[r3.7]` backport will follow.

## Changes

- `cl/phase1/forkchoice/on_execution_payload.go`: in
`applyEnvelopeCoordinated`, record the payload status also when
`validatePayload` is false (`NotValidated`, or `Validated` if a
validated verdict is cached).
- `cl/phase1/forkchoice/on_execution_payload_test.go`:
`TestOnExecutionPayloadWithoutEngineMarksPayloadOptimistic` has a new
case that attaches a mock engine, which fails the test on any
`NewPayload` call, and calls `OnExecutionPayload` with
`validatePayload=false`. Both cases now use a fork graph that tracks
accepted payloads and check that the payload is not verified.
- `cl/phase1/stages/chain_tip_sync_recovery_test.go`:
`TestForwardSyncReplayMakesGloasPayloadAvailableForHeadSelection`
replays one envelope through the forward-sync helper
`processDownloadedGloasEnvelope` with an insertion-capable EL, adds a
child that builds on the replayed block's FULL payload, and checks that
this child becomes the head without a `NewPayload` call.

## Testing

- **TDD:** with the production file from `main`,
`TestOnExecutionPayloadWithoutEngineMarksPayloadOptimistic/without_EL_validation`
fails (the payload is not available) and
`TestForwardSyncReplayMakesGloasPayloadAvailableForHeadSelection` fails
(the head stays at the parent instead of moving to the child that builds
on its FULL payload). Both pass with the fix.
- Without the cached `Validated` check (always `NotValidated`), the
existing
`TestExecutionPayloadIngressAppliesTerminalResultBeforeDuplicateShortCircuit`
fails.
-
`TestExecutionPayloadIngressAppliesTerminalResultBeforeDuplicateShortCircuit`,
`TestPersistedEnvelopeDoesNotSynthesizeValidatedELResult`,
`TestLocalSelfBuildPreservesTerminalInvalidationAcrossYield` and
`TestForwardSyncValidatesOnlyWhenInsertionIsUnavailable` pass unchanged.
- `go test -p 2 -count=1 ./cl/phase1/forkchoice/...
./cl/phase1/stages/...`
- Consensus spec tests `Test/mainnet/.*/fork_choice` (v1.7.0-beta.2):
same results as on `main`, no failures.
- `make lint`, `make erigon integration`.
- Not yet run on a devnet or Sepolia with this change. The tests cover
one replayed block and its child, with a fake block collector; they do
not cover a full restart, EL insertion, the sweep or the forkchoice
update.

Co-authored-by: Alex Sharov <AskAlexSharov@gmail.com>

author: lystopad
subject: cl/phase1/forkchoice/fork_graph: read the anchor state off the dump grid (#24718)
body:
Fixes #24717

`forkGraphDisk.getState` reads a state file from disk only at slots
divisible by `dumpSlotFrequency`. The anchor state is always written to
disk by `NewForkGraphDisk`, but when the anchor is at a slot that is not
a multiple of 4, `getState` never reads it. This happens when Caplin
resumes from a finalized checkpoint whose block is followed by a missed
first slot of an epoch.

Once `currentState` moves past such an anchor, no state that descends
from it can be rebuilt. `getCheckpointState` then fails with `baseState
not found in graph` on every slot. Head states are written to disk only
after a successful fork choice, so the node never recovers. It keeps
importing blocks, but its head never moves.

This change makes `getState` read the anchor's state file whatever its
slot. All other behaviour is unchanged: if the anchor is at a slot
divisible by 4, the condition was already true. This covers both a
post-block anchor (local resume) and an anchor advanced through empty
slots (checkpoint sync with an empty epoch-start slot).

An advanced anchor state is at a later slot than its block. So for a
slot or state-root `state_id`, the Beacon API handlers that look up a
state by block root (`getFullState` and the builders endpoint) now treat
a fork-choice state at a different slot as missing, and fall back to the
historical reader. Without this, a request for the anchor block's slot
or state root could return the advanced state. `head`, `finalized` and
`justified` still get the fork-choice state as it is: for them the
advanced anchor state is the checkpoint state, which matches Lighthouse
and Nimbus for `finalized`.

#### Tests

- `TestGetState_AnchorOffDumpSlot` uses blockA's post-state as an
off-grid anchor, both as it is and advanced through an empty slot. It
adds blockB, reloads the anchor state and compares its root, then
rebuilds blockB's state from the anchor file and compares it with the
block's state root. Both cases fail on `main` and pass with the fix.
- `TestGetStateFullSkipsForkchoiceStateAtLaterSlot` and
`TestPostStateBuildersSkipsAdvancedForkchoiceStateForSlotAndStateRoot`
put an advanced state into fork choice for the head root. They check
that a request by slot or by state root does not return the advanced
state; the builders test asserts the 400 of the pre-Gloas archive
fallback.
- `TestGetStateFullFinalizedServesAdvancedForkchoiceState` and
`TestPostStateBuildersServesAdvancedForkchoiceStateForFinalized` check
that `finalized` still returns the advanced fork-choice state.
- `go test -race ./cl/beacon/handler/ ./cl/phase1/forkchoice/...` and
`make lint` pass.

#### Verification

I ran a `release/3.7` build with this change on the Hoodi node from
#24717. It resumed from the same slot-4109535 finalized state that had
stalled the old binary. Fork choice succeeded right away, the head
followed the wall-clock slot and finality advanced.

A backport to `release/3.7` will follow after review.

A failed read of the anchor state file is logged at Warn: once
`currentState` has moved on, the file is the only copy of the anchor
state, and a silent failure would leave the #24717 stall without a cause
in the logs.

author: Bruce0X
subject: cl/clparams: use the gnosis data column request window on gnosis and chiado (#24720)
body:
The Gnosis and Chiado beacon configs set
`MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS` to 16384 but do not set
`MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS`, so both networks inherit
the mainnet default of 4096 epochs. The network configs in
gnosischain/configs set it to 16384 for both `mainnet` and `chiado`,
next to the blob value.

The value feeds `DataColumnSidecarServeRangeStartSlot`, which the
pruning stage, the blob downloader and checkpoint sync use as the
retention floor, and the data column req/resp handler uses it to bound
the requested range and the age of served columns. With 4096 a Gnosis
node prunes columns four times earlier than the network requires,
refuses `DataColumnSidecarsByRange` requests that span more than 4096
epochs, and backfills a shorter window than its peers expect.

Both configs now set the field to 16384.
`TestGnosisNetworksUseConfiguredDataColumnRequestWindow` checks the
field and the resulting serve-range start slot for both chains; on main
it reports 4096.

The wider window also showed that `earliest_available_slot` only follows
the prune floor. A node restarted on a store pruned under the old
4096-epoch window would advertise columns it no longer has, for up to
about 11 days. `PeerDas.PruneBelow` now advertises the start of the
lowest non-empty column bucket when that is above the floor.
`TestPeerDasPruneBelowDoesNotAdvertiseColumnsPrunedUnderAShorterWindow`
reopens a store pruned under a shorter window; on main it advertises the
lower floor. ChangeLog.md notes the larger retention on both chains.

---------

author: lystopad
subject: cl/das: recover the blob rows of a block in parallel (#24861)
body:
Fixes #24858.

## Problem

`RecoverMatrix` recovers the blob rows of a block one after another,
about 0.1 s per row with go-eth-kzg. A supernode that completes a
block's columns by recovery waits for the whole sequential recovery
before the block enters fork choice and reaches the EL. On a mainnet
supernode running release/3.7, the time from the 64th to the 128th
stored column grew by about 0.12 s per blob (0.49 s for 4 blobs, 0.76 s
for 6, 0.93 s for 8, 1.08 s for 9), and the block was imported about
0.15 s after its last column.

## Change

`cl/das/utils/das_utils.go`: `RecoverMatrix` recovers the rows in
parallel. A package-level semaphore of `GOMAXPROCS` slots bounds the
rows in flight across all calls (Caplin runs 8 recovery workers). Each
row is written to its own index, so the result keeps row order. Every
row is attempted; if any fails, the error of the lowest failing row is
returned, the same row the sequential version reported. go-eth-kzg
ignores the `numGoRoutines` argument for recovery, so rows were never
recovered concurrently. The multi-exponentiations inside FK20 already
spread over the cores on their own, outside this bound; the slots bound
the rows in flight and their working buffers, not cores.

## Results

`BenchmarkRecoverMatrix` (half of the columns of dense blobs, Apple M3
Max, 16 cores, 5 iterations, both versions on the same input):

| blobs | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 99 ms | 99 ms |
| 6 | 594 ms | 163 ms |
| 9 | 892 ms | 194 ms |
| 16 | 1,589 ms | 334 ms |

With `GOMAXPROCS=8` the first version of this change took 206 / 351 /
512 ms for 6 / 9 / 16 blobs. The mainnet node above runs with
`GOMAXPROCS` 24.

## Tests

No unit test covered `RecoverMatrix`. This is a performance change with
the same output, so the first two tests pass before and after and
protect the behaviour:
- `TestRecoverMatrixRestoresEveryRowInOrder`: three blobs, the even
columns given last row first; the recovered matrix equals the original
one. Writing rows to the wrong index fails it.
- `TestRecoverMatrixReportsTheRowThatCannotBeRecovered`: one row with
too few cells returns its error. Dropping the row errors fails it.
- `TestRecoverMatrixReportsTheLowestBrokenRow`: rows 1 and 2 broken, 20
runs, always `blob 1`. It failed with the first version of this change
(first error recorded) and passes on main.
- `TestRecoverMatrixWaitsForAFreeRowSlot`: with every slot taken no row
starts, and each row gives its slot back. It fails with a per-call limit
and without the deferred release.
- `BenchmarkRecoverMatrix` in `das_utils_bench_test.go`.

`go test -race ./cl/das/...`, `make lint` (twice), `make erigon
integration`.

author: lystopad
subject: cl/p2p: cap connections per /24 and /16 in the resource manager (#24815)
body:
Refs #24444. Replaces #24449.

## Problem

`buildOptions` already installs go-libp2p's resource manager. In v0.49.0
its defaults cap connections per IPv4 address (8) and per IPv6 /56 (8)
and /48 (64), rate-limit them per source, release each slot when the
connection scope ends on every exit path, and act on QUIC before the
handshake. It has no cap for larger blocks, so one operator holding a
/24 or a /16 can still fill the peer pool, slowly, under the per-address
limits.

## Change

`newResourceManager(cfg)` passes per-block limits through
`rcmgr.WithLimitPerSubnet`:

| Block | Cap | At the default `--caplin.max-peer-count=128` |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 address, IPv6 /56 | 8 (go-libp2p's default, repeated because the
option replaces the defaults) | 8 |
| IPv4 /24, IPv6 /48 | max(16, max-peer-count/8) | 16 |
| IPv4 /16, IPv6 /32 | max(/24 cap, max-peer-count/2) | 64 |

A /24 (or a /48, one end site) may hold an eighth of the pool and a /16
half of it, so filling the pool takes several blocks. The floor of 16,
two per-address caps, keeps small pools from refusing two busy hosts.
The lists are ordered broadest first: go-libp2p stores a zero count for
every prefix it checks before the one that refuses, and only a closed
connection removes it, so with the narrowest prefix first refused
connections would leave entries until restart.

With `--caplin.local-discovery`, private (RFC 1918, RFC 6598),
link-local and IPv6 ULA networks are exempt from all of these caps
through `rcmgr.WithNetworkPrefixLimit`, the per-address one included, so
LAN and docker peers are not limited. All connections of one exempt
network share one limit of max(32, 8 × max-peer-count), which never
limits the pool; it stays finite because go-libp2p uses half of it as
the network's QUIC source-address verification burst. Loopback keeps
go-libp2p's unlimited default.

Static peers (`--sentinel.staticpeers`, including direct bootnodes)
given by IP address are counted only per address: each gets its own
network prefix limit on its IPv4 /32 or IPv6 /56 with go-libp2p's cap of
8, which skips the block caps, so a full block does not keep refusing
the dials to them. A static peer on loopback or inside an exempt network
keeps that network's allowance (go-libp2p matches the most specific
prefix first, so no entry is added for it). Static peers given by DNS
name are not covered.

There is no custom accounting: slots are go-libp2p connection scopes.
Refusals are counted per /24 or /48 by a thin wrapper and logged at Info
once a minute when there were any, with the five most refused blocks,
because go-libp2p refuses them before its metrics count anything and
logs them only at Debug.

## Behaviour changes (need a team decision)

- **New refusals:** more than 16 connections from one IPv4 /24 or IPv6
/48, or more than 64 from one IPv4 /16 or IPv6 /32, at the default pool
size. Inbound and outbound connections both count, so our own dials into
a full block are refused locally too. An IPv6 /32 is often a whole ISP
or hoster.
- **New acceptances:** with `--caplin.local-discovery`, private,
link-local and ULA addresses are no longer capped at 8 per address or
/56.
- A ChangeLog entry under Breaking Changes is included.

## Operator overrides

- `--caplin.ip-block-limits.disable` restores go-libp2p's default limits
exactly, including for private networks.
- `--caplin.ip-block-limits.trusted-cidrs=203.0.113.0/24,...` exempts
the listed networks like private ones (sharing the same finite limit),
with or without local discovery. Empty entries are skipped; values with
host bits set, broader than an IPv4 /8 or an IPv6 /16, or invalid stop
the node while flags are parsed. IPv4-mapped prefixes are converted to
IPv4.

Both flags reach embedded Caplin and the standalone `caplin` binary and
are documented in `configuring-erigon.mdx`.

## Tests

`cl/p2p/resource_manager_test.go` opens connection scopes on the
resource manager built by `newResourceManager`, alternating inbound and
outbound so each direction stays below go-libp2p's transient limits on
small machines. Refusals are checked by the per-subnet error text.

- Caps: per IPv4 /24 (and that a closed connection frees its slot), per
IPv4 /16, per IPv6 /48 and /32, the kept per-address caps.
- Private networks: capped like before without local discovery, exempt
per block and per address with it; loopback (IPv4 and IPv6) unlimited
with the default, local-discovery and trusted lists; the shared limit of
an exempt network; QUIC source verification still applies.
- Overrides: trusted networks (including a spaced and an IPv4-mapped
entry) exempt while other public blocks stay capped; `ParseTrustedCIDRs`
(empty entries, host bits, breadth); `disable` gives the released
limits; `TestCaplinIPBlockLimitFlagsReachConfig` through `setCaplin`.
- Static peers: one in a full IPv4 /24 and one in a full IPv6 /48 still
connect while other addresses there are refused; a static peer keeps the
cap of 8 per address; one inside a trusted network keeps the trusted
allowance; static peers on loopback stay unlimited.
- `TestRefusalCounterSummarisesRefusedBlocks` (TCP and QUIC endpoints)
and `TestResourceManagerCloseTwice`;
`TestIPBlockConnLimitsScaleWithPeerCount` and
`TestExemptNetworkConnLimitCoversThePeerPool` check the formulas.

Every cap, exemption and override has a mutation that makes the matching
test fail.

author: Andrew Ashikhmin
subject: execution, cl: reject block access indices beyond len(transactions)+1 (#24908)
body:
EIP-7928 bounds every `block_access_index` by `len(transactions) + 1`,
the post-execution index, but `ValidateForBlock` only knew the block gas
limit. A BAL whose indices lie past that bound passed every up-front
check and was refuted only after the block had been executed and its
computed BAL compared against the header. By then the parallel executor
had already expanded each spurious change into version-map cells, so a
payload could make a node do a disproportionate amount of work before it
answered INVALID.

`ValidateForBlock` now takes the transaction count and rejects an
out-of-range index at every entry point that has the block body:
`engine_newPayload`, `InsertBlocks`, the Caplin payload path and the
block builder. The eth/71 BAL fetcher only knows the header, so it keeps
the gas-limit checks under the name `ValidateForHeader`; the blocks it
assembles are bounded again by `InsertBlocks`. The sidecar memoizes the
two levels separately, so a header-validated BAL only pays the index
pass on insert.

`TransactionsSSZ` gains a nil-safe `Len`, since a payload built by
`NewEth1Block` has no transaction list.

## Tests

- `execution/types`: `TestBlockAccessListValidateForBlockBoundsIndices`
covers all four change lists, accepting `len(transactions) + 1` and
rejecting `+ 2`, and checks that `ValidateForHeader` stays
index-agnostic. The sidecar memo test also covers a changed transaction
count. Both were red before the check existed.
- `engine_newPayloadV5`: an out-of-range index returns INVALID naming
the block access index before insertion. With the check stubbed out, the
same payload was executed and failed only with "block access list
mismatch". The in-range post-execution index is kept as a control.
- `InsertBlocks` and Caplin's `DecodeAndValidateBlockAccessList` get the
same pair. The `InsertBlocks` test fails when the bound is disabled.

The behaviour change followed red → green. The `ValidateForHeader` split
and the `Len` accessor are mechanical and rely on the existing suites.

Fixes ethereum-bounty/erigon#33

author: Kewei
subject: cl: align consensus and fork choice with v1.7.0-beta.4 (#24831)
body:
## Summary

Align Caplin with `consensus-specs` v1.7.0-beta.4 (from beta.2) and pin
the official beta.4 mainnet fixtures. ACDT #100 asks client releases for
the Hoodi Glamsterdam fork to support beta.4.

## Main changes

- **Gloas `apply_parent_execution_payload`** settles the parent's
builder payment before it processes the parent's execution requests, so
a builder exit request is rejected while the payment is pending. The
builders sweep withdraws only the balance left after the withdrawals
already selected for that builder
(`get_builder_balance_after_withdrawals`). ethereum/consensus-specs#5695
- **Gloas `slash_validator`** clears every pending builder payment of
the slashed proposer, for proposer and attester slashings alike. The
Gloas override of `process_proposer_slashing` is removed.
ethereum/consensus-specs#5719
- **`calculate_committee_fraction`** counts only unslashed active
validators. This changes the proposer boost on every fork, including
current mainnet, and the weak-head reorg threshold on Gloas.
ethereum/consensus-specs#5679
- **Gloas `get_head`** walks the filtered node tree: the EMPTY and FULL
variants of a block are filtered separately, and the justified root's
EMPTY node is returned when no node is viable.
ethereum/consensus-specs#5509
- **Payload envelopes** newer than the finalized checkpoint are served
even outside the `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS` window.
ethereum/consensus-specs#5681
- **Spec test runners** read the beta.4 formats: a per-message
`current_time_ms` in gossip vectors, and `head.payload_status` in fork
choice checks. Before this change the runner read a
`head_payload_status` key that no fixture contains, so the Gloas head
payload status was never asserted.

## Implementation notes

- **Gloas filter cost.** The filter does at most one ancestor walk from
the justified root to the finalized start slot, then one iterative pass
over the justified subtree that carries that ancestor down the tree: O(N
+ D) fork-graph reads, where N is the subtree size and D the ancestor
distance. A per-leaf `get_checkpoint_block` walk would cost O(N·D) under
`f.mu` during long non-finality, because in the node tree almost every
block has a leaf variant.
- **Gloas walk.** It reuses the children sampled by the filter, so a
change of payload availability between the two passes cannot produce a
PENDING head.
- **Pre-Gloas head path with the head state** (`GetHead(prevHeadState)`,
the synced path on mainnet):
- When the justified checkpoint state is not cached, the head
computation loads it before taking the fork-choice lock, so the proposer
boost uses the justified checkpoint state's unslashed balance, as in the
spec, and the head does not depend on the cache contents.
- A load error is not returned. The boost then falls back to the head
state's unslashed active balance, an O(validators) scan.
- The stage loads the justified checkpoint state before it enters
`ViewHeadState`, so the head computation normally finds it cached.
`OnAttestation` takes `f.mu` and then the head-state read lock, the
stage takes them in the opposite order, and a head-state writer can
queue between them; a long load inside `ViewHeadState` would make that
deadlock much easier to hit.
- The head computation still loads under the read lock if the stage's
load fails, or if the justified checkpoint changes between the two
calls. On a cache miss, the Gloas head computation already loads the
checkpoint state under the same read lock.
- **Test coverage of the Gloas filter.** The mainnet fixtures have no
`filter_node_tree_variants` cases, so new unit tests cover the
node-level filtering:
  - the empty-tree fallback;
  - FULL excluded while EMPTY is viable, and the reverse;
  - a justified root below the finalized start slot;
  - a bound on fork-graph reads.


## Not changed

- **ethereum/consensus-specs#5680**, the Gloas
`compute_min_epochs_for_block_requests` (14299 epochs on mainnet).
Caplin keeps 33024, which serves a superset of the required range.
- **ethereum/consensus-specs#5665** (proposer preferences signing
domain) and **#5706** (ENR `next_fork_version`). Caplin already behaves
as specified.
- **#5672 and #5673.** They only affect the fast confirmation rule,
which Caplin does not implement.
- **The `time_ms` fork-choice refactors** (#5667, #5668, #5671, #5675).
Caplin's store keeps whole-second time, as before. Fork-choice vectors
still tick in seconds.
- **Network gating.** The new consensus rules apply to every network
where Gloas is active, including Sepolia, without a separate activation
epoch. Prysm (OffchainLabs/prysm#17661) and Lighthouse
(sigp/lighthouse#10307) merged the same rules without one either.
- **Spectests that are still skipped.** This PR does not change the
runner's skip policy. Unregistered gossip handlers, Heze, and
`get_proposer_head` are still skipped. The fork-choice runner still
ignores `payload_attestation_message` steps and payload-vote checks (a
stacked follow-up PR runs them), and does not assert
`viable_for_head_roots_and_weights`, which no mainnet fixture uses.

## Tests

- **TDD:**
- The beta.4 fixtures were the Red step for the consensus changes.
Before the production changes, 12 vectors failed:
    - `proposer_boost_excludes_slashed_validators` in 7 forks;
-
`process_parent_execution_payload__older_than_previous_epoch_builder_exit`;
    - `builder_sweep_after_pending_withdrawal`;
    - `randomized_1` and `randomized_12`;
    - `builder_payment_removed_when_proposer_slashes_itself`.
- The unit tests for new behaviour failed before the fix (node-level
filtering, the PENDING-head case, the cached-balance boost, the envelope
serve bound).
`TestGloasHeadFinalizedCheckpointWhenJustifiedRootPredatesEpochStart`
pins the finalized-checkpoint carry in `getFilteredNodeTree`: it fails
when the carry is removed.
`TestPreGloasHeadWithAuxiliaryStateDoesNotDependOnCheckpointStateCache`
failed before the checkpoint-state load was added: a cold and a warm
cache selected different heads.
`TestComputeForkChoiceLoadsJustifiedStateBeforeViewingHeadState` fails
when the stage does not load the state before `ViewHeadState`. The other
tests pin preserved pre-Gloas behaviour.
  - The fixture-version bump itself is mechanical.
- **Run locally on this commit:**
  - `cd cl/spectest && make mainnet`: pass.
  - `go test -short ./cl/... ./p2p/forkid/ ./execution/chain/...`: pass.
  - `make lint`: 0 issues.
  - `make erigon integration`: builds.




Closes #17334

author: Kewei
subject: cl/phase1/network/services: reject aggregates whose aggregation bits have the wrong length (#24903)
body:
## Summary

Caplin's `beacon_aggregate_and_proof` validation did not check that the
aggregate's `aggregation_bits` length equals the size of the selected
committee. The Electra and Gloas gossip specs require
`len(aggregation_bits) == len(get_beacon_committee(state,
aggregate.data.slot, index))` and reject the aggregate otherwise.
Lighthouse and Prysm enforce it.

`ProcessMessage` fetched the committee but only called
`GetAttestingIndicies(aggregate, false)`. From Electra on, that accessor
ignores the flag and, for this single-committee call, rejects bitlists
that are too short but not those that are too long. Before Electra, it
performs the exact-length check only when the flag is true. For
`aggregation_bits`, `ValidateForConfig` checks only the fork-wide
maximum, not the selected committee size. So an aggregate with extra
trailing bits, unset or set, passed validation. The aggregate
attestation signature was checked against only the in-range committee
members, and the selected aggregator signs the whole
`AggregateAndProof`, so all BLS checks could pass. Before Electra, a
bitlist that is too short could also pass if its bytes still covered the
committee.

Trigger: the aggregate must be signed by a validator that is selected as
aggregator for that slot, so it comes from a malicious or buggy
aggregator; a relaying peer cannot change the bitlist of an honest
aggregate.

Impact, on nodes that fully verify gossip aggregates (nodes with local
validators; from Fulu on, only nodes with a local proposer in the
current or next epoch) and for aggregates submitted through `POST
/eth/v1/validator/aggregate_and_proofs`:

- the invalid aggregate was accepted and forwarded; peers that enforce
this rule reject it;
- it was added to the attestation pool;
- from Electra on, block production could include it, and the block
transition, which requires an exact length, then rejected the locally
produced block, so the local proposal failed.

The fix rejects the aggregate when `aggregation_bits` length differs
from the committee size, right after the committee is fetched. It
applies to all forks because a `beacon_aggregate_and_proof` gossip
aggregate selects exactly one committee. The REST endpoint goes through
the same `ProcessMessage`, so it is covered too.

## Not changed here

- `GetAttestingIndicies` in `cl/phase1/core/state/cache_accessors.go`
still ignores `checkBitsLength` from Electra on (and has no final length
check), and `getAttestingIndicies` in
`cl/phase1/forkchoice/checkpoint_state.go` also does not reject bitlists
that are too long. Enforcing the length there would be defense in depth
for the other callers (fork choice, block production); this PR only adds
the gossip rule.
- Block production and the attestation pool are not changed: the pool is
filled only by this service, so wrong-length aggregates no longer reach
it.

## Changes

- `cl/phase1/network/services/aggregate_and_proof_service.go`: reject an
aggregate whose `aggregation_bits` length differs from the committee
size.
- `cl/phase1/network/services/aggregate_and_proof_service_test.go`: two
new tests; the two shared fixtures used 9 bits for an 8-member committee
and now use 8.

## Testing

- **TDD:** `TestAggregateAndProofRejectsAggregationBitsLengthMismatch`
uses the real Electra fixture under Electra, Fulu and Gloas configs,
with `n-1` and `n` bits and with `n+1` bits whose trailing bit is either
unset or set.
`TestAggregateAndProofRejectsAggregationBitsLengthMismatchBeforeElectra`
checks `n-1` bits and `n+1` bits (trailing bit unset or set) under
Phase0. With the production file from `main`, only these subtests fail,
because `main` accepts these aggregates: the six `n+1` subtests under
Electra, Fulu and Gloas, and all three Phase0 subtests. The Electra,
Fulu and Gloas `n-1` and `n` cases pass on `main` and with the fix. All
other `TestAggregateAndProof*` tests pass on `main` with the fixture
change.
- `go test -p 2 -count=1 ./cl/phase1/network/services/
./cl/beacon/handler/` passed.
- `make lint` reported 0 issues on two runs.
- `make erigon integration` succeeded.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/phase1/forkchoice: bound the checkpoint state cache (#24902)
body:
## Summary

`ForkChoiceStore.checkpointStates` caches the checkpoint states that
`getCheckpointState` builds: effective balances, active and slashed
bitsets, the shuffled active indices and a copy of the RANDAO mixes. In
local benchmarks with one million validators, each entry retained about
18-22 MB. The cache has no size bound: entries are removed only by
`onNewFinalized`, when finality advances, and only those below the new
finalized epoch.

While finality does not advance, every checkpoint state that
`getCheckpointState` builds stays in memory:

- each new justified checkpoint: `getHeadGloas`, `getHeadOnce` (when it
gets no auxiliary state), the same-slot Gloas head check in `OnBlock`,
`isHeadWeak` and `NewWeightStore` read the state of the current
justified checkpoint;
- attestation targets in `OnAttestation`. On `main` this path runs only
after fork choice is marked synced and before the first head state is
published (`syncedDataManager.Syncing()`). With #24807 (open),
`OnAttestation` also reads the target checkpoint state after that, when
the head state does not have the target's shuffling, so during a
persistent split without finality each side-branch target with a
different shuffling adds an entry.

Now an insert leaves at most `maxCheckpointStates` = 10 entries in the
cache, about 180-220 MB at one million validators. Prysm bounds its
checkpoint state cache to 10 entries as well, and Teku's default is 20.
Ten leaves nine entries next to the justified one, enough for the
current- and previous-epoch targets of four branches.

After each insert, `storeCheckpointState` evicts the entries with the
lowest epoch above the cap. It never evicts:

- the current justified checkpoint, which is read to compute the head.
Rebuilding it took about 230-290 ms at one million validators in local
benchmarks;
- the entry just stored, so that a call does not evict its own result.

Lowest epoch first, because an attestation targets the current or
previous epoch, so an older target is the least likely to be read again.
Inserts with their eviction pass, and justified promotion in
`updateCheckpoints`, take a new mutex, `checkpointStatesMu`, so that
concurrent misses cannot leave more than ten entries and each eviction
pass sees a stable justified checkpoint. A checkpoint evicted before it
becomes justified is built again by the next read. Lookups do not take
the new mutex, and `getCheckpointState` still does not take `f.mu`.
Finalization pruning is unchanged.

## Not changed here

- `OnAttestation` still builds a missing target checkpoint state while
it holds `f.mu`. With the bound, an evicted target is built again there
if it is requested again; if more than nine checkpoints other than the
justified one are in use at the same time, entries can be rebuilt
repeatedly. Building checkpoint states outside `f.mu` is a separate
change.
- `newCheckpointState` copies the RANDAO mixes together with their
merkle tree when the source state has one, although it reads only one
mix, to compute the shuffling. Copying the mixes without the tree would
make each entry smaller.
- Concurrent misses for the same checkpoint still build it more than
once, as before.

## Changes

- `cl/phase1/forkchoice/forkchoice.go`: the `maxCheckpointStates`
constant and the `checkpointStatesMu` field.
- `cl/phase1/forkchoice/utils.go`: `getCheckpointState` stores through
the new `storeCheckpointState`, which evicts above the cap;
`updateCheckpoints` promotes the justified checkpoint under
`checkpointStatesMu`.
- `cl/phase1/forkchoice/forkchoice_test.go`: five tests.

## Testing

- **TDD:** with `utils.go` from `main` (only the `maxCheckpointStates`
constant and the `checkpointStatesMu` field added), all five new tests
fail: `TestCheckpointStatesBoundedWithoutFinalization` (11 entries, want
10), `TestCheckpointStatesKeepJustStoredState` (11),
`TestCheckpointStatesKeepCurrentJustified` (12),
`TestJustifiedPromotionWaitsForCheckpointStateEviction` and
`TestCheckpointStateEvictionWaitsForJustifiedPromotion`. Removing one
part of the change at a time:
`TestCheckpointStatesKeepCurrentJustified`, whose justified checkpoint
has the lowest epoch, fails when the justified checkpoint is not
excluded from eviction; `TestCheckpointStatesKeepJustStoredState` fails
when the entry just stored is not excluded; the two lock tests fail when
`updateCheckpoints` or `storeCheckpointState` does not take
`checkpointStatesMu`. All five pass with the change.
- `go test -p 2 ./cl/phase1/forkchoice/...`, also with `-race`.
- `fork_choice` spec tests (`go test -run 'Test/mainnet/.*/fork_choice'
./cl/spectest/`): no failures, and the same tests pass and skip as on
`main`.
- `make lint`, `make erigon integration`.
