chain on the FULL variant below the served head, 16-core dev machine:
excluded (served EMPTY, payload available) 0.19 to 0.21 µs and 288 B at
128 and 7,200 descendants, against 11.2 µs and 702 µs before the
first-step filtering; counted (served FULL) 17 µs and 1.3 ms, unchanged
and linear in the subtree.

author: lystopad
subject: cl/beacon/handler: verify the selected attestations against the proposal state (#24959)
body:
Fixes #24826.

## Problem

Block production does not verify the attestations it packs:
`processBlockForProduction` runs the transition without
`FullValidation`. Aggregation bit positions are mapped to validators
with the head-state committees when an attestation is received. After a
reorg that changes the shuffling, a packed attestation can be invalid
for the proposal state, and then our own block is invalid. Gossip
aggregates already go through this path, and since #24813 local
aggregates do too.

## Change

After `selectAttestations` picks at most `MAX_ATTESTATIONS` (8 from
Electra, 128 before), `findBestAttestationsForBlockProduction` verifies
each selected attestation against the proposal state, as block
processing would: attesting indices from the proposal state, then
`IsValidIndexedAttestation`, which checks the indices and the aggregate
signature. An attestation that fails is dropped with a warning; the rest
of the block is unchanged.

From Electra, aggregates of the same data from several committees are
merged into one attestation. If one committee fails, the merged
attestation is dropped with it. The block stays valid; this is a
backstop for a rare case, so it does not re-split or re-select.

## Cost

`BenchmarkVerifySelectedAttestations` (new, `_bench_test.go`): a full
Electra block, 8 attestations of 64 committees of 512 signers each, with
the decompressed public keys cached as Caplin runs them
(`bls.SetEnabledCaching(true)`). About 143 ms per block on a 16-core dev
machine. This runs in the operations goroutine of `produceBeaconBody`,
in parallel with the payload goroutine, which collects the payload about
0.65 to 0.9 s into the slot. Today the operations goroutine takes a few
ms, so the check stays off the critical path. Verifying the 8
attestations in parallel saved only about 30 ms, so it is sequential.
Before Electra a block holds up to 128 single-committee attestations;
each check is cheaper there (one committee of signers), and all current
networks are past Electra.

## Tests

-
`TestFindBestAttestationsDropsAttestationsThatFailAgainstTheProposalState`:
real BLS keys and signing roots behind a mocked proposal state that
rotates one committee's members, as a changed shuffling would. The
attestation of that committee is dropped, the other one is packed.
-
`TestFindBestAttestationsDropsAMergedAttestationWithAFailingCommittee`:
the merged attestation is dropped as a whole.
- `TestFindBestAttestationsKeepsAttestationsThatVerify`: valid
attestations are packed as before.

The first two failed before the change. Packing the selection unchecked,
or checking the indices without the signature, fails them again.

`go test -race` passes for `cl/beacon/handler/...` and
`cl/phase1/core/state/...`; `make lint` is clean twice.

author: lystopad
subject: cl/aggregation: count each committee member's vote once (#24955)
body:
Follow-up to #24813, from @domiwei's review of it.

## Problem

In a committee with a local aggregator, the pool keeps aside up to
`MAX_VALIDATORS_PER_COMMITTEE` refused data, so every data that got a
vote keeps it. That relies on each member voting once per epoch, and
nothing enforced it. `validatorAttestationSeen` keeps only the last
target epoch per validator (#24824), so a validator that alternates
votes for two target epochs gets every vote claimed, and each new vote
can carry new data. One such validator could fill the refused set of a
duty committee to 2048 data. Each new data then cost about 240 µs under
the pool lock, and honest one-vote data could be evicted. The double
votes are slashable, but the pool's guarantee did not hold.

## Change

- A member votes once per epoch, in one slot and committee. The pool now
records the members whose vote it counts, per slot and committee
(`voters`). A vote of a member already counted for other data of the
committee is refused with `ErrVoterAlreadyCounted`, both for stored data
and for data kept aside. A vote for data that already holds the member
is still `ErrIsSuperset`.
- So every data needs its own voter: the data of a committee never
outnumber its members, and the bound for duty committees holds by
construction. The comment on `refusedLimit` now says
`MAX_VALIDATORS_PER_COMMITTEE` instead of "the committee size".
- The counted members are pruned with the inclusion window.
- The attestation service logs `ErrVoterAlreadyCounted` at Debug, like
`ErrPoolLimit`, and still emits the attestation event.

This also covers the duty case of #24824 at the pool. The seen-cache key
in #24824 itself does not change here.

## Tests

- `TestAddAttestationElectraRefusesAMemberAlreadyCountedForOtherData`: a
second vote of a member for other data is refused, for stored and
refused data; the same vote again is still `ErrIsSuperset`.
-
`TestAddAttestationElectraEquivocatingMemberCannotFlushALocalAggregatorsData`:
in a full duty committee, one member voting for 100 new data adds none
of them, and the honest data kept aside stays.
- `TestPruneStaleDropsCountedMembers`.
- `TestAddAggregatorDutyKeepsOnlyDutiesInTheWindow` now also keeps a
duty of the previous epoch through the prune.
- `TestAttestationOfACountedMemberIsNotAWarning` (services): the event
is emitted and nothing is logged at Warn.
- Three existing pool tests used one member's vote for several data of a
committee, which an honest committee does not produce. They now give
each data its own voters; their assertions do not change.

The new pool tests failed before the change. Mutation checks: removing
the member check, not recording members, dropping the exemption for the
member's own data, not looking up the refused data, not pruning the
members, pruning previous-epoch duties, and logging the new error at
Warn each fail a test.

`BenchmarkAddAttestationElectra` (425 single votes, real BLS, `-count
5`): about 10.60 ms/op on `main` and 10.64 ms/op here, 9371 and 10223
allocs/op.

`go test -race` passes for `cl/aggregation/...`,
`cl/phase1/network/services/...`, `cl/beacon/handler/...` and
`cl/validator/...`; `make lint` is clean twice.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/beacon/handler: collect unprepared Gloas payloads at a third of the attestation window (#24948)
body:
## Summary

After the Gloas fork, Lighthouse finished verifying Caplin's gossip
blocks about 2.2 s into the slot. In Gloas a block counts as timely only
if it is from the current slot and arrives before the attestation
deadline (`ATTESTATION_DUE_BPS_GLOAS`, 3 s with 12-second slots). A late
block cannot get the proposer boost, and if it is also weak, the next
proposer may re-org it (`get_proposer_head`, which checks several more
conditions). At 2.2 s, little time is left for the block to reach the
rest of the network.

In a local Kurtosis rehearsal of the Hoodi Glamsterdam fork (no added
network latency), Lighthouse verified the gossip blocks after the fork
at these times into the slot:

| proposer | blocks | median | p90 (nearest rank) | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| erigon + Caplin | 93 | 2234 ms | 2250 ms | 2431 ms |
| geth + Prysm | 46 | 55 ms | 70 ms | 124 ms |
| nethermind + Teku | 54 | 30 ms | 34 ms | 48 ms |
| geth + Nimbus | 65 | 80 ms | 93 ms | 586 ms |

## Why

- Gloas payload preparation stands down when the parent is FULL or
FULL-to-EMPTY (`gloasPathRequiresForkChoiceUpdate`, #23436): both need
production's normal FCU, because preparation uses `StartPayloadBuild`,
which cannot change fork choice. In the rehearsal FULL was the usual
case.
- So the builder starts with the production FCU, and an unprepared
payload is collected in a window that ends at `attestationDue -
attestationDue/4` (#21989): first poll at 2.15 s, deadline 2.25 s in
Gloas.
- In the rehearsal, 67 of 70 `BlockProduction:
ForkChoiceUpdate&GetPayload took` records after the fork were above 2 s.

## Changes

- An unprepared Gloas payload is now collected in a window that ends at
a third of the attestation window: first poll at 0.9 s, deadline 1 s
with 12-second slots (the retry window stays 100 ms). These are nominal
times; the FCU or a running `GetAssembledBlock` call can take longer.
- An unprepared Gloas production that starts late gets a later deadline:
500 ms after the time taken just before its FCU, capped at the prepared
deadline (2.25 s in Gloas). The FCU itself uses part of this time. As
before, the first poll is never earlier than the request, so a request
that comes in after the deadline is polled once, right away. Without the
later deadline, a late start (a slow FCU, state work at an epoch
boundary, a late request from the validator client) would stop the
builder at once and publish an almost empty payload.
- A prepared payload (an exact payload-ID match with warmup) can still
be retried until 2.25 s. Its first poll is the earlier of the prepared
first poll (0.65 s after at least 1.5 s of warmup) and the unprepared
one, so a payload prepared late is first polled no later than an
unprepared one.
- The wait for a parked parent envelope from #24832 now uses the
prepared collection point, so its cutoff stays at 1.5 s with 12-second
slots instead of moving to 0.25 s.
- Blocks before Gloas are unchanged.

Trade-off: on a FULL parent the builder now has about 1 s instead of
about 2.2 s to fill the payload. Preparing the payload on a FULL parent
would remove this trade-off, but it needs a change to the preparation
design and is not part of this PR.

## Tests

These window tests now expect the new unprepared Gloas values, and fail
on the old code:
- `TestBlockBuilderWindowGloas`
- `TestBlockBuilderWindowReservesPublicationMargin`
- `TestBlockBuilderWindowTakesPreparedPayloadEarly`: it also checks that
the prepared Gloas window stays at 0.65 s to 2.25 s.

`TestMaximumPreparedAdvancePreservesRecentBuildTime` now also checks
that the Gloas advance cap stays 1.5 s.

New tests, which fail on the earlier version of this PR:
- `TestBlockBuilderWindowGloasLateStartKeepsMinimumBuildTime`: a
production that starts at 1.3 s is first polled at 1.7 s with a deadline
of 1.8 s; one that starts at 2 s is capped at 2.15 s and 2.25 s.
- `TestBlockBuilderWindowShortGloasWarmupPollsNoLaterThanUnprepared`:
with 500 ms of warmup the first poll is at 0.9 s, and the polling cutoff
stays at 2.25 s.

These tests cover the window arithmetic only, not how full a payload is
after 1 s of building.

author: Andrew Ashikhmin
subject: cl/beacon: use Gloas preferences for proposer fee recipients (#24937)
body:
Gloas block production ignores the fee recipient in signed proposer
preferences. A proposer without a `prepare_beacon_proposer` registration
therefore builds with the zero address, while a conflicting registration
overrides the signed preference.

Use the preference matching the proposal slot, dependent root, and
validator before falling back to `prepare_beacon_proposer`. An explicit
zero address in a matching preference is valid. This precedence matches
existing Gloas bid validation.

Production, configured builder bids, and background preparation share a
non-logging fee resolver. Only production warns when neither source
exists. Preparation reuses its registration lookup and records the
effective recipient in its cache key so recipient changes trigger a new
build. Preparation still requires a local validator registration.

Resolve the dependent root to the genesis block for epochs up to
`MinSeedLookahead`, including when the head state is still at slot 0.
This allows valid early-epoch preferences to supply the fee recipient
and target gas limit on chains with Gloas active from genesis.

Regression tests failed before the fixes for production fee selection,
preparation attributes, retrying after a recipient change, and
genesis-epoch preference lookup. Coverage includes registration
conflicts, explicit zero, unrelated preferences, the first Gloas slot,
epochs 0 and 1, and the first proposal from a slot-0 state. Additional
tests exercise repeated real preparation and compare the genesis root
with actual slot processing. The resolver extraction, unused
registration flag removal, and warning text update add no new behavior
and use existing tests rather than new Red steps.

Fixes #23300.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/phase1/forkchoice: keep fork-choice store time in milliseconds (#24875)
body:
## Summary

Caplin's fork-choice store kept time in whole seconds, and every tick
after genesis could overwrite the store time. Two problems followed:

- Block timeliness and the proposer boost were decided with one-second
resolution. On 5-second slots (Gnosis, Chiado), a block whose timeliness
was sampled 1666–1999 ms into the slot was treated as timely before
Gloas, although the attestation deadline is 1666 ms.
- The stage loop and block publication tick the store to the slot start.
That moved store time backwards, so a locally published block could be
recorded as timely late in its slot.

This aligns the store with consensus-specs v1.7.0-beta.4, where the
fork-choice store keeps `time_ms`.

## Changes

- **Store time in milliseconds.** The store keeps time in milliseconds
and `OnTick` takes milliseconds; the 2 ms ticker passes `UnixMilli()`.
`Time()` still returns seconds.
- **Time never moves backwards.** The spec requires callers to call
`on_tick` only with a later time; `OnTick` now enforces this itself and
ignores a time that is not later than the store time. A CAS advances the
store, and only the tick that crosses a slot boundary runs the
slot-start work (head and proposer-boost reset, checkpoint pull-up). The
boundary is published without taking `f.mu`, as before, so readers see
the new slot even while another goroutine holds the fork-choice lock.
- **Millisecond timeliness.** `recordBlockTimeliness` and the
proposer-boost decision use the time into the slot in milliseconds,
taken from one read of store time.
- **Saturating conversion.** `utils.SecondsToMilliseconds` saturates
like the spec's `seconds_to_milliseconds`.
- **Spec attestation deadline.** The pre-Gloas attestation deadline is
`ATTESTATION_DUE_BPS` (3333) of the slot: 3999 ms on 12-second slots,
1999 ms on 6 s and 1666 ms on 5 s. It was `SECONDS_PER_SLOT /
INTERVALS_PER_SLOT` (4000, 2000, 1666). Gloas deadlines are unchanged.

## Behaviour changes

- **Mainnet (pre-Gloas).** The attestation deadline moves from 4000 to
3999 ms. Block-production timing derived from it (builder window,
publication margin, signing window, payload-preparation stale-head wait)
shifts by at most 1 ms.
- **Gnosis and Chiado.** The effective timeliness cutoff moves from 2000
ms to 1666 ms before Gloas. Under Gloas it becomes 1250 ms, and the PTC
cutoff 3750 ms.
- **Wall-clock steps.** If the wall clock jumps forward and is then
corrected, store time stays ahead until real time catches up.
- **Custom network configs.** The pre-Gloas attestation deadline no
longer follows `INTERVALS_PER_SLOT`. `ATTESTATION_DUE_BPS` is a
constant, like the Gloas BPS values, so it is not loaded from a network
config. Every built-in network uses 3 intervals per slot.

## Not changed

These follow-ups existed before this PR:

- The slot boundary is published before the slot-start work runs under
`f.mu`. A block that takes the lock in between can lose its proposer
boost.
- Before Gloas, the proposer boost does not check
`is_same_dependent_root`.
- Timeliness is read after the state transition, not at block receipt.
- Slot start times are computed in seconds before the conversion to
milliseconds.

## Tests

- **Red tests.** These failed on the code before the fix:
  - a late block on a 5-second slot;
  - `OnTick` moving time backwards;
  - a late locally published block after a slot-start tick;
- the 3999 ms pre-Gloas deadline (fails with the `INTERVALS_PER_SLOT`
formula).
- **Regression pin.** A genesis time near the `uint64` limit makes
`OnTick` a no-op instead of wrapping the millisecond conversion.
- **Deadline table.** It checks deadline−1 and deadline for the
attestation and PTC deadlines on 12-second slots before and after Gloas,
the attestation deadline on 5-second slots before Gloas, the PTC
deadline on 5-second slots under Gloas, and a non-zero genesis.
- **Run locally on this branch:**
  - `cd cl/spectest && make mainnet`: pass.
  - `go test ./cl/... ./cmd/caplin/...`: pass.
  - `go test -race ./cl/phase1/forkchoice/`: pass.
  - `make lint`: 0 issues.
  - `make erigon integration`: builds.

---------

Co-authored-by: yperbasis <andrey.ashikhmin@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Oleksandr Lystopad <oleksandr.lystopad@erigon.tech>

author: lystopad
subject: cl/phase1/network/registry: let one peer forward a whole PTC's votes at once (#24973)
body:
Fixes #24972.

The `payload_attestation_message` topic allowed 8 messages per second
per peer, with a burst of 16. PTC votes are due at the same point in the
slot, so peers forward them in bursts. Gossipsub marks a message as seen
before Caplin validates it, so a vote the limiter ignored was also
dropped when other peers sent it, and the node lost it.

This change allows one peer to forward a whole committee's votes in one
burst (`MaxPtcSize`), refilled at the same rate per second. The other
topics' limits are unchanged.

Measured on a Sepolia node, 1 s into the next slot, over about 20 slots
each:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| votes in the node's pool (of 512) | 455 | 511 |
| votes included by the next block | 510 | 512 |

author: lystopad
subject: cl/phase1/execution_client: back off the direct payload build retry from 10 ms (#24965)
body:
Fixes #24964.

## Change

`retryAssembleBlock` now waits 10 ms before the first retry and doubles
the delay up to the previous 200 ms cap, with the same 30 attempts. The
direct forkchoice update answers before its commit releases the
execution semaphore, so the `AssembleBlock` that follows it is usually
busy for tens of milliseconds. A fixed 200 ms wait made almost every
production start its payload build about 200 ms late; on a Gloas FULL
parent, where preparation does not run, that time came out of the
building window.

## Measurements

A Sepolia node (Gloas, embedded Caplin) at the chain head, asked for an
unsigned block at the start of the slot:

| | productions | wait before the build starts (p50 / p90 / max) |
|---|---|---|
| fixed 200 ms (`main`) | 328 | 200 / 200 / 1003 ms |
| this change | 32 | 71 / 151 / 312 ms |

The payload is collected at the same time either way (about 2.1 s into
the slot), so the saving is building time.

## Tests

- `TestAssembleRetryDelayBacksOffToTheCap`: 10, 20, 40, 80, 160, then
200 ms.
- `TestRetryAssembleBlockRetriesOneBusyAnswerQuickly`: one busy answer
costs the first delay, not the cap. With a fixed delay at the cap it
fails.
- The existing retry tests pass with both delays.

`go test -race ./cl/phase1/execution_client/...` passes; `make lint` is
clean twice.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/phase1/network/registry: scale the attestation gossip budget with expected traffic (#24970)
body:
## Summary

Caplin admits attestation gossip through one node-wide budget of 250
messages per 6-second fixed window
(`withGlobalTimeBasedRateLimiter(6*time.Second, 250)` in
`cl/phase1/network/registry/register.go`). The budget is shared by all
peers, all 64 `beacon_attestation_{subnet_id}` topics and, during a fork
transition, both fork digests. It is checked before the message is
decoded, and a message over the budget gets `ValidationIgnore`: Caplin
does not process it and gossipsub does not forward it. go-libp2p-pubsub
marks a message as seen before it runs the validator, so copies of an
ignored attestation from other peers are dropped as duplicates.

From Electra on, every attester publishes one `SingleAttestation`, so a
subnet carries active validators / (32 x 64) attestations per slot:
about 408 on mainnet (835,924 active validators) and about 559 on Hoodi
(1,144,656). Attesters broadcast when the slot's block arrives or at the
attestation deadline, whichever comes first. If all of a slot's
attestations land in one 6-second window, the node drops:

| Subscribed subnets | Mainnet | Hoodi |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 39% | 55% |
| 2 | 69% | 78% |
| 64 (`--caplin.subscribe-all-topics`) | 99% | 99% |

A validator node subscribes to the subnets of its validators' duties.
The dropped attestations are not relayed to the node's mesh peers, they
do not reach the aggregation pool, so the aggregates built for local
aggregators miss them, and event stream subscribers do not see them.

The budget comes from #12830 and was moved before decoding in #17606.
Its purpose is to bound the CPU and memory Caplin spends on attestation
gossip. This PR keeps it for that purpose but sizes it from the traffic
the node should receive. At the start of each window the budget is set
to max(250, 3/2 x expected), both values rounded down, where

expected = S x N x B / (SLOTS_PER_EPOCH x ATTESTATION_SUBNET_COUNT)

- S is the number of attestation subnets the node is subscribed to. It
counts distinct subnet ids of topics that are actually subscribed, so a
subnet subscribed under both fork digests during a fork transition
counts once (the traffic moves from one digest to the other, it does not
double), and joined but unsubscribed topics do not count (gossipsub does
not deliver their messages).
- N is the number of active validators in the head state, 0 without a
head state, so the budget is then 250.
- B is the number of slots whose burst can fall into the 6-second
window, ceil(6 s / SECONDS_PER_SLOT): 1 for 12-second slots, 2 on Gnosis
and Chiado (5-second slots).

Resulting budgets per window:

| Network | Active validators | S = 1 | S = 2 | S = 64 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Mainnet | 835,924 | 612 | 1,224 | 39,183 |
| Hoodi | 1,144,656 | 837 | 1,675 | 53,655 |
| Sepolia | ~1,782 | 250 | 250 | 250 |
| Small devnet (mainnet or minimal preset) | 64 to 512 | 250 | 250 | 250
|

Sepolia and small devnets keep 250, which is above their whole per-slot
traffic (Sepolia: ~56 attestations per slot over all subnets).

Above the 250 floor, the limiter admits at most 1.5 times the expected
attestations per window, with the expected count taken when the window
starts. Assuming 0.25 to 1 ms of CPU per accepted attestation (snappy
decompression, SSZ decoding, committee lookup on the head state and
batched BLS verification), the mainnet budgets correspond to about 0.05
to 0.2 cores for 2 subnets and 1.6 to 6.5 cores for all 64 subnets. As
before, a burst around a window boundary can use the budgets of both
adjacent windows.

The budget is recomputed by the first message of each window: one read
lock on the head state to read its active validator set (normally
cached) and one read lock on the topic subscriptions, every 6 seconds at
most. Other messages only do the existing counter check.

## Not changed here

- Persistent subnets: by default (without
`--caplin.subscribe-all-topics`), the initial ENR advertises attestation
subnets 0 and 1, but Caplin does not subscribe to them (attestation
topics are registered with an expiry in the past), so a node without
validator duties receives no attestation subnet traffic. This is a
separate issue.
- Duty subnets of non-aggregators: the committee subscription subscribes
to the duty subnet also when the validator is not an aggregator; the
validator spec requires the subscription only for aggregators.
Subscribing only for aggregators would drop the subnets that only
non-aggregator duties need, so a validator node would receive less
attestation traffic, and a lower S can also lower the budget.
- There is no metric for the reason a message was ignored. The in-memory
gossip stats count ignores by topic name with the subnet suffix removed,
so all attestation subnets share one bucket; they do not record the
reason, and their periodic printer is disabled. A counter labelled by
reason would show how often the budget is reached.
- With fewer committees per slot than subnets (fewer than 262,144 active
validators with 32-slot epochs and the default target committee size), a
subnet carries a whole committee in some slots and none in others, so
the expected count per subnet is an average and a window can hold more
than budgeted. The budget is never lower than the previous 250.
- The budget is still one budget for all peers and is used before
decoding, so messages that turn out to be invalid still use it.

## Changes

- `cl/phase1/network/registry/register.go`: compute the attestation
budget per window from the expected traffic; `RegisterGossipServices`
takes a function returning the active validator count;
`withGlobalTimeBasedRateLimiter` takes a function for the limit (the
blob sidecar limiter still uses 32).
- `cl/phase1/network/registry/tb_rate_limiter.go`: read the limit from
the function when a window starts.
- `cl/phase1/network/gossip/gossip_manager.go`: `ExpectedAttestations`,
the attestations expected on the subscribed subnets within a window.
- `cl/phase1/network/gossip/gossip_subscription.go`: count the distinct
attestation subnets that are actually subscribed.
- `cl/beacon/synced_data/synced_data.go`: `ActiveValidatorCount`, the
active validators of the head state's epoch, 0 without a head state.
- `cmd/caplin/caplin1/run.go`: pass
`syncedDataManager.ActiveValidatorCount`.
- Tests: `register_attestation_budget_test.go` and
`tb_rate_limiter_test.go` (new), `active_validator_count_test.go` (new),
`gossip_subscription_test.go`, and the new argument in
`register_gloas_boundary_test.go`.

## Testing

- **TDD:** `TestAttestationGossipBudgetScalesWithExpectedTraffic`
registers the services through `RegisterGossipServices`, subscribes 2
attestation subnets and publishes locally while the mocked
`P2PManager.Host()` returns nil, so the self-publish bypass is off and
every message runs through the validator. Rows: the mainnet config with
262,144 active validators and the Gnosis config with 65,536 (both expect
256 attestations per window, budget 384), and no head state (budget
250). Each row checks that a burst of the expected count (or 250 without
a head state) reaches decoding, and that of budget + 100 messages
exactly the budget does. On `main` (the test adapted to the old
`RegisterGossipServices` signature) the mainnet and Gnosis rows fail:
250 of 256 messages reach decoding. With B forced to 1, the Gnosis row
fails the same way.
- `TestSubscribedAttestationSubnetCount` (a subnet subscribed under two
fork digests counts once, a joined but unsubscribed subnet and a sync
committee topic do not count), `TestActiveValidatorCount` (0 without a
head state, a validator that is not active yet does not count) and
`TestTimeBasedRateLimiterRefreshesLimitEachWindow` (the limit is read
once per window and follows the function across windows) fail when the
count includes unsubscribed topics or counts topics instead of subnets,
counts all validators, or reads the limit only once.
- `go test -p 2 -count=1 ./cl/phase1/network/registry/
./cl/phase1/network/gossip/ ./cl/beacon/synced_data/
./cmd/caplin/caplin1/` and `-race` on the first three packages passed.
- `make lint` reported 0 issues on two runs.
- `make erigon integration` succeeded.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/phase1/network/gossip, cl/p2p: subscribe to the persistent attestation subnets (#25007)
body:
## Summary

Without `--caplin.subscribe-all-topics`, Caplin advertises attestation
subnets 0 and 1 in its ENR `attnets`, but it subscribes to no
attestation subnet unless a validator duty asks for one (line numbers on
`main`):

- `setupENR` sets bits 0 and 1 (`cl/p2p/p2p.go:313-318`). The MetaData
handlers (`cl/sentinel/handlers/heartbeats.go:72-126`) and
`Sentinel.Identity` read `attnets` from the same ENR, so MetaData
advertises the same bits.
- `defaultExpiryForTopic` gives every `beacon_attestation_{subnet_id}`
topic the expiry `time.Unix(0, 0)`
(`cl/phase1/network/gossip/gossip_manager.go:402-407`), so
`TopicSubscriptions.SubscribeWithExpiry` returns `ErrExpiryInThePast`
before `Topic.Subscribe` (`gossip_subscription.go:181-188`). The topics
are joined, but nothing subscribes them. The only other path that starts
an attestation subscription is the beacon committee subscription of a
validator duty, which lasts two epochs
(`cl/validator/committee_subscription/committee_subscription.go:87-97`);
the fork-digest lookahead copies existing subscriptions to the next
digest.
- `TopicSubscriptions` also sets and clears the `attnets` bit of an
attestation topic on its first subscription, its expiry, `Unsubscribe`
and `Remove` (`gossip_subscription.go:136-141`, `159-164`, `194-200`,
`232-237`). So duty subnets are advertised while their two-epoch
subscription lasts, a duty that expires on subnet 0 or 1 clears the
initial bit, and the removal of the old fork digest's topics, 16 slots
after a fork-digest change is detected with an 8-slot lookahead
(`gossip_manager.go:563-614`), clears the bits of the old digest's
subscribed topics, also when the same subnet is still subscribed under
the new digest. A node with `--caplin.subscribe-all-topics` therefore
advertises no attestation subnet after its first fork-digest change (BPO
forks change the digest too), although it is still subscribed to all 64.

The phase0 p2p spec, [Attestation subnet
subscription](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/460fd37c3a58f6baf8a9a285d2adf71c4f818929/specs/phase0/p2p-interface.md#L1804-L1845):

> each beacon node should:
> - Remain subscribed to `SUBNETS_PER_NODE` for
`EPOCHS_PER_SUBNET_SUBSCRIPTION` epochs.
> - Maintain advertisement of the selected subnets in their node's ENR
`attnets` entry by setting the selected `subnet_id` bits to `True` (e.g.
`ENR["attnets"][subnet_id] = True`) for all persistent attestation
subnets.
> - Select these subnets based on their node-id as specified by the
following `compute_subscribed_subnets(node_id, epoch)` function.

`SUBNETS_PER_NODE` is 2 and `EPOCHS_PER_SUBNET_SUBSCRIPTION` is 256.
`compute_subscribed_subnet` shuffles the 6-bit node-ID prefix with a
seed from `(epoch + node_id % 256) // 256`, so each node gets two
consecutive subnets, selected again every 256 epochs at an epoch
staggered by its node ID (the new pair can overlap the old one).
[MetaData](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/460fd37c3a58f6baf8a9a285d2adf71c4f818929/specs/phase0/p2p-interface.md#L455-L477):
"`attnets` is a `BitVector` representing the node's persistent
attestation subnet subscriptions", and [the ENR `attnets`
entry](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/460fd37c3a58f6baf8a9a285d2adf71c4f818929/specs/phase0/p2p-interface.md#L1733-L1747)
must equal `MetaData.attnets` when it has a non-zero bit. The validator
guide's
[Lookahead](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/460fd37c3a58f6baf8a9a285d2adf71c4f818929/specs/phase0/validator.md#L325-L359)
says that when too few peers are subscribed to a duty subnet, the
validator must find peers whose ENR `attnets` has the subnet's bit and
validate them with `GetMetaData`.

Other clients:

- Prysm computes the pair with the node-ID shuffle and caches it for the
epochs left in the current selection period
([subnets.go](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/120bdea8a5d74b3d8da7359a44ddcd89ce4476cb/beacon-chain/p2p/subnets.go#L494-L577)),
builds ENR and MetaData `attnets` from that cache only
([discovery.go](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/120bdea8a5d74b3d8da7359a44ddcd89ce4476cb/beacon-chain/p2p/discovery.go#L154-L305),
[subnet_ids.go](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/120bdea8a5d74b3d8da7359a44ddcd89ce4476cb/beacon-chain/cache/subnet_ids.go#L107-L123)),
and joins the persistent and aggregator subnets
([subscriber.go](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/120bdea8a5d74b3d8da7359a44ddcd89ce4476cb/beacon-chain/sync/subscriber.go#L236-L244),
[persistentAndAggregatorSubnetIndices](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/120bdea8a5d74b3d8da7359a44ddcd89ce4476cb/beacon-chain/sync/subscriber.go#L799-L805)).
- Teku computes the pair and the slot at which it rotates
([MiscHelpers.java](https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/e59e16e32aea108df97ca40a9e68df582735e8da/ethereum/spec/src/main/java/tech/pegasys/teku/spec/logic/common/helpers/MiscHelpers.java#L285-L338)),
checks it on every slot and subscribes the new pair once the old one has
expired
([NodeBasedStableSubnetSubscriber.java](https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/e59e16e32aea108df97ca40a9e68df582735e8da/networking/eth2/src/main/java/tech/pegasys/teku/networking/eth2/gossip/subnets/NodeBasedStableSubnetSubscriber.java#L51-L105)),
keeps one unsubscription slot per subnet, the later of the persistent
and the aggregation one, and sets the ENR from the persistent subnets
only
([AttestationTopicSubscriber.java](https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/e59e16e32aea108df97ca40a9e68df582735e8da/networking/eth2/src/main/java/tech/pegasys/teku/networking/eth2/gossip/subnets/AttestationTopicSubscriber.java#L54-L177)).
- Lighthouse (stable) derives two consecutive subnets from the node-ID
prefix, without the shuffle and the rotation, "for the duration of the
node's runtime"
([subnet_id.rs](https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/blob/6db6ae9382b7d6f5bd1e0ca0d349bc0dc94adba2/consensus/types/src/attestation/subnet_id.rs#L103-L128)).
It subscribes to them and adds them to the ENR at startup
([subnet_service/mod.rs](https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/blob/6db6ae9382b7d6f5bd1e0ca0d349bc0dc94adba2/beacon_node/network/src/subnet_service/mod.rs#L116-L174));
short-lived attestation subscriptions are subscribed and removed without
ENR changes; the only other ENR updates are for sync committee subnets
([subnet_service/mod.rs](https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/blob/6db6ae9382b7d6f5bd1e0ca0d349bc0dc94adba2/beacon_node/network/src/subnet_service/mod.rs#L433-L600)).

Consequences: a default Caplin node gives the attestation subnets none
of the two-subnet backbone that the spec asks of every node. It still
claims subnets 0 and 1, so peers that look for peers on those subnets
through discovery and MetaData can pick a Caplin node that is not in the
topic, and the duty and fork-rollover updates make the advertised bits
disagree with the actual subscriptions in both directions.

The change:

- `subnets.ComputeSubscribedSubnets` implements
`compute_subscribed_subnets` with the existing
`shuffling.ComputeShuffledIndex`, and
`subnets.SubscribedSubnetsRotationEpoch` returns the next epoch at which
the seed changes (both use plain `uint64` arithmetic, which cannot
overflow for an epoch a clock can reach).
- `GossipManager.SetLocalNodeID` takes the discovery node ID
(`cmd/caplin/caplin1/run.go` passes `localNode.ID()`, as for PeerDAS).
The new `subscribePersistentAttestationSubnets` computes the pair for
the current epoch, calls `SubscribeWithExpiry` with the start of the
second slot of the rotation epoch on every registered
`beacon_attestation` topic of the pair (on every fork digest), and sets
`attnets` to exactly the pair. It runs when the node ID is set, at the
end of each gossip service registration, and on the existing per-slot
tick of `goCheckForkAndResubscribe`. It does nothing with
`--caplin.subscribe-all-topics`.
- Startup: `run.go` sets the node ID before `RegisterGossipServices`, so
the pair is advertised from just before the gossip services are
registered. After the attestation service has joined its 64 topics, the
call at the end of its registration subscribes the pair, without waiting
for a tick.
- Fork-digest change: `subscribeUpcomingTopics` already copies each
topic's expiry to the new digest's topic, so the pair is subscribed
under both digests from the lookahead (about 8 slots before the change)
on; the per-slot call covers both digests (including a rotation inside
the overlap), and removing the old digest's topics no longer changes
`attnets`.
- Duties: `SubscribeWithExpiry` only moves an expiry later, so a duty
and the persistent subscription on the same topic do not shorten each
other, and duties no longer change `attnets`.
- ENR: `UpdateENRAttSubnets(subnetIndex, on)` is replaced by
`SetENRAttSubnets(subnets)`, which writes the whole field once.
`LocalNode.Set` ignores an entry equal to the current one, so a per-slot
call with an unchanged pair does not re-sign the ENR or bump its
sequence number; `attnets` changes when the node ID is first set and
when the computed pair changes. Refreshes are not serialized with each
other, so one that read the epoch before a rotation can write the old
pair after a newer one, until the next tick; if a subscription attempt
fails, the pair is still advertised and the next refresh retries.
`setupENR` no longer sets bits 0 and 1: until the node ID is set,
`attnets` is all zeros. With `--caplin.subscribe-all-topics` it still
sets all 64 bits, and they now stay set after a fork-digest change.
`syncnets` handling is unchanged.
- At a rotation, the first per-slot tick after the start of the rotation
epoch subscribes the new pair (later ticks retry a failure). A topic of
the old pair that is not in the new pair and has no later duty expiry
keeps the start of the epoch's second slot as its expiry and is
cancelled by the first run of the existing 12-second expiry check after
it. The extra slot covers the time until that tick, so nominally the new
pair is subscribed before the old one is dropped, and both are
subscribed for up to about one slot plus 12 seconds (24 seconds on
mainnet).

Relation to other changes:

- #25008 makes beacon committee subscriptions subscribe to the duty
subnet only for aggregators (`cl/validator/committee_subscription`).
After it, a validator node without `--caplin.subscribe-all-topics` and
without this change would be subscribed to no attestation subnet outside
its aggregation duties, so this PR should land first or together with
it.
- The attestation gossip budget (#24970) is max(250, 1.5 x the
attestations expected on the subscribed attestation subnets). A node
without duties and without `--caplin.subscribe-all-topics` was
subscribed to none and got the 250 floor; it now has the two persistent
subnets (up to four during the overlap at a rotation), e.g. 1,224 per 6
seconds on mainnet with 835,924 active validators (the S = 2 column in
#24970).

## Not changed here

- `syncnets`: `TopicSubscriptions` still sets and clears sync committee
bits per topic, so the old-digest removal after a fork-digest change can
still clear `syncnets` bits that are subscribed under the new digest.
- `MetaData.seq_number` is still the ENR sequence number, which the spec
says is independent of it; a new pair changes the ENR, so the next
signed record and MetaData get a higher sequence number, as other ENR
changes do.
- The spec's note that a node subscribes to the persistent subnets of an
upcoming fork at least 256 epochs before it: the next digest's topics
are still joined about 8 slots before the change.
- A duty subscription received after the fork-digest lookahead
subscribes only the current digest's topic.
- The MetaData v3 handler, which returns without a response before Fulu.
- Duty subscriptions for non-aggregators (#25008), and the formula of
the attestation gossip budget (#24970); its result now includes the
persistent subnets (see above).

## Changes

- `cl/phase1/network/subnets/subnets.go`: `ComputeSubscribedSubnets` and
`SubscribedSubnetsRotationEpoch`.
- `cl/phase1/network/gossip/gossip_manager.go`: `SetLocalNodeID` and
`subscribePersistentAttestationSubnets`, called from `SetLocalNodeID`,
`registerGossipService` and the per-slot tick.
- `cl/phase1/network/gossip/gossip_subscription.go`: subscribing,
expiring, unsubscribing and removing an attestation topic no longer
change `attnets`.
- `cl/p2p/p2p_interface.go`, `cl/p2p/p2p.go`,
`cl/p2p/mock_services/p2p_manager_mock.go`: `SetENRAttSubnets` replaces
`UpdateENRAttSubnets`; `setupENR` no longer sets subnets 0 and 1 without
subscribe-all.
- `cmd/caplin/caplin1/run.go`: pass the node ID to the gossip manager.
- Tests: new `cl/phase1/network/subnets/subnets_test.go` and
`cl/phase1/network/gossip/persistent_attestation_subnets_test.go`, new
tests in `cl/phase1/network/gossip/gossip_subscription_test.go` and
`cl/p2p/p2p_enr_cgc_test.go`; the `UpdateENRAttSubnets` expectations are
removed from `gossip_subscription_test.go` and
`cl/phase1/network/registry/register_attestation_budget_test.go`, and
the stub in `cl/sentinel/ban_on_connection_test.go` implements
`SetENRAttSubnets`.

## Testing

- **TDD**, with the production files from `main`:
- `TestAttestationDutySubscriptionDoesNotUpdateENR`,
`TestAttestationDutyExpiryDoesNotUpdateENR` and
`TestAttestationOldDigestRemovalDoesNotUpdateENR` (strict P2P mock) fail
with `Unexpected call to
*mock_services.MockP2PManager.UpdateENRAttSubnets([3 true])`, `([3
false])` from the expiry check and `([3 false])` from `Unsubscribe`.
- `TestSetupENRAttestationSubnets` fails without subscribe-all
(`expected: 0x0, actual: 0x2` set bits); its subscribe-all case passes
before and after.
- `TestComputeSubscribedSubnets`, `TestSetENRAttSubnets` and the gossip
manager tests `TestPersistentAttestationSubnetsStartupOrder`,
`TestPersistentAttestationSubnetsRotate`,
`TestPersistentAttestationSubnetDutyDoesNotShortenExpiry`,
`TestPersistentAttestationSubnetsSurviveForkRollover` and
`TestPersistentAttestationSubnetsSubscribeAll` use the new functions and
do not build on `main`. Mutations of the change also make the gossip
manager tests and `TestSetENRAttSubnets` fail: removing the call at the
end of `registerGossipService` or in `SetLocalNodeID` breaks the startup
order test, limiting the refresh to the current fork digest breaks the
fork rollover test, removing the subscribe-all check breaks the
subscribe-all test, an expiry at the start of the rotation epoch or one
hour later breaks the startup, rotation, duty and fork rollover tests,
and a `SetENRAttSubnets` that keeps existing bits breaks
`TestSetENRAttSubnets`.
- `TestComputeSubscribedSubnets` checks 16 vectors from a Python
transcription of the spec's `compute_subscribed_subnet` (with
`SHUFFLE_ROUND_COUNT` 90): node IDs 0x00..00, 0xff..ff, 0x0c..0c and
0xa000..07 (offsets 0, 255, 12 and 7) on both sides of their rotation
epochs, and the wrap from subnet 63 to 0.
- The gossip manager tests call the persistent-subnet and fork helpers
directly with a mocked clock instead of waiting for the tickers.
- `go test -p 2 -count=1 ./cl/phase1/network/subnets/
./cl/phase1/network/gossip/ ./cl/phase1/network/registry/ ./cl/p2p/...
./cl/sentinel/... ./cmd/caplin/...
./cl/validator/committee_subscription/`, `go test -race
./cl/phase1/network/gossip/ ./cl/phase1/network/subnets/ ./cl/p2p/`,
`make lint`, `make erigon integration`.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/validator/committee_subscription: subscribe to the duty subnet only for aggregators (#25008)
body:
## Summary

On a synced node, each entry of `POST
/eth/v1/validator/beacon_committee_subscriptions` that
`CommitteeSubscribeMgmt.AddAttestationSubscription` processes requests a
subscription to the `beacon_attestation_{subnet_id}` topic of the
entry's slot and committee on the current fork digest (the subnet is
computed with the head state's committee count), with an expiry two
epochs after the request (an existing later expiry is kept). It does
this whether or not the validator is an aggregator: `is_aggregator` only
decides whether the duty is registered in the aggregation pool
(`AddAggregatorDuty`).

Each validator has one attestation duty per epoch, and a subscription
lasts two epochs, so with V validators about 2V duties are subscribed at
any time, on subnets that are spread uniformly. That is about 64 x (1 -
(63/64)^(2V)) subnets:

| Validators | Subscribed subnets now | Attestations per slot on them
(mainnet) | Aggregator subnets (expected) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 2.0 | ~810 | 0.08 |
| 10 | 17 | ~7,060 | 0.8 |
| 32 | 41 | ~16,590 | 2.5 |
| 64 | 55 | ~22,640 | 4.9 |

From Electra on every attester publishes one `SingleAttestation`, so
with 835,924 active validators (the mainnet figure #24970 uses) a subnet
carries about 408 attestations per slot. The last column assumes
408-member committees, where a validator is an aggregator with
probability 1/25 (`TARGET_AGGREGATORS_PER_COMMITTEE` = 16).

The node receives the attestations of every subscribed subnet, and the
gossipsub message-ID function decompresses each one. Attestations
admitted by the attestation gossip budget then go through decoding and
validation, which includes a committee check against the head state and
signature verification, and accepted ones are relayed to mesh peers.
Since #24970 the budget, shared by all subnets, is set at the start of
each 6-second window to max(250, 1.5 x the attestations expected on the
subscribed attestation subnets in that window), with integer arithmetic
rounding down, so above its 250 floor the decoding and validation work
it admits grows with the number of subscribed subnets.

The consensus specs only require the subscription for aggregators. The
phase0 validator guide,
[Lookahead](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/12c8b24bc09b12f62688d439ba20ef00b1fdfe1f/specs/phase0/validator.md#lookahead):
"If the validator is assigned to be an aggregator for the slot (see
`is_aggregator()`), then subscribe to the topic." and "If the validator
is _not_ assigned to be an aggregator, the validator only needs
sufficient number of peers on the topic to be able to publish messages.
The validator does not need to _subscribe_ and listen to all messages on
the topic." The [beacon
API](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/blob/01e99a6530b22941f619bde525cbf8bb61991d42/apis/validator/beacon_committee_subscriptions.yaml#L4-L10)
says the same:

> If validator `is_aggregator`, beacon node must:
> - announce subnet topic subscription on gossipsub
> - aggregate attestations received on that subnet

For committee subscriptions, Lighthouse, Prysm and Teku subscribe to the
requested subnet only for aggregators:
[Lighthouse](https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/blob/6db6ae9382b7d6f5bd1e0ca0d349bc0dc94adba2/beacon_node/network/src/subnet_service/mod.rs#L265-L275)
calls `subscribe_to_subnet` only if `subscription.is_aggregator`;
[Prysm](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/948f8d2052432ebae3f6e2194c83b35f46566a99/beacon-chain/rpc/core/subnets.go#L50-L53)
records an aggregator subnet only for aggregators and
[joins](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/948f8d2052432ebae3f6e2194c83b35f46566a99/beacon-chain/sync/subscriber.go#L236-L243)
only persistent and aggregator subnets (attester subnets are used to
find peers);
[Teku](https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/e59e16e32aea108df97ca40a9e68df582735e8da/beacon/validator/src/main/java/tech/pegasys/teku/validator/coordinator/ValidatorApiHandler.java#L726-L729)
calls `subscribeToCommitteeForAggregation` only if
`request.isAggregator()`.

A non-aggregator's attestation does not need the subscription to be
published. All 64 attestation topics are joined when the gossip service
is registered (and again for the next fork digest before a fork),
`PublishToForkDigest` only needs the joined topic handle, and
go-libp2p-pubsub publishes on a joined topic without a subscription
through fanout peers.

Now a non-aggregator request returns before the subscription.
Aggregators keep the duty registration and the subnet computation, and
still request the two-epoch expiry. A syncing node still answers 503 for
both kinds of request.

With this change, the local aggregates that Electra block production
takes from the aggregation pool (#24813) are built only from
attestations on subscribed subnets (the subnets of local aggregators
and, with #25007, the node's two persistent subnets, or all of them with
`--caplin.subscribe-all-topics`) and from attestations submitted to the
node over the validator API. Other committees can reach block production
only as aggregate-and-proofs, received on the
`beacon_aggregate_and_proof` topic (which every node subscribes to) or
submitted over the validator API.

## Not changed here

- Persistent subnets: on `main`, without
`--caplin.subscribe-all-topics`, the initial ENR advertises attestation
subnets 0 and 1, but Caplin does not subscribe to them (attestation
topics are registered with an expiry in the past), so with this change
alone a validator node without an unexpired aggregator subscription
would be subscribed to no attestation subnet, like a node without
validators today. #25007 subscribes every node to the two persistent
subnets returned by `compute_subscribed_subnets`, as the phase0 P2P spec
recommends; this PR should land after it or together with it.
- The attestation gossip budget (#24970).
- Peer discovery for duty subnets: the beacon API asks the node to look
for peers on the subnet of every request. Caplin does not do this per
request; independently of these requests, the sentinel looks every 12
seconds for peers on subnets with fewer than 4 peers, at most 16 subnets
per round.
- ENR `attnets`: not changed here. On `main`, subscribing to an
attestation topic sets its subnet's bit and expiry or removal clears it,
and non-aggregator requests no longer trigger these updates; #25007
removes these per-topic updates, so without
`--caplin.subscribe-all-topics` `attnets` advertises only the two
persistent subnets, while with the flag it advertises all 64.

## Changes

- `cl/validator/committee_subscription/committee_subscription.go`:
return before the subnet subscription when the request is not for an
aggregator. The `gossipManager` field uses the `gossip.Gossip` interface
instead of `*gossip.GossipManager` (the constructor is unchanged), so
the tests can use its mock.
- `cl/validator/committee_subscription/committee_subscription_test.go`:
two new tests.

## Testing

- **TDD:** `TestAddAttestationSubscriptionDoesNotSubscribeNonAggregator`
fails without the new early return (only the field type changed):
`Unexpected call to
*mock_services.MockGossip.SubscribeWithExpiry([beacon_attestation_1
...])`, and passes with it.
`TestAddAttestationSubscriptionSubscribesAggregator` passes before and
after; it pins the aggregator subscription to the duty's subnet (subnet
1) and fails if the condition is inverted.
- A probe test on `main`, not part of this PR, published from a joined
but unsubscribed attestation topic through
`GossipManager.PublishToForkDigest` to a second host subscribed to it,
and the message was delivered.
- `go test -p 2 ./cl/validator/committee_subscription/
./cl/beacon/handler/`, `make lint`, `make erigon integration`.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/phase1/forkchoice, cl/phase1/stages: take the fork-choice lock before the synced-data lock (#25011)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #24923.

`ForkChoiceStore.mu` and `SyncedDataManager.mu` are both `sync.RWMutex`.
The fork-choice stage took them in the opposite order to the rest of
fork choice:

- The stage called `GetHead` inside `syncedData.ViewHeadState`. It also
called `saveFinalizedStateOnDiskIfNeeded` inside the same kind of view,
and at head slots that are a multiple of 5 epochs that helper calls
`GetStateAtBlockRoot`. In both cases the stage held the synced-data read
lock while it waited for `f.mu`.
- `OnAttestation` and `OnAttesterSlashing` can take the synced-data read
lock while they hold `f.mu`. `OnBlock` can do the same indirectly while
it reconstructs a state.

When a node publishes its own block, the request goroutine updates the
synced head state in `storeBlockAndBlobs` and can wait for the
synced-data write lock behind existing readers. A queued writer blocks
new readers, so these three goroutines could block each other
permanently.

## Changes

- **One lock order: `f.mu`, then the synced-data lock.** No production
caller takes `f.mu` while it holds a synced-data lock any more. I
checked every production `ViewHeadState`, `ViewHeadStateWithIdentity`
and `ViewPreviousHeadState` callback in `cl/`. Only the two stage sites
above took `f.mu`; the other callbacks call only fork-choice methods
that do not take it.
- **`GetHeadWithSyncedHeadState`.** A new method on `*ForkChoiceStore`.
It computes the head the same way `GetHead(headState)` did with the
synced head state, but it reads that state itself while it holds `f.mu`,
as `OnAttestation` does. The synced-data read lock is held only while
the votes are computed.
- If a pre-Gloas recomputation needs the synced head state and there is
none, it returns `synced_data.ErrNotSynced` without changing the cached
head. The stage then falls back to `GetHead(nil)`, as before. The
cached-head, anchor and Gloas paths do not read the synced head state.
- The head-selection code and the source of its inputs do not change.
Vote weights come from the synced head state, with optional LMD
sampling. The proposer boost uses the cached justified checkpoint state
when it is available, and the synced head state otherwise. Because the
view is now opened after `f.mu` is taken, a head state published in the
meantime can be the one used.
  - `GetHead` keeps its signature and behaviour for its other callers.
- **Stage.**
- `computeAndNotifyServicesOfNewForkChoice` calls the new method outside
any synced-data view.
- `postForkchoiceOperations` calls `saveFinalizedStateOnDiskIfNeeded`
after the view returns and passes the stage's `headSlot`. The head-state
dump and the shuffling pre-cache stay inside the view.
- **`LoadJustifiedCheckpointState` removed.** The stage called it before
`ViewHeadState` only so that the justified checkpoint state was not
loaded under the synced-data read lock. `getHeadOnce` and `getHeadGloas`
already load it before they take `f.mu` or the synced-data lock.

## Behaviour changes

- **`f.mu` waits.** While the stage holds `f.mu`, it can now wait for
the synced-data read lock if a head-state writer is queued: until the
readers already in progress finish and the writer releases the lock.
`OnAttestation`, `OnAttesterSlashing` and `OnBlock` already wait like
this. In return, the stage holds the synced-data read lock for a much
shorter time: only while the votes are computed, instead of during the
whole `GetHead` call, including the wait for `f.mu`.
- **Finalized-state cadence.** The finalized-state persistence cadence
uses the head slot that the stage selected. Before, it used the slot of
the synced head state viewed afterwards. They differ only if a published
block replaces the synced head state between the two calls. If the two
slots are on different sides of a 5-epoch boundary, that call can save
when the old code would not, or the other way round. The saved state is
the finalized checkpoint state in both cases. The pre-cache call now
comes before the save, so a save error no longer prevents the pre-cache
from being scheduled.
- **Justified state loading.** The stage no longer loads the justified
checkpoint state itself before each head computation. The state is
loaded when the head is recomputed, before `f.mu` or the synced-data
lock is taken. Before, a load that failed in the stage was tried again
in `getHeadOnce` or `getHeadGloas`. With a synced head state there is
now no immediate second attempt: if the load fails, the pre-Gloas
proposer boost uses the synced head state and Gloas gives zero
attestation weight, as both did before when both attempts failed.
Without a synced head state, the stage falls back to `GetHead(nil)`,
which tries the load again.

## Not changed

- `DumpBeaconStateOnDisk` still runs inside the synced-data view, as
before. It does not take `f.mu`.

## Tests

- **Red tests.** `TestComputeForkChoiceDoesNotInvertSyncedDataLockOrder`
and `TestPostForkchoiceOperationsDoesNotInvertSyncedDataLockOrder` fail
on `main` with "operation deadlocked". They reproduce the cycle with the
real locks:
- the stage holds the synced-data read lock, paused in a `ViewHeadState`
wrapper;
  - `OnAttesterSlashing` holds `f.mu`;
  - an `OnHeadStateWithBlockRoot` writer is queued.

Short sleeps (250 ms) arrange these steps, and the waits on the stage
operation have time limits, so the deadlock makes the test fail instead
of hanging. On the fixed code, `computeAndNotifyServicesOfNewForkChoice`
does not enter the wrapped view at all.
- **Lock order inside fork choice.**
`TestGetHeadWithSyncedHeadStateTakesForkChoiceLockFirst` pauses the call
while it loads the checkpoint state. It checks that neither lock is held
at that point, and that the synced-data lock is not taken before `f.mu`.
Mutation checks confirmed that it fails in each of these cases:
  - the synced-data view wraps the head computation;
  - the view is entered before `f.mu`;
  - the checkpoint load moves under `f.mu`.
- **Behaviour.** Further tests check that:
- the new method returns the same head as `GetHead(headState)` on a
pre-Gloas store with votes and a proposer boost (without LMD sampling);
  - it leaves the cached head unchanged when it returns `ErrNotSynced`;
  - a failed checkpoint load still gives a head;
- the stage falls back to `GetHead(nil)` when there is no synced head
state.
- **Removed test.**
`TestComputeForkChoiceLoadsJustifiedStateBeforeViewingHeadState` is
removed, because the stage no longer views the head state around
`GetHead`. The new lock-order test checks that the checkpoint state is
loaded outside both locks.
- **Validation.**
- `go test` for `cl/phase1/forkchoice/...`, `cl/phase1/stages/...`,
`cl/beacon/...` and `cl/phase1/network/...`;
  - `-race -count=10` for the new tests;
  - the CL spec tests (v1.7.0-beta.4);
  - `make lint`;
  - `make erigon integration`.

author: lystopad
subject: cl/phase1/network/services: verify gossip aggregates on nodes with validators (#25014)
body:
Part of #24554 (point 2).

## Problem

Since #18521, a Fulu node verifies a gossip aggregate only when a local
validator proposes in the current or next epoch
(`isLocalValidatorProposer`). In other epochs every aggregate returns
`ErrIgnore`. So a validator node:

- does not relay `beacon_aggregate_and_proof` in most epochs (gossipsub
forwards only accepted messages);
- fills its block attestation pool only after a local proposal is
detected, and keeps stale entries between proposals;
- does not pass aggregate votes to fork choice.

On a mainnet validator node (release/3.8), accepted bytes on
`beacon_aggregate_and_proof` are 0 outside proposal epochs.

## Change

- A node with validators verifies every aggregate, as before #18521.
- Nodes without validators still skip them, which keeps the goal of
#18521.
- `isLocalValidatorProposer` and its proposer-index cache are removed.

## Cost

About 1,000 aggregates per slot on mainnet, three signature sets each,
verified in batches. The attestation op pool already holds 10 slots × 64
committees × 16 aggregators (10,240 entries), so a constant fill keeps
about the last 10 slots.

## Tests

- `TestAggregateAndProofIsVerifiedWhenTheNodeHasValidators`: a Fulu head
state and a local validator that proposes neither in this epoch nor the
next. With validators the aggregate is verified and stored; without
validators it is ignored. Fails on `main`. Mutations caught: the old
gate, an always-on gate.
- `go test -race` for `cl/phase1/network/services`, `cl/aggregation`,
`cl/beacon/handler`; `make lint` (twice); `make erigon integration`.

## Follow-up

`sync_contribution_service.go` has the same proposer gate for sync
committee contributions.

author: lystopad
subject: cl/beacon/handler: keep payload preparation state work away from the builder cutoff (#25029)
body:
Part of #24119 (item 1). Items 2 and 3 are not covered here.

## Problem

Payload preparation admitted an attempt while more than
`minimumPreparationLead` (500 ms) remained before the proposal slot, and
the same 500 ms was the builder cutoff. The head-state copy and slot
processing cannot be cancelled mid-call. So an attempt admitted late
spent its remaining lead on state work and was then discarded by the
post-work check, after it had competed with production for CPU and for
the head-state read lock.

The loop ticks every quarter slot from when it starts, not from a slot
boundary, so the last tick before a proposal can fall anywhere from 0 to
3 s before the slot. A head that changes late in the slot (a late block)
makes the loop start the state work again near the cutoff.

## Change

- `stateWorkLead(slotDuration)` = `minimumPreparationLead` + one eighth
of a slot: 2 s on 12-second slots.
- The loop admits an attempt only with more than `stateWorkLead` left.
- `preparePayloadForWithScratch` checks it again inside the head-state
view, right before the copy, because the view can wait behind a
head-state writer.
- The builder cutoff is unchanged: the post-work check and the deadline
of the builder start still use 500 ms.
- The "Gloas preparation window is too short" warning compares the
post-PTC window with `stateWorkLead`. On 12-second slots the window is 3
s, so the attempt at the payload attestation deadline is still admitted.
- The "primed execution layer" log line reports `stateWork`, the time
from the start of the copy to the end of slot processing, so the budget
can be checked on live nodes.

With 12-second slots, a head selected in the first two thirds of the
slot is still prepared on a later tick. A head that changes in the last
2 s is left to normal production, which stays the fallback.

## Why an eighth of a slot

From two validator nodes on release/3.8 (one mainnet, one Hoodi):

- Head-state copy (`CachingBeaconState.CopyInto`): 2.81 s and 1.77 s of
CPU in 60-second CPU profiles, about five copies each, so roughly 0.56 s
(mainnet) and 0.35 s (Hoodi) of CPU per copy.
- Epoch processing (`epoch_processing_time`): 275 ms (mainnet) and 210
ms (Hoodi), the last observed value.

A copy plus an epoch transition is under 1 s on mainnet, so 1.5 s of
budget leaves headroom for a loaded node. The figures are per-copy CPU
estimates and single samples, not wall-clock percentiles; the new
`stateWork` field gives the wall-clock value.

## Tests

- `TestPreparePayloadLoopSkipsStateWorkWithoutItsLead`: with 1 s left on
12-second slots, the loop does not open the head-state view.
- `TestPreparePayloadForRejectsStateWorkWithoutItsLead`: with 1 s left
inside the view, the attempt returns `errPreparationTooLate` and does
not copy the state.
- `TestPreparePayloadLoopWarnsWhenGloasWindowCannotFitStateWork`: on
4-second slots, the 1 s post-PTC window triggers the warning.
- These fail on `main`. Mutations caught: the loop using the builder
cutoff, no check before the copy, the old warning threshold, no
state-work budget, and a budget of a quarter slot (which breaks the
Gloas post-PTC tests).
- Three existing loop tests used leads at the new boundary (2 s on
12-second slots, 600 ms on 1-second slots) and now use 2.5 s and 700 ms.
`TestPreparePayloadLoopMemoizesRealPreparation` checks two eligible
ticks instead of three: with a 2 s margin and the attestation-due wait,
its 7-second window can no longer hold three.
- `go test -race ./cl/beacon/handler/...`, `make lint` (twice), `make
erigon integration`.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/phase1/forkchoice: take execution payload event fields from the block (#25002)
body:
Caplin could emit the wrong `slot` in the `execution_payload` and
`execution_payload_available` SSE events, and the wrong `builder_index`
in `execution_payload`. In a capture from a local Gloas devnet, both
Caplin `execution_payload` samples had `slot` and `builder_index` at 0,
and both matching `execution_payload_available` samples had `slot` at 0.
A Lighthouse sample from the same run, for comparison:

```
Caplin:     event: execution_payload  {"slot":"0","builder_index":"0","block_hash":"0x2b20…","block_root":"0x038f…","execution_optimistic":false}
Lighthouse: event: execution_payload  {"slot":"599","builder_index":"18446744073709551615","block_hash":"0x9d12…","block_root":"0x78f4…","execution_optimistic":false}
```

The correct `slot` is the slot of the block named by `block_root`, and
the correct `builder_index` is the builder of its payload; for a
self-build that is `BUILDER_INDEX_SELF_BUILD` (2^64-1).

`emitExecutionPayloadIntegrationEvents` took the slot from
`Payload.SlotNumber` and the builder index from the envelope. Its
callers can pass an envelope built by `envelopeForIndexRepair`, which
contains only the block number and hash, so both fields were 0.

The helper now takes the slot from the beacon block and the builder
index from the block's committed bid. Envelope validation already
requires the envelope's builder index to match that bid. If the block is
not in the store, the helper skips both events instead of emitting a
wrong slot; the fallback in `cl/beacon/handler/epbs.go` behaves the same
way. All four fork-choice emission sites use this helper.

`release/3.8` has the same code. I will open a backport after this
merges.

## Testing

`TestExecutionPayloadOperationEventsDoNotRequireHeadData` now makes the
test fork graph return a block at slot 64 with a self-build bid, passes
an envelope from `envelopeForIndexRepair`, and checks the fields of both
events. `TestExecutionPayloadOperationEventsSkipMissingBlock` checks
that nothing is emitted without the block. Without the production
change, both fail:

```
expected: &beaconevents.ExecutionPayloadData{Slot:0x40, BuilderIndex:0xffffffffffffffff, ...}
actual  : &beaconevents.ExecutionPayloadData{Slot:0x0, BuilderIndex:0x0, ...}

emitted operation event without the beacon block: &beaconevents.EventStream{Event:"execution_payload", ...}
```

- With the change, both pass.
- `go test ./cl/phase1/forkchoice/... ./cl/beacon/...` passes.
- `make lint`: 0 issues. `make erigon integration` builds.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/rpc: skip column peers that answered a by-root request with no sidecars (#24992)
body:
## Problem

`runDownload` in `cl/das` requests missing columns with
`DataColumnSidecarsByRoot` on a 100 ms ticker until they arrive. Peer
selection rotates over the peers that custody the requested columns and
does not remember how a peer answered. When the peers do not have the
columns and answer quickly with nothing, each download loop can ask
peers up to ten times a second. Each batch of up to four blocks has its
own download loop.

In a local Kurtosis devnet with Gloas at slot 128 (Hoodi fork
rehearsal), the network split after the fork. In its busiest minute, a
Lighthouse node received 2,351 `DataColumnsByRoot` requests, all
answered with no sidecars; 2,290 of them came from four Caplin peers.
Over the whole run, 9,587 of the 9,655 by-root column requests that
Lighthouse received returned no sidecars.

An empty by-root response is allowed by the spec, so the responders did
nothing wrong. The requester should not ask the same peer again straight
away.

## Change

When a by-root column response has no sidecars, peer selection skips
that peer for 2 s. Other peers remain eligible for the next request.
When every eligible peer is cooling down, the request fails with
`ErrNoGoodPeer` without network traffic. The cooldown is kept by peer ID
across the 15 s peer refresh, and successful refreshes remove expired
entries. 2 s is the maximum backoff that blob sidecar backfill already
uses (`requestBlobMaxBackoff`).

Failed requests do not start a cooldown. This keeps the `main` behaviour
for the local `ErrPeerBusy`, for context failures, and for peer-reported
errors such as `ResourceUnavailable`. `ErrPeerBusy` is our own limit of
two concurrent streams per peer and request type.

This limits repeated requests to the same peer. It does not bound the
node-wide request rate: with many eligible peers, each download loop can
still send up to ten requests a second to different peers. Non-empty
responses that fail validation keep their current handling.

## Tests

The first two tests use `testing/synctest`.

- `TestRunDownloadDoesNotRepeatRequestsToPeerThatAnsweredNothing`
(`cl/das`): one peer that always answers with no sidecars, for 20 s, so
the run crosses the peer refresh. Every gap between requests is at least
2 s; on `main` it is 100 ms.
- `TestColumnSidecarsRequestSkipsPeerThatAnsweredNothing` (`cl/rpc`):
with two peers that answer with no sidecars, the second request goes to
the other peer at once, the third fails with `ErrNoGoodPeer`, and after
2 s a peer is asked again. On `main` the third request is sent.
- `TestColumnSidecarsRequestKeepsPeerAfterFailedRequest` (`cl/rpc`):
after a failed request, the same peer is asked again at once. This test
also passes on `main`; it guards the decision not to cool down after
errors.
- Two existing tests send a second request to the same single peer after
an empty answer to check the wrapper; they now clear the cooldown first.

Mutation checks: removing the cooldown, a cooldown that never expires, a
refresh that clears active cooldowns, and a cooldown after a failed
request each fail at least one of the new tests.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/beacon/handler: use the head root as the dependent root for slots after the head (#24980)
body:
## Problem

`getDependentRoot` returns the head root only when the dependent slot
equals the head slot. For a later dependent slot within the accepted
lookahead, `GetBlockRootAtSlot` rejects every slot at or after the head
state slot, so the backward scan reaches `headSlot - 1` and returns the
root of the block before the head. If the head is the genesis block, it
returns not found instead.

The Beacon API defines the dependent root as
`get_block_root_at_slot(state, compute_start_slot_at_epoch(epoch - 1) -
1)` for attester duties and proposer duties v2, and as
`get_block_root_at_slot(state, compute_start_slot_at_epoch(epoch) - 1)`
for proposer duties v1, and both use the genesis block root on
underflow. Processing the empty slots after the head carries the head
root into their block roots, so until another block arrives, the
dependent root of a slot at or after the head slot is the head root.

In the first case, if there is no reorg and the next block comes after
the dependent slot, that block changes the answer from the older root to
the root that was the head at the first query. As a result:

- validator clients can report a duties re-org even though the duties
did not change, and
- Caplin rejects proposer preferences signed with the older root
(`dependent root is not a possible dependent block`), because that root
is neither the current head nor the parent of an imported block at or
after the start of the epoch after the dependent slot.

The changed helper is used by attester duties, proposer duties v1 and
proposer duties v2 (which uses the attester slot from Fulu on). PTC
duties and `head_v2` events compute their dependent roots separately,
sync committee duties have no dependent root, and historical duty
queries use separate paths.

## Change

Return the head root when the dependent slot is at or after the head
slot, not only when it is equal. While the node is syncing, the
behaviour does not change.

This also affects accepted lookahead requests whose dependent slot has
not occurred yet: they now get the current head root, which can still
change as blocks arrive, as before. The existing lookahead limits of the
handlers do not change.

## Evidence

Local Kurtosis devnet with Gloas at slot 128 (Hoodi fork rehearsal, 12 s
slots). Slot 479 was empty, so the dependent slot of epoch 16 (attester
and proposer v2) was after the head at slot 478:

- The Lighthouse VC whose only beacon node was Caplin logged `Proposer
duties re-org` for epoch 16, from the root of block 477 to the root of
block 478. The same happened for epoch 6, where slot 159 was empty.
- At epoch 16, that Lighthouse VC and a Teku VC logged `dependent root
is not a possible dependent block`; the Lighthouse VC also logged it at
epoch 6. The client logs do not include the submitted root, so this is a
timing correlation; the validation code above explains the rejection.

## Tests

`TestGetDependentRootUsesHeadRootForSlotsAfterHead` replaces
`TestGetDependentRootReturnsNotFoundWhenRootUnavailable`, which expected
not found for a dependent slot beyond the scan bound. The new test calls
the helper for both the attester and the proposer dependent slot after
the head. It gets an older root before this change and the head root
after it. It does not cover the endpoints, the syncing path, or the
end-to-end sequence of a block arriving after the empty dependent slot
and clients fetching the duties again.

author: Kewei
subject: cl: look up execution bodies by block hash in standalone Caplin (#25020)
body:
## Summary

Standalone Caplin stores pre-Gloas beacon blocks blinded and rebuilds
them on read with the execution body from `ExecutionEngineReader`. That
reader ignored the execution block hash:

- it asked the EL for the body at the block number
(`GetBodiesByRange(number, 1)`), which is the canonical body at that
height;
- it returned empty transaction and withdrawal lists when the EL had no
body;
- its cache of recently produced bodies was keyed by block number.

So for a block that was not canonical on the EL, or whose payload the EL
did not have yet, Caplin could rebuild the requested block with the
transactions and withdrawals of another block, or with empty lists. When
those lists differed, the root of the rebuilt block did not match the
requested root. On a Hoodi shadow fork, a Lighthouse node on its own
fork asked a standalone Caplin node for a block by root and got the
canonical body at that height: 66 transactions instead of 121.
Lighthouse penalised each such response as `UnrequestedBlockRoot` and
then banned the Caplin peer.

Caplin's gossip path stores a block before the EL has its payload, so a
by-root read in that window could also rebuild the block with empty
lists.

## Changes

- **Body by hash.** `ExecutionEngineReader` gets the body with
`GetBodiesByHashes`. If the EL has no body for the hash, it returns the
new `snapshot_format.ErrExecutionBodyNotFound` instead of empty lists.
`GetBodiesByRange` is removed from `ExecutionEngineBodyFetcher`.
- **Cache.** The body cache is keyed by block hash, so it never returns
a body for another hash, and two bodies at the same height can both be
cached. It holds up to 64 block hashes and evicts the oldest inserted
one. `CacheBody` and `CacheBlockBody` take the block hash, and block
production passes `payload.BlockHash`.
- **Embedded mode.** `ExecutionSnapshotReader` already looked bodies up
by hash and returned an error when it found none. It now wraps
`ErrExecutionBodyNotFound`, so both readers report a missing body in the
same way.
- **Req/resp handlers.**
- BlocksByRoot uses the existing fork-choice fallback. If the block is
still unavailable, it leaves the block out and continues with the next
root.
- BlocksByRange stops at the first block whose body is unavailable. The
spec allows a shorter response and requires the returned blocks to be
consecutive, so stopping avoids sending a later block after a missing
one.
- BlocksByHead uses the existing fork-choice fallback and ends the
response if the block is still unavailable.
- **Liveness.** The endpoint reads blocks with
`ReadBeaconBlockBodyBySlot`, because it only uses consensus fields.
Otherwise a missing execution body would now make it fail.

## Behaviour changes

- In standalone mode, a missing execution body for a stored pre-Gloas
block makes these Beacon API endpoints return 500: the full-block and
block-attestation endpoints, and the blinded-block,
sync-committee-rewards and `/eth/v1/beacon/blobs/{block_id}` endpoints.
So do expected-withdrawals reads for a state other than the head, which
read the next stored block. Before, these endpoints worked with a block
rebuilt from the wrong body or from empty lists, so full and blinded
blocks could have the wrong root. The blob-sidecars endpoint is not
affected.
- Other readers of pre-Gloas blocks, such as the state antiquary and the
historical states reader, now get the error in standalone mode too, as
they already did in embedded mode.
- In embedded mode, a missing body no longer returns an error that
resets the BlocksByRoot, BlocksByRange or BlocksByHead stream.
BlocksByRoot leaves the block out and continues; BlocksByRange and
BlocksByHead end the response.
- Gloas blocks are not affected, because they do not carry an execution
payload.

## Tests

- `TestExecutionEngineReaderUsesBlockHash`: with bodies for two hashes,
a request for the side-chain hash returns its transactions and
withdrawals.
- `TestExecutionEngineReaderRejectsMissingBody`: no body for the hash,
or no engine, gives `ErrExecutionBodyNotFound`.
- `TestExecutionEngineReaderCacheMatchesBlockHash` and
`TestExecutionEngineReaderCacheKeepsBodiesAtSameHeight`: the cache does
not return a body for another hash, and it keeps both bodies at one
height.
- `TestExecutionSnapshotReaderReportsMissingBody`: the embedded reader
returns `ErrExecutionBodyNotFound`.
- `TestBeaconSnapshotReaderPropagatesUnavailableExecutionBody`: the
error reaches `ReadBlockByRoot` and `ReadBlockBySlot` callers. This
already worked; the test protects it because the handlers now rely on
it.
- `TestBlockHandlersOmitUnavailableExecutionBody`: BlocksByRange does
not send the block after an unavailable one. With no fork-choice
fallback configured, BlocksByRoot and BlocksByHead send nothing.
- `TestLivenessEndpointReadsConsensusBodyWithoutExecutionData`: liveness
works when the full block cannot be read.
- `TestCacheExecutionBodyUsesBlockHash`: block production passes the
payload number and hash to `CacheBlockBody`.

Mutation checks: each of these changes, reverted on its own, makes the
matching test fail: the lookup by hash, the not-found error instead of
empty lists, the hash-keyed cache, the payload hash in block production,
the stop in BlocksByRange, and the body-only read in liveness.

Validation: `go test` for `cl/persistence/...`, `cl/sentinel/...`,
`cl/beacon/...`, `cl/phase1/...`, `cl/antiquary/...`, `cl/das/...` and
`db/snapshotsync/freezeblocks/...`; `-race -count=5` for the new tests;
`make lint`; `make erigon integration`.

release/3.8 and release/3.7 have the same `ExecutionEngineReader` and
need backports.

Co-authored-by: Alex Sharov <AskAlexSharov@gmail.com>

author: lystopad
subject: cl: pick the sync committee by the message slot (#25027)
body:
Fixes #24694.

## Problem

Members assigned to slot `S + 1` sign sync committee messages and
contributions for slot `S`. Caplin chose the committee from the head
slot instead, in three places:

- the gossip subnet check (`subnets.ComputeSubnetsForSyncCommittee`);
- the sync contribution service (`getSyncSubcommitteePubkeys`);
- the sync contribution pool (`AddSyncCommitteeMessage`).

At the last slot `P − 1` of a period, the next committee signs. A
message that arrives before the node imports block `P − 1` is checked
with the head still at `P − 2`, so against the current committee. The
node rejects valid next-committee members with `validator is not into
any subnet N` and bans their peers. The issue's case, a previous-slot
message seen with the head already at `P − 1`, is the opposite mistake.

A Hoodi validator node logged this at every period boundary between
2026-09-19 and 2026-10-16 (13 bursts, all in slot `P − 1`, 0.5–4.1 s
into the slot, up to ~100 rejected messages and 1–9 banned peers each).
Details in the issue.

## Change

- `state.SyncCommitteeForMessageSlot(state, slot)` returns the current
committee when `slot + 1` is in the state's period, the next committee
when it is in the following period, and `ErrSyncCommitteeNotInState`
otherwise.
- The subnet check, the contribution service and the pool use it with
the message or contribution slot. A slot whose committee the state does
not hold is ignored, not rejected.
