- `POST /eth/v1/beacon/pool/sync_committees` computes the subnets for
the message slot. The subscription endpoint keeps the head slot.
- The pool's cleanup dropped every contribution whose slot differed from
the head slot, so a message for the slot after the head was aggregated
and then deleted at once. It now keeps the head slot and the next one,
so a stalled head cannot let later slots accumulate.
- Conditions that do not need the committee run before the committee
lookup: the validator index in `ComputeSubnetsForSyncCommittee` (an
unknown index stays a REJECT) and the aggregator selection proof in the
contribution service.
- `POST /eth/v1/validator/contribution_and_proofs` reports a
contribution whose committee is not in the head state as a failure
instead of publishing it.

## Tests

- `TestSyncCommitteeForMessageSlot`: committee choice around a period
boundary, and slots outside the state.
- `TestSyncCommitteesChecksTheCommitteeOfTheMessageSlot`: the issue's
case, the last slot before its block is imported, a current-committee
member signing for the last slot (still rejected), and a committee
outside the head state (ignored).
- `TestSyncSubcommitteePubkeysUseTheCommitteeOfTheContributionSlot` and
`TestSyncContributionPoolAggregatesTheLastSlotOfAPeriodBeforeItsBlock`.
- `TestSyncContributionServiceCommitteeNotInHeadState`,
`TestPoolContributionsAndProofsReportsCommitteeNotInHeadState`,
`TestPoolSyncCommitteesPublishesTheLastSlotOfAPeriodOnTheNextCommitteeSubnet`,
`TestSyncContributionPoolKeepsTheHeadSlotAndTheNextOne`, and an
unknown-validator row in
`TestSyncCommitteesChecksTheCommitteeOfTheMessageSlot` (added after
review).
- The new tests fail on `main`. Mutations caught: swapped committees,
the period of `slot` instead of `slot + 1`, the head slot in each of the
three call sites, a rejection instead of an ignore, the old pool
cleanup, either pool bound removed, the committee lookup before the
index check, the selection-proof check after it, the head slot in
`PostEthV1BeaconPoolSyncCommittees`, and publishing an ignored
contribution over REST.
- `go test -race` for `cl/phase1/core/state`,
`cl/phase1/network/services`, `cl/validator/...`,
`cl/beacon/handler/...`; `make lint` (twice); `make erigon integration`.
The spec tests were not run locally (fixtures not downloaded); CI runs
them.

author: lystopad
subject: cl: keep a wider sync contribution window and publish only accepted contributions (#25056)
body:
Follow-up to #25027, from yperbasis's review.

## Changes

- **Sync contribution pool window.** The pool kept only the head slot
and the next one. After two empty slots, the next proposer reads
`GetSyncAggregate` for head+2, and an aggregator at head+2 reads
`GetSyncContribution` for it; both got an empty result, because the
entry was removed right after it was aggregated. The pool now keeps
slots from the head to one epoch after it. That still bounds what is
kept while the head stalls.
- **`POST /eth/v1/validator/contribution_and_proofs`.** The handler
published a contribution the service ignored, for example one rejected
by the clock check, although it was not verified. It now reports every
ignore as a pooling failure instead of publishing it. A contribution for
an already-seen (aggregator, slot, subcommittee) still returns `nil`
before the signature checks and is published, as before; that is tracked
separately.
- **Spec-test harness.** The contribution harness picks the committee
with `state.SyncCommitteeForMessageSlot(beaconState,
contribution.Slot)`, like the message harness, and returns "ignore" when
the state does not hold it.

## Tests

- `TestSyncContributionPoolKeepsOneEpochFromTheHead`: head−1 removed;
head, head+2 and head+epoch kept; head+epoch+1 removed.
- `TestSyncContributionPoolKeepsOneEpochFromTheHeadForBlocks`: the same
window for the contributions the proposer reads through
`GetSyncAggregate`.
- `TestPoolContributionsAndProofsReportsIgnoredContributions`: a plain
ignore and a committee-not-in-state ignore both return 400 and publish
nothing.
- Mutations caught: the old head+1 window, no upper bound, publishing
ignored contributions.
- `go test -race` for `cl/validator/sync_contribution_pool`,
`cl/phase1/network/services/...`, `cl/spectest/consensus_tests`,
`cl/beacon/handler/...`; `make lint` (twice); `make erigon integration`.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/phase1/forkchoice, cl/spectest: assert Gloas PTC fork-choice steps and votes, run the remaining ssz_static vectors (#24859)
body:
## Summary

Execute the Gloas PTC fork-choice steps and checks that the spectest
runner previously ignored silently, align
`on_payload_attestation_message` with the spec so they pass, and run the
remaining ssz_static vectors that had no handler.

## Fork-choice runner

- `steps.yaml` is decoded with `KnownFields`, and an unknown step type
fails the test. Before this change an unknown step or check key was
dropped, so a vector could pass without checking anything.
- New `payload_attestation_message` step, including `valid: false`.
- New `payload_timeliness_vote` and `payload_data_availability_vote`
checks. A check fails when the root has no vote entry (the spec asserts
the root is present), not only when the votes differ.
- New `genesis_time` check.

Before this change the 13 Gloas cases under
`on_payload_attestation_message`, `payload_timeliness` and
`payload_data_availability` ran and passed without asserting any vote.
Now the votes are asserted: forcing present vote entries to contain
all-zero arrays fails 11 cases (nine of those 13 plus two `get_head`
payload-tiebreak cases), and removing the entries fails all 15 cases
that contain vote checks.

## PTC message handling

- `OnPayloadAttestationMessage` follows the spec handler for wire
messages. A vote counts only for the store's current slot. A message for
another slot of the referenced block is a no-op, as in the spec's
`data.slot != state.slot` return.
- `OnGossipPayloadAttestationMessage` adds the p2p first-valid rule per
(slot, validator). The current-slot decision is taken under the store
lock. First-valid is tracked per (slot, validator) for the store's
current and previous slots; a message for an older slot is ignored. A
late gossip message for the previous slot that passes validation is
accepted for propagation, but its vote is not counted; fork choice
reports it with `ErrPayloadAttestationNotCurrentSlot`, which is separate
from `ErrIgnore`.
- Before this change a vote from a previous slot could be counted in
fork choice.
- The isFromBlock path is removed: block-carried PTC votes keep going
through `notifyPtcMessages`.

Red evidence: with only the runner change,
`on_payload_attestation_message_valid`, `_slot_mismatch` and
`_current_slot_and_signature` fail. They pass with the handler changes.

## ssz_static

`HistoricalBatch` (phase0 to bellatrix) and `NewPayloadRequest`
(bellatrix to gloas) have no Caplin production type, so their 45 mainnet
cases were skipped. They now run against test-only types. The Gloas
`NewPayloadRequest` uses the progressive container root.

The runner's skip for `on_execution_payload_envelope__wrong_withdrawals`
is removed. The case name has one underscore, so the skip never matched,
and the case already ran and passed.

## Not changed

- Gossip validation still takes the PTC, public keys and domain from the
referenced block's state. The p2p spec uses the head state. This
deviation existed before this PR and is left for a follow-up.
- The 13 `gloas/networking/gossip_payload_attestation_message` vectors
are still unregistered, like the other gossip vectors without a handler.
- The runner still ends a test early on `on_payload_info` and
`pow_block` steps.
- A gossip PTC message for a slot ahead of the store's slot is ignored
rather than accepted for propagation. This branch is unreachable for a
known referenced block: `OnBlock` cannot import slot S while the store
is before S, and `OnTick` never moves store time backwards. It is
reachable only with inconsistent mocked or preloaded state, and is then
not limited to the lower clock-disparity boundary. The unregistered
gossip vector `valid_slot_at_lower_disparity` expects acceptance.

## Tests

Run locally on this branch:
- `cd cl/spectest && make mainnet`: pass.
- `go test ./cl/phase1/forkchoice/... ./cl/phase1/network/services/...
./cl/beacon/handler/...`: pass; `-race` on the PTC tests: pass.
- `make lint`: 0 issues.
- `make erigon integration`: builds.

subject: cl/phase1/network/services: keep the head above zero in the sync committee slot test (#25069)
body:
Test-only follow-up to #25027, from domiwei's note on #25067.

The fixture head is at slot 160, so `nextPeriod` was 8192 and
`SetSlot(nextPeriod - (1+2*period))` wrapped around: the two "committee
not in the head state" rows tested a message period older than the head,
not a head two periods behind the message. The test now starts three

No production change. The test passes; `make lint` is clean twice. To be
cherry-picked to release/3.8 after merge, so the branch stays aligned
with main.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/clparams, cl/rpc, cl/sentinel: bound req/resp chunks by MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE and max_compressed_len (#25079)
body:
Part of #24417 (req/resp half). The gossip half is #25078.

## Problem

Caplin's req/resp read paths did not use the consensus-spec limits
(`specs/phase0/p2p-interface.md`, v1.7.0-beta.2):

- `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE = 10 * 2**20`: the maximum uncompressed size of an
RPC chunk. The length prefix must be within the SSZ type bound or
`MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE`, whichever is smaller.
- "A reader MUST NOT read more than `max_compressed_len(n)` bytes after
reading the SSZ length-prefix `n`", where `max_compressed_len(n) = 32 +
n + n / 6`.

Before this PR:

| Path | Uncompressed limit | Compressed limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Request / status decode (`ssz_snappy.DecodeAndReadNoForkDigest`, used
by every sentinel handler, the handshake and peer selection) | 16 MB |
none (only the `Exact` variant had one) |
| Client response parsing (`rpc.parseResponseData`) | 18 MB | none |
| Response byte budgets (`cl/rpc`) and the multi-chunk ceiling
(`httpreqresp.maxMultiChunkResponse`) | derived from
`clparams.MaxChunkSize` = 15 MiB | — |

## Changes

- `cl/clparams`: add `MaxPayloadSize = 10 MiB`.
- `cl/sentinel/communication/ssz_snappy`: reject a length prefix above
`MaxPayloadSize`, and bound the compressed input of every decode by
`snappy.MaxEncodedLen(n)` (identical to `max_compressed_len(n)`). The
two limits are applied separately: 10 MiB applies to the decoded length,
never to the compressed bytes.
- `cl/rpc`: apply the same two limits to each response chunk. The
compressed limit is an `io.LimitReader` around the snappy input of one
chunk, so the next chunk's result byte and context bytes stay aligned.
Remove the per-envelope `len(raw) > MaxChunkSize` checks, which the
per-chunk 10 MiB check now covers.
- `cl/rpc`, `cl/sentinel/httpreqresp`: compute the response byte budgets
and the multi-chunk ceiling from `MaxPayloadSize`.

The sentinel handlers need no change: they decode through `ssz_snappy`
and get the new limits from there.

No legitimate object exceeds 10 MiB on any supported network. The
largest are `DataColumnSidecar` (about 8.8 MB at
`MAX_BLOB_COMMITMENTS_PER_BLOCK` = 4096), `BlobSidecar` (about 131 KB),
and blocks, which are capped network-wide by the 10 MiB gossip limit and
by EIP-7934. Compliant snappy writers emit at most `10 + n + 8 * ceil(n
/ 65536)` framed bytes, which is below `max_compressed_len(n)`.

## Why #13058 raised the limit, and whether that still holds

#13058 ("Bump limits from 10MiB to 15Mib", no description) changed only
`cl/clparams/config.go`, in the same week as the 30M → 36M gas-limit
bump (#13057):

- `GossipMaxSizeBellatrix`: 10 MiB → 15 MiB. This was the change that
had an effect.
- `MaxChunkSize`: 1 MiB → 15 MiB. At that time no req/resp code read
`MaxChunkSize`; req/resp used the hardcoded 16 MB and 18 MB limits shown
above.

`MaxChunkSize` became the req/resp ceiling later, in #21562. So the bump
was about large blocks on gossip, not about req/resp.

That reason no longer holds:
- The EIP-7623 calldata floor (Pectra) and the 8 MiB RLP block cap of
EIP-7934 (Osaka) keep execution blocks well below 10 MiB.
- Every other client enforces 10 MiB, so a larger object does not
propagate.

## Non-wire uses of `MaxChunkSize` (unchanged)

`clparams.MaxChunkSize` (15 MiB) stays as it is for these uses. None of
them is a req/resp chunk limit.

| Use | What it bounds | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cl/cltypes/epbs_payload.go` (`ValidateForPersistence`, `EncodeSSZ`) |
envelope SSZ size | unchanged, see below |
| `cl/cltypes/solid/transactions.go` | transaction list decode bounds |
unchanged, local sanity bound |
| `cl/cltypes/execution_requests.go`,
`cl/beacon/handler/block_production.go` | progressive execution-request
list decode limit | unchanged, local sanity bound |
| `cl/phase1/core/checkpoint_sync/remote_checkpoint_sync.go`,
`cl/phase1/network/beacon_downloader.go` | Beacon API HTTP body size |
unchanged, not req/resp |
| `cl/phase1/forkchoice/fork_graph/fork_graph_disk_fs.go` | envelope
file size on disk | unchanged, see below |
| `cl/phase1/network/services/execution_payload_service.go` |
pending-envelope memory budget | unchanged |

Possibly wrong, not fixed here: envelope validation and persistence
still accept up to 15 MiB, and so does gossip until #25078 lands. A
10–15 MiB envelope can therefore be imported from Erigon gossip, but it
can no longer be fetched over req/resp: an Erigon peer will serve it,
and the receiver rejects the chunk. Before this PR, Erigon-to-Erigon
req/resp accepted it. Other clients already reject such objects, so this
only affects Erigon-only networks with very large payloads. The fix
belongs at ingress (envelope validation and gossip), so it is left for
#25078 and a follow-up.

`NetworkConfig.MaxChunkSize` (yaml `MAX_CHUNK_SIZE`) is not read
anywhere. It is left as it is.

## Spec-config test

The `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` exclusion in `cl/spectest/mainnet_config_test.go`
is kept. Gossip is not aligned on main yet. #25078 maps
`MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` to `NetworkConfig.GossipMaxSize` and removes the
exclusion.

## Follow-ups (pre-existing, not changed by this PR)

- After #25078 merges, read the req/resp limit from the configured
`MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` instead of the `clparams.MaxPayloadSize` constant.
- Non-exact decodes do not check the length prefix against the SSZ type
bound before decompressing. For example, a 24-byte `BeaconBlocksByRange`
request may declare up to 10 MiB. Fixed-size requests could use
`DecodeAndReadNoForkDigestExact`.
- Decoded bytes after the declared `n` in the same snappy frame are
dropped instead of rejected, both in `parseResponseData` and in the
non-exact decoder.
- `httpreqresp.ResponseCode.ErrorMessage` ignores the declared length
and has no `max_compressed_len` bound. The response body cap still
bounds it.
- The serving side (`EncodeAndWrite`) has no `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` check.

## Tests

TDD: each new or changed test was run against the old production code
first and failed for the expected reason.

- `ssz_snappy`:
- `TestDecodeAndReadNoForkDigestMaxPayloadSize`: 10 MiB of random bytes
is accepted; 10 MiB + 1 is rejected.
- `TestDecodeAndReadNoForkDigestBoundsCompressedInput`: a padded frame
of exactly `max_compressed_len(n)` is accepted and the bytes after it
stay unread; +1 is rejected.
- `rpc`:
- `TestParseResponseDataAcceptsMaxPayloadSize`: a random 10 MiB chunk
round-trips.
- `TestParseResponseDataRejectsOversizedCompressedChunk`: a chunk of
exactly the limit is accepted and the following chunk stays aligned; +1
fails in the snappy read.
-
`TestExecutionPayloadEnvelopeRequestsRejectOversizedDecompressedChunk`:
now uses 10 MiB + 1.
  - The response budget assertions use `MaxPayloadSize`.
- `httpreqresp`: `TestMaxMultiChunkResponse` pins the ceiling to `1024 *
(max_compressed_len(10 MiB) + 64)`.

I mutated each new limit to `-1`, and the at-limit cases failed.

Commands run, all passing:

- `go test -race -count=1 ./cl/sentinel/... ./cl/rpc/...
./cl/clparams/...`
- `go test -count=1 -run Mainnet ./cl/spectest/`
- `make lint`, several times, clean
- `make erigon integration`

## Review

Before opening, the change went through two independent reviews
(standards, spec, adversarial and complexity passes), and then each
review cross-checked the other's findings.

- **Round 1:** no defect in the production change. The confirmed
in-scope findings were test gaps: the limits were not pinned at
equality, the next chunk after an at-limit chunk was not checked,
incompressible payloads were not tested, and one assertion was too weak.
They were fixed in tests only.
- **Round 2:** a fresh pass over the cumulative diff by both reviewers
found nothing new in scope. Only optional test nits were left: one
length assertion that repeats the full-equality check that follows it,
and the magic frame offsets in one test.
- The remaining findings predate this PR and are listed under
"Follow-ups" above. They include the 10 MiB / 15 MiB asymmetry.

author: awskii
subject: cl/phase1/network/registry: sweep idle peer limiters inside acquire (#25039)
body:
`newTokenBucketRateLimiter` started a `cleanup` goroutine that slept 10
s in a loop forever, 13 per `RegisterGossipServices`. `acquire` wrote
`lastAccess` to a copy of the map value, so the sweep wiped every bucket
every 10 s. Closes #20663.

## Changes
- Sweep buckets idle over 3 min inside `acquire`, at most once per 10 s,
under the existing mutex; no goroutine.
- The map holds `*tokenBucketLimiter`, so `lastAccess` persists.
Per-peer limits now hold at their configured rate instead of gaining
`burst` tokens every 10 s.

## Notes
Mainnet tip node, internal Caplin, 30-min windows: `cleanup` goroutines
13 → 0, head blocks 145/145 and 151/151 slots, equal accepted column
bytes across 8 subnets, 0 EROR.

author: awskii
subject: cl: copy each new head into a reused beacon state instead of allocating one (#25003)
body:
Since #24165 every head update copies the new head into a fresh
`CachingBeaconState`, ~1 GB of allocation per slot on mainnet. This
copies into a spare state instead.

## Changes
- `SyncedDataManager` keeps a spare state as the copy target, rotated
per publish. A failed copy drops the spare and keeps head and previous,
as #23962 expects; cost: one more state (~650 MB).
- A reused buffer is overwritten one publish after it stops being
previous, so two readers that kept head-state internals past their view
now finish inside it: the shuffled-set pre-cache and
`validator_identities`.

## Numbers
Mainnet tip node (`awskii/v3-commitment`), 3 interleaved 40-min arms per
binary:

| | base | this |
|---|---|---|
| allocation | 96 MB/s | 22 MB/s |
| process CPU | 0.258 cores | 0.232 |
| anon RSS | 18.2 GB | 12.4 GB |
| flush+commit p50 | 76 ms | 60 ms |

FCU → head and validate → FCU: no change.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/phase1/network/gossip: keep sync subnets and duties across fork-digest changes (#25086)
body:
## Summary

Around a fork-digest change (a fork or a blob-parameter-only fork),
`goCheckForkAndResubscribe` joins the next digest's topics about 8 slots
before the change with `subscribeUpcomingTopics`, which copies each
topic's expiry, and about 16 slots later a goroutine calls `Unsubscribe`
and `Remove` on every topic of the old digest. Two problems in that
window:

- **syncnets cleared while still subscribed.**
`TopicSubscriptions.Remove`, `Unsubscribe` and the expiry check call
`UpdateENRSyncNets(subnet, false)` whenever a `sync_committee_{subnet}`
topic's subscription is cancelled. When the old digest's topics are
removed, the same subnet is still subscribed under the new digest, but
its `syncnets` bit is cleared, and since `SubscribeWithExpiry` only sets
the bit when it subscribes a topic that was not subscribed, nothing sets
it again while that subscription lasts. Peers then do not see the subnet
in the ENR or MetaData `syncnets`.
- **Duty subscriptions miss the next digest.**
`GossipManager.SubscribeWithExpiry(name, expiry)` subscribes only
`composeTopic(CurrentForkDigest(), name)`. Its callers are beacon
committee subscriptions for aggregators
(`cl/validator/committee_subscription`), sync committee subscriptions
(`POST /eth/v1/validator/sync_committee_subscriptions`) and PeerDAS
custody (`cl/das`). A request made after the next digest's topics were
joined subscribes the current digest only, so for a duty slot after the
change the node is not subscribed to the subnet under the digest in use.

## Changes

- `cl/phase1/network/gossip/gossip_subscription.go`: when a sync
committee topic's subscription is cancelled, the `syncnets` bit is
cleared only if no registered topic with the same name (the same subnet
under another digest) is still subscribed. Setting the bit is unchanged.
- `cl/phase1/network/gossip/gossip_manager.go`: `SubscribeWithExpiry`
subscribes the current digest's topic as before (including the deferred
subscription and the error when that topic is not registered), then also
subscribes every other registered topic with the same name with the same
expiry. An error on one of those topics is logged and does not fail the
request, so a topic that the old digest's cleanup removes between the
listing of the topics and the call does not fail it (that topic is then
left as a deferred subscription, which is never used because the old
digest is not registered again).

## Not changed here

- The 8-slot lookahead and the removal of the old digest's topics. The
phase0 P2P spec
[says](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/460fd37c3a58f6baf8a9a285d2adf71c4f818929/specs/phase0/p2p-interface.md#L1840-L1845)
a node must subscribe to the persistent subnets of the future fork at
least `EPOCHS_PER_SUBNET_SUBSCRIPTION` epochs before it; Caplin joins
them about 8 slots before. Lighthouse subscribes to the next digest's
topics one epoch before the change
([`SUBSCRIBE_DELAY_EPOCHS`](https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/blob/014ba06b56514d383426f2c727e7233dad973e0d/beacon_node/network/src/service.rs#L59),
[timer](https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/blob/014ba06b56514d383426f2c727e7233dad973e0d/beacon_node/network/src/service.rs#L1658-L1665))
and Prysm when the change is in the next epoch
([`ensureRegistrationsForEpoch`](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/64c1dfc98abaf55d1d091049afc3f479385be6bc/beacon-chain/sync/fork_watcher.go#L65-L69)).
- `subscribeUpcomingTopics` copies the expiry the old topic has when the
next digest's topic is added; a duty that extends the old topic's expiry
while the next digest's topic is being added can leave the earlier
expiry on the new topic.

## Testing

- **TDD**, with the production files from `main`:
- `TestSyncCommitteeOldDigestRemovalKeepsENRWhileNewDigestSubscribed`
(strict P2P mock) fails with `Unexpected call to
*mock_services.MockP2PManager.UpdateENRSyncNets([1 false])` from
`Unsubscribe` of the old digest's topic.
- `TestSyncCommitteeTopicsExpiringTogetherClearENROnce` fails with the
same unexpected call from the expiry check: the first of the two expired
topics clears the bit while the other is still subscribed.
- `TestDutySubscriptionIncludesUpcomingDigest` fails because the next
digest's topic is not subscribed after
`GossipManager.SubscribeWithExpiry`.
- `TestRemovingSubscribedSyncCommitteeOldDigestKeepsENR` (strict P2P
mock) fails with `Unexpected call to
*mock_services.MockP2PManager.UpdateENRSyncNets([1 false])` from
`Remove` of the old digest's topic while it is still subscribed.
- `TestDutySubscriptionContinuesAfterAnotherDigestFails` closes the
topic handle of one other digest and checks that the request succeeds
and the remaining digest is subscribed; it fails on `main` because that
digest is not subscribed, and it also fails if the closed topic's error
is returned instead of logged.
- `go test -p 2 -count=1 ./cl/phase1/network/gossip/
./cl/validator/committee_subscription/ ./cl/beacon/handler/ ./cl/das/...
./cl/p2p/... ./cl/sentinel/...`, `go test -race -p 2 -count=1
./cl/phase1/network/gossip/`, `make lint`, `make erigon integration`.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/gossip, cl/p2p: enforce per-topic gossip payload bounds and spec size limits (#25078)
body:
Closes #24930. Part of #24417 (gossip half; the req/resp half is a
separate PR).

Supersedes #24618: this branch keeps its first commit (author
yperbasis), rebased on main, and adds the fixes from review.

## Problem

Gossip messages were decompressed in full twice before any check on what
the topic's type can hold: once in the message-id function, which then
copied the decompressed bytes again into a hashing buffer, and once in
the validator. Both paths accepted up to 15 MiB uncompressed on every
topic, even where the SSZ type caps the payload at a few hundred bytes.
The pubsub frame limit was also 15 MiB, while the spec uses
`MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` (10 MiB).

## Changes

- `gossip.MaxUncompressedSize`: the SSZ bound per topic for aggregates,
attestation subnets, attester and proposer slashings, exits, BLS
changes, sync committee messages and contributions, capped by
`MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE`. Other topics use `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` alone.
- `gossip.DecompressMessage`, used by both the message-id function and
the validator:
  - rejects `Message.data` above `max_compressed_len(MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE)`;
- checks the per-topic bound against the snappy header before
allocating.
The message-id falls back to the invalid-snappy domain for such data, as
it already did for undecodable data.
- The message-id is hashed incrementally instead of concatenating
domain, topic and payload into a second buffer.
- The pubsub frame limit is the spec's `max_message_size()` (12,234,442
bytes on mainnet) instead of 15 MiB.
- `NetworkConfig.GossipMaxSize` is read from the YAML key
`MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE`, the key current spec configs use. Before this PR,
nothing read the field and the key was ignored. The JSON key served by
`/eth/v1/config/spec` is unchanged.
- The `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` exclusion in
`cl/spectest/mainnet_config_test.go` is removed, because the key now
maps to `GossipMaxSize`, which matches the spec.

For a maximal message on a small-type topic, the work before rejection
goes from three decompressed copies to one varint read.

## Changes compared to #24618

- Rebased on main, with conflicts resolved against the reworked topic
subscriptions.
- `MaxUncompressedSize` is capped by `GossipMaxSize`, so a topic bound
never exceeds the network limit.
- The race in `TestNewPubsubValidator_RejectsPayloadAboveTopicBound`: it
assigned the manager's config after `NewGossipManager` had started its
goroutines. It now uses its own manager.
- `register_gloas_boundary_test.go` passed an empty `NetworkConfig`, so
its gossip limit was 0 and every message was rejected. It now uses the
mainnet network config.
- The compressed-size check, the `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` YAML key and the
spectest exclusion are new.

## Behaviour changes to note

- RPC frames between 12,234,442 bytes and 15 MiB are now dropped.
Spec-compliant clients already drop them. Peers that still use a 15 MiB
frame, such as older Erigon nodes on mixed-version devnets, can lose an
RPC that batches several large messages.
- A custom config that sets only the legacy `GOSSIP_MAX_SIZE` key now
gets the default 10 MiB.

## Not changed (possible follow-ups)

- Static-size Gloas and light-client topics
(`payload_attestation_message`, `proposer_preferences`,
`light_client_*`) still use the network limit, not a type bound.
- Self-published messages skip the validator, and `PublishToForkDigest`
does not check the uncompressed size. This is the same as on main.
- `GossipMaxSizeBellatrix` and `DecompressSnappy(..., true)` no longer
have production readers. They stay in this PR to keep config and API
compatibility, and can be removed separately.
- The bounds are not fork-aware: pre-Electra topics get the larger
Electra bound, and SSZ decoding still rejects anything above the real
bound.

## Testing

TDD, each behaviour red first:

- `TestDecompressSnappyWithLimit`: rejects above the limit with zero
allocations.
- `TestMaxUncompressedSizeMatchesLargestEncoding`: cross-checks every
hand-derived bound against `EncodingSizeSSZ()` of max-shaped `cltypes`
values. `TestMaxUncompressedSizeIsCappedByNetworkLimit` covers the
network cap.
- `TestDecompressMessageRejectsCompressedDataAboveMaxCompressedLen`: a
valid snappy stream within the uncompressed limit but above
`max_compressed_len` is rejected.
- `TestMsgIDUsesInvalidDomainAbovePayloadBounds`: covers the network
limit, the per-topic bound and the compressed limit.
- `TestNewPubsubValidator_RejectsPayloadAboveTopicBound`: the message is
rejected before `DecodeGossipMessage` runs.
- `TestMaxGossipMessageSizeFollowsSpec` and
`TestPubsubFrameLimitFollowsMaxGossipMessageSize`: an RPC exactly at
`max_message_size` is delivered, and one byte more resets the stream.
- `TestCustomConfigReadsMaxPayloadSize`.
- Mutation checks:
  - Restoring the 15 MiB frame limit makes the frame test fail.
- Bypassing the compressed check in the message-id function makes the
message-id test fail.

Checks run:

- `go test -race` for `cl/p2p`, `cl/phase1/network/gossip` and
`cl/phase1/network/registry`.
- `go test -short` for `cl/gossip`, `cl/utils`, `cl/p2p/...`,
`cl/clparams`, `cl/phase1/network/...` and `cl/sentinel/...`.
- `make lint`, twice.
- `make erigon integration`.

`cl/spectest` `mainnet_config` was run only against an older local
fixture set, where `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` matched. CI uses the pinned
fixtures.

The branch had two independent reviews, each cross-checking the other's
findings, until no in-scope findings remained.

---------

Co-authored-by: yperbasis <andrey.ashikhmin@gmail.com>

author: lystopad
subject: cl/beacon/handler: wait for the voted block before rejecting REST attestations (#25094)
body:
Fixes #25093.

`POST /eth/v1|v2/beacon/pool/attestations` rejected an attestation with
400 `ignore: block not seen` when its block was not imported yet, and
did not publish it. On mainnet, blocks with blobs are often imported
2–2.5 s into the slot, so a validator client can attest before that.

Now the handlers wait for the voted block, then process and publish the
attestation:
- `ErrBlockNotSeen` sentinel (wrapped in `ErrIgnore`; error text
unchanged) marks this case.
- The wait polls fork choice every 50 ms, bounded by one slot per
request (shared by all attestations in the request) and by the request
context.
- A failure is reported only if the block does not arrive in time.

This matches Lighthouse, which requeues such attestations and waits up
to one slot.

Tests: a block that arrives after submission gives 200 and one publish;
a block that never arrives gives 400 for every attestation after about
one slot (not one slot per attestation).

author: Andrew Ashikhmin
subject: rpc, db: gate historical requests by physical availability (#23776)
body:
## Summary

Historical RPC pruning checks combine configured retention with observed
state-history and block-transaction boundaries, returning `PrunedError`
below the effective boundary. This applies to finite and unbounded modes
without changing retention or restoring pruned data.

A wider configured window does not prove its data is present. #23708
should merge after or together with this PR to avoid advertising missing
history after a retention increase.

Review order: gates in `rpc/jsonrpc/eth_api.go`, capabilities in
`eth_system.go`, then pinned file views and `prune_floor_cache.go`.

## Behaviour

RPC history gates combine configured retention with physical boundaries
matched to each reader's position. State-reader constructors retain
their own boundary checks. Parallel block-tracing workers also check the
first replay position when opening their separate read view; all jobs in
that block read at or after it.

For requested block `B`, `Min(B)` is the txNum of its first system
transaction:

| Reader | Required history position |
| --- | --- |
| Post-block state | `Min(B+1)` |
| State after the next block's initial system transaction | `Min(B+1)+1`
|
| Transaction replay / indexed pre-state | `Min(B)+i+1` (`i = 0` for
full replay) |
| Whole-block history | `Min(B)` |

`i` is a zero-based transaction position, including the position after
the last user transaction. If the block-level replay boundary rejects a
request, an exact txNum check can still admit retained pre-state within
that block. This exception requires exact, known block bounds and an
in-block position, so oversized indices cannot bypass the boundary.
Availability checks do not use the latest-state fallback for missing
mappings. They can recover missing mappings from snapshot bodies, but
not MDBX body IDs, which also count side forks. Local readers use pinned
body files; remote readers restrict this fallback to an observed frozen
range and return an error while that range is unknown. Fully retained
blocks keep existing index behaviour; broader validation is in stacked
PR #24388.

- Rebuilding pre-Byzantium receipt roots requires history from `Min(B)`,
including commitment history when enabled; receipt gates and
capabilities enforce this. The commitment bound does not apply to
post-Byzantium receipts or logs.
- Log-index checks do not require history for the initial system entry.
Filtered queries check replay history once, also covering receipt
generation when cached receipts are unavailable.
- Otterscan transaction searches check full replay history once per
visited block, before skipping system entries. Ascending scans skip
reward-only entries without requiring block transactions. Descending
scans can still require block data for those entries because of an
existing iterator limitation. A completed page stops before checking the
next block.
- Count-limited `erigon_getLatestLogs` queries can finish within
retained history even when the requested range extends into pruned data.
If they cannot satisfy the count without entering unavailable history,
they return `PrunedError` instead of incomplete results.
- The MDBX boundary includes genesis when block 1 is retained. With a
gap after genesis, genesis remains individually readable, subject to
configured pruning and chain-history expiry, without lowering the
contiguous boundary or allowing ranges across the gap.
- In `eth_capabilities`, `oldestBlock` includes the observed
state-history and block-transaction boundaries;
`deleteStrategy.retentionBlocks`, where present, reports the configured
window. Physical boundaries and configured windows are combined
independently, so missing data does not hide a deletion policy. The
window may be wider than available data. State proofs also account for
commitment history and report the tighter state/commitment retention
policy.
- Local boundaries use pinned database and file views. Local
`MinimumBlockAvailable` requires a pinned block-files view even for
MDBX-only reads and panics without one. History checks return errors for
unsupported views. `HistoryStartFrom` propagates lookup and transport
errors; optional commitment-history lookups run only when needed.
- Gas-price estimation skips unavailable samples and keeps its fallback.
Fee history stops at the first unavailable block; reward requests
starting at a pruned block return an empty result without a pruning
error. Header-only fee history remains available, and backend errors
propagate.

## Limits and performance

The history boundary uses the earliest start across accounts, storage,
and code: a later first change may reflect a sparse domain, not pruning.
This avoids rejecting valid reads but can still admit requests with
missing history in another domain. Remote block boundaries and
txNum-to-block lookups use separate server-side views and remain best
effort.

Log and trace index files can start later than state history. The gates
use the state-history boundary as a proxy instead of checking these
index starts independently, so log queries, `trace_filter`, and
Otterscan searches can still return incomplete results in that case.

Persisted receipt availability still uses the configured receipt-cache
window, not its physical start. Receipt gates and
`eth_capabilities.receipts` can therefore overstate availability after
widening that window or enabling persistence late.

Some readers and range anchors still use latest-state fallback for
missing txNum mappings. They can return incorrect historical results
when both the mapping and its snapshot fallback are unavailable,
including during startup with a stale cached zero frozen range. Exact
historical position resolution is tracked in #25074.

RPC gates resolve the head even under an unbounded policy. They skip
physical lookups at the current head or when the configured cutoff
already rejects the request.

Each shared floor cache holds up to 64 entries with a one-second TTL and
insertion-order eviction, keyed by head, MDBX view and relevant file
generations. Local history keys include both history and block files
because txNum conversion can read body snapshots.

Current remote servers include the pinned history generation and updated
MDBX view ID in stream replies, enabling shared history caching without
extra requests. History lookups and indexed checks retry after remote
view renewal. `eth_capabilities` and pre-Byzantium receipt checks retry
the state and commitment floors together. Views lacking generation
metadata, including older servers, bypass the shared history cache.
Remote block observations remain TTL-cached. The frozen-range cache
loads on demand with a five-second fetch timeout and a 30-second backoff
after failure. Lookups needing a snapshot mapping return an error until
a frozen range has been observed.

Fresh floor-cache hits use `sync.Map.Load` and atomic value reads,
avoiding both cache mutexes. `concurrent.CachedValue` coalesces same-key
refreshes. After a shared failure, waiters retry once on their own
transactions. Waiters can cancel independently; reads run synchronously
within the caller's transaction lifetime. Errors do not extend
floor-cache expiry, and panics do not leave keys blocked. Each gas-price
backend caches its contiguous block boundary; genesis uses its
single-block availability check.

On Apple M2 Max, fresh cache hits measure about 41 ns/op serially and
6–8 ns/op with eight workers using shared or distinct views, with zero
allocations. Parallel figures measure aggregate throughput, not
per-request latency; these are not end-to-end RPC measurements.

## Verification

Behaviour fixes were driven by failing regression tests covering missing
txNum mappings, side-fork MDBX body IDs, unknown remote snapshot bounds
and recovery, real mid-block retirement, ascending scans over
reward-only entries without block data, capability policies, and
zero-start log ranges below the block boundary. A characterization test
confirms that log and trace indices can start later than state history.
The commitment-renewal test fails without the paired retry. Direct
oracle tests cover bypassed block floors and swallowed lookup errors.
Cache tests cover non-blocking warm hits and bounded eviction under
concurrent access. The unknown-range regression checks the specific
error, so unrelated failures cannot satisfy it. Behaviour-preserving
refactors use existing tests; assertion-only and documentation changes
do not change production behaviour.

Passed on `46f148a574`: `make lint`, `make erigon integration`, `make
test-short`, and full `db/snapshotsync/freezeblocks` tests. Full
non-short tests for `rpc/jsonrpc`, `execution/bal`, `db/rawdb`, and
`db/kv/rawdbv3` passed on `412e9365e8`, before the assertion-only
update. Focused race tests passed on `11c8e3e322` for remote snapshot
lookup/cache (10 runs), indexed-history gates, Otterscan searches,
capability policies, log ranges, and genesis.

author: Andrew Ashikhmin
subject: cl/phase1/forkchoice: export GLOAS weights in v1 debug fork choice (#24936)
body:
`/eth/v1/debug/fork_choice` returns no current GLOAS nodes because
`ForkNodes()` still reads the pre-GLOAS `f.weights` map, which
`getHeadGloas` does not fill.

## Design

Under GLOAS, `ForkNodes()` exports the maintained GLOAS weight tree:

- **Refresh first.** `ForkNodes()` calls `GetHeadNode()` before it takes
`f.mu.RLock`. When the head cache is valid this is the cheap read-lock
fast path. When an input changed (vote, block, tick, payload decision,
checkpoint update), it runs the same head computation the next `GetHead`
would run, which prepares the tree. No lock is held during the call, so
the lock order (`f.mu` before the synced-data lock) is kept.
- **Snapshot.** Each node in the prepared justified subtree, including
the justified root, is exported with its aggregate PENDING attestation
score. The proposer score is added to the boost root and its ancestors
when `should_apply_proposer_boost` holds, which is what head selection
uses for PENDING nodes. For siblings with 100 and 90 votes, a boost of
40 makes the second sibling's weight 130. Boost eligibility is checked
once per snapshot, and only when the boost root's ancestry reaches an
exported node. The snapshot never writes the head walk's boost cache.
- **Freshness guard.** The snapshot is empty when the tree has no
checkpoint state, was prepared for a different justified checkpoint, or
was pruned and not prepared again.
- **Prepare on the fallback head.** `computeHeadGloas` now prepares the
tree before it returns the justified root as the fallback head when no
leaf is viable. The returned head does not change. Without this, the
export kept weights from an older preparation during a non-viability
period.

Pre-GLOAS behavior is unchanged: `ForkNodes()` exports `f.weights` and
does not refresh the head.

## Checkpoint-sync anchor

The fork graph has no per-root justified or finalized checkpoints for
the checkpoint-sync anchor, so the anchor was dropped from the export.
When the anchor is the store's justified root, `ForkNodes()` now uses
the store's justified and finalized checkpoints for that node, as
`get_forkchoice_store` initializes them from the anchor. The fork graph
is not changed: `hasCorrectJustification` reads the same per-root
checkpoints for viability filtering, so adding anchor metadata there
would change head filtering. An anchor that is only an ancestor of the
justified root is still skipped, as before.

## Known limits

All are limited to this debug endpoint:

- The refresh and the snapshot use two lock acquisitions. A checkpoint
update or prune between them gives one empty response. A vote or block
between them is missing from that response, and a parent can already
carry the boost of a child that is not yet listed.
- When the justified checkpoint state cannot be loaded, the response is
HTTP 200 with an empty `fork_choice_nodes`, not HTTP 500.
- After an epoch with no blocks, the anchor can report a justified epoch
above its own.

The upstream API deprecates v1 for GLOAS. The v2 endpoint, where the
checkpoints and nodes should come from one snapshot, is tracked in
#24956.

This completes the v1 debug export deferred by #21913. Closes #21704.

## Testing

- `go test -race ./cl/phase1/forkchoice/` covers: the fork boundary
(last pre-GLOAS slot exports `f.weights`, first GLOAS slot exports the
tree), refresh of an unprepared or pruned tree, the pruned tree with a
cached head, proposer boost inside and outside the subtree, the anchor
as justified root and as an ancestor, and the fallback head with no
viable leaf.
- `make lint` and `make erigon integration` pass.
- Two independent review rounds converged with no open in-scope
findings.

author: Andrew Ashikhmin
subject: cl/sentinel: check cancellation before returning responses (#25110)
body:
`httpreqresp.Do` could return a nil error for a cancelled request when
the handler response and context cancellation were both ready. This
caused `TestRequestContextCancelClosesEstablishedStream` to fail in [the
consensus race-test
job](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/actions/runs/39371425311/job/118459972799).

Check the request context again after receiving a response. If it is
cancelled, close the response body and return the context error.

This makes `Do`'s cancellation contract consistent: the service caller
already checks the context after `Do`, and the handshake caller treats
either error shape as a handshake failure during shutdown.

Add a focused `synctest` regression that makes both select cases ready
and checks the context error and body cleanup. It reproduced the
nil-error failure before the production fix and passed afterwards. The
existing libp2p regression remains unchanged.

Validation:

- Both cancellation regressions passed 100 repetitions with `-race`.
- `ERIGON_COMMITMENT_PARALLEL=true go test -race -count=1 -timeout=5m
./cl/sentinel/httpreqresp ./cl/sentinel/handshake ./cl/sentinel/service`
- `make lint`
- `make erigon integration`

author: lystopad
subject: cl/beacon/handler: derive sync committee subscription subnets from the requested indices (#25117)
body:
Fixes #25047.

`POST /eth/v1/validator/sync_committee_subscriptions` decoded
`sync_committee_indices` but never used them. It computed the subnets
from the head state's committee for the validator. A validator client
subscribes before the period in which its validator joins the committee
(see the [Beacon
API](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/#/Validator/prepareSyncCommitteeSubnets)),
so the node got the current committee's subnets or none, and was not on
the right sync subnets when the new period started.

Changes:
- The subnets come from `sync_committee_indices`: `index /
(SYNC_COMMITTEE_SIZE / SYNC_COMMITTEE_SUBNET_COUNT)`, each subnet once.
Lighthouse does the same.
- Every request is validated before any subscription. A missing or
`null` `sync_committee_indices`, or a non-numeric or out-of-range index,
gives 400. An empty list is a valid request with nothing to subscribe.
- The subnets no longer depend on the head state, so the endpoint no
longer returns 503 while the node is syncing. The Beacon API declares
only 200, 400 and 500 for it, and Lighthouse has no syncing check here.
- The subscription still lasts until the start of `until_epoch`.

Tests (red first):
- `TestSyncCommitteeSubscriptionUsesRequestedIndices`: validator 1
requests positions on subnets 1 and 3; the head committee would give it
subnets 0 and 2, which the old handler subscribes.
- `TestSyncCommitteeSubscriptionRejectsInvalidIndices`: out-of-range,
non-numeric and negative indices give 400, and nothing is subscribed.
- `TestSyncCommitteeSubscriptionRequiresIndices`: missing indices give
400; `[]` gives 200.
- `TestSyncCommitteeSubscriptionSucceedsWhileSyncing`: a syncing node
subscribes and returns 200.
- Mutation checks: removing the range check or the de-duplication fails
the tests.

`cl/beacon/handler` tests pass; `make lint` is clean twice; `make erigon
integration` builds.

author: lystopad
subject: cl/beacon/handler: report sync committee messages from validators outside the committee (#25115)
body:
Fixes #25046.

`POST /eth/v1/beacon/pool/sync_committees` computes the subnets of each
message from the validator's positions in the sync committee for the
message slot. For a validator outside the committee the list is empty,
so the message was neither validated nor published, but the handler
still returned 200.

Now such a message is reported as a pooling failure (`validator N is not
in the sync committee for slot S`), so the response is 400 with the
failing index, as the [Beacon
API](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/#/Beacon/submitPoolSyncCommitteeSignatures)
requires. Other messages in the same request are processed as before.

A head state from before Altair has zero-filled sync committees, so such
a head is reported as `head state is before Altair and has no sync
committee` instead.

Tests (red before the fix):
- `TestPoolSyncCommitteesRejectsValidatorOutsideCommittee`: `[member,
outsider, member]` gives 400 with one failure at index 1, and both
member messages are still published.
- `TestPoolSyncCommitteesReportsPreAltairHead`.

`cl/beacon/handler` tests pass; `make lint` is clean twice; `make erigon
integration` builds.

author: awskii
subject: cl/phase1/forkchoice: build the next justified checkpoint state early (#23981)
body:
When the justified checkpoint moves at an epoch's first slot, the next
`GetHead(nil)` misses the checkpoint-state cache and rebuilds it. On
`dev-bm-e3-arb-arb1-n1` (`fb7c9898b96`), `OnBlock` → `clstage finish` at
that slot drops from p50 557.5 ms to 68.0 ms (diff at `84b7833c633`,
before single-flight; other slots 68.0 ms in both).

## Changes
- `OnTick` builds the unrealized justified checkpoint's state once its
epoch passes the justified one, behind the promotion's sync gate
(`nearChainTip`).
- `getCheckpointState` coalesces misses with `singleflight`; a failed
build is not cached.
- `updateCheckpoints` stores finalized before pruning; a build below
finalized is not stored, or is dropped if finalized passes it mid-store.
- Gloas `getHeadGloas` and current-slot `onBlock` return a failed
justified-state build instead of a nil state; an unknown justified root
still yields the anchor.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/phase1/network/registry, cl/phase1/network/services: relay the proposer preferences lookahead window without amplifying state loads (#24776)
body:
Caplin rate-limits the `proposer_preferences` gossip topic per
forwarding peer with a token bucket of burst 4. Validator clients
publish the preferences for several slots at once (we observed bursts of
10 to 13 messages on Sepolia), so the limiter ignores most of a burst
that arrives through one peer.

Ordinary gossip propagation does not recover an ignored preference:
gossipsub marks a message as seen before the topic validator runs, so
copies from other peers are dropped as duplicates, and IHAVE/IWANT does
not request seen IDs. The seen cache keeps the ID for about 6.5 minutes
(`gossipSubSeenTTL` × heartbeat), long after gossip stopped carrying the
message. Preferences published by the node itself are not affected.

The bids that need such a preference are lost with it:
`execution_payload_bid` validation ignores a bid when the node has no
preference for its slot and dependent root, so the node neither keeps
nor forwards it.

## Changes

**Burst sized to the accepted lookahead window.** The per-peer burst is
now `(MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1) * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH` from the beacon config:
64 on mainnet, 32 on Gnosis, 16 on minimal. One peer can relay one
preference per slot for every accepted epoch. The refill rate (2/s) is
unchanged. `RegisterGossipServices` takes the beacon config for this.

**Cheaper validation, so the larger burst does not amplify state
rebuilds.** Before, every preference that passed the header lookup
loaded the dependent block's state (a disk decode plus block replay
under the fork-choice read lock, then an epoch transition) before any
signature check. With burst 64, one peer could make the node do that 64
times at once. Now:

- A dependent root that is not a possible dependent block is ignored
before the state is loaded. The spec ignores it with or without the
state, so the outcome is the same.
- A dependent block after the shuffling dependent slot is rejected
without loading the state. The fork graph stores a header only after the
block's state transition succeeded, so a known header already means the
spec's missing-state IGNORE cannot apply.
- The remaining messages are validated against a small view (epoch,
proposer lookahead, proposer pubkeys, genesis validators root). It is
computed once per dependent root and epoch, shared by concurrent
messages through singleflight, and kept in an 8-entry LRU. Honest
traffic has about 2 such keys.

The IGNORE/REJECT outcome matches `validate_proposer_preferences_gossip`
in the Gloas p2p spec for every input, except one local-failure case: a
known header whose state cannot be read from disk now gets REJECT
instead of IGNORE when its slot is after the dependent slot. Such a
message is invalid anyway.

## Evidence

On a Sepolia node, the limiter ignored about 30% of the published
preferences in a sample. With burst 64, the node had the preferences for
803 of the 813 slots won by a builder bid over the next 4.7 hours.

## Tests

- `TestProposerPreferencesRateLimiterAdmitsLookaheadWindowFromOnePeer`:
mainnet (64), minimal (16) and a lookahead of 2 (96) accept exactly the
window from one peer and ignore the next message.
- `TestProposerPreferencesServiceImpossibleDependentRootSkipsStateLoad`,
`TestProposerPreferencesServiceLateDependentRootRejectedWithoutStateLoad`:
no state load on these paths.
- `TestProposerPreferencesServiceSharesDependentStateAcrossSlots`,
`TestProposerPreferencesServiceSharesDependentStateLoadInFlight`: one
load for preferences that share a dependent root, sequential and
concurrent.
-
`TestProposerPreferencesServiceLateDependentRootRejectedWithoutStateLoad`
replaces
`TestProposerPreferencesServiceMissingStatePrecedesBoundaryReject`,
which pinned the old missing-state IGNORE for that case.

## Not in this PR

- The burst counts proposal slots, but preferences are keyed by (slot,
dependent root). More than one burst-worth from one honest peer needs
several competing dependent roots at once; it is still far better than
burst 4.
- `TestProposerPreferencesServiceSharesDependentStateLoadInFlight` waits
with a short sleep. On a very slow runner it could pass through the
cache instead of the singleflight, but it cannot fail falsely.

author: lystopad
subject: cl/das, cl/phase1/stages: backfill custody columns of forward-synced blocks (#24967)
body:
Part of #24704.

## Problem

Forward sync imports blocks with `checkDataAvailability = false`, so it
never fetches or queues their data columns. The deferred column sync
(`syncColumnDataWorker`) only learns about roots from the data checks on
the gossip and chain-tip import paths. A node that forward-synced
through Fulu or Gloas slots, for example after downtime, therefore kept
a custody gap for those blocks for the whole data-column serve range. It
answered `DataColumnSidecarsByRange`/`ByRoot` for them with a partial
set, which peers score down.

## Change

- When forward sync finishes, or hands off to chain-tip sync after
stalling, it calls `PeerDas.BackfillCustodyColumns(startSlot,
highestProcessed)`. The call returns at once; a request that comes while
another one waits is merged into it.
- A PeerDAS worker runs the backfill:
- It waits until the canonical chain in the beacon indices reaches the
end of the range. Forward sync stores its blocks before the fork choice
stage marks them canonical. After two epochs it stops waiting and walks
what is marked.
- It walks the canonical roots from the newest slot down, clipped to the
data-column serve range, so the most recent blocks are served first.
- It reads each block without its execution payload
(`ReadBeaconBlockBodyBySlot`), and takes the root from the canonical
index.
- It queues a block that commits to blobs and whose columns are not
available for the existing column sync worker, due at once. That worker
already handles download rounds, retries with backoff, giving up
orphans, and the serve-range cutoff.
- Queue entries are light (`backfillColumnBlock`: version, slot, root,
commitments, signature), not whole blocks.
- The backfill waits while the column sync queue holds 32 roots below
the maximum backoff. It neither crowds out the roots gossip queues nor
asks peers for a whole range at once, and roots at the maximum backoff,
which may never complete, do not stall it.
- A root the backfill queued is given up when its backoff reaches an
epoch, so roots peers cannot serve do not pile up. The stale
forward-sync handoff covers blocks up to the highest seen slot.
- A Gloas block is queued only once its envelope was processed: without
a revealed payload no columns exist. Nothing is walked before Fulu, and
the walk stops when its context ends.

Not covered: a restart during a backfill does not resume it. The next
forward sync only covers its own range. Resuming would need a persisted
cursor.

Related: #24787 (`earliest_available_slot` and the stored custody
columns), #24789 (per-peer pacing of by-root requests).

## Tests

- `TestBackfillCustodyColumnsQueuesBlocksMissingColumns`: only blocks in
the range with blob commitments and missing columns are queued, with the
canonical root and due at once.
- `TestBackfillCustodyColumnsQueuesNewestFirstWithinItsBound`: at most
32 roots, newest first.
- Added after review: `...SkipsGloasBlocksWithoutAnEnvelope`,
`...IsNotStalledByRootsAtTheMaximumBackoff`, `...MergesWaitingRequests`
(replaces the drop test), `...StopsWhenCancelled`,
`...DoesNothingBeforeFulu`.
- `TestBackfillCustodyColumnsSkipsSlotsBelowTheServeRange`.
- `TestBackfillCustodyColumnsWaitsForTheCanonicalChain`: the walk starts
only once the canonical chain reaches the range end.
- `TestBackfillCustodyColumnsRequestIsAsynchronous`.
- `TestRequestCustodyBackfillAsksForTheImportedRange` (stages): the
range is requested, and an empty one is not.

Each fails with its rule removed: the serve-range clamp, the bound, the
newest-first walk, the canonical wait, queueing available blocks too,
and the empty-range check in the stage helper.

`go test -race` passes for `cl/das/...`, `cl/phase1/stages/...`,
`cl/phase1/network/...` and `cl/phase1/forkchoice/...`; `make lint` is
clean twice; `make erigon integration` builds.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/beacon/handler: serve fork-epoch PTC duties once the clock reaches the fork (#25087)
body:
## Problem

`POST /eth/v1/validator/duties/ptc/{epoch}` answers 503 ("PTC duties for
fork epoch F are not available until the head reaches the Gloas fork")
for the Gloas fork epoch while the head is still the last Fulu block. It
does so even after the wall clock has entered the fork epoch.

The Lighthouse VC starts asking for PTC duties only once its clock
reaches the Gloas fork epoch, and after a failed request it waits until
the next slot. On a local Gloas shadow fork, its request for the
fork-epoch duties got this 503. The VC logged the failure 4 ms into the
first Gloas slot, before Caplin had imported that slot's block, and it
missed every PTC duty of that slot. PTC participation in that slot was
64%. The Teku VC on the other Caplin node fetches one epoch ahead and
retries every second, so it got its duties in time.

The 503 was added on purpose in #24393. Computing the fork epoch's PTC
directly from the Fulu state is only a prediction: `upgrade_to_gloas`
computes it after the last Fulu epoch processing, which can change
effective balances, and the PTC is drawn by effective balance.

## Fix

The handler already copies the head state and processes slots on the
copy when the head lags the clock by one epoch. It now does the same for
a pre-Gloas head once the clock has reached the requested epoch, which
can only be the fork epoch with the head in the epoch before it. The
copy is processed to the first slot of the fork epoch, which runs the
last Fulu epoch processing and `upgrade_to_gloas`, and the duties are
read from its PTC window. Lighthouse serves this request the same way.

Unchanged:

- While the clock is still in the epoch before the fork, the answer is
still 503.
- The dependent root is still the one the Beacon API defines, the block
root at the last slot of epoch F-2. At the fork epoch this root does not
cover the blocks of epoch F-1, which feed the PTC. Lighthouse returns
the root at the last slot of epoch F-1 for the fork epoch instead. I did
not copy that here, because it differs from the API definition.
- The head state is not modified, and a Gloas head still reads its PTC
window directly.
- A head two epochs before the fork still gets 503: the existing lag
path advances it only to epoch F-1, which is still Fulu.

As on the existing lag path, concurrent requests each copy and process
the state; there is no cache.

## Tests

- `TestPostPtcDutiesForkEpochUsesAdvancedFuluState`: a real Fulu head at
the last slot before the fork (minimal preset, 64 validators) with the
clock in the fork epoch. The fixture zeroes the balances of most
validators that a direct Fulu prediction puts in the PTC, so the last
Fulu epoch processing lowers their effective balances, and it asserts
that the direct prediction differs from the PTC of a state advanced into
the fork. The response must be 200, with the duties of the advanced
state and the API dependent root. On `main`: 503.
- `TestPostPtcDutiesForkEpochUnavailableBeforeClockReachesFork`: the
same head with the clock one epoch before the fork must still get 503.
It replaces `TestPostPtcDutiesForkEpochUnavailableBeforeGloasHead`,
which did not fix the clock. It passes on `main` and pins the clock
condition of the fix.
- `TestPostPtcDutiesForkEpochDoesNotMutatePublishedHead`: after a
successful request, the published head is still the same Fulu state
(version, slot, root and state root). On `main`: 503.

Mutation check: without the clock condition, the second test fails;
without the new branch, the first and third fail.

`go test ./cl/beacon/handler/...` passes, and the new tests pass with
`-race -count=5`.

## Release branches

`release/3.8` has the same handler, so the change applies there.
`release/3.7` lacks the copy-and-advance path for the PTC duties
handler, so a backport would need that first.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/phase1/core/caches, cl/phase1/core/state, cl/phase1/stages, cl/transition: share lookahead shuffles and active sets across state copies (#25143)
body:
Part of #25120 (item 1).

## Problem

During epoch processing at the E → E+1 boundary, `ProcessPtcWindow`
(Gloas) and the proposer lookahead (Fulu and later) need the active set
and the attester shuffle of epoch E+2. The global caches
(`ShuffledIndiciesCacheGlobal`, `ActiveValidatorsCacheGlobal`) are keyed
by `(epoch, decision block root)`, where the decision root is the block
root at slot `(E+1)*SLOTS_PER_EPOCH-1`. During epoch processing that
slot is the state's own slot, and `GetBlockRootAtSlot` rejects `slot >=
state.slot`. So the lookup never hits, the result is never stored, and
every fresh state that crosses the boundary scans the registry and
reshuffles the full validator set again: block import (under the
fork-choice write lock), gossip validation, replays, payload
preparation.

`ProcessPtcWindow` on a fresh copy with 500k validators took ~110-137 ms
locally; at Hoodi/mainnet scale on our test node this is several hundred
ms per state per epoch.

## What changed

- When the decision slot equals `state.slot` and the slot transition has
already run for that slot (the latest header's state root is set and
`block_roots[slot]` equals the header root), the main caches use that
block root as the decision root. `transitionSlot` writes exactly this
value before `ProcessEpoch`, so it is the root the spec would return one
slot later. If the slot transition has not run yet (a block at the
current slot was just processed), the lookup misses as before and
nothing is stored.
- Values computed in this case go into two small lookahead caches (4
entries each, separate metric names) keyed by `(epoch,
state_roots[slot])`. The state root identifies the registry and RANDAO,
so states that share a header but differ in their registry cannot share
an entry, and replays of old states cannot evict the fork-choice
precache entries in the main caches. Lookahead active-set entries carry
no total active balance.
- The fork-choice precache promotes a lookahead shuffle into the main
cache instead of computing it again.
- `ComputeCommittee` returns a capped slice (`[start:end:end]`), so
callers cannot append into the shared array.

Why the key is safe: with the mainnet configuration (`MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD
= 1`), the active set and the seed of epoch E+2 are fixed by the chain
up to the decision block. Activation and exit epochs are always at least
`current epoch + 1 + MAX_SEED_LOOKAHEAD` ahead, execution requests are
applied in the child block, and the Gloas envelope does not change the
registry or the header. The total active balance is not covered by this
argument (it also depends on effective balances updated at the end of
the previous epoch), which is why lookahead entries never carry it. The
existing main-cache total active balance has a separate problem, tracked
in #25138; this PR does not change it.

## Testing

TDD. These tests fail on the base for the intended reason and pass with
the change:
- a second fresh copy crossing the same boundary reuses the E+2 shuffle
(`Same` assertion) instead of recomputing it;
- `ProcessSlots` across a boundary stores the result in the lookahead
cache;
- two states that share a header but have different registries get
different results (registry collision, 16383 vs 16384 active
validators).

Differential tests check that the PTC window and the proposer lookahead
are identical with and without the caches for: branches with different
registries, the Fulu → Gloas upgrade epoch, a latest header whose state
root is not set yet, empty slots vs slots with a block, replay of old
states (no eviction of precache entries), and concurrent first lookups
under `-race`.

Commands:
- `go test -race` on `cl/phase1/core/state/...`,
`cl/phase1/core/caches/...`, `cl/transition/...` passes, also after the
squash.
- `go test ./cl/phase1/... ./cl/beacon/... ./cl/persistence/...` passes.
- `go build ./...`, `make lint` (clean on repeated runs) and `make
erigon integration` pass.
- Mainnet spec tests (twice): the failing set is identical to the base.
The local fixtures are older than the pinned ones, so the Gloas spec
tests are left to CI.

`ProcessPtcWindow` on a fresh copy, 500k validators, Apple M3 Pro:
~110-137 ms/op before, ~14-25 ms/op after.

## Not included

- Concurrent cold misses for the same key are not merged (both compute);
this existed before.
- The precache does not promote the lookahead active set, so the head
state still scans the registry once per epoch for it.
- The 4-entry lookahead caches can be evicted while the antiquary
catches up; that only costs a recomputation.
- The Gloas upgrade boundary itself is not shared between copies.

## Backport

Not planned for release/3.8. This is a performance improvement for epoch
processing; it does not fix a correctness problem.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/phase1/forkchoice, cl/transition/impl/eth2: verify the Gloas envelope builder signature once (#25134)
body:
Part of #25120 (item 2, the two quick parts).

## Problem

When a Gloas execution payload envelope is applied on the validated
fork-choice path, two pieces of work run twice or for nothing while the
fork-choice write lock is held:

- The builder signature is BLS-verified twice: once by
`validateEnvelopeAgainstBlock` and again by the transition
(`ValidatingMachine`, full validation), on the same state and envelope.
- `ProcessExecutionPayloadEnvelope` builds a full `PayloadHeader`, which
hashes the transaction list, withdrawals and the block access list, only
to read five scalar fields.

## What changed

- `applyEnvelopeCoordinated` uses `DefaultMachine` when
`validatePayload` is true, because that branch has already verified the
signature on the same state and envelope without yielding the lock. With
`validatePayload` false the transition still verifies it
(`ValidatingMachine`).
- `ValidateExecutionPayloadEnvelopeForConsensus` uses `DefaultMachine`
after `validateEnvelopeAgainstBlock`.
- `ProcessExecutionPayloadEnvelope` reads `prev_randao`, `gas_limit`,
`block_hash`, `parent_hash` and `timestamp` from the payload directly.
Error messages are unchanged; the other `PayloadHeader` callers are
untouched.
- `ProcessExecutionPayloadEnvelope` rejects a payload with nil
transactions, like nil withdrawals and execution requests.
`PayloadHeader` used to dereference the list; ingress validation
(`ValidateForConfig`) already rejects nil transactions, so no valid
envelope changes outcome.
- `verifyEnvelopeBuilderSignature` calls a package-level `blsVerify` so
tests can count verifications.

Every path still verifies the signature at least once:

| Path | Verification |
|---|---|
| Fork choice, `validatePayload` true (gossip, API publish, pending
retry, sync with EL validation) | once, in fork choice |
| Fork choice, `validatePayload` false (forward / chain-tip sync) |
once, in the transition |
| `ValidateExecutionPayloadEnvelopeForConsensus` | once, in
`validateEnvelopeAgainstBlock` |
| Operations spec tests | once, in the transition |
| Local self-build | none, as before (no production caller) |

The post-state root is unchanged.

## Testing

TDD for the behaviour changes. These tests fail on the base production
code and pass with the change:
- the validated path and the consensus validation path each verify the
signature exactly once (a stubbed fork-choice verifier plus a signature
from another key, which any second verification would reject);
- the transition no longer builds the payload header;
- the transition rejects nil transactions with both machines.

Further tests: invalid signatures are rejected with `validatePayload`
true and false, by the consensus validation path and by
`ValidatingMachine`; self-build uses the proposer key.

The scalar-check table and the state-root checks pass both before and
after the change. They are characterization tests for the refactor part
(reading five fields instead of building the header), so that part does
not follow red/green.

`BenchmarkApplyEnvelopeValidatedPath` (Apple M3 Pro, interleaved runs),
per envelope:
- 300 txs / 100 KB BAL: 2.99 ms → 1.36 ms
- 1500 txs / 400 KB BAL: 9.09 ms → 3.66 ms

Commands:
- `go test ./cl/phase1/... ./cl/transition/... ./cl/beacon/...
./cl/persistence/... -count=1` passes.
- `go test -race` passes on `cl/phase1/forkchoice` and
`cl/transition/impl/eth2`.
- `go build ./...`, `make lint` (clean on repeated runs) and `make
erigon integration` pass.
- Gloas spec tests: the local fixtures are older than the pinned ones,
and the set of failing cases is identical to the base (envelope cases
fail to decode on both). CI runs the pinned fixtures.

## Not included

- Caching the Gloas payload hash and the transaction / BAL progressive
roots.
- Moving `DumpEnvelopeOnDisk` out of the fork-choice lock.
- The REST publish path and the gossip "indices pending" branch still
verify the signature once more on the caller side; that code is not
changed here.

## Backport

Not planned for release/3.8. This is a performance improvement for Gloas
envelope processing. It does not fix a correctness problem.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/cltypes/solid, cl/merkle_tree: build the validator Merkle tree in parallel on cold rebuilds (#25101)
body:
Part of #25120.

## Problem

A beacon state decoded from disk has no validator Merkle cache. Its
first `HashSSZ` (or `NextSyncCommitteeBranch`, or the first
`transitionSlot` after an empty slot) rebuilds the whole validator tree
on one goroutine. On a Hoodi node (Xeon E-2288G, 8 cores / 16 threads,
about 1.14M validators) this takes 3.45 s of the 3.52 s cold state hash,
and the time is the same with 1, 4, 8 or 16 threads. Several of these
paths run under the fork-choice lock. The same happens after the Fulu to
Gloas upgrade, because `SetProgressiveHashing` drops the tree: the first
Gloas hash took 3.56 s.

## What changed

- `cl/cltypes/solid`: on a cold build (`MerkleTree == nil` in `HashSSZ`,
`progressiveTrees == nil` in `HashSSZProgressive`) of at least 4,000
validators, the validator leaf roots are computed in parallel into a
temporary buffer, and the tree (or every progressive segment tree) is
built from that buffer. After the build, the normal per-validator leaf
function is installed again, so warm updates work exactly as before, and
the buffer is released. Both paths publish the cache (`v.MerkleTree`,
`v.progressiveTrees`) only when it is fully built. Before this, the
Gloas path published an empty slice and appended the segment trees one
by one, so a concurrent copy (`BeaconState.CopyInto` takes no state
lock) could take only the first segments and keep a permanently wrong
root; the leaf functions were also rebound afterwards without a lock.
- Leaf hashing in workers calls gohashtree directly (no global hasher
mutex) and each worker has its own scratch array. A test checks it
against `CopyHashBufferTo` + `MerkleRootFromFlatLeaves` on random
validators.
- Workers per build: at most 8 and at most `GOMAXPROCS/2` (at least 1).
On the node, 8 workers were as fast as 16 in wall time with about 40%
less CPU; hyperthreads add CPU, not speed.
- A process-wide budget is shared by all cold builds: an atomic count of
live helpers, limited to `GOMAXPROCS` in total. Each build still takes
at most its own cap minus one, so two overlapping builds both run with
full parallelism on a 16-thread node (7 + 7 helpers), and a third one
gets what is left. The calling goroutine always works; it takes helpers
only with a non-blocking try-acquire and holds them for the whole build
(leaf roots and tree layers). A build that gets no helper runs the old
serial code in its own goroutine. It never waits, so it cannot deadlock
under a caller lock.
- The limit counts helpers, not the calling goroutines, so with three or
more overlapping cold builds the number of hashing goroutines can go a
little above `GOMAXPROCS`, and each build allocates its own leaf-root
buffer (32 bytes per validator). Overlapping cold builds are rare; two
at once was the case seen on the node.
- `cl/merkle_tree`: new `BuildFromLeafRoots(leafRoots, leavesCount,
maxDepth, limit, workers, computeLeaf)`. It builds a new tree from a
precomputed leaf-root buffer in parallel and returns the finished tree
with the caller's normal leaf function installed. There is no exported
way to run the parallel code on an existing (warm) tree. `ComputeRoot`
and all other users are unchanged. Only layers with at least 4,096 nodes
are split across workers; narrower layers stay serial. This was needed
because with only the leaves parallel, the serial upper layers were
43–50% of the cold wall time.
- Warm hashing stays serial. The prototype parallelized any layer wider
than 8,192 nodes, and a warm change of 100 validators then cost 22.7 ms
CPU instead of 8.5 ms. Here only cold builds fan out.

### Thresholds

- `parallelMinValidators = 4000`: smallest cold build size where
parallel was consistently faster (Apple M3 Pro, 3 samples): 1k serial
0.83–1.24 ms vs parallel 0.36–1.04 ms (overlap); 4k 1.73–2.10 ms vs
0.57–0.85 ms; 16k 6.5–7.3 ms vs 1.6–2.7 ms; 64k 25.6–26.0 ms vs 6.8–7.1
ms.
- `parallelLayerMinNodes = 4096`: smallest layer width where 6 workers
were consistently faster: 2,048 nodes 210–225 µs vs 132–239 µs
(inconsistent); 4,096 327–340 µs vs 233–293 µs; 8,192 687–784 µs vs
446–462 µs; 16,384 1.30 ms vs 0.85–0.90 ms.
- No parallel path for "many dirty validators": warm `HashSSZ` on 1M
validators costs 2.5 ms (1 dirty), 2.5 ms (100), 2.9 ms (1,000) and 7.0
ms (10,000) serially, so there is little to gain.

## Benchmarks

Node (Hoodi, prototype with the same approach), cold hash: serial 3.89 s
CPU; 4 / 8 / 16 workers = 0.97 / 0.53 / 0.49 s wall, 3.77 / 4.07 / 6.64
s CPU. First Gloas hash 0.47 s instead of 3.56 s. Roots identical.

Local (Apple M3 Pro, 12 cores, so 6 workers; other jobs were running,
numbers are noisy), `validator_set_bench_test.go`, 1M validators,
`-benchtime=3x -count=3`:

| Benchmark | serial | parallel |
|---|---|---|
| Cold `HashSSZ` (Fulu) | 395–457 ms (some samples up to 1.3 s under
load) | 66–96 ms (one outlier at 133 ms) |
| Cold `HashSSZProgressive` (Gloas) | 397–431 ms | 69–127 ms (one
outlier at 218 ms) |

The parallel cold build allocates about 32 MB more per build (the
temporary leaf-root buffer, 32 bytes per validator).

## Tests

TDD: the new tests were written first (they did not compile on main
because the hooks and the parallel tree builder did not exist; the
fan-out test then failed with zero helpers).

- `TestValidatorRootMatchesSerialReference`: parallel leaf hasher equals
the existing serial one.
- `TestValidatorSetRootsMatchSerialReferences`: Fulu and Gloas roots
against an independent serial reference for lengths 0–7, progressive
segment boundaries and neighbours (20–22, 83–86, 340–342, 1364–1366) and
21,845 / 21,846 random validators (parallel tree layers); cold, warm
no-op, one dirty, many dirty, copy then mutate (original unchanged).
- `TestValidatorSetProgressiveAppendAcrossSegmentBoundary`,
`TestValidatorSetParallelColdHashThenAppend` (parallel cold build, with
the cold root checked, then append across the segment boundaries at
5,461 and 21,845 and into the partly filled segment at 50,003, Fulu and
Gloas), `TestValidatorSetDecodedColdRootsAndCacheModeSwitches` (decode,
then Fulu → Gloas → Fulu).
- The root-equality tests use a fixed 4-worker pool and check that
helpers were used, so they run the parallel path on every host, also
when `GOMAXPROCS` is below 4.
- `TestValidatorSetParallelFanOutIsColdAndSizeBounded`,
`TestValidatorSetProgressiveParallelFanOutIsColdOnly`: a large cold
build takes helpers; a set below the threshold and warm hashes with 1
and 100 dirty validators take none.
- `TestValidatorSetParallelWorkerBudget`: with a cap of 3, while one
build holds both helper slots, six other cold builds finish without
waiting and the live helper count never goes above 2.
- `TestValidatorSetParallelColdHashCopy`: a `CopyTo` made while another
goroutine is in the middle of a cold parallel build gets a correct,
usable tree. `HashSSZ` now publishes the new tree only after it is
built, so a copy or hash during the build never sees an empty tree.
- `TestValidatorRootWorkerPoolHonorsRuntimeBudgetAcrossBuilds`: with a
static maximum of 8, a runtime per-build cap of 4 and a total cap of 5,
three builds get 3, 2 and 0 helpers.
- `TestValidatorRootWorkerPoolLetsOverlappingBuildsRunInParallel`: with
`GOMAXPROCS` 16, three overlapping builds get 7, 7 and 2 helpers. Before
the second commit they got 7, 0 and 0: on the Hoodi test node a second
cold build that overlapped another one ran serially and held the
fork-choice read lock for 3.7 s.
- `TestValidatorSetProgressiveParallelColdHashCopy`: the same for Gloas;
a copy taken after the first segment tree is built gets a correct root.
It fails when the trees are published segment by segment, as before.
- `TestValidatorRootWorkerPoolTracksGOMAXPROCS`,
`TestBuildFromLeafRootsMatchesComputeRoot` (against `ComputeRoot` and
`MerkleizeVector`, and a warm update after the build).

Mutation checks: removing the size threshold makes the fan-out test fail
(2 helpers on a small set); removing the process-wide limit makes both
budget tests fail (12 live helpers instead of 2, and 9 instead of 5); a
wrong segment offset in the parallel Gloas build makes the
root-equality, append and decode tests fail.

Commands run:
- `go test -race ./cl/cltypes/solid/ ./cl/merkle_tree/ -count=1`
- `go test ./cl/phase1/core/state/... ./cl/transition/... -count=1`
- `go test ./cl/spectest/... -run 'SSZ|ssz|Gloas|gloas' -count=1`
- `go build ./...`, `make lint`

## Not included

- Persisting the Merkle caches to disk.
- Caching for Gloas balances and inactivity scores.
- Any change to fork-graph, locks or state loading.
- Parallel warm hashing for many dirty validators (see the numbers
above).

## Backport

Not planned for release/3.8 for now. This is a performance improvement,
not a correctness fix, and it changes how the consensus layer computes
state roots. It should run on main and in an A/B test on a Hoodi node
first. If the cold-hash stalls turn out to hurt release/3.8 users, we
can reconsider it for a 3.8.x release.

author: Shadow
subject: cl/beacon/handler: don't let a stalled /eth/v1/events client block the event emitters (#24447)
body:
