`ErrMissingGloasData`.

## Tests

- `TestReadRequiredQueueSSZ_MissedForkSlotBlock`: aligned fork slot with
a missed block. There is no dump, and the full diff is at the next slot.
- `TestReadRequiredQueueSSZ_MissingDumpAtForkSlotWithBlock`: the dump at
an aligned fork slot is missing and the full diff is at the fork slot.
- `TestReadRequiredQueueSSZ_MissingDump`: adds a dump slot right after
an unaligned fork, which still returns an error.
- `TestReadHistoricalState_GloasQueuesBeforeFirstDump`: end-to-end read
with fork epoch 49, which is not a multiple of 48. The fork slot is 1568
and the pre-fork dump slot is 1536.
- `TestReadHistoricalState_GloasQueuesMissingDumpAfterFork`: end-to-end
reverse case. The dump slot is after the fork and the dumps are missing,
so the read returns `ErrMissingGloasData`.

**TDD:** each new test was written first and failed on the previous code
for the intended reason:
- `MissedForkSlotBlock`, `MissingDumpAtForkSlotWithBlock` and
`GloasQueuesBeforeFirstDump` failed with `ErrMissingGloasData` on the
origin/main reader.
- `MissingDumpAtForkSlotWithBlock` returned `[b]` instead of `[a, b]`
before the replay-start fix.
- The added `MissingDump` case expects an error, so it also passes on
origin/main. It guards the relaxed check against admitting a dump slot
after the fork.
- The two `ReadHistoricalState` tests fail under the mutations
`gloasForkSlot := r.cfg.GloasForkEpoch` and `gloasForkSlot :=
^uint64(0)`. Both mutations passed the suite before these tests existed.

## Validation

- `go test ./cl/persistence/state/historical_states_reader/
./cl/antiquary/ -count=1`
- `make lint`, two runs, 0 issues
- `make erigon integration`

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Builders queue encoder: in-place updates are lost, and a duplicate
trailing entry breaks the truncate count (#25205).
- If every slot from the fork slot through the next dump slot is missed,
there is no Gloas dump there and reads still return
`ErrMissingGloasData` until the following dump. This needs 33+ missed
slots; on Sepolia it needs 513.
- `GloasForkEpoch * SlotsPerEpoch` overflows for a far-future fork
epoch. It is reachable only when the reader's config differs from the
config that wrote the DB, for example in capcli.
- There is no writer-to-reader test across the Gloas fork.
- The empty-base path cannot tell a lost first full diff from a missed
slot. This happens only with lost rows, not with data the antiquary
writes.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/cltypes/solid: cache progressive list roots across state copies (#25216)
body:
Part of #25120 (item 5).

## What and why

Gloas hashes six state lists with `ListSSZ.HashSSZProgressive(nil)`:
pending deposits, pending partial withdrawals, pending consolidations,
builders, builder pending withdrawals and payload expected withdrawals.
`HashSSZProgressive` had no cache, and raw `CopyInto` marks every
top-level leaf dirty, so the first hash after each state copy recomputed
all six lists. With about 7.6k pending deposits, that is about 4.6 ms
per hash after a copy, while Fulu uses the cached legacy root. Gloas
copies the state several times per slot.

`ListSSZ.HashSSZ()` cannot be used instead: its cached root is the
pre-Gloas list root.

## Changes

All production changes are in `cl/cltypes/solid/list_ssz.go`.

- `ListSSZ` gets a progressive-root cache, separate from the legacy
`root`. It is filled with `CompareAndSwap(nil, ...)` after a
`HashSSZProgressive(nil)` call. A call with a custom element hasher
never reads or writes it.
- Every mutator (`Set`, `Append`, `Clear`, `Truncate`, `Cut`, SSZ
decode, `UnmarshalJSON`) clears both caches through one
`invalidateRoots` helper. A list reuses its cache holder, so a mutation
does not allocate after the first one.
- The cache holder records its owner, and only the owner uses it. A Go
value copy of a `ListSSZ` (for example inside `ExecutionPayloadBid`)
therefore never reads a root that belongs to another list.
- `ShallowCopy` always gives the copy its own holder and carries the
source's progressive root into it, filled or not. A copy of an unchanged
list hashes for free, a copy of a list that was not hashed yet caches
its root on its first hash, and a later mutation on either side
invalidates only that side.
- `raw/hashing.go`, `raw/copy.go` and the state setters are unchanged.

## Contract

The cache relies on the same rule as the existing legacy root: list
contents change only through `ListSSZ` methods or by replacing the whole
list. I audited every writer of the six lists. All of them use `ListSSZ`
methods or set a new or `ShallowCopy`'d list, and no production code
writes fields of an element obtained through `Get` or `Range`. Writing
through a Go value copy (`cpy := *list; cpy.Set(...)`) shares the
backing array and leaves the original's caches stale, as it already did
for the legacy root. No production code does that.

## Benchmark

Apple M-series, 6 runs each, `origin/main` vs this PR:

| Benchmark | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `BenchmarkHashSSZAfterCopyInto/gloas` (7.6k pending deposits) | ~4.6
ms, 2.83 MB, 39,746 allocs | ~375 µs, 280 KB, 1,442 allocs |
| `BenchmarkHashSSZAfterCopyInto/fulu` | ~310 µs, 265 KB, 1,187 allocs |
~292 µs, 265 KB, 1,190 allocs |
| `BenchmarkListSSZAppend` (7,600 appends) | ~21.5 µs, 17 allocs | ~25.9
µs, 19 allocs |

The append loop is about 4 µs slower per 7,600 appends, from the cache
check on each mutation. Fulu `CopyInto` has 3 more allocations, from the
holders of the copied lists.

## Tests

- `cl/cltypes/solid/list_ssz_progressive_root_test.go`: memoization;
invalidation by each mutator; `ShallowCopy` with a cold and a warm root,
mutated on the source and on the copy; a cold copy and a copy of it
cache their root after the first hash
(`TestListSSZColdShallowCopyCachesProgressiveRoot`); Go value copies;
the legacy and progressive caches stay separate in both call orders;
custom element hashers; concurrent first hashes; `Clone`; steady-state
`Append` allocations.
- `cl/phase1/core/state/raw/hashing_copy_gloas_test.go`: for each of the
six lists, mutated on the source and on the copy, the state root matches
a freshly decoded state.
- `TestUpgradeToGloasStateRootMatchesDecodedState` (`upgrade_test.go`)
now has non-empty queues before the Fulu hash, so warm legacy roots
cannot leak into the Gloas root.
- Gloas spectests with the beta.4 fixtures: the same PASS/SKIP set as
`main` (operations, epoch_processing, sanity, transition, fork,
ssz_static). `go test -race ./cl/cltypes/solid/
./cl/phase1/core/state/...` passes.

Each invalidation and copy path was checked by removing it and
confirming that a test fails.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/antiquary, cl/persistence, db: store the Gloas PTC window once per epoch (#25201)
body:
Part of #25120 (item 7).

## What and why

The Caplin archive stored the Gloas `ptc_window` (96 slots × 512
validator indices, 393,216 bytes raw) in `PtcWindowTable` for every
slot. The window changes only at epoch boundaries
(`process_ptc_window`), so 31 of every 32 rows were copies. On mainnet
this would cost about 0.74–1.2 GB per day.

This PR stores the window once per epoch in a new table and Caplin state
snapshot type, `PtcWindowEpoch`. The estimate is about 23 MB per day at
Sepolia size and about 37 MB per day at mainnet size, roughly 32× less.

A new type is used instead of changing the meaning of the existing
`PtcWindow` rows: old binaries would misread sparse rows in the old
type, and a minor file-version bump does not stop them, because Caplin
state snapshots accept minor bumps as content-only.

## Changes

- New `kv.PtcWindowEpochTable` and snapshot type `PtcWindowEpoch`
(`MinCaplinEnum+35`). The key is the epoch-start slot. The value is the
zstd-compressed SSZ of the exact window.
- The antiquary writes one row per Gloas epoch:
- in `addGenesisState`, which covers a fork at genesis and the anchor
state;
- at each Gloas epoch boundary, which also covers epochs without blocks;
- at the fork. If the first Gloas block is after the fork slot, the
state is advanced to the fork slot first.
- `ReadHistoricalState` reads the row at `RoundSlotToEpoch(slot)`. A
missing row returns `ErrMissingGloasData`. A row that does not decode,
or has the wrong SSZ length, is a hard error.
- `PtcWindowTable` is no longer written or read. Its table, snapshot
type and existing data stay, so old binaries keep working.
- Startup: if states were already processed past the fork but the
fork-epoch row is missing (in the DB and in snapshots), the antiquary
re-processes from the last pre-Gloas epoch start that has a block.
- Snapshot dump: a range with an empty epoch-start row at or after the
fork is not dumped yet, and is retried later.
- Availability: `IndicesMax` treats `PtcWindowEpoch` as covered up to
the Gloas fork slot (`GloasForkEpoch × SlotsPerEpoch`, saturated),
because its files are empty by definition before the fork. Without a
beacon config the strict rule stays.
- `seg publishable` requires `PtcWindowEpoch` files ending at the common
end of the other state types only when that end is past the fork slot;
otherwise present files get only the structural checks. If the beacon
config cannot be resolved, the files are always required. For a known
chain, it also checks that every epoch-start word at or after the fork
is non-empty and that each file has the expected word count. `seg
integrity --check=Publishable` runs the same check.
- A no-op migration, `create_ptc_window_epoch_table`, creates the new
table in existing databases, so tools that open chaindata in accede mode
do not fail. `DBSchemaVersion` is unchanged.

## Rollout

`PtcWindowEpoch` limits state-snapshot availability only at and after
the Gloas fork slot.

- Chains before the fork (mainnet and Gnosis, where it is not scheduled,
and Hoodi until 2026-10-26): Caplin state snapshots work as before,
without any `PtcWindowEpoch` files. Nodes that dump state snapshots
write the all-empty pre-fork files themselves, so publishing them is
optional.
- Chains past the fork (Sepolia today, Hoodi after its fork): until
`PtcWindowEpoch` files are published, state-snapshot availability ends
at the last pre-fork slot, and the antiquary processes the rest locally
from just before the fork. To keep full availability, publish the new
files before releasing:
1. Run the snapshot generator with this binary. It re-processes from the
fork and produces the post-fork range.
2. Publish the new files in the preverified lists. Keep the old
`PtcWindow` files, because older releases still need them.
  3. Then release the binary.

Effects:
- Existing archive nodes continue from their DB progress. A Sepolia node
that is past the fork re-processes from just before the fork once.
- Older binaries ignore the new type. On Sepolia, their state snapshots
end at the last `PtcWindow` file, and they antiquate the rest locally.
- Existing `PtcWindowTable` rows on upgraded nodes are not deleted (on
Sepolia, about 10 GB since the fork, estimated, not measured).
- Downgrading after running this binary leaves slots without old rows;
the old binary then re-antiquates them through its normal backoff.

## Tests

- `TestPtcWindowStoredOncePerEpoch`
(`cl/antiquary/ptc_window_epoch_test.go`) checks the exact row for every
epoch over six Gloas spec fixtures: a block exactly at the fork, a first
block later in the fork epoch, the only block in the epoch after the
fork, a fork at genesis, an anchor followed by two epochs without
blocks, and a 64-block chain. It also checks that `PtcWindowTable` stays
empty. The expected rows come from replaying the fixture blocks through
the state transition and taking the window of each Gloas state,
independently of the antiquary code.
- `TestPtcWindowEpochSnapshotRead`: the row is read from a snapshot
segment.
- `TestPtcWindowEpochRestart`: a restart in the middle of an epoch.
- `TestPtcWindowEpochUpgradeReplay`,
`TestPtcWindowEpochUpgradeReplayStartsBeforeFork`,
`TestPtcWindowEpochReconstructionStart`: upgrade from a DB without new
rows, for a fork at genesis and a later fork.
- Missing and corrupt rows: `gloas_roundtrip_test.go`.
- Dump guard: `db/snapshotsync/caplin_state_ptc_window_epoch_test.go`.
- Fork-aware availability:
`TestCaplinStateBlocksAvailableBeforeUnscheduledGloasFork`,
`TestCaplinStateBlocksAvailableAtGloasFork`,
`TestCaplinStateBlocksAvailableRequiresPtcWindowEpochFromGenesis`
(`db/snapshotsync/caplin_state_lifecycle_test.go`).
- Publishability and content check:
`cmd/utils/app/publishable_check_test.go` (including the fork-aware
cases before an unscheduled or future fork, after the fork, and at the
fork boundary), `db/integrity/caplin_state_integrity_test.go`.
- `TestGloasHistoricalStateRoots` (`empty_epoch_transition`) checks the
full state root across an epoch boundary. Multi-block and later-fork
fixtures cannot be used for a full-root check yet because of #25199 and
#25200, which exist on `main` already. In those fixtures, a
field-by-field diff shows that the PTC window matches.

The Gloas spec fixtures under `cl/antiquary/tests/test_data/gloas/` add
3.8 MB.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/beacon/handler: format node identity metadata as the Beacon API spec requires (#25179)
body:
## Problem

`GET /eth/v1/node/identity` returned `metadata` in a shape that does not
match the Beacon API spec:

```json
"metadata": {"seq": "6", "attnets": "0000000000030000", "syncnets": "0f"}
```

The spec `MetaData` type ([beacon-APIs v4.0.0
`types/p2p.yaml`](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/blob/v4.0.0/types/p2p.yaml))
defines:

- `seq_number` (a `Uint64` string, required), not `seq`;
- `attnets` (required) and `syncnets` (from Altair) as `Bitvector`,
which is 0x-prefixed hex (`^0x[a-fA-F0-9]{2,}$`);
- `custody_group_count` (a `Uint64` string), present from the Fulu fork.

Strict Beacon API consumers can reject this response. For example, the
Dora DAS Guardian (`services/dasguardian.go` in ethpandaops/dora) passes
`attnets` and `syncnets` to `hexutil.Decode`, which rejects values
without the `0x` prefix, so its node identity lookup fails against a
Caplin node. Dora also expects the sequence number under `seq_number`
(Erigon returned it under `seq`) and reads `custody_group_count`, which
Erigon did not return.

## Fix

In `GetEthV1NodeIdentity`:

- rename `seq` to `seq_number`;
- add the `0x` prefix to the hex values from the sentinel `Identity`
RPC. The in-repository sentinel formats the fixed-size `[8]byte` /
`[1]byte` bitvectors with `%x`, so it returns non-empty, unprefixed
values;
- from Fulu (`currentEpoch >= FuluForkEpoch`, the same gate as the
`metadata/3` req/resp handler), add `custody_group_count` from
`peerDas.StateReader().GetAdvertisedCgc()`.

The sentinel RPC response does not change; only the Beacon API response
changes. In this repository the handler is the only caller of the
sentinel `Identity` RPC.

An alternative is to encode with `hexutil.Encode` in
`cl/sentinel/service/service.go` and to add a custody group count field
to the `sentinelproto.Metadata` message. That needs a proto change and
`make grpc`, so this PR keeps the change in the handler.

## Tests

New tests in `cl/beacon/handler/node_identity_test.go`. Both fail on the
old handler:

- at the Fulu fork epoch and one epoch after, `metadata` contains
exactly `seq_number`, `attnets`, `syncnets` and `custody_group_count`,
with 0x-prefixed bitvectors;
- one epoch before Fulu, `custody_group_count` is absent.

Each branch was mutation-checked locally: removing the prefix, removing
the Fulu gate, changing `>=` to `>` or `==`, or reading the count from
`CustodyRequirement` instead of PeerDAS makes a test fail.

## Out of scope

Other deviations in the node endpoints are left for separate PRs:

- `meta.count` in `GET /eth/v1/node/peers`;
- multiple values for the `state` and `direction` filters in `GET
/eth/v1/node/peers`;
- `404` instead of `400` for a malformed peer ID in `GET
/eth/v1/node/peers/{peer_id}`;
- a TCP multiaddress in `discovery_addresses` of `GET
/eth/v1/node/identity`;
- peers without an ENR are omitted instead of being returned with
`"enr": null`.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/persistence, cl/antiquary: apply Gloas payload match in historical participation replay (#25211)
body:
## Summary

`HistoricalStatesReader.ReadParticipations` rebuilds the Gloas
participation lists by replaying block attestations. The replay did not
apply the Gloas payload-match rule, and it dropped errors from the
attestation callback. A rebuilt Gloas state could have wrong
`TIMELY_HEAD` flags and a wrong state root, or a partial participation
list with a nil error.

Fixes #25199

## Payload-match rule (consensus-specs v1.7.0-beta.4)

`get_attestation_participation_flag_indices` now applies the Gloas rule
in the historical path:

- a same-slot attestation (`is_attestation_same_slot`) needs `data.index
== 0`;
- any other attestation gets `TIMELY_HEAD` only when `data.index ==
execution_payload_availability[parent_slot %
SLOTS_PER_HISTORICAL_ROOT]`.

`parent_slot` is `state.latest_block_header.slot` before
`process_block_header`, which is the slot of the block at
`block.ParentRoot`. The replay resolves it from the block index and
falls back to the genesis state's latest block header. The availability
bit is read from the stored post-state of the including block.
`process_parent_execution_payload` runs before `process_operations` and
nothing later in the block changes the bit, so the stored value is the
one the spec uses. Blocks without attestations skip the lookup; this
keeps the synthetic genesis block of a Gloas-at-genesis chain (zero
`ParentRoot`) a no-op. Pre-Gloas behaviour of the rule is unchanged.

Errors from the replay (randao mix, attesting indices, flag computation,
parent lookup, availability) are now returned.

## Genesis-boundary fixes

The fixture tests could not pass without three more fixes:

- `readHistoricalBlockRoot` returned an error for the root at the
genesis slot, so attestations that target epoch 0 were dropped. It now
reads the DB for every slot from the genesis slot on and uses the
genesis `block_roots` vector only for slots before it.
- In the genesis epoch, attestations were written to the previous epoch
participation. An attestation now goes to the current epoch list exactly
when its target is the epoch of the requested slot (`data.target.epoch
== get_current_epoch(state)`). This also changes epoch-0 output for
Altair through Fulu, to the value the spec state has.
- The antiquary wrote the active validator indices of the genesis epoch
only at the next epoch boundary. `addGenesisState` now writes them too.

## Tests and fixtures

- `TestReadHistoricalStateGloasParticipation` rebuilds two Gloas mainnet
chains through the antiquary and compares current/previous participation
and the block state roots with the live transition. The fixtures are
copied from consensus-spec-tests **v1.7.0-beta.2**
(`sanity/blocks/attestations_after_missed_slot_use_applied_parent_payload_availability`
and `sanity/blocks/attestation`); the beta.4 transition accepts them
with full validation.
- `TestReadHistoricalStateGloasGenesisBlockWithoutAttestations`:
synthetic Gloas genesis block with a zero parent root.
- `TestReadParticipationsReturnsBlockRootError`: error propagation.
- Unit tests: `TestReadHistoricalBlockRootAtGenesisSlot`,
`TestGloasSameSlotAttestationRejectsNonzeroIndex`,
`TestGloasSameSlotAttestationAfterGenesisSlot`,
`TestPayloadMatchAppliesFromGloas` (Fulu keeps `TIMELY_HEAD`, Gloas
drops it).

TDD note: `TestGloasSameSlotAttestationAfterGenesisSlot` and
`TestPayloadMatchAppliesFromGloas` were added in the second commit,
after the behaviour landed in the first one, to close coverage gaps
found in review. They were checked by mutation: disabling the `data.slot
!= 0` same-slot branch, or removing the Gloas version gate, makes them
fail. The genesis-block test was red before its fix.

## Validation

- `go test ./cl/persistence/state/... ./cl/antiquary/...`
- the pre-Gloas reader round-trips with `ERIGON_RUN_HEAVY_TESTS=1`
- `make lint` (clean, repeated)
- `make erigon integration`

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- `ReadRandaoMixBySlotAndIndex` has the same genesis off-by-one as
`readHistoricalBlockRoot` had: on chains with genesis slot 0 it uses the
genesis mix instead of the final epoch-0 mix for epoch-2 attestations,
so states in epochs 2 and 3 are rebuilt with wrong committees.
- The replay needs the `BlockRootToSlot` index and the availability rows
for Gloas blocks with attestations; while the snapshot index is rebuilt,
direct `ReadParticipations` callers (liveness, lighthouse) return an
error, and antiquary init does not back off on that untyped error.
- A missing `ActiveValidatorIndicies` row is still read as an empty
list.
- No test crosses the Fulu→Gloas fork or covers Heze; pre-Gloas reader
tests run only with `ERIGON_RUN_HEAVY_TESTS`.
- The Gloas predicate is not shared with the live path in
`cl/phase1/core/state`.
- Anchors at a slot other than 0 are only partly handled.
- `attestingIndicies` picks the attestation format from the attestation
slot's epoch, not from the including block's version.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/persistence, cl/antiquary: write queue diffs from the longest overlap (#25230)
body:
Fixes #25205

Stacked on #25212: review only the last four commits. The last commit
updates one test of this PR for the `ReadRequiredQueueSSZ` signature
from #25212.

This PR must ship in the same release as #25231 (builders per-index
diff) and #25234 (builder pending payments base plus deltas), which are
stacked on it. Without them, a Gloas node writes `builders` rows that
rewrite the whole list on every in-place change.

## Problem

The state antiquary stores per-slot diffs of the Electra queues
(`pending_deposits`, `pending_consolidations`,
`pending_partial_withdrawals`) and the Gloas lists (`builders`,
`builder_pending_withdrawals`, `payload_expected_withdrawals`) with
`SSZQueueEncoder`. The encoder remembered only the previous size and the
previous last element. It searched the new list backwards for that
element and wrote "truncate N from the front" plus the elements after
it. Two cases broke this:

- `builders` changes in place (withdrawals, deposits, exits). When a
builder that is not the last one changed, the diff was "truncate 0,
append nothing", so the change was lost until the next dump.
- When an appended entry equalled the previous last entry, the search
picked the appended copy, the truncate count went negative and wrapped
in `uint32`, and replay emptied the queue.

## Fix

The diff byte format and the replay format are unchanged.

- `Initialize` keeps a copy of the previous list's element pointers in a
slice the encoder owns.
- `WriteDiff` first tries a fast path based on pointer identity: queue
elements are copy-on-write, so equal pointers hold equal values. If the
previous list's tail and the new list's head hold the same pointers, it
writes the diff directly. This covers unchanged queues, append-only
slots and front pops plus appends.
- Otherwise it finds the longest suffix of the previous list that equals
a prefix of the new list with KMP, which is linear in the list sizes,
and writes `truncate = prevLen - overlap` plus `new[overlap:]`. An
in-place builder change becomes a full rewrite of the list for that
slot.
- `ApplySSZQueueDiff` returns the new `ErrCorruptQueueDiff` when the
truncate count is larger than the queue length, before it changes the
queue. The readers wrap it, and the antiquary resume backs off on it
like it does for `ErrMissingGloasData`.

## Upgrade note

There is no migration: the stored bytes of a wrong diff cannot be
repaired, and each wrong window ends at the next dump (at most 1535
slots). Re-antiquation does not repair rows already frozen in Caplin
state snapshot files, and nothing regenerates a frozen range
automatically. On Sepolia the Gloas range written by older releases
stays wrong. Electra ranges are affected only in the rare case where two
equal queue entries were appended in a row.

## Tests

- Collector tests: an in-place change to builder 0 is kept, and an
appended duplicate builder pending withdrawal no longer empties the
queue.
- Encoder tests: in-place `Set` on the same list, duplicate last append,
front cut plus postponed re-append, the fast path and its fallback when
equal values have different pointers, `truncate == len` accepted and
`truncate > len` rejected without changing the queue, an exhaustive
round trip over all small lists with duplicates, and a check that the
overlap search makes a linear number of equality calls.
- Reader and antiquary tests: the corrupt-diff error is wrapped by both
readers, and the antiquary backoff includes it.
- Benchmark in `ssz_queue_bench_test.go`: at 100k `pending_deposits`
entries, a diff takes about 0.24 ms.

TDD: the tests were written first and failed on the old code for the
intended reason, except the `truncate == len` check and the linear-call
check, which also pass on the old encoder and guard the new one. The
fast-path test failed before the fast path was added.

## Validation

- `go test ./cl/persistence/... ./cl/antiquary/... -count=1`
- `make lint`, two runs, 0 issues
- `make erigon integration`

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- `builders` gets its own per-index row format in #25231, so an in-place
builder change no longer rewrites the whole list.
- No end-to-end test drives the antiquary backoff through a stored
corrupt row.
- Copy-on-write of queue elements is a convention, not enforced by the
type.

author: Kewei
subject: cl: hand the post-fork-choice head state to synced data without copying it (#25237)
body:
## Problem

`postForkchoiceOperations` copies the head state twice per slot:

1. `GetStateAtBlockRoot(headRoot)` returns a private copy. On the normal
path it is a copy of the fork graph's current state, taken under the
fork-choice read lock. Hoodi p50 is about 56 ms.
2. The head event, the payload attributes event and the attestation data
producer read that copy.
3. `OnHeadStateWithBlockRoot` then copies it again into synced data.
Hoodi p50 is about 38 ms.

After step 3, `postForkchoiceOperations` reads the head state only
through `ViewHeadState`, so the second copy is not needed.

## What changed

- `synced_data`: new `OnOwnedHeadStateWithBlockRoot`. It takes ownership
of a state that is already private and does not copy it. It uses the
same `writeLock -> mu -> accessLock` order as the copying publish. The
head becomes the new state, the previous state becomes the old head, and
the spare is not touched. It rejects nil and any state the manager
already holds, and in that case it changes nothing.
- `forkchoice`: new `GetOwnedStateAtBlockRoot`, a method on
`ForkChoiceStore` only (the interface does not change).
  - Current-state path: the same copy as `GetStateAtBlockRoot`.
- Replay path: the replayed state is copied. Replay applies stored
fork-graph blocks, and some transition setters keep the block's pointers
in the state: `AddEth1DataVote` / `SetEth1Data` (block `Eth1Data`) and
`SetLatestExecutionPayloadBid` (Gloas bid). The copy makes sure that the
published state shares no storage with fork-graph blocks.
- `GetStateAtBlockRoot` and its other callers (for example
`saveFinalizedStateOnDiskIfNeeded`) keep the same behavior and cost. The
locked current-state copy moved into a small `copyCurrentState` helper
that both getters use.
- `stages`: `postForkchoiceOperations` uses both new methods and does
not use its local head state after the publish. Block production,
forward sync and startup still use the copying publish.

## Cost

- Normal path (head is the fork graph's current state): one full state
copy per slot instead of two.
- Replay path (head is not the current state, for example after a
side-branch block): the copy work is the same as before, one full copy.
The difference is that the copy is a new allocation instead of a
`CopyInto` into synced data's spare state. This path is not the steady
state, and it already allocates a full state when it reads the base
state from disk.
- Synced data still keeps at most three full states (head, previous,
spare).

## Hoodi results

Measured on a Hoodi node (about 1.14M validators) with probe timings,
comparing the same build with and without this commit (about 2,000 slots
each, after warm-up):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Second copy (`OnHeadStateWithBlockRoot`) p50 | 38 ms | 0 ms |
| `postForkchoiceOperations` total p50 | 189 ms | 150 ms |
| `postForkchoiceOperations` total p99 | 1648 ms | 1629 ms |
| First copy (`GetStateAtBlockRoot`) p50 / p99 | 55 / 141 ms | 55 / 147
ms |
| Epoch transition p50 | 428 ms | 428 ms |
| Go anonymous memory | 9.0-9.5 GB | 8.0-8.4 GB |
| GC pause per hour | ~0.02 s | ~0.03 s |

No errors, no invalid blocks and no fork-choice writer waits of 1 s or
more in either run. The p99 is dominated by the head-state dump every
fourth slot, which this change does not touch.

## Tests

All new tests were written first and failed before the production
change:

- `cl/beacon/synced_data`: owned publish on a cold manager; copy ->
owned -> copy rotation; owned -> owned; rejection of nil and of the
head, previous and spare pointers with no state change; disabled
manager; concurrent copy publish, owned publish, `UnsetHeadState` and
readers (run with `-race`).
- `cl/phase1/forkchoice`: `GetOwnedStateAtBlockRoot` on the replay path
returns a state that does not change when the block's `Eth1Data` and
Gloas bid are mutated; on the current-state path it returns a copy with
the same root.
- `cl/phase1/stages`: `postForkchoiceOperations` publishes through the
owned method exactly once and never calls the copying publish. The
published state is not the fork graph's current state object, and the
state visible through `ViewHeadState` is the same object it handed over.

Verification: `go build ./...`; `go test -race` for
`cl/beacon/synced_data/...`, `cl/phase1/stages/...` and
`cl/phase1/forkchoice/...`; `go test ./cl/...` (only `cl/spectest`
`Test/mainnet_config` fails, because the mainnet spec fixtures are not
downloaded locally; this is not related to the change); `make lint`
clean twice.

author: lystopad
subject: cl/phase1/network/registry: let one peer forward a slot's aggregates at once (#25236)
body:
Fixes #25235.

The `beacon_aggregate_and_proof` topic allowed 8 messages per second per
peer, with a burst of 16. Aggregates for a slot are published at the
same point in the slot, so peers forward them in bursts. Gossipsub marks
a message as seen before Caplin validates it, so an aggregate the
limiter ignored was also dropped when other peers sent it, and the node
lost whole committees.

One peer may now forward a whole slot's expected aggregates in one burst
(`MaxCommitteesPerSlot * TargetAggregatorsPerCommittee`, 1,024 on
mainnet), refilled over the slot. The other topics' limits are
unchanged.

## Measurement

Mainnet node, pool read 1.4 s into the next slot, 40 slots each:

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| committees with no aggregate (vs a Lighthouse reference: 0) | 24 | 0 |
| votes in the pool vs finally included | 98.8–99.0% | 99.87% |

## Tests

`TestAggregateAndProofRateLimiterAdmitsSlotBurstFromOnePeer` covers the
mainnet and minimal presets; it fails on the old limit. `make lint` is
clean twice; `make erigon integration` builds.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/persistence, cl/antiquary: store builders history as a per-index diff (#25231)
body:
Stacked on #25230 (which is stacked on #25212): review only the last two
commits.

## Problem

The state antiquary writes one `kv.Builders` row per processed Gloas
block with `SSZQueueEncoder`. Builders is a registry, not a queue:
deposits, withdrawals and exits change builders in place. With the
overlap encoder from #25205, any change to a builder that is not the
last one rewrites the whole list for that slot, about 97 bytes per
builder. At 200 builders that is about 19 KB per block, roughly 46–51 GB
a year. The format has to change before Gloas reaches Hoodi and mainnet,
because after that old rows would need a migration.

## Fix

`kv.Builders` gets a per-index diff format. Same table, same snapshot
type. `kv.BuildersDump` and the other five queues are unchanged.

Row layout, little-endian, not compressed:

```
00 00 00 00 | 00 00 00 00 | 47 4c 4f 41 ("GLOA") | 01 (version) | 01 (kind)
newLength u64 | count u32 | count × (index u64, 93-byte Builder SSZ)
```

- The total length must be exactly `26 + 101*count`. A block with no
builder change writes a 26-byte row. With one change at 200 builders a
row is 127 bytes, against 19404 with the queue encoder.
- The writer, `BuildersDiffWriter`, keeps the pre-block builders as
copied values. It writes every changed index plus the appended indices,
in increasing order. The first Gloas row after the fork (empty baseline)
carries the full list as appends. A shrink is an error.
- The decoder, `ApplyBuildersDiff`, checks the whole row before it
changes the list. It rejects:
  - a wrong preamble, version or kind;
  - a wrong exact length;
  - a length above the registry limit, or a shrink;
- indices that are not strictly increasing, or not below the new length;
  - appends that are not contiguous;
  - a builder that does not decode.
- `ReadBuildersSSZ` replays the rows on top of the dump, using the same
dump rules as `ReadRequiredQueueSSZ` (#25212). A processed block (one
with `kv.SlotData`) at or after the fork slot that has no row is an
error. A missed slot is skipped. The Gloas genesis state writes a
no-change row at its own slot, so it can be read when its slot is not a
dump slot.
- Every rejection wraps the new `ErrHistoryRebuildRequired`, and the
antiquary backs off on it like it does for `ErrMissingGloasData`.

The first 8 zero bytes are for old binaries. An older reader takes them
as "truncate 0", then a zero-length builder, and fails decoding the
empty builder before it changes the list. It does not mistake the row
for a corrupt queue diff, so it does not back off and rewrite new rows
in the old format.

## Upgrade note (for the release notes)

Hoodi operators must upgrade before the Gloas fork on 2026-10-26. This
release changes the on-disk format of Caplin historical state rows for
builders (per-index diff) and builder pending payments (epoch base plus
per-block deltas, #25234).

- The Caplin state snapshot types keep their file version.
- A node that reads an old-format row from its DB backs off and
re-antiquates from before the Gloas fork.
- An older release that reads a new-format row fails with a decode error
and does not read wrong data. Downgrading after new rows were written is
not supported.
- #25205 must not ship without this format change.
- Sepolia is not repaired. Rows already frozen in Caplin state snapshot
files, including the published Sepolia range 11250000–11300000, stay in
the old format. Snapshot files are read before the DB and frozen ranges
are not regenerated, so historical state reads that replay those rows
keep failing until the range is reset or republished.
- The same applies to a node that passed a Gloas fork on an older
release and has already frozen Gloas state snapshots.

## Tests

- **Codec:**
- round trip over: no change, first, middle or last change, several
changes, index reuse, append, reuse plus append, empty to one;
  - a change to each single non-balance field;
  - exact byte layout;
  - the baseline is a value copy;
  - shrink is an error;
  - about 20 rejected rows, each with no mutation;
- both legacy queue decoders, before and after #25205, fail on a new row
without changing the list.
- **Reader:** exact fork slot, missed fork slot, dump plus change plus
append, a processed-block hole at the target and between the dump and
the target, a missed slot, a pre-fork slot, and a legacy row (sentinel,
with table and slot in the error).
- **Antiquary:**
  - backoff on the sentinel;
  - collector → mdbx → reader round trip;
  - the hook across the Fulu → Gloas fork;
- a Gloas genesis state at a dump slot (0) and at a slot that is not a
dump slot (32): the genesis row is the 26-byte no-change row, and both
the genesis state and the next block's change read back;
- a seam test with real 1000-slot snapshot files, pruning, and reads
that cross the file boundary and the snapshot/DB boundary, compared with
the lists actually written.
- **Benchmark:** `BenchmarkBuildersRowSize`. At 200 builders with one
change per block, Initialize plus WriteDiff takes about 1.7 µs, 7 allocs
and 127 bytes per row.

TDD: the codec, reader and backoff tests were written first and failed
for the intended reason, either on undefined symbols or with the backoff
predicate returning false. The genesis test also failed first: at slot
32 with `historical state row needs a rebuild: missing row from table
Builders at slot 32`, and at slot 0 because the genesis slot had no row
(an empty value where a 26-byte row was expected). Some later tests, the
append-end check, the hole after a dump, and the single-field changes,
guard existing behaviour and passed on first run. Each one was checked
to fail when its target branch is disabled.

The snapshot file version is deliberately not bumped, so no Caplin
snapshot republish is needed. The raw preamble tells old and new rows
apart.

## Validation

- `go test ./cl/persistence/... ./cl/antiquary/... ./db/snapshotsync/...
-count=1`, and `-race` on `cl/antiquary`
- `make lint`, two runs, 0 issues
- `make erigon integration`
- Dual review until converged: two review rounds, a fix-delta review and
a fresh adversarial pass. The genesis-row commit had its own dual
review, with no blocker.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Gloas required-queue history is unreadable when every slot from the
fork through the next dump slot is missed: no Gloas dump is written at
that slot. This is pre-existing and affects all three Gloas queues.
- `LatestExecutionPayloadBidTable` stores a redundant full bid per slot.
It can be changed after the Hoodi fork.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/phase1/network/services, cmd/caplin: republish queued execution payload envelopes (#25259)
body:
## Problem

An execution payload envelope that arrives over gossip before its beacon
block is IGNOREd and, if the queue has room, kept pending for about 30
seconds until the block is known, as the Gloas p2p spec allows for the
`execution_payload` topic. Gossipsub does not forward IGNOREd messages,
and Caplin did not publish the envelope after it processed it from the
pending queue. Peers that could only receive the envelope through Caplin
nodes never got it over gossip, so they built on an EMPTY parent and
their PTC votes did not count the payload as present. We saw this in a
local multi-client network, where Prysm publishes its envelope a few
milliseconds after its block.

## What changed

- `NewExecutionPayloadService` takes the gossip manager, wired in
`cmd/caplin/caplin1/run.go`.
- When an envelope from the pending queue is processed without error,
the service SSZ-encodes it and calls `PublishBackground` on the
`execution_payload` topic. These are the same outcomes for which the
direct gossip path returns ACCEPT. Envelopes that fail processing are
not published.
- go-libp2p-pubsub v0.17.0 validates and forwards a local publish of a
message that it saw and ignored before. Caplin's message ID hashes the
topic, including the fork digest, and the decompressed SSZ. Outside a
fork transition the relayed message is published on the same topic, so
it has the same ID as the original, and peers that already have it drop
it as a duplicate. Caplin's validator accepts its own messages without
processing them again.
- Prysm and Teku also publish an envelope after deferred validation;
Lighthouse does it only for envelopes of the current slot. The spec has
no current-slot rule for this topic (the only time rule is IGNORE before
the finalized slot), so Caplin adds no current-slot check either. It
still checks the finalized slot, and only envelopes that leave the
pending queue before it expires are published.

Not changed here: Caplin still forwards an envelope only after
`processMessage` succeeds, which normally includes the EL call, and not
right after the gossip checks.

## Tests

-
`TestExecutionPayloadServiceRepublishesPendingEnvelopeAfterBlockArrives`:
an envelope ignored while its block is unknown is passed once to the
gossip manager's `PublishBackground` after the block arrives (mocked;
the test does not cover delivery to peers). Before the change the
expected publish call was missing.
- `TestExecutionPayloadServiceDoesNotRepublishInvalidPendingEnvelope`: a
pending envelope that fails fork choice validation is not published.
- Removing the publish call, or publishing without the success check,
makes the matching test fail.

author: Kewei
subject: cl: validate boundary blocks without a state copy (#25253)
body:
Part of #25136 (direction 3).

## What and why

Gossip validation of a block needs four values from its parent: the
expected proposer, `latest_block_hash`, and the latest bid's block hash
and presence. A parent in the same epoch is already read in place. A
parent in an earlier epoch was copied (under `f.mu.RLock` when it is the
fork graph's current state), advanced with `ProcessSlots` across the
epoch boundary, and then thrown away. On a Hoodi node this costs about
0.45 s for the first block of every epoch, before the block is forwarded
and imported.

From Fulu on, the advanced state does not differ from the parent in
these values when no fork upgrade happens in between:

- `ProcessProposerLookahead` only shifts `proposer_lookahead` and
appends a new last epoch, so the parent's entry for a slot in the next
`MinSeedLookahead` epochs is the entry the advanced state reads.
- `latest_block_hash` and the latest bid are written only by block
processing and `UpgradeToGloas`, not by slot or epoch processing. The
bid was already read before advancing.

## Changes

- `cl/phase1/core/state`: extract the lookahead read of
`GetBeaconProposerIndexForSlot` into `ProposerIndexFromLookahead(slot)
(uint64, bool)`. It returns false before Fulu or when the slot's epoch
is outside `[stateEpoch, stateEpoch+MinSeedLookahead]`.
`GetBeaconProposerIndexForSlot` calls it first; its behaviour does not
change.
- `cl/phase1/network/services`: `computeBlockValidationContext` also
reads a parent from an earlier epoch in place when:
- the header shows the parent at most `MinSeedLookahead` epochs back
(checked before viewing, so a non-head parent is not replayed twice),
- the scheduled state version is the same at the parent's and the
block's epoch and is at least Fulu (this excludes the Fulu and Gloas
activation epochs and any later fork's activation epoch),
- the viewed state has the block epoch's version, and
`ProposerIndexFromLookahead` covers the slot.

  In all other cases the existing copy path runs.

The in-place read under `f.mu.RLock` is a few field reads, which is much
less work than the state copy it replaces. It adds no new lock edges.

## Trade-off

The copy path's `ProcessSlots` used to fill the global lookahead shuffle
and active-set caches, and block import's `ProcessEpoch` (under `f.mu`)
then found them already filled. After this change import computes them
itself: about 10-15 ms on Fulu, and more on Gloas when no bid was
gossiped. This PR adds no warm-up code for it.

## Tests

- `TestProposerIndexFromLookahead`: window edges (pre-Fulu false, first
and last slot of the window true, one epoch past the window and one slot
before the state epoch false).
- `TestBlockValidationContextReadsParentFromPreviousEpochWithoutCopy`
(Fulu and Gloas subtests): parent at the last slot of epoch E-1, block
at the first slot of E, +1 and +5 (empty slots at the start of the
epoch). The copy path returns an error. All four values equal a `Copy` +
`ProcessSlots` oracle, and the parent state's slot and hash tree root do
not change. The Gloas case uses a distinct `latest_block_hash` and bid
hash. This test fails on `main`.
- `TestBlockValidationContextCopiesFuluParentFromTwoEpochsBack`: the
state is not viewed and is fetched once.
- `TestBlockValidationContextCopiesParentAtFuluActivation` (earlier
forks at 0, Fulu at E, Gloas far future): the state is not viewed and is
fetched once.
-
`TestBlockValidationContextFallsBackWhenViewedParentCannotServeLookahead`:
the viewed state has a different version from the schedule, or is
outside the lookahead window. Each case falls back to one copy.
- Existing
`TestBlockValidationContextReadsSameEpochParentStateWithoutCopy`,
`TestBlockValidationContextAdvancesCopiedParentStateAcrossEpoch` and
`TestBlockServiceGossipUsesPostUpgradeExecutionHeadAtGloasBoundary`
still pass.

Mutation checks. Each guard was removed, the named test failed, and the
guard was restored:

| Mutation | Failing test |
|---|---|
| Remove the header distance check |
`...CopiesFuluParentFromTwoEpochsBack` (state viewed) |
| Remove the header version-equality check |
`...CopiesParentAtFuluActivation` (state viewed) |
| Remove the header `>= Fulu` check |
`...AdvancesCopiedParentStateAcrossEpoch` (state fetched twice) |
| Remove the callback version check | `...FallsBack.../state version
differs` (no copy) |
| Ignore the `ok` of `ProposerIndexFromLookahead` |
`...FallsBack.../slot is outside` (proposer 0) |
| Lookahead index `slot % SlotsPerEpoch` only |
`...ReadsParentFromPreviousEpochWithoutCopy` (Fulu and Gloas) |
| Remove both version checks |
`...UsesPostUpgradeExecutionHeadAtGloasBoundary` (wrong execution head)
|

`make lint`, `make erigon integration` and `go test -race
./cl/phase1/core/state/ ./cl/phase1/network/services/` pass.

## Expected gain

We estimate about 0.4 s less at each epoch boundary on a Hoodi node,
based on the cost of the same copy-and-advance step measured elsewhere.
We will measure it after merge.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/phase1/forkchoice/fork_graph: stop fsyncing fork-graph dump files (#25251)
body:
## Problem

Caplin's fork graph writes two kinds of dump files and calls
`File.Sync()` on each one:

- the head state, in `DumpBeaconStateOnDisk`
(`cl/phase1/forkchoice/fork_graph/fork_graph_disk_fs.go`), every 4th
slot (`dumpSlotFrequency = 4`);
- the execution payload envelope, in `DumpEnvelopeOnDisk` (same file),
after Gloas.

On a Hoodi node (1.14M validators) one head-state dump writes about 143
MB. `dumpMs` is p50 ~540 ms, p90 ~1.06 s and max 2.65 s. Measured
locally, encoding takes ~4 ms and snappy + write ~100 ms, so most of the
node time is likely writeback and fsync. The split on the node was not
measured separately.

Every dump holds a shared lock, and the head dump after fork choice also
holds a lock and a transaction, so every millisecond counts:

- every dump holds `stateDumpLock` (`fork_graph_disk_fs.go:122`). The
same lock is needed by fork-graph replay (`readBeaconStateFromDisk`,
`:57`), by req/resp and API envelope reads (`ReadEnvelopeFromDisk`,
`:205`), and after Gloas by envelope import (`DumpEnvelopeOnDisk`,
`:354`), which runs while it holds the fork-choice `f.mu`
(`cl/phase1/forkchoice/on_execution_payload.go:780`, `:1176`);
- the head dump after fork choice runs inside
`syncedData.ViewHeadState`, which holds the synced-data read lock
(`cl/phase1/stages/forkchoice.go:469`,
`cl/beacon/synced_data/synced_data.go:167`). A waiting writer makes new
readers queue behind it;
- it also runs inside the stage's `indiciesDB` RW transaction
(`cl/phase1/stages/forkchoice.go:498-518`).

## Why removing fsync is safe

The durability that fsync gives (data survives a power loss or a kernel
crash) is never used, because nothing reads these files after such an
event:

- Both files live in `path.Join(dirs.Tmp, "caplin-forkchoice")`. Caplin
removes and recreates this directory on every start, before it builds
the fork graph (`cmd/caplin/caplin1/run.go:365-384`). This is the only
production fork-graph filesystem; the spectests use
`afero.NewMemMapFs()`
(`cl/spectest/consensus_tests/fork_choice.go:314`). The removal came in
the same PR that added the dump and its Sync (#8546). Comments in
`cl/phase1/stages/forward_sync.go` call the forward-sync dumps "restart
checkpoints", but they are also wiped on start; the real restart anchor
is the finalized-state save.

Inside the running process the files stay usable without fsync:

- Reads see written data through the page cache, fsynced or not.
- All content reads and writes of these files hold `stateDumpLock`
(`fork_graph_disk_fs.go:57`, `:122`, `:205`, `:354`). `Prune` removals
and the `hasBeaconState` existence check run outside it
(`fork_graph_disk.go:755`, `:850-858`); this is unchanged.
- If a head-state dump cannot be read, replay walks back to an older
dump when the block is still kept (`fork_graph_disk.go:639-645`), or
returns no state when only the header is kept, for example for the
anchor (`:623-633`). This is the same as for any missing dump.
- Envelopes are still written to a `.tmp` file, closed with a checked
`Close`, and renamed (`fork_graph_disk_fs.go:377-427`). Readers never
see a partial file, and a write, flush, close or rename error keeps the
existing final file (`TestDumpEnvelopeFailurePreservesExistingFinal`).

History: the head-state Sync came with the original feature (#8546,
which gives no rationale; its error was always returned) and was moved
in #8851. The envelope dump copied the pattern in #18956, and #23548
moved envelopes to tmp+rename and kept the Sync. No change relies on the
durability of these files.

Trade-off: fsync is also the point where the kernel reliably reports a
delayed writeback error (EIO). `close(2)` on a local filesystem usually
does not report it. Such an error may now go unnoticed by the dump and
show up later, for example when the data is read again after the pages
were evicted. Before, the dump itself failed. A head-state read error
makes replay fall back as described above. An envelope that fails to
decode is marked invalid and can be fetched again. If the re-read itself
returns EIO, the envelope stays marked as present, so normal ingestion
skips it while the error lasts: until a later read succeeds, the anchor
envelope is rewritten, or the block is pruned. This needs a failing
disk, and it is accepted here for the cost above.

## What changed

- `DumpBeaconStateOnDisk`: removed `Sync()`. The file was closed by an
unchecked `defer`. It is now closed once in a defer that joins the
`Close` error into the returned error, like the envelope dump, so errors
reported at close (for example on NFS) are not lost.
- `DumpEnvelopeOnDisk`: removed `Sync()`. The order stays write, flush,
checked `Close`, `Rename`.

## What is not changed

- The finalized-state save under `dirs.CaplinLatest`
(`saveFinalizedStateOnDiskIfNeeded` / `replaceDurableFile`,
`cl/phase1/stages/forkchoice.go:372-430`) is the restart anchor. It
keeps its file fsync, rename and directory fsync.
- Every dump still holds `stateDumpLock`, and the head dump after fork
choice still runs under the synced-data read lock and inside the
`indiciesDB` RW transaction. This PR only makes the dumps shorter.

Follow-ups (not in this PR):

- Move the head-state dump and the finalized-state save after
`tx.Commit()`. This also fixes a silent rollback: today a failed dump
makes `postForkchoiceOperations` return an error, so the canonical-chain
and finalized-slot writes in the same transaction are rolled back.
- Gloas envelope import holds the fork-choice `f.mu` while it waits for
`stateDumpLock` (`on_execution_payload.go:780` → `:1176`), so a long
head-state dump still stalls fork choice. Either release `f.mu` around
persistence or give envelopes their own lock and buffer.

## Tests

- `TestForkGraphDumpsDoNotRequireSync`: with an afero file whose
`Sync()` fails, `NewForkGraphDisk` (forced anchor dump) and
`DumpEnvelopeOnDisk` must succeed, and the state and the envelope must
read back with equal SSZ hashes. Fails on `main` with the injected Sync
error.
- `TestDumpBeaconStateReturnsCloseError`: with an afero file whose
`Close()` fails, `DumpBeaconStateOnDisk` must return that error and
close the file exactly once. Fails on `main` because the error was
dropped.
- `TestDumpEnvelopeFailurePreservesExistingFinal`: removed the `"sync"`
stage, because Sync is no longer called. The open, write, close and
rename stages still pass.
- `go test -race ./cl/phase1/forkchoice/...` passes. `go test ./cl/...`
passes except `cl/spectest` `Test/mainnet_config`, which needs the
downloaded `mainnet` fixtures (not present locally, unrelated to this
change). `make lint` is clean.

## Backport

Not planned for release/3.8.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/phase1/network/services, cl/phase1/forkchoice: validate gossip attestations and aggregates against the target shuffling (#25208)
body:
## Problem

Caplin validates `beacon_attestation_{subnet_id}` and
`beacon_aggregate_and_proof` with the committee of its head state. The
committees of an epoch depend on the chain up to the epoch's shuffling
dependent slot. When a vote is for a known block on a branch whose
shuffling for the target epoch differs from the head branch, the head
committee is the wrong one, and an honest, correctly signed vote can
fail the committee checks:

- an Electra or later attestation fails with `attester is not a member
of the committee`;
- a pre-Electra attestation fails the aggregation bits length check, or
the set bit maps to the wrong validator;
- an aggregate fails the aggregation bits length, aggregator membership
or signature checks. The attesting indices that the aggregate path
passes to fork choice (`ProcessAttestingIndicies`) also come from the
head committee.

Each failed committee or signature check is a REJECT. On the attestation
subnets a REJECT counts as an invalid message in the gossipsub peer
score (`InvalidMessageDeliveries`, weighted with the square of the
count), and the gossip manager also tries to queue a ban of the sending
peer.

The order of the checks makes this worse. Subnet attestations ran all
committee checks before the "[IGNORE] The block being voted for has been
seen" check, so a vote for a block that is not imported yet (the usual
case for the other branch during a split) was rejected instead of
ignored and queued. Aggregates ran the committee index range check
before it.

Spec, consensus-specs v1.7.0-beta.4:
- `validate_beacon_attestation_gossip` and
`validate_beacon_aggregate_and_proof_gossip` in `specs/phase0`,
`specs/electra` and `specs/gloas` `p2p-interface.md` check that the
voted block has been seen (IGNORE, may be queued) before the committee
count, lookup, size and membership checks.
- Fork choice `on_attestation` (`specs/phase0/fork-choice.md`) takes the
committees from `store.checkpoint_states[attestation.data.target]`
(`store_target_checkpoint_state`), so for fork choice the head committee
does not decide whether such a vote counts. Caplin's `OnAttestation`
already does this when the head state does not have the target's
shuffling.
- The beta.4 gossip pseudocode itself reads the committee from the head
state, so this change deviates from it on purpose. See "Deviation from
the gossip pseudocode" below.

Devnet evidence (Kurtosis, Gloas): according to the operator, one client
followed its own branch from slot 194. From slot 256, the first epoch
whose shuffling depends on a slot after the split, the two Caplin logs
contain 141 and 143 rejections of that client's subnet attestations
(same peer) with `attester is not a member of the committee`. The
operator reported that after that the client received no gossip at all.

## What changed

- `cl/phase1/forkchoice`: `headStateHasTargetShuffling` is exported as
`HeadStateHasTargetShuffling` and added to `ForkChoiceStorageReader`,
unchanged. New `TargetBeaconCommittee(target, slot, committeeIndex)`
returns the committee and the committee count per slot from the target
checkpoint state. It uses the existing cached and singleflight
`getCheckpointState`. The committee slicing is shared with
`checkpointState.getAttestingIndicies`.
- `cl/phase1/network/services`: a shared `beaconCommittee` helper reads
the committee from the head state when `HeadStateHasTargetShuffling` is
true, which keeps the head-branch fast path, and otherwise from
`TargetBeaconCommittee` after the head-state view is released. If the
target state is not available, the message is ignored.
- A vote on another shuffling can make us build a checkpoint state
before all of its signatures are checked, so the build path is bounded:
- the services ask for the checkpoint of the voted block's own target,
`(target.epoch, Ancestor(beacon_block_root, start slot of
target.epoch))`, instead of the target root from the message. If that
ancestor is unknown, the message is ignored; the message root is never
used for a build. If the committee lookup succeeds, a message whose
target root does not match is still rejected by the existing
target-ancestor check;
- `TargetBeaconCommittee` serves cached checkpoint states with no limit.
For a missing state it allows at most 2 concurrent calls
(`maxConcurrentTargetCommitteeBuilds`). It returns an error, so the
message is ignored, when no slot is free or when the target does not
descend from the finalized checkpoint read at that moment. The slot is
taken before the finalized ancestor lookup and the state read. Otherwise
it builds the state with the existing `getCheckpointState`: concurrent
calls for the same checkpoint share one build through singleflight, and
later calls reuse it while it stays cached. Each call takes a slot, so
this bounds concurrency, not the total work over time.
- before asking for the target committee, the services apply the
seen-cache IGNORE and verify the signatures that do not need the
committee: the attestation signature of an Electra or later single
attestation (it names the attester), and the selection proof and
aggregator signature of an aggregate. An invalid signature is a REJECT.
So an Electra or later single attestation must carry a valid validator
signature before a state is built, and two attestations of one validator
with different data for the same target epoch form a slashable double
vote. For an aggregate that reaches full verification (immediate
processing, or a node with local validators), the aggregate attestation
signature is checked later; other aggregate gossip keeps the existing
IGNORE before that step. Pre-Electra single attestations name the
attester only through the committee, so they have no pre-check;
- for a missing state, `TargetBeaconCommittee` also refuses a target
whose block is unknown or more than 4 epochs older than the attestation
slot (`maxTargetCheckpointBlockAge`). Together with the finalized
precondition, this limits uncached targets to known descendants of the
finalized checkpoint within a 4-epoch window, by the target block's
slot. It does not bound the replay distance to the nearest stored state,
nor the total work over time.
- The head committee is copied inside the head-state view, because the
view must not leak slices of the head state.
- Subnet attestations: the block-seen IGNORE (with the existing queue)
now runs before the committee lookup. The Electra/Gloas `data.index`
checks stay before the block-seen check, as in the spec, so they now run
before the committee index and subnet checks (all three are REJECT). The
other REJECT and IGNORE checks keep their relative order from `main`;
the public key and domain lookup moves to just before signature
verification. A nil subnet is passed through to the queued retry instead
of being dereferenced.
- Aggregates: the committee lookup and the committee index range REJECT
now run right after the block-seen IGNORE (on the target path the lookup
first does the checks described below). The other checks keep their
order. The attesting indices are computed from the committee and the
aggregation bits, so fork choice is credited with the target-shuffling
validators.
- Public keys and the signing domain still come from the head state.
Committee members are active, activation needs a finalized eligibility
epoch, and both the head and the voted block descend from the finalized
checkpoint, so each committee member has the same index and key in the
head state.
- A real non-member of the committee selected by its target shuffling is
still rejected.

## Tests

Test-first (author-reported): the new acceptance, ordering,
unavailable-state and build-bound tests were written first and failed
before the production change. The REJECT and fast-path tests are guards
that keep the existing behavior; the mutation checks below show that
they are not vacuous.

- `TestElectraAttestationUsesTargetShuffling`,
`TestPreElectraAttestationUsesTargetCommitteeMember`,
`TestAggregateAndProofUsesTargetShuffling`,
`TestAggregateAndProofElectraUsesCommitteeBitsIndexForTargetShuffling`:
a vote on another shuffling is accepted, the target committee is
requested with the message's target epoch, the voted block's ancestor at
the start of that epoch as the root, the attestation slot and the
committee index, the pre-Electra public key is the one of the target
committee member, and the aggregate credits the target committee in fork
choice.
- `TestElectraAttestationRejectsNonMemberOfTargetCommittee`,
`TestAggregateAndProofRejectsAggregatorOutsideTargetCommittee`: a member
of the head committee that is not in the target committee is rejected.
- `TestAttestationForUnseenBlockIsIgnoredBeforeCommitteeChecks`,
`TestAggregateAndProofUnseenBlockIsIgnoredBeforeCommitteeRange`,
`TestAttestationForUnseenBlockWithNilSubnetIsIgnored`: a vote for an
unseen block is ignored before the committee checks.
- `TestAttestationIgnoresUnavailableTargetCheckpointState`,
`TestAggregateAndProofIgnoresUnavailableTargetCheckpointState`: a
missing target state gives IGNORE.
- `TestAttestationKeepsHeadShufflingFastPath`: when
`HeadStateHasTargetShuffling` is true, the service does not ask for the
target committee and does not do the extra ancestor lookup that derives
the target root from the voted block.
- Order guards: `TestElectraAttestationAlreadySeenBeforeTargetAncestor`,
`TestAggregateAndProofAlreadySeenBeforeTargetAncestor`,
`TestElectraAttestationRejectsNonMemberBeforeFinalizedAncestor`,
`TestAggregateAndProofRejectsCommitteeRangeBeforeFinalizedAncestor`,
`TestElectraAttestationChecksEpochRangeBeforeStructuralIndex`.
- `TestTargetBeaconCommitteeUsesCheckpointState` uses a real fork choice
store with a side branch.
- Build bound: `TestTargetBeaconCommitteeLimitsUncachedBuilds` (at the
limit no state is read and fork choice looks up no ancestor, one build
below the limit is admitted, cached states are still served, the slot is
released after a failed build),
`TestTargetBeaconCommitteeRejectsTargetOutsideFinalizedChain` (no state
is read for a target outside the finalized chain; the finalized root
itself is admitted),
`TestElectraAttestationBuildsVotedBlockTargetBeforeRejectingMessageTarget`
and
`TestAggregateAndProofBuildsVotedBlockTargetBeforeRejectingMessageTarget`
(the target is derived from the voted block root, and a wrong message
target is still rejected).
- Signature and age checks:
`TestElectraAttestationRejectsInvalidSignatureBeforeTargetShuffling`,
`TestElectraAttestationAlreadySeenBeforeTargetShuffling`,
`TestAggregateAndProofRejectsInvalidSignatureBeforeTargetShuffling`,
`TestAggregateAndProofAlreadySeenBeforeTargetShuffling` (an invalid
signature is rejected and a seen vote is ignored, both before the target
committee is requested; the valid target-path tests check that the
signature is verified before the lookup),
`TestTargetBeaconCommitteeLimitsCheckpointBlockAge` (more than 4 epochs
old and unknown target blocks are refused without reading a state;
exactly 4 epochs is allowed), and
`TestAttestationIgnoresUnknownVotedBlockTargetAncestor` and
`TestAggregateAndProofIgnoresUnknownVotedBlockTargetAncestor` (an
unknown voted-block ancestor is ignored before any signature check or
lookup).
- Existing REJECT cases in `TestAttestationProcessMessage` and the
aggregate tests now set up a known block so that they still reach their
rule. They also assert that the error is not an IGNORE.
- Mutation checks: removing each new branch (target path, head fast
path, IGNORE on a missing state, block-seen order, aggregate attesting
indices, the out-of-range guard in fork choice, seen-before-target
order, the build limit and its exact capacity, the limit before the
ancestor lookup, the finalized precondition, the cache bypass of the
limit, the counter release, the derived target root, the IGNORE for an
unknown ancestor, the age limit and its boundary, the unknown target
block, the signature pre-check, its position before the lookup and its
absence on the fast path, the seen checks in the pre-check) makes at
least one of these tests fail.
- `go test -race -p 2 ./cl/phase1/network/services/
./cl/phase1/forkchoice/`, `go test -p 2 ./cl/phase1/forkchoice/...
./cl/phase1/network/...`, `make lint`, `make erigon`.

## Deviation from the gossip pseudocode

The executable gossip checks in consensus-specs v1.7.0-beta.4 read the
committees from the head state,
`store.block_states[get_head(store).root]` (phase0
[attestation](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/aa16bb4c156184e9548a997d53efaf2a228a6304/specs/phase0/p2p-interface.md#L1037)
and
[aggregate](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/aa16bb4c156184e9548a997d53efaf2a228a6304/specs/phase0/p2p-interface.md#L746),
electra
[aggregate](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/aa16bb4c156184e9548a997d53efaf2a228a6304/specs/electra/p2p-interface.md#L284)).
For a vote whose shuffling differs from the head, this PR uses the
shuffling of the vote's target checkpoint instead. That is the state
fork choice `on_attestation` uses,
[`store.checkpoint_states[attestation.data.target]`](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/aa16bb4c156184e9548a997d53efaf2a228a6304/specs/phase0/fork-choice.md#L1025).
When the shuffling is the same, both states give the same committees, so
nothing changes for votes on the head branch.

Why:
- The head-state wording was added in consensus-specs #4902 (first
released in v1.7.0-alpha.4). A reviewer
[asked](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4902#discussion_r2896273921)
which `state` the validation should use and noted that clients use
different approaches. The editor
[answered](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4902#discussion_r2925049154)
with a commit that "tells the reader that the state is the head state",
and added: "This feels a bit lazy, so maybe we can follow up later which
explains why for each one." consensus-specs #5563 (v1.7.0-beta.1) then
loaded the state from the store with `get_head(store)` to remove the
ambiguous `state` parameter. The discussions in #4902 and #5563 do not
cover votes on a branch with a different shuffling.
- The clients take the shuffling of the voted branch. The target is
checked to be an ancestor of the voted block, so this is the same as the
target checkpoint shuffling:
- Lighthouse v8.3.0, [`with_committee_cache(target.root,
...)`](https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/blob/014ba06b56514d383426f2c727e7233dad973e0d/beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/attestation_verification.rs#L1617-L1663);
- Prysm v7.3.0,
[`AttestationTargetState`](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/d01132449756e217d7f6c460e780174c34139b41/beacon-chain/blockchain/process_attestation_helpers.go#L23-L47),
which uses the head state only when its dependent root matches the
target's;
- Teku 26.10.1,
[`AttestationStateSelector`](https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/115ab400185bebee063ce13d0ab7f9f80b296c4e/ethereum/statetransition/src/main/java/tech/pegasys/teku/statetransition/validation/AttestationStateSelector.java#L57-L184);
- Nimbus v26.10.1, [`getShufflingRef(target.blck, target.slot.epoch,
false)`](https://github.com/status-im/nimbus-eth2/blob/963756c91c19b7824cea57e7aab5857ce2c776c7/beacon_chain/gossip_processing/gossip_validation.nim#L1081-L1089);
- Lodestar v1.50.0, [shuffling keyed by the voted block's dependent
root](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/blob/003bd66543fa65b5c1e954eec9e8077054c226dc/packages/beacon-node/src/chain/validation/attestation.ts#L712-L748);
- Grandine 3.0.0-rc.1, [the target
state](https://github.com/grandinetech/grandine/blob/e60be4773c0c87648ad399df58a8fdafa38b1cdd/fork_choice_store/src/store.rs#L2904-L2933).

## Not changed here

- Failed checkpoint state builds are not cached. With the limits above,
validators can still keep up to 2 uncached calls running, for
checkpoints of known blocks that descend from the finalized checkpoint
and are at most 4 epochs older than the attestation. On the target path
the pre-checked signatures are verified again when the message reaches
the normal batch verification, also when the checkpoint state is cached.
- Empty pre-Electra subnet attestations are still ignored, while the
spec rejects them. This is unchanged by this PR.

This replaces the approach of draft #24808, which only skipped the peer
ban and kept the REJECT.

author: awskii
subject: cmd/capcli, freezeblocks: don't freeze holes over good blob segments (#25173)
body:
Fixes #24037. `capcli dump-blobs-snapshots` passed no blob count, so a
slot with a pruned count row froze as an empty entry, and it rewrote
every segment from Deneb at v1.1. One run hollowed ~1,580 gnosis
segments and exited 0.

## Changes

- `DumpBlobSidecarsRange` requires a count fn: the antiquary's, moved to
`freezeblocks.BlobCountFromBlocks`. It errors on a slot outside every
frozen block segment.
- `--from` (lystopad's) starts at a segment boundary at or above Deneb.
- Ranges on disk or in `preverified.toml` are skipped. `--overwrite`
refuses pinned or other-version ones.
- Old `.idx` and `.torrent` files go only after the new segment replaces
the old one.
- Only beacon-block segments are opened; the dump stops at their
frontier.

## Notes

Without `--overwrite` a damaged blob segment counts as present; `erigon
snapshots integrity` detects it.

---------
