- `TestCleanupAndPruningKeepsBlocksWhileFinalityIsUnknown`: nothing is
pruned while `HighestFinalized` is 0.

Reviewed by Claude and Codex (dual review, then a fix-delta review).
`make lint` (twice), `make erigon integration`, `go test
./cl/phase1/stages/ ./cl/clparams/ ./cl/persistence/beacon_indicies/
./cl/antiquary/...` pass.

author: Andrew Ashikhmin
subject: cl/beacon/handler: fix pending parent retry test flake (#25481)
body:
When the completion observer runs late, the pending-parent retry worker
can poll again after applying the envelope. The test mock counted that
no-op poll as a third attempt, failing the exact count assertion in
[Windows CI for
#25471](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/actions/runs/40674305817/job/122769883364).

Make the mock return no work after application, matching
`RetryPendingExecutionPayloadEnvelope`. Count actual attempts and
explicitly assert that the envelope was applied. This is a test-only
fix.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/persistence, cl/phase1, db/kv: persist Gloas execution payload envelope signatures (#25384)
body:
Part of #21680. It follows the agreed design in
https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/issues/21680#issuecomment-6394752054.

## Problem

Caplin keeps Gloas `SignedExecutionPayloadEnvelope`s only in the
fork-graph disk cache, and that cache is pruned soon after finalization.
A later PR will rebuild historical envelopes from the beacon block, the
next canonical block's `parent_execution_requests` and EL data. The
96-byte builder signature is the only field that cannot be rebuilt. If
we do not store it, history before the serve-path PR is lost.

## Change

- New Caplin table `ExecutionPayloadEnvelopeSignatures` in
`ChaindataTables`. The key is `slot (8 bytes, big-endian) || beacon
block root`, the same layout as `kv.BeaconBlocks`. The value is the
96-byte signature. There is no schema version bump and no snapshot
change. A no-op migration,
`create_execution_payload_envelope_signatures_table` (the same as
`create_ptc_window_epoch_table`), records the schema change. The table
is created by a writable open: erigon start-up or `integration
run_migrations`. Accede and read-only openers (rpcdaemon, downloader,
seg, capcli) cannot create it, so on an old chaindata they need one of
those to run first. Other `integration` commands reopen the database in
exclusive mode when a migration is pending, but that reopen kept
`Accede` and so could not create the table either. This predates this
PR, also affected `create_ptc_window_epoch_table`, and is fixed in
#25438.
- `beacon_indicies`: `WriteExecutionPayloadEnvelopeSignature`,
`WriteExecutionPayloadEnvelopeSignatureIfAbsent` (used by backfill),
`ReadExecutionPayloadEnvelopeSignature` and
`PruneExecutionPayloadEnvelopeSignatures`. The reader reports a stored
value that is not 96 bytes long as not found, and the if-absent writer
decides presence with the reader. Forkchoice and backfill therefore
follow one rule: a malformed row counts as absent and the next writer
replaces it.
- The signature is written in the same transaction as the execution
envelope indices:
- forkchoice import, local self-build, `StoreAnchorEnvelope` and the
index-repair retry. These paths share
`writeExecutionPayloadEnvelopeIndices`. The row is keyed by
`Payload.SlotNumber`, which every entry path checks against the beacon
block slot. The repair token now carries the slot and the signature, so
a retry still works after the fork graph drops the envelope;
- history backfill (`writeDownloadedBlock`), keyed by the block slot,
only for a verified signature (see below). This also covers downloaded
blocks that are already in CL snapshots, because snapshots do not hold
signatures. Backfill writes only when no valid row exists for (slot,
root), so it never replaces a signature that forkchoice or the anchor
path verified; it does replace a malformed row.
- The forkchoice "indices already present" checks now also require a
matching signature row. An envelope that is processed again on a node
that already has its indices therefore gets the row too. Forkchoice
still replaces a different row, so a verified signature replaces an
earlier backfilled one. A malformed row reads as missing, so forkchoice
replaces it; any other read error still fails the write. Both checks use
one reader of the index state and keep their own predicates
(structurally usable for the early check, exact values for the write).
- Backfill verifies the envelope signature and stores it only when the
check ran. The check runs in the backward downloader's envelope
validation hook, after the bid check, so it covers the range batch, the
single P2P fetch and the HTTP fallback. It uses the anchor state the
backfill starts from, which is newer than every backfilled block:
- self-build: the pubkey of the block's proposer (validator indices are
never reused);
- builder `i`: `builders[i].Pubkey` when `builders[i].DepositEpoch` is
before the envelope epoch;
- domain: `DOMAIN_BEACON_BUILDER` with the fork version of the envelope
epoch.

An invalid signature fails the hook, so the envelope is discarded and
fetched again through the existing retry path. When the anchor state
does not name the key (a builder index outside the registry, or a
builder deposited in or after the envelope epoch, so the index may have
been reused), the envelope is still accepted, because backfill needs it
to progress, and its block and EL indices are written as before, but no
signature row is written. One helper selects the key; the hook and
`BackwardBeaconDownloader.GloasEnvelopeSignatureVerifiable` both use it,
and the history stage asks the downloader before it writes the row. The
history stage and `capcli chain` both set the validator and share this
write path. Without a validator nothing is verified, so no row is
written.
- `PruneBlocks` (non-archive cleanup) also prunes signatures below the
same bound as the blocks, which since #25412 is the block-serving window
clamped to the finalized epoch start. Like the block prune, one call
deletes at most `snaptype.CaplinMergeLimit` signature rows; later runs
delete the rest, so one cleanup run never holds a long write
transaction. The antiquary does not prune them (`PruneBlocksLimit` is
unchanged), because they are not in snapshots yet, so archive nodes keep
every row (about 140 bytes per Gloas slot, roughly 0.4 GB per year on
mainnet).

Nothing reads the table yet. The serve path (ByRange, ByRoot, Beacon
API) comes in a later PR.

## Trade-offs

- Backfilled signatures are stored only when they were verified: always
for self-build, and for builders whose index was not reused after the
envelope. The remaining case (builder exit, full withdrawal and reuse of
the index by a new builder in or after the envelope epoch) is not
stored, so it will not be served: a missing row only ends a ByRange
response early, while a stored unverified signature could never be
replaced on those blocks (forkchoice does not write rows below the
anchor, backfill never overwrites a valid row, archive nodes never
prune). Storing it would need the historical builder registry.
- `DepositEpoch < envelope epoch` is strict on purpose: a builder
registered in the envelope epoch may have taken the index after the
envelope, and checking against its key would reject a valid envelope and
stall backfill.
- Rows written on import for blocks that later become orphans are kept.
Non-archive pruning removes them. Rows are keyed by root, so they never
answer a lookup for the canonical root.

## Not in this PR

- Reading the table and rebuilding envelopes for ByRange, ByRoot and the
Beacon API.
- Shipping signatures in Caplin snapshots.
- Filling signatures for history that is not processed again: Gloas
blocks that backfill skips because their indices and EL blocks already
exist, blocks below the point where backfill stops, and envelopes lost
to a restart before their index write was retried.
- Signatures of backfilled envelopes whose builder key the anchor state
does not name (index outside the registry, or reused in or after the
envelope epoch).
- The pre-existing `applied=false` index-repair race in
`ensureClaimedEnvelopeIndexRepair`; it gets its own PR after this one.

## Tests

- `beacon_indicies`: round-trip, not found, a stored value of 0, 95 or
97 bytes reads as not found, the if-absent writer replaces a malformed
row and keeps a valid one, and prune boundary (slot `to-1` deleted, slot
`to` kept).
- forkchoice: import stores the signature; `StoreAnchorEnvelope` stores
it; a redelivered envelope and the untracked repair path both add a
missing signature when the indices already exist; the retry path stores
it after the fork graph has pruned the envelope or has no header; the
existing panic-recovery test now also checks the signature.
- forkchoice: a redelivered envelope replaces a stored signature of 0,
95 or 97 bytes and leaves no repair pending;
`TestPendingEnvelopeRepairsMalformedIndices` stores a matching
signature, so each case fails only because of the malformed index row.
- stages: backfill stores the signature of a verified downloaded
envelope, also for a block already in CL snapshots; an unverified
envelope is accepted and its block and EL indices are written, but no
signature row is written (also for a block already in CL snapshots);
backfill keeps an existing valid row and replaces a malformed one; an
EMPTY slot stores no row.
- stages cleanup, under the #25412 bound: non-archive cleanup prunes the
row at slot 943,231 and keeps the row at 943,232 (the first slot of the
block-serving window for head 2,000,017); archive cleanup keeps both;
one run deletes exactly `CaplinMergeLimit` blocks and `CaplinMergeLimit`
signature rows when both tables have a backlog (slot
`CaplinMergeLimit-1` pruned, slot `CaplinMergeLimit` kept in each
table).
- migrations: an old chaindata without the table, with every earlier
migration applied, has the new migration pending; after the exclusive
open runs it, an accede open can read the table.
- network: the backfill signature check accepts a self-build envelope
signed by the proposer and a builder envelope signed by a builder
deposited before the envelope epoch, and rejects both when signed by
another key; it accepts, without a check, a builder deposited in the
envelope epoch and an index outside the registry.
`GloasEnvelopeSignatureVerifiable` is true for the first two cases and
false for a builder deposited in or after the envelope epoch, an index
outside the registry, a nil builder list, a proposer outside the
validator set, and when no validator is set. The tests sign with the
Gloas fork version independently of production and put the envelope in
the first Gloas epoch, so a lookup of the wrong epoch gets the Fulu
version and fails.
- network: with the validator set, the range filter drops an invalidly
signed envelope and keeps a valid one.
- The tests cannot tell the envelope epoch from the anchor epoch for the
signing domain (passing the anchor epoch to `ComputeDomainAtEpoch` stays
green), because the anchor state is in the same fork. Consensus pins it
today: the domain must use the envelope epoch. Gloas is the last fork in
`GetCurrentStateVersion`, so the two fork versions cannot differ yet.
- The tests cannot tell the block slot from `Payload.SlotNumber` for the
row key: forkchoice rejects an envelope whose `Payload.SlotNumber`
differs from the block slot, and backfill checks it against `bid.slot`,
which consensus requires to equal the block slot. Consensus pins that
equality today.
- The one-line wiring in `clstages.go` and `cmd/capcli/cli.go` has no
test seam; it is covered by build and review (TDD skipped as a
mechanical wiring change).
- `git diff origin/main -- cl/antiquary/` is empty.

author: Andrew Ashikhmin
subject: cl: persist beacon blocks only after fork choice accepts them (#25442)
body:
Rejected P2P beacon blocks could overwrite `StateRootToBlockRoot` before
validation and break exact-state-root Beacon API reads. Both sync and
gossip imports now persist blocks and their indices only after fork
choice accepts them.

- **Acceptance:** `OnBlock` can return nil for an old block without
importing it, so initial acceptance is confirmed by a header in fork
choice.
- **Persistence retries:** Sync, gossip, and Beacon API publishing
retain accepted blocks after a failed database write. Pending writes
survive job expiry, header pruning, and sync-stage transitions.
Forward-sync retries also preserve the pending execution insertion.
- **Canonical updates:** Updates wait for the required block indices
along the path from the new head to an existing canonical block or the
trusted anchor. The anchor may come from a checkpoint state, so it can
lack block indices. This prevents a concurrent reorg from marking the
new head canonical while leaving ancestors from the previous fork.

Fixes https://github.com/ethereum-bounty/erigon/issues/56.

Regression tests reproduced the state-root overwrite in both import
paths and the ignored-block case before the fixes. They also cover
acceptance, storage retries, sync-stage handoffs, and canonical
publication. Refactors use existing coverage without a new red/green
cycle because they do not change behavior.

This prevents new corruption; it does not rebuild index entries already
damaged on an existing node. The live devnet reproduction was not rerun.

author: Andrew Ashikhmin
subject: cl/beacon: preserve actionable production failures (#23393)
body:
Payload polling and concurrent block-body production can hide a useful
failure behind busy/unknown-payload responses or cancellation. Preserve
that failure in the returned error and production log.

- Rank errors by diagnostic value: concrete failure > unexpected
internal cancellation > unknown payload > execution busy > caller
cancellation. A terminal unknown-payload response takes precedence over
transient contention.
- Keep the earlier polling error on equal priority. When concurrent
execution-payload and sync-aggregate failures have equal priority,
prefer the execution error. If both are concrete failures, retain the
sync-aggregate failure as text in the same returned error and log.
- Identify fork-choice and payload-collection cancellations observed
while the request is still active. Keep them distinct from caller
cancellation even if the request is canceled before reporting.
- Use consistent log levels: caller cancellation at debug, unknown
payload at warning, and busy responses, unexpected internal
cancellation, and concrete failures at error.
- Document and test bounded fee-recipient warning deduplication:
warnings can repeat after eviction. Runtime cache behavior is unchanged.

Follow-up to #23274.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/das, cl/persistence/beacon_indicies: move earliest_available_slot to the custody group count raise (#25475)
body:
Part of #24787: this PR covers the case of a custody group count
increase.

## Problem

`fulu/validator.md`:

> When a value for `custody_group_count` is set, the
`earliest_available_slot` field in the status RPC message SHOULD reflect
the slot at which the `custody_group_count` was updated.

On an increase, `PeerDasState.SetCustodyGroupCount` raises the
advertised count and updates the ENR at once, but
`earliest_available_slot` only follows the column prune floor in
`PeerDas.PruneBelow`. The increase does not schedule a fetch of the new
custody columns for older slots. So the node advertises columns it does
not have, and `DataColumnSidecarsByRange`/`ByRoot` leave them out of the
response for slots before the increase.

This happens only when the increase adds custody columns. Erigon
custodies `max(SAMPLES_PER_SLOT, advertised cgc)` groups, and for the
same node ID a larger count gives a superset. With the default config,
the usual 4 → 8 step for a validator node adds no columns. The first
count that adds columns is 9, which needs 288 ETH of attached effective
balance.

## Change

- `PeerDasState` keeps a custody raise slot separately from the prune
floor. `GetEarliestAvailableSlot` returns the larger of the two.
- `SetCustodyGroupCount(cgc, raiseSlot)` moves the raise slot only when
the increase adds custody columns, and never lowers it. In that case it
calls `raiseSlot` under `cgcMutex`, after the new count is installed and
the custody column cache is cleared, so a raiser that stalls across a
slot boundary cannot record a slot whose block was checked with the old
columns.
- `UpdateValidatorsCustody` passes a function that returns the current
slot + 1, where the current slot is the larger of the wall-clock slot
and the fork-choice slot. It runs in `OnBlock`, after the Fulu data
availability check of that block, which used the old custody columns.
Fork choice rejects a block above its own slot (`ErrBlockTooEarly`) and
ignores backward ticks, so a wall clock that steps back cannot put the
raise slot at or below a block that was already checked with the old
columns. `PeerDas` reads the fork-choice slot through a new
`BlockGetter.Slot()` method. A node without a fork choice uses only the
wall clock.
- The raise slot is written in the same transaction as the highest
custody group count, and `Start` restores both from one read
transaction. Neither stored value can decrease, and
`SetCustodyRaiseSlot` does not lower the in-memory value either.
- When `Start` finds a stored count above `SAMPLES_PER_SLOT` without a
stored raise slot, it treats the restore as a raise: it sets the raise
slot to the current slot + 1 with the same function and then writes it
to the database. At that point the fork choice is still at its anchor
slot, so the function uses the wall-clock slot when it is higher.
- `GetMyCustodyColumns` takes `SamplesPerSlot` from the injected beacon
config instead of the global one, through the same helper as the raise
check.

## Limitations

- A node that raised its count above `SAMPLES_PER_SLOT` while running
v3.8.1, or `main` after #25187, has the stored count but no stored raise
slot, and the database does not record when the raise happened. On the
first start after the upgrade, `Start` uses the current slot + 1. The
node stores the new columns from its real raise on, so it advertises
less history than it has until the prune floor passes that slot, which
takes about 18 days with the mainnet retention window (4096 epochs). A
node that upgrades from v3.8.0 or older has the same trade-off: it has
no stored count, and it records the current slot + 1 at its first
increase that adds custody columns after the restart.
- After a restart, the fork choice starts again at its anchor slot, so
its slot bounds only the blocks imported since the start. If the wall
clock steps back across a restart, an increase before the clock catches
up can still record a slot at or below a block that the previous run
checked with the old columns. The restored raise slot is a lower bound,
but it does not cover blocks above it.
- The spec allows lowering `earliest_available_slot` again as a backfill
fills the gap. This PR does not do that.
- The other cases of #24787 (empty column store, bucket granularity,
gaps inside the window, `ByRange` without `ResourceUnavailable`) are not
covered.

## Tests

- `cl/das`:
- `TestPeerDasCustodyRaiseMovesEarliestAvailableSlot`: an increase to
`SAMPLES_PER_SLOT + 1` at slot 1000 moves `earliest_available_slot` to
1001, and a later `PruneBelow` keeps it there. It fails on `main`
(expected 1001, actual 100). The count is the first one that adds a
custody group, so the test also covers the boundary of the raise check.
-
`TestPeerDasCustodyRaiseWithinSampledColumnsKeepsEarliestAvailableSlot`:
an increase to 8 keeps the prune floor.
- `TestPeerDasRestoresCustodyRaiseSlot`: a new `PeerDas` over the same
database restores the stored raise slot.
-
`TestPeerDasRestartAfterRaiseWithinSampledColumnsKeepsEarliestAvailableSlot`:
after an increase to 8 and a restart, `earliest_available_slot` follows
the prune floor. It fails if `UpdateValidatorsCustody` writes the slot
of the call instead of the raise slot of the state, or if `Start` also
treats a stored count of 8 as a raise.
- `TestPeerDasStartRecordsRaiseSlotForCountStoredWithoutOne`: a stored
count of 96 without a raise slot, restored at slot 5000, gives 5001, and
a second restart at slot 9000 keeps 5001. Without the `Start` change it
fails (expected 5001, actual 200).
- `TestPeerDasStartInstallsRecordedRaiseSlotBeforeWritingIt`:
`GetEarliestAvailableSlot` already returns the recorded raise slot when
`Start` begins the database write.
- `TestPeerDasReadsCustodyRaiseSlotAfterInstallingRaise`: the clock is
read after the raised count is in the ENR. It fails if the slot is read
before `SetCustodyGroupCount`.
- `TestPeerDasCustodyRaiseAfterClockStepsBackIsAboveForkChoiceSlot`: a
block at slot 1001 passes its availability check with the old columns
while the clock and the fork-choice slot are at 1001. The clock steps
back to 1000, and an increase to `SAMPLES_PER_SLOT + 1` follows. The
block is no longer available, and `earliest_available_slot` is 1002.
Without the fork-choice bound it fails (expected 1002, actual 1001).
- `TestPeerDasStartRecordsRaiseSlotFromClockAheadOfForkChoice`: at
`Start` the fork choice is still at its anchor slot (4000 here) and the
clock is at 5000, so a stored count without a raise slot gives 5001. It
fails if the raise slot uses only the fork-choice slot when a fork
choice is set (actual 4001).
- `cl/das/state`:
`TestSetCustodyGroupCountNeverLowersTheCustodyRaiseSlot` and
`TestSetCustodyRaiseSlotNeverLowersIt`: a lower slot from a later raise
or a restore keeps the higher one.
- `cl/persistence/beacon_indicies`:
`TestCustodyRaiseSlotNeverDecreases`: writing a lower slot after a
higher one keeps the higher one.

author: Andrew Ashikhmin
subject: cl/beacon: cover production error priority and cancellation (#25524)
body:
Follow-up to #23393. Runtime behavior is unchanged.

- Pin the first-error-wins rule when payload polling sees failures with
equal priority.
- Verify that fork-choice cancellation after request cancellation logs
at Debug without an internal-cancellation marker.
- Verify that an internal cancellation observed while the request is
active still logs at Error after the request is canceled.
- Rename the diagnostic ranking type to `productionErrorPriority`.
- Correct test comments about caller cancellation. Node shutdown can
leave HTTP requests active during the API drain, so it is not equivalent
to caller cancellation.

author: Andrew Ashikhmin
subject: cl/phase1/execution_client: reject RLP-wrapped typed transactions (#25529)
body:
Caplin accepted RLP-wrapped typed transactions through direct payload
validation and forward-sync block collection, while the Engine API
rejected the same encoding. Apply the existing guard before decoding
payload transactions in both paths so wrapped transactions cannot reach
execution insertion.

Fixes https://github.com/ethereum-bounty/erigon/issues/58.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/phase1/network/services, cl/phase1/forkchoice: accept execution payload envelopes before the EL verdict (#25469)
body:
### Problem

Gossip validation of `SignedExecutionPayloadEnvelope` ran the whole
import inside the pubsub validator: it could replay state, and it ran
the state transition and `NewPayload` before returning the verdict. An
`INVALID` response from the EL became a gossip REJECT. The forwarding
peer always got the gossipsub invalid-delivery penalty and, with at
least 32 active peers, was normally banned for 30 minutes. The same
happened for import-only CL checks that are not part of the gossip
rules: `prev_randao`, `gas_limit`, `parent_hash`,
`parent_beacon_block_root`, the expected-withdrawals-root and timestamp
checks in the state transition, and the local block-hash recomputation.
Every Erigon hop also waited for the EL before forwarding.

So a builder with a winning bid could publish a correctly signed,
CL-valid but EL-invalid envelope. Other clients would forward it, and
Erigon nodes would then penalize, and usually ban, those honest peers.

### Spec

`validate_execution_payload_envelope_gossip` (consensus-specs
v1.7.0-beta.4, `specs/gloas/p2p-interface.md`) has no EL step, no
data-availability step and no state transition:
- IGNORE: an already-seen envelope, an unknown block root, a slot below
the finalized slot.
- REJECT: a known block without a validated state, slot mismatch,
builder index, block hash, `execution_requests` root, request and
withdrawal limits, builder signature.
- On success, the envelope is marked seen and its payload is cached by
block hash (`seen.execution_payloads`).

The `prev_randao`, `gas_limit`, `parent_hash`, timestamp and
expected-withdrawals-root checks belong to
`verify_execution_payload_envelope` in fork choice, which is part of the
import, together with `verify_and_notify_new_payload`. Bellatrix
`p2p-interface.md`, "Why allow invalid payloads on the P2P network?",
says: "nodes should never downscore/disconnect nodes due to such invalid
payloads".

### Other clients

None of them waits for the EL before ACCEPT, and none turns an
EL-invalid payload into a gossip REJECT.

| Client | Waits for the EL? | Forwarder penalty on EL INVALID |
|---|---|---|
| Lighthouse | No: `verify_envelope_for_gossip`, then Accept, then
import | none |
| Prysm | No: the validator returns Accept, the EL runs in the
subscriber | none (`setBadPayload`) |
| Teku | No: no EL call in the gossip validator, the import runs async |
none |
| Nimbus | No: `validateExecutionPayload`, then `enqueuePayload` | none
(`addUnviable`) |
| Grandine | No: `notify_new_payload` only enqueues | none |
| Lodestar | No: the import runs in `callInNextEventLoop` |
application-level `reportPeer`; the gossip verdict stays ACCEPT |

Lighthouse and Lodestar were checked again at their dev-branch heads.
The references for the other four clients were not checked again.
Erigon's own REST `broadcast_validation=gossip` path publishes after the
synchronous import attempt, not before it. An EL `INVALID` import result
does not stop the publication.

### Change

- The import result no longer decides the gossip verdict. The verdict
comes from the service's existing structure, limit, finality,
block-availability, builder-index and duplicate checks, and then from
`ValidateExecutionPayloadEnvelopeForGossip`, which checks the block
content and the builder signature. As before, a known block whose state
is not available gets IGNORE (beta.4 says REJECT), and
`seen.execution_payloads` is not implemented yet.
- On success, the node records the payload arrival (used for PTC
`payload_present`), takes the payload-preparation hold, marks the
envelope seen, emits `execution_payload_gossip` and returns ACCEPT.
- The import runs in a goroutine on the service context. The goroutine
owns the admission token, the seen entry and the hold until the import
ends, and it recovers a panic. A panic during the gossip-event emission
before the hand-off also releases the admission token, the seen entry
and the hold.
- Import results never change the verdict and never ban. An EL `INVALID`
still marks the payload invalidated, as before.
- A transient import failure that leaves the envelope unpersisted rolls
back the seen markers, so a later copy can still be imported. Terminal
invalid results and missing data availability keep them.
- If the block state is not available yet, the envelope is ignored and
parked in the fork-choice pending queue, as the import did before. A
replay error is ignored without parking.
- Envelopes from the service pending queue are already off the gossip
path, so they still import synchronously. A local import error that is
not classified as IGNORE or invalid keeps the service job for retry. A
block state that is not available yet moves the envelope to fork choice.
After a successful or terminal attempt, including a persistence failure
that fork choice queues, the service emits the gossip event once and
republishes once.
- `ValidateExecutionPayloadEnvelopeForGossip` no longer copies the state
for each envelope. It hashes the payload and the execution requests
before taking the read lock and verifies against the cached current
state in place. Only when that state is not cached does it run the
state-free bid checks first and then replay off the lock, under the
validation semaphore. It releases the semaphore before the lock-free
finality recheck.

### Tests

Service-level tests now check that:
- an injected EL-invalid, import-only-invalid or
state-transition-invalid import result still gives ACCEPT, and the
envelope stays seen;
- the verdict is returned while the import is blocked, the import runs
on the service context, and a concurrent admission claim (as used by
REST) waits for the token;
- an injected gossip-validation error still gives REJECT, and an
injected `ErrIgnore` still gives IGNORE;
- the seen markers roll back after a transient failure;
- the payload-preparation hold stays active after ACCEPT while the
import is blocked, and is released when the import ends (this covers
payload preparation only, see the known limitations);
- the arrival is recorded before the import ends;
- a block state that is not available yet parks the envelope in fork
choice, and a plain `ErrIgnore` from the gossip check (for example a
replay error) does not park it, both on the direct path and on the
pending path;
- a panic during the gossip-event emission or inside the import releases
the admission token, the seen entry and the hold.

Pending-queue tests now check: retry on a local failure with exactly one
`execution_payload_gossip` operation event; moving an envelope to fork
choice and removing the service job when the block state is not
available; and publishing once after a persistence failure.

Fork-choice tests now check current-state validation without the
semaphore, replay-error classification as IGNORE rather than
state-unavailable (so the service does not park it), rejection of a bid
mismatch before replay, the parking API, and that the arrival API keeps
the first arrival time.

Four tests run against a real `ForkChoiceStore` and an
`ExecutionClientDirect`-backed client: EL `INVALID` and a blocked
`NewPayload` (both through a `NewPayload` test hook), a `prev_randao`
mismatch, and a bad signature. They take about 11 s each and use the
file's `testing.Short()` convention.

Existing tests that tied the gossip verdict to the import result were
updated, and renamed where their meaning flipped. Six old service tests
were removed. Five were replaced, and their scenarios are covered by new
or renamed tests. The sixth, the forged-envelope-slot test, did not
exercise the real slot check: its mock returned the slot-mismatch error,
and the test checked that error text and the REJECT class; the REJECT
path is covered by the gossip-validation service test, and the slot
check by `TestValidateEnvelopeAgainstBlock_SlotNumberMismatch`. A bad
signature is covered by an integration test, and a bid mismatch before
replay by a fork-choice test.

The hashing before the read lock in gossip validation is not directly
tested.

### Known limitations (follow-ups)

- Some import failures after ACCEPT have no automatic retry: an
inconsistent EL status/error result, some refresh failures after the EL
call, and a recovered panic inside the import. (Missing data
availability, interrupted EL validation and persistence failures are
queued by fork choice.) The seen markers are rolled back, but nothing
retries the import unless another copy arrives (req/resp, a REST
re-POST, another publication). Before this change such a non-panicking
failure gave IGNORE and pubsub dropped identical copies, so another copy
was needed then too. The difference is that the envelope is now
forwarded, its arrival is recorded, and the gossip event is emitted
before the import.
- The Beacon API can answer "already seen" for an envelope that this
node has not imported, when a gossip copy was accepted and its import
then failed with a terminal result. The seen state is kept on purpose,
as the spec does.
- `blob_data_available` still requires `HasEnvelope`, so it stays false
until the envelope is persisted, and it remains false after an import
that fails before persistence.
- The spec's `seen.execution_payloads` cache, used for a child bid's
parent gas limit, is still missing.
- There is no per-import deadline. The existing 1024-identity admission
bound applies.
- The fork-choice pending queue keeps one unverified envelope per block
root, and the latest envelope replaces the previous one for that root,
unchanged from before. A later forged envelope can replace a valid one
that was parked while the state was not available.
- Block production's parent-envelope wait (`envelopeParked` in
`cl/beacon/handler/payload_preparation.go`) does not see the
payload-preparation hold. For an envelope that is not persisted yet, it
checks only the fork-choice pending queue and
`ExecutionPayloadApplyInFlight`. The service starts the import goroutine
and returns ACCEPT, but the import reaches `beginEnvelopeApply` only
after the goroutine is scheduled, the second signature check and, when
the state is not cached, a replay. In that window, a proposal that
builds on the EMPTY head does not wait for the envelope. This window
existed before in kind and is slightly longer now.
- On the P2P gossip path, an accepted envelope normally has its builder
signature verified twice: once in gossip validation and once in the
import. If the block state is not cached at a check, that check replays
it, so the state can be replayed twice; on the `main` branch, the normal
successful gossip import replayed it once. The uncached case should be
uncommon: only the state of the most recently processed block is cached,
and an envelope usually arrives before the next block.

author: Nikolay Lebedinsky
subject: cl/cltypes/solid: clear reused uint64 list hash buffer (#25310)
body:
`RawUint64List.HashSSZ` reuses a buffer but did not clear padding after
the current values. Decoding a shorter list into an already-hashed
object could therefore produce a different root from a fresh list with
the same values.

Clear the resized buffer before writing the values. Add a regression
that decodes and hashes 12 values, then decodes shorter lists and checks
their roots against fixed SSZ roots and fresh lists. It covers the
reported five-value case, other partial chunks, a complete chunk, and an
empty list.

Fixes #25278.

Validation:
- The regression fails without the fix for lengths 1, 5, and 9,
including the exact five-value mismatch from the issue.
- `go test ./cl/cltypes/solid ./cl/merkle_tree -count=1`
- `go test -race ./cl/cltypes/solid ./cl/merkle_tree -count=1`
- `make lint`
- `make erigon integration`

author: lupin012
subject: cl/beacon/handler: fix flaky timing in wait tests (#25492)
body:
Fix flaky tests in `cl/beacon/handler`.

Two tests failed on the Windows serial runner in the merge queue (run
https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/actions/runs/40759087718), one in
each attempt of `make test-all`:

- `TestAwaitPendingParentPayloadDoesNotWaitForASlotThatIsNotCurrent`:
`"142.2025ms" is not less than "100ms"`
-
`TestGetEthV1ValidatorAttestationDataWaitsForSlotImport/request_canceled`:
expected 500, got 200. The 60ms import-wait cap expired before the 20ms
context cancel was observed.

Both assert wall-clock bounds only a few tens of milliseconds away from
the events they measure, so a scheduling delay on a loaded runner
crosses them.

## Changes

- `TestGetEthV1ValidatorAttestationDataWaitsForSlotImport`: the
import-wait cap goes from 60ms to 1s, and the elapsed time is bounded by
half of it (500ms) instead of a per-row 100ms `maxWait`. The 20ms cancel
and import events stay the same, so the test still checks that the
response comes from them and not from the cap.
- `pending_parent_wait_test.go`: the five "does not wait" bounds go from
100ms to 500ms. A broken wait in the not-current-slot tests takes 1.5s
(the cutoff), so 500ms keeps a 3x margin.

## Verification

- Reproduced the failures locally by pinning the tests to one core at
low priority next to CPU burners: 3 failures in 5 iterations before the
change, 0 in 8 after.
- Mutation check: removing the `ctx.Done()` case in
`waitForAttestationHead`, or the
`IsSlotCurrentSlotWithMaximumClockDisparity` checks in
`awaitPendingParentPayload` / `awaitHeadStateAfterChange`, still makes
the affected tests fail.
- `go test ./cl/beacon/handler` passes, `make lint` is clean.

No new test is added: the change only widens the bounds of existing
tests, and the reproduction used a stress harness rather than a new
test.

author: Andrew Ashikhmin
subject: cl: enforce peer bans for invalid backfill envelopes (#25528)
body:
A peer serving invalid Gloas envelopes can repeatedly stall historical
backfill. Backfill now validates envelopes against their canonical
blocks during fetching, while the serving peer is still known. This
includes signature checks when the signer's public key is known. When
envelope validation or RPC parsing detects invalid data, backfill bans
the serving peer and retries missing envelopes within the batch
deadline. HTTP fallback validates only newly fetched envelopes.

A dedicated Sentinel ban RPC bypasses the 32-peer grace threshold for
invalid data. Both by-root and by-range backfill requests use it.
Regression tests cover bid mismatches, forged signatures, malformed RPC
responses, recovery through an honest peer, and actual disconnection
with only one peer.

The decoder and helper refactors, along with comment-only edits, rely on
existing tests (TDD exemption).

Partially addresses https://github.com/ethereum-bounty/erigon/issues/57.
The history-stage restart loop when no source has the required envelope
remains tracked in https://github.com/erigontech/security/issues/86.

author: Andrew Ashikhmin
subject: cl: harden block persistence and head publication (#25533)
body:
Follow-up to domiwei's review of #25442. A block accepted before its
index write completes could delay head publication until the next slot.
During a storage outage, each queued job also retried the same failing
database.

- [Head
publication](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/25442#discussion_r4410728323):
treat missing indices as an expected wait and log at Debug. Block-index
commits from sync, gossip, and API publishing wake publication, with a
one-second fallback before and after Gloas. The fork-choice stage waits
for the required indices before updating the canonical chain and served
head.
- [Storage
retries](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/25442#discussion_r4410728328):
share storage backoff across scheduled jobs. A storage failure delays
further attempts for scheduled jobs; the current scan still checks
remaining jobs for expiry. Jobs without an accepted block can expire;
accepted blocks remain queued and are persisted after recovery.
- [Signed
copies](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/25442#discussion_r4410728334):
sync persists the signed copy retained by fork choice. A peer's copy of
a known block cannot overwrite its validated signature, and failed
writes keep their execution-insertion work.
- [Peer
scoring](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/25442#discussion_r4410728341):
classify a failed accepted-block write as a local error so forward sync
does not ban the serving peer.

The [acceptance
contract](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/25442#discussion_r4410728345)
is documented once on the fork-choice interface. Regression tests
reproduced the behavior failures before the fixes; refactors and comment
cleanup use existing coverage.

Broader persistence and head-publication ownership, including
retained-block memory limits, is tracked in #25544. The
ignored-publication case remains in #25483.

author: lystopad
subject: cl/das, cl/phase1/network/services: publish columns built from EL blobs and check the blob limit first (#25522)
body:
Closes #25478. Part of #25446. Addresses domiwei's review of the
release/3.8 backport #25474; the fixes land on main first and will be
added to that backport.

The EL blob-to-column path from #25447 had two gaps:

1. **Blob limit.** A block queued on an unknown parent can start the EL
import before gossip validation checked its commitment count.
`importColumnsFromELBlobs` now returns before the EL call when the block
has more commitments than `GetBlobParameters(epoch).MaxBlobsPerBlock`,
which covers every trigger.
2. **Gossip behaviour** (Fulu p2p, "Distributed blob publishing using
blobs retrieved from local execution-layer client": clients MUST behave
as if the sidecar had been received via gossip).
`ImportColumnsFromBlobs` stores the custody columns (all columns in
archive mode) and returns the sidecars on the subnets the node
subscribes to: the stored ones, or every built column with
`--caplin.subscribe-all-topics`. The block service hands them to the new
`DataColumnSidecarService.PublishColumnsFromEL`, with a context that
does not expire with the EL wait. It marks each one in the
anti-equivocation cache and publishes it on its subnet, unless a sidecar
for its (slot, proposer, index) was already seen; a column whose publish
fails is unmarked again, so a copy from gossip is still processed and
relayed. Before marking or publishing, it applies the gossip finality
rules (slot after the finalized epoch start, finalized checkpoint an
ancestor of the block), since a queued block may have waited while
finality moved on, and it publishes on the fork digest of the sidecar's
epoch.

Also from the review: `TryScheduleRecover` now runs after every EL
import (it returns early unless the node is in archive mode or is a
supernode), so a non-archive supernode also recovers blobs; and
`ProcessMessage`'s trigger is covered by a test.

`NewDataColumnSidecarService` takes the gossip manager, and
`NewBlockService` takes the column service.

Tests (all fail with the corresponding change removed):
`TestImportColumnsFromELBlobsSkipsBlockAboveBlobLimit`,
`TestImportColumnsFromELBlobsPublishesStoredColumns`,
`TestImportColumnsFromELBlobsDoesNotPublishFailedImport`,
`TestPublishColumnsFromELPublishesUnseenColumnsAndMarksThemSeen`,
`TestProcessMessageStartsELColumnsImportForValidGossipBlock` /
`...DoesNotStart...ForInvalidGossipBlock`,
`TestImportColumnsFromBlobsSupernodeSchedulesRecovery`,
`TestPublishColumnsFromELSkipsColumnsFinalityNoLongerAllows`,
`TestImportColumnsFromBlobsPublishesAllColumnsWhenSubscribedToAllTopics`,
`TestImportColumnsFromELBlobsUsesTheBlobLimitOfTheBlockEpoch`,
`TestImportColumnsFromELBlobsPublishesAfterTheImportContextExpires`,
`TestPublishColumnsFromELReleasesTheClaimOfAFailedPublish`. `go test
-race ./cl/das/... ./cl/phase1/network/services ./cmd/caplin/...`, `make
lint` (twice) and `make erigon integration` pass.

#25510 and #25514 touch `cl/das/el_blobs.go` too (verification and cell
computation, not storage or publishing); whichever merges later needs a
small rebase there.

Follow-up: #25583 (the gossip path ignores valid non-custody sidecars on
subscribed subnets instead of relaying them).

author: lystopad
subject: cl/das: skip cell proof verification for columns built from EL blobs (#25510)
body:
Part of #25446.

The Fulu p2p spec says clients SHOULD skip verification of blobs
retrieved from the local EL ("Distributed blob publishing using blobs
retrieved from local execution-layer client"). The EL verifies cell
proofs when it admits a blob transaction (Erigon's txpool does so in
`validateTx` after Osaka), and Lighthouse, Prysm, Teku, Lodestar and
Nimbus do not re-verify these columns. `ImportColumnsFromBlobs` verified
all 128 × N cell proofs although it stores only the custody columns. It
now keeps the structural checks (every blob, blob size, 128 proofs per
blob, proof size), runs them before computing cells, and no longer
verifies the proofs.

On a mainnet node, the time from the fleet's first sight of a block to
its import there grew by ~28 ms per blob (0.06 s with no blobs, 0.58 s
with 18–21). `BenchmarkImportColumnsFromBlobs` (new): 6 blobs 65.3 →
16.8 ms, 21 blobs 218 → 58 ms.

Tests: `TestImportColumnsFromBlobsTrustsELCellProofs` (fails before the
change); the rejection cases keep the structural checks. `go test -race
./cl/das ./cl/phase1/network/services`, `make lint` (twice) and `make
erigon integration` pass.

author: lystopad
subject: cl/phase1/network/registry: let one peer forward a slot of each sync subnet at once (#25593)
body:
Fixes #25592.

The `sync_committee_{subnet_id}` topics allowed 8 messages per second
per peer, burst 16, in one bucket shared by all sync subnets. A subnet
carries 128 messages per slot, signed at the same point in the slot, so
a mesh peer forwards most of them in one burst. Gossipsub marks a
message as seen before Caplin validates it, so a message the limiter
ignored was also dropped when other peers sent it: the node neither
pooled nor relayed it. On an instrumented lab node the limiter ignored
about 69% of the sync messages that reached Caplin, and every
sync-message IGNORE came from it.

## Change

The limit stays per peer, but is keyed by peer and topic and sized from
the config:
- the burst is one slot of one subnet, `SyncCommitteeSize /
SyncCommitteeSubnetCount` (128 on mainnet, Hoodi and Gnosis; 8 on
minimal);
- it refills over `SecondsPerSlot`.

An honest peer can relay a whole subnet in one burst, and a peer that
floods one subnet is still capped at one slot's worth there. The other
topics' limits are unchanged, including sync contributions, whose
IGNOREs in the lab came from validation, not the limiter.

For comparison, Lighthouse has no per-peer count limit on gossip; it
bounds global work queues (2,048 sync messages). Prysm has no per-peer
limit on sync committee messages.

## Tests

`TestSyncCommitteeMessageRateLimiterAdmitsEachSubnetsSlotFromOnePeer`
covers the mainnet and minimal presets. One peer sends a full slot on
every subnet, which is admitted, and then one more message on a full
subnet, which is refused. On the old limit it fails at message 17 on
mainnet, and on minimal at the third subnet, because the bucket was
shared.

`go test -race ./cl/phase1/network/registry` passes, `make lint` is
clean twice, and `make erigon integration` builds.

A lab A/B with the limiter relaxed is running; its results will follow
in a comment.

author: lystopad
subject: cl/das: compute the cells of EL blobs in parallel (#25514)
body:
Part of #25446. Stacked on #25510.

`ImportColumnsFromBlobs` computed the cells of each blob one after
another, and go-eth-kzg's `ComputeCells` does no internal parallelism
(it ignores `numGoRoutines`). The new `peerdasutils.ComputeBlobsCells`
computes them in parallel with `errgroup`, under the same
`rowRecoverySlots` bound (`GOMAXPROCS`) as `RecoverMatrix`, so EL
imports and blob recovery together cannot oversubscribe the CPU.
`ComputeCells` moves from `cl/das` to `cl/das/utils` unchanged, and its
callers in `cl/beacon/handler` use it from there. Prysm, Teku and
Grandine also compute EL blob cells per blob in parallel.

`BenchmarkImportColumnsFromBlobs` (sequential → parallel): 6 blobs 17.0
→ 3.6 ms, 21 blobs 58.8 → 8.2 ms on 16 cores; with `-cpu 4`, 3.6 and
10.7 ms.

Tests: `TestComputeBlobsCellsMatchesPerBlobCells` and
`TestComputeBlobsCellsFailsOnInvalidBlob` (new); `go test -race ./cl/das
./cl/das/utils`, `go test ./cl/beacon/handler`, `make lint` (twice) and
`make erigon integration` pass.

author: lystopad
subject: cl/das/utils: set up KZG before the recovery slot test starts its timer (#25603)
body:
Follow-up to #25514 (review suggestion and nit from domiwei).

Run alone, `TestComputeBlobsCellsDoesNotWaitForRecoverySlots` fails: its
5 s timer also covered the lazy KZG setup
(`goethkzg.NewContext4096Secure()`), which is slow, mostly under
`-race`. It passed in the package run only because earlier tests had set
KZG up first. The test now calls `kzg.InitKZGCtx()` before it starts the
timer.

The test's docstring repeated the comment in `das_utils.go` and is
removed.

`go test -race -count=1 -run
'^TestComputeBlobsCellsDoesNotWaitForRecoverySlots$' ./cl/das/utils`
failed at 5.00 s on `main` and passes on this branch (twice). The full
`./cl/das/utils` package passes with `-race`, `make lint` is clean
twice, and `make erigon integration` builds. Test-only change, so no new
test (TDD exemption).

author: Kewei
subject: cl/beacon/handler: check blob data on the legacy envelope POST route (#25531)
body:
## Summary

`POST /eth/v1/beacon/execution_payload_envelope` (the legacy route)
called fork choice `OnExecutionPayload` with `checkBlobData=false`. The
canonical `POST /eth/v1/beacon/execution_payload_envelopes` route and
the gossip path both pass `true`. So the legacy route could import and
persist an envelope, which makes the FULL variant of its block available
in fork choice, without the data-availability check that Gloas
`on_execution_payload` requires.

Changes:

- `processExecutionPayloadEnvelope` always calls `OnExecutionPayload`
with `checkBlobData=true`. Its `checkBlobData` parameter is removed,
because the function has one caller.
- The legacy route now also attaches the cached blob data of a local
non-self-build bid (`pendingLocalExecutionPayloadEnvelopeContents`), as
the canonical route does when `Eth-Blob-Data-Included: false`. Without
this, now that the check is on, an envelope for such a bid that is
posted on the legacy route could stay queued until its columns become
available through another path.

## Behaviour change

When the columns of an envelope are not available, the legacy route now
answers 400, as the canonical route does with `Eth-Blob-Data-Included:
false` (beacon-APIs `envelope_post.yaml` prescribes 400 for an envelope
without blob data when the node has none cached). Fork choice still
queues the envelope, and it schedules deferred column sync when PeerDAS
is configured and the node is not syncing. The envelope is not published
on gossip. The handler releases the `(block root, builder index)`
admission key without marking it as seen, so a re-POST is admitted
again, unless the background retry has already imported the envelope.
Before, the legacy route skipped the check and returned 200.

## Tests

`TestPostExecutionPayloadEnvelopeAttachesPendingLocalBlobData` now runs
for both handler variants, and it also asserts that fork choice is
called with `checkBlobData=true`. With the old production code, the new
`legacy` subtest fails with 202 and no stored columns. If only the
`checkBlobData` change is reverted to the old route-dependent value, the
`legacy` subtest fails on the `checkBlobData` assertion.


`TestPostExecutionPayloadEnvelopesRejectsStatefulEnvelopeWhenColumnsAreMissing`
now runs on both routes. Its fixture gave the envelope a different
builder index than the bid, so its 400 came from the builder-index check
and not from the missing-columns branch; the bid now uses the envelope's
builder index. Each subtest asserts 400 with no event and no gossip
publish, then 200 and one publish on a re-POST after the columns become
available. With the `canonical` condition still on the 400 case, the
legacy subtest fails because the first POST returns 202; if that first
assertion is removed, the re-POST fails with 400 "already seen". Without
the 400 case, both subtests fail with 202.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

No beacon-APIs release defines the singular `POST
/eth/v1/beacon/execution_payload_envelope`. Deleting the legacy route
and its `canonical` flag would remove the remaining differences between
the two routes.

author: lystopad
subject: cl/phase1/stages: serve a validated head while the execution layer applies it (#25581)
body:
## Problem

The fork choice stage (`doForkchoiceRoutine`) sends
`engine.ForkChoiceUpdate` and waits for it. Only after that does it:
- update the canonical chain;
- emit the head event and produce the attestation data;
- publish the head to `syncedData`, which `GET
/eth/v1/beacon/blocks/head/root` and the other `head` endpoints read.

Every head therefore reaches validators later by the duration of the
execution layer's head commit. On a mainnet node we measured 0.23 s at
the median and 0.35 s at p90 between the block event and the head event.

The delay matters most for blocks that arrive late in the slot. A sync
committee message is due at 4 s. For a block first seen by the network
at about 3.3–3.6 s, the delay moves our head past that point, so the
validator signs the previous block and the vote is not included. Over a
sync period on that node, the missed votes concentrated on exactly those
blocks.

## Change

- `computeAndNotifyServicesOfNewForkChoice` is split into
`selectForkChoiceHead` and `notifyServicesOfHead`. The combined function
is kept for its existing callers.
- For a pre-Gloas head whose payload has a recorded VALID verdict from
`newPayload` (`GetRecentExecutionPayloadStatusByRoot`),
`doForkchoiceRoutine` runs `notifyServicesOfHead` (the forkchoice update
and the RPC status) concurrently with the canonical chain update and the
post-forkchoice operations. It waits for the update before it commits
and always before it returns, so the next stage never runs while the
update is in flight.
- The payload of such a head was validated by `newPayload` on import, so
the update only moves the execution head. Lighthouse orders it the same
way: it switches its cached head and emits the head events first, and
spawns the execution layer update afterwards.
- Any other head keeps the current order, where the update comes first:
a forward-synced head that skipped `newPayload`, an optimistic or
invalidated one, one whose verdict is no longer cached, and a Gloas
head. For such a head the update is the first execution check, and a
rejection stops it before it is served.
- While block indices are still pending (the early return added in
#25533), the routine returns the update's error instead of dropping it.
- If the update fails after the head was published, the stage commits
the canonical chain, so the database matches the head the API serves,
and then returns the error. Before, a failed update left both unchanged.
The timeout and busy cases are unchanged.

## Tests

The tests were written first. On `main`:
- `TestForkchoiceRoutinePublishesValidatedHeadWhileExecutionAppliesIt`
fails: the forkchoice update blocks, and the head is published only
after it returns.
-
`TestForkchoiceRoutineReturnsExecutionErrorAfterPublishingValidatedHead`
fails: the head is never published, and the canonical chain is not
written.

`TestForkchoiceRoutineWaitsForExecutionOnHeadWithoutValidation` pins the
forward-synced case: no publication while the update is in flight,
publication after it returns. The predicate is pinned by
`TestPublishHeadBeforeExecutionOnlyForValidatedPreGloasHeads`, which
covers validated, optimistic, invalidated, no-verdict and Gloas heads.

Mutation checks:
- Accepting a head without a VALID verdict fails the predicate test and
the forward-synced routine test.
- Dropping the Gloas check fails the predicate test.
- Never publishing early fails both routine tests.

Run locally:
- `go test -race ./cl/phase1/stages/` passes.
- `make lint` is clean on two runs.
- `make erigon integration` builds.

## Not in this PR

- Gloas heads. Their payload may still be unverified when the update is
sent, so they keep the current order.

author: lystopad
subject: cl/phase1/network/services: verify sync committee messages before accepting them (#25605)
body:
Fixes #25604. Follow-up to the #25593 review (domiwei).

## Problem

On the gossip path, `syncCommitteeMessagesService.ProcessMessage` queued
the BLS check with `AsyncVerifySyncCommitteeMessage` and returned nil,
so libp2p accepted, and could forward, a sync committee message before
its signature was verified. #24629 fixed this for attestations,
aggregates, voluntary exits and BLS-to-execution changes. The queue send
also ran while the service mutex and the `SyncedDataManager` read lock
were held, so a full queue stalled every sync message and, with a
head-state write pending, every new head-state reader. #25593 raised the
per-peer budget on these topics, which made this path easier to fill.

## Change

- `checkMessage` runs the checks that need no signature and builds the
verification data under the service mutex and the head-state read lock,
as before.
- `ProcessMessage` then releases the locks and waits for this message's
own verdict through the new
`BatchSignatureVerifier.VerifySyncCommitteeMessage` (the same
`verifyAndWait` as the other topics):
  - a valid signature returns nil, so the message is accepted;
- an invalid one returns `ErrInvalidBlsSignature`, so it is rejected
instead of forwarded;
  - a cancelled wait returns `ErrIgnore`.
- Batching is kept: concurrent validators share a batch.
- After a valid verdict, `storeVerifiedMessage` takes the service mutex
again, records the message as the one valid message for its (subnet,
slot, validator) and adds it to the pool. If a different message for
that key was verified at the same time and recorded first, this one
returns `ErrIgnore`, so verification runs without the lock and the
first-valid-message rule still holds. This covers the REST path
(`ImmediateVerification`) too, which used to run its callback under the
lock.
- A duplicate of an already verified, not yet published message still
returns nil without verification.

Sync contributions have the same accept-before-verify path and are left
for a separate change (noted in #25604).

The second commit shortens the comment on the sync limiter from #25593:
the seen-cache rationale was spelled out on three limiters (review nit).

The third commit addresses the Copilot finding: the first version stored
the seen entry in the verification callback, after the lock was
released, so two different valid messages for one key verified at the
same time were both accepted.

## Tests

- `TestSyncCommitteesGossipRejectsInvalidSignatureBeforeAccepting`: a
gossip message whose signature fails verification. It failed on `main`,
where `ProcessMessage` returned nil, and now returns
`ErrInvalidBlsSignature`.
- `TestSyncCommitteesGossipWaitsForVerificationWithoutHoldingLocks`:
while a gossip message waits for its verdict, a head-state publication
completes. It pins that the wait holds no lock; it passes on `main` too,
where nothing waits.
-
`TestSyncCommitteesAcceptsOneOfConcurrentlyVerifiedMessagesForTheSameValidator`:
two different valid messages for one validator and slot are verified at
the same time; exactly one is accepted and the other is ignored. It
failed on the first version of this PR, where both were accepted.

`go test -race ./cl/phase1/network/services ./cl/beacon/handler` passes,
`make lint` is clean twice, and `make erigon integration` builds.

author: awskii
subject: cl/phase1/network: keep block ranges in flight in the backward beacon downloader (#25417)
body:
Caplin's history download sends one 64-slot `BeaconBlocksByRange` at a
time and waits for it, so catching up ~438k blocks on mainnet runs at
~30 blk/s, about 4 h. Profiling showed 9% of one core in use; goroutine
dumps showed the walk waiting on its one P2P request.

While the current range is in flight, each `reqInterval` tick prefetches
the next 64 slots below, up to 8 pending; a pending range is used only
when it holds the block with `expectedRoot`, otherwise the range is
requested fresh. Still one request per tick. snap-arb1 mainnet: 27.4 →
91.6 blk/s median, 5 runs × 600 s per arm, Mann-Whitney p 0.0079, all
over P2P (at `da902279fa4`).

With 64+ empty slots right below the last processed block, every range
request came back empty and the walk stalled for good, on main too. An
empty range is now followed by a `BeaconBlocksByRoot` for
`expectedRoot`.

---------

author: Kewei
subject: cl/utils/bls: aggregate public keys with blst batch addition (#25542)
body:
## Problem

`Signature.VerifyAggregate` used blst `FastAggregateVerify`. It sums the
public keys with `P1Aggregate.Aggregate`, which starts GOMAXPROCS
goroutines and makes one cgo call plus one `runtime.Gosched` per key. On
mainnet, each Electra block carries aggregates with about 25-30k keys in
total, and they are verified inside the block state transition under the
fork-choice lock. With 32k keys the key aggregation alone takes about
13-16 ms on an M3 Pro, and more when the cores are busy.

## Change

- Sum the keys with blst batch addition (`P1Affines.Add`, which calls
`blst_p1s_add`), then verify once against the aggregate key. The flags
are the same as inside `FastAggregateVerify`: the signature is
group-checked, the keys are not validated again (they were validated
when decoded). An empty key list and a nil key still return false.
- At most 512 keys go into one cgo call. The chunks are summed on up to
GOMAXPROCS goroutines, each with its own buffer, and the partial sums
are added in Go.

Why 512: `blst_p1s_add` puts its scratch buffer on the C stack (`alloca`
of `min(n, 1024)` points at 144 bytes each, so up to `SCRATCH_LIMIT` =
144 KiB), see supranational/blst#142. Go starts cgo threads with the
libc default thread stack size, which is 128 KiB on musl. 512 points
need 72 KiB of scratch. A compile-time check keeps the chunk scratch
below the musl thread stack.

Which builds are affected: glibc builds (8 MiB thread stacks) are not.
Of our images, only `debug.Dockerfile` (Alpine) is musl. The root
`Dockerfile` is Debian, CI builds the Hive image from it, hive's own
erigon Dockerfiles are Debian too, and hive runs erigon with
`--externalcl`. On musl, passing all keys to one `P1Affines.Add` call
crashes with SIGBUS at 2048 keys under GOMAXPROCS=1. With more procs,
blst splits the call into at most GOMAXPROCS slices of at least 512
points, so 32768 keys still give slices of more than 1024 points (the
full 144 KiB of scratch) with fewer than 32 procs.

Callers that benefit: block attestation verification, attester slashings
(gossip, block, Beacon API pool), and the sync aggregate (512 keys or
fewer, so one call without goroutines). Gossip aggregates and sync
committee contributions use `AggregatePublickKeys` with
`VerifyMultipleSignatures` and are not changed.

## Results

`BenchmarkSignatureVerifyAggregate`, 32768 keys, Apple M3 Pro:

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| GOMAXPROCS unset (12) | 15.8 ms | 1.8 ms |
| GOMAXPROCS=4 | 11.4 ms | 2.5 ms |

Each worker allocates one buffer of up to 512 keys (48 KiB), so a
32768-key call allocates about 200 KB with 4 workers and about 600 KB
with 12.

The same benchmark on the machine of the mainnet dev node (Intel Xeon
E-2288G, 16 threads), run with `nice -n 19` next to the running node.
The old and new test binaries ran alternately, six times each; the table
shows the median:

| Keys | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.77 ms | 0.77 ms |
| 128 | 0.90 ms | 0.79 ms |
| 513 | 1.10 ms | 0.92 ms |
| 2048 | 1.65 ms | 1.15 ms |
| 32768 | 12.5 ms | 2.6 ms |

For 2048 and 32768 keys the ranges of the six runs do not overlap. With
16 workers, a 32768-key call allocates about 800 KB.

Mainnet dev node: block attestation verification takes 9 ms at p50 and
11 ms at p90, for 25.4k keys per block at p50. That run had no baseline
with the old code; the benchmark above is the same-machine comparison.
The fork-choice lock hold after `newPayload` went from 50 to 44 ms at
p50 compared to the previous day, which is within day-to-day noise, so I
do not claim more than about 10 ms per block from the node data.

## Tests

- The aggregate verification gives the same results for 1 key and for
511, 512, 513, 1024, 1025 and 4096 keys; a wrong message, a missing key,
an extra key and a nil key return false; empty key lists keep the
existing behaviour.
- With 16 or more keys (blst's batch path): an adjacent duplicate pair
that reaches the doubling branch (18 keys), an adjacent P/-P pair, a
P/-P pair in a 32-key batch whose infinity result goes into the next
tree round, and a cancelling pair across a 512-key chunk boundary.
- With GOMAXPROCS=2, so that one worker sums several chunks (1025 and
2049 keys).
- Benchmarks for `bls.VerifyAggregate` (with the key cache warm) and
`Signature.VerifyAggregate`. The tests and benchmarks share one lazily
built set of keys, and the 32768-key benchmark size runs only outside
`-short`, so `make test-bench` does not sign 32768 keys.

These tests pass on `main` as well, because the change does not alter
results. The musl stack limit has no test in the repository, because it
needs a thread with a small stack. I checked it with a cgo probe that
calls `Signature.VerifyAggregate` from a pthread with a 128 KiB stack
and GOMAXPROCS=1: a version that passes all keys to one `P1Affines.Add`
call crashes with SIGBUS at 2048 keys, while `main` and this PR pass at
1024, 2048 and 8192 keys. I did not run it on a real Alpine host or
inside `debug.Dockerfile`.

author: Kewei
subject: cl/phase1/forkchoice/fork_graph: skip re-dumping an already dumped head state (#25539)
body:
## Problem

On Gloas the ForkChoice stage runs again for the same head root when the
head's payload status changes from EMPTY to FULL (`GetExecutionHead`
changes and `sleep_for_slot.go` wakes the stage), and again about once
per second while the forkchoice update returns busy. Each run calls
`postForkchoiceOperations`, which dumps the head state with
`DumpBeaconStateOnDisk`. The envelope does not change the beacon state,
so every extra run encodes and rewrites the same state for the same
root.

A head-state dump takes about 405 ms p50 on a mainnet node with the
current dump code (no fsync since #25251), and it holds `stateDumpLock`,
which disk state reads (replays) also need. By code reasoning this can
add up to 8 redundant dumps per epoch on Gloas (one per dump slot, more
while the forkchoice update is busy). There is no Gloas mainnet data for
this yet.

## Fix

`forkGraphDisk` remembers the block root and slot of its last successful
state dump, guarded by `stateDumpLock`. `DumpBeaconStateOnDisk` returns
early when both match. The slot is part of the key because a state
advanced through empty slots keeps its block root but has different
content. The marker is cleared before each write and set only after the
write finished and the file closed without error, so a failed or
panicked write is retried (stage panics are recovered, so the next run
would otherwise skip a truncated file).

## Tests

New tests in `fork_graph_test.go` count state-file writes through the
existing failing-fs wrapper:
- the same root and slot dumped twice writes once (red on main: 2
writes);
- a close error is retried (`TestDumpBeaconStateReturnsCloseError`);
- a panic during the write is retried
(`TestDumpBeaconStateRetriesAfterPanic`);
- a different root is still written;
- the same root at a different slot is still written, and the file holds
the later state;
- a failed later-slot write does not block a new dump of the earlier
slot.

Each test fails when the production branch it targets is removed.

## Out of scope

- `stateDumpLock` contention between state dumps and replays in general,
and making the state dump atomic (temp file + rename).
- Avoiding the repeated ForkChoice stage run itself.

Related to #25120 and #25136.

author: Kewei
subject: cl, cmd/caplin: precompute the next-epoch state off the fork-choice lock (#25473)
body:
Part of #25136 (direction 4, block import only).

## Problem

The first block of each epoch runs the epoch transition inside
`AddChainSegment`, under the fork-choice write lock `f.mu`. Head
updates, attestation processing and `get_head` wait during that time.

On a mainnet node on `main` (24 h, 2026-10-27 to 2026-10-28), this
transition took 467 ms p50. At the boundary, `f.mu` was held 491 ms
after `newPayload`, compared to 61 ms in the slot before.

Public Xatu head events for 2026-10-27 show the effect. We compared each
slot with the per-slot median of each client:
- Normal slots: our node is within about 0.1 s of Lighthouse, Prysm,
Teku and Lodestar.
- First slot of an epoch: these clients update the head 0.3-0.5 s
earlier than our node. That matches the transition time.

Directions 1-3 of #25136 are merged. This PR does the remaining part for
block import.

## Change

- `ForkChoiceStore.RunNextEpochPrecompute` runs in a goroutine started
by `RunCaplinService`. At 2/3 of the last slot of each epoch, if the
node is synced and the head is in that epoch, it copies the head state,
runs `ProcessSlots` to the first slot of the next epoch and hashes the
state. None of this holds `f.mu`.
- The result goes to the fork graph with `SetNextEpochState(parentRoot,
state)`, keyed by the head root. The fork graph keeps one entry.
- The first `AddChainSegment` that reaches the state transition with a
block at or after the entry's slot takes the entry. It uses it only when
the block's parent root matches and full validation is on, and drops it
otherwise. An import that stops before the transition (for example
`MissingSegment`) leaves the entry in place; it is still correct for any
later child of the same parent.
- With the entry, the import calls the new
`TransitionStateFromPrecomputedEpochState`. It runs only the block part
when the state is already at the block slot, and the normal
`TransitionState` otherwise.
- If that fails, the import falls back to the normal transition on the
parent state, so a wrong precomputed state cannot reject a valid block.
A failure only on the precomputed path logs `Precomputed epoch state
diverged` at Warn.
- `AddChainSegment` records the highest block slot that reached the
state transition, valid or not. `SetNextEpochState` ignores a state at
or below that slot, so a precompute that finishes after the boundary
block was imported is dropped. The precompute stops without publishing
once ctx is cancelled.
- `caplin_next_epoch_state_outcomes_total{outcome}` counts what happens
to the precomputed state. At an import: `hit`, `no_entry` (a block that
crosses an epoch and finds no entry, also while the node is not synced
and no precompute runs), `parent_mismatch`, `no_full_validation`,
`diverged`, `invalid`. At publication: `late`. Each outcome is also
logged at Debug, except `diverged`, which stays at Warn.
- `machine.TransitionState` is split into `ProcessSlots` and
`transitionBlock`. Its behavior does not change.

Not in this PR: payload preparation, block production, checkpoint
states, gossip validation and the Beacon API do not use the precomputed
state. After #25359, `attestation_data` no longer advances the state at
the boundary. Payload preparation already advances its own copy before
the slot, outside `f.mu`.

## Why 2/3 of the last slot

From the mainnet node's logs over 87 epochs:
- The head at 2/3 (8 s) of the last slot was the parent of the next
epoch's first imported block in 87 of 87 epochs. The head never changed
between that point and the boundary block.
- Starting when the last slot's block becomes the head would have missed
one epoch, where the last slot was empty.
- The earliest boundary block arrived 4.7 s after the trigger. The
precompute takes about 0.5 s.

On the canonical chain, 998 of the last 1000 epochs had a block in the
last slot.

These numbers use the fork-choice head. The precompute reads the head
from synced data, which is published at the end of the fork-choice pass,
so a last-slot block imported just before the trigger but not yet
published is a miss. The node measurement below will show the real hit
rate.

## Cost

- In the background, once per epoch: one copy of the head state (taken
under the synced-data read lock), one epoch transition and one state
hash.
- One extra beacon state in memory from the trigger until the boundary
import, about 4-5 s per epoch.

## Tests

- `cl/transition`:
- The precomputed path gives the same state, state root and rewards as
the normal path at every epoch boundary of the Bellatrix test chain.
  - A state ahead of the block is rejected.
- `TestTransitionStateRejectsBlockAtStateSlot` guards the
`TransitionState` split and passes on `main`.
- `fork_graph`: the matching entry is used, also when empty slots remain
before the block (Electra fixture: entry at 8288, block at 8290); a
wrong parent, a missing full validation and an invalid block drop it; a
missing segment keeps it; a corrupted entry falls back to the normal
transition; a late publication is ignored, also after an invalid block;
each import or late publication counts exactly one outcome, and a block
that does not cross an epoch counts none.
- `forkchoice`: the target epoch calculation, the trigger slot of the
loop, the synced and head-epoch gates, the published state is used by
`OnBlock`, and no publication after cancellation.
- Spectests: `sanity/blocks`, `finality` and the transition `core`
vectors that cross an epoch also run the precomputed path. Both paths
must agree on whether the block is valid, and when it is valid they must
produce the same state. Error messages are not compared, because the two
paths can fail with different messages for the same invalid block.

## Measurements

Mainnet dev node, same machine and datadir, about 24 h per run:
- without: `main` 85258cd2fd + #25359 + #25258 + #25274, 2026-10-27
07:31 to 2026-10-28 11:58 UTC;
- with: `main` cdf7da1af3 + this PR + #25423 + #25274, 2026-10-28 12:00
to 2026-10-29 13:12 UTC.

The base moved between the runs, but none of the other changes touch the
epoch transition. The first row is measured directly in
`AddChainSegment`.

| | without | with |
|---|---|---|
| Epoch transition under `f.mu`, first slot of an epoch, p50 / p90 | 463
/ 528 ms | 45 / 56 ms |
| EL "head validated", first slot of an epoch, p50 (time after slot
start) | 2.58 s | 2.13 s |
| First slots of an epoch with "head validated" after 3.5 s | 25% | 12%
|
| EL "head validated", other slots, p50 | 1.87 s | 1.89 s |
| `attestation_data` latency, first slot of an epoch, p90 / p99 | 46 /
470 ms | 0 / 25 ms |

Precomputed state: used in 215 of 224 epochs, not available in 9, and
never diverged. In most of the 9 misses, the first block of the epoch
arrived late and used the entry, and the next block was built on the
same parent, so no entry was left for it.

Per-slot comparison with other clients, from the public Xatu
`beacon_api_eth_v1_events_head` data. For each slot, the value is the
client's median head time minus the Caplin node's head time; positive
means Caplin is earlier. Without: 2026-10-27 07:32-24:00 UTC; with:
2026-10-28 12:01-24:00 UTC.

| Client | first slot of an epoch, without | first slot of an epoch,
with | other slots, without | other slots, with |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Grandine | -0.676 s | -0.240 s | -0.227 s | -0.231 s |
| Teku | -0.454 s | -0.009 s | -0.118 s | -0.095 s |
| Lighthouse | -0.395 s | +0.040 s | -0.068 s | -0.067 s |
| Lodestar | -0.467 s | -0.021 s | -0.081 s | -0.067 s |
| Prysm | -0.261 s | +0.205 s | -0.082 s | -0.074 s |
| Nimbus | -0.375 s | +0.062 s | +0.049 s | +0.060 s |

On other slots the difference stays almost the same, so the network
conditions were similar. On the first slot of an epoch, the node moved
from behind all clients to level with Teku and Lodestar.

author: lystopad
subject: cl/phase1/network/services: relay valid Fulu data column sidecars outside custody (#25587)
body:
Part of #25583. Builds on #25522 (merged).

## Problem

`processFuluMessage` returned `ErrIgnore` for a sidecar whose column is
not in the node's custody, before any validation. The node only gets
such sidecars on subnets it subscribes to beyond its custody, which
today means `--caplin.subscribe-all-topics`. An IGNORE verdict is not
forwarded, so on those subnets the node received valid sidecars but
never relayed them.

The Fulu `data_column_sidecar_{subnet_id}` gossip conditions have no
custody condition. A sidecar that passes them should be accepted and
forwarded.

## Change

In normal custody mode, a non-custody sidecar now goes through the same
validation as a custody one:
- If it is valid, the tuple is claimed in the seen cache and the sidecar
is accepted, so it is forwarded.
- It is not stored, and no blob recovery is scheduled.
- An invalid one is now rejected instead of ignored.

Custody sidecars are processed as before. The cost: a node subscribed to
every column subnet now verifies the KZG proofs of every column it
relays, which a node that forwards those columns has to do anyway.

## Not in this PR (tracked in #25583)

- **Archive mode** still ignores sidecars once more than half of a
block's columns are stored or its blobs are recovered. The
spec-consistent fix there is to publish the recovered columns and mark
them seen, after which later copies are ignored as duplicates. That is a
separate change.
- **Gloas** has the same custody check. There, a non-custody sidecar for
a block that is not yet known would also enter the deferred queue, so it
needs its own change.

## Tests

The tests were written first; both fail on the base branch:
-
`TestProcessMessage_WhenValidSidecarOutsideCustody_AcceptsWithoutStoring`:
the sidecar is accepted and its tuple marked seen, with no storage write
and no recovery scheduled (strict mocks). If storage is not skipped for
a non-custody column, the test fails on an unexpected
`WriteColumnSidecars` call.
- `TestProcessMessage_WhenInvalidSidecarOutsideCustody_ReturnsError`:
with failing KZG proofs, the result is a REJECT error, not `ErrIgnore`.

Run locally:
- `go test -race ./cl/phase1/network/services/` passes.
- `make lint` is clean on two runs.
- `make erigon integration` builds.

author: Andrew Ashikhmin
subject: cl/beacon/builder: fix admission test maximum counter (#25656)
body:
Fix the flaky maximum counter in
`TestDynamicBuilderCallsShareBoundedAdmission` ([failed CI
job](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/actions/runs/41312972395/job/124867095186)).
The comparison and CAS used separate loads, allowing a request with
count 23 to overwrite a recorded maximum of 24. Each CAS attempt now
uses one captured value.

Confirmed with a controlled interleaving: 24 active calls left the old
counter at 23; the fixed loop keeps 24. The existing test passed 4,000
race-enabled runs across 1, 2, 4 and 8 CPUs, and the full builder
package passes with `-race`.
